### Comicraft
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/comicraft-01e5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Drago-03/Comicraft-main) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://comicraft.xyz/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Electrothon%208.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://electrothon-8.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-33-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Comicraft - Creativity Tokenization Patform (CTP)

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Creators today face a fragmented ecosystem: you write on one platform, mint NFTs on another, trade on a third, and lose royalties everywhere in between. There's no single place where a creator can generate AI-powered stories, comics, and poetry — then mint, distribute, license, and earn from them — all under one roof.

**Comicraft solves this by being the world's first Creativity Tokenization Platform (CTP).**

- **No AI creation tools on NFT platforms** — OpenSea, Blur, and Rarible let you trade NFTs but can't help you create them. Comicraft has 4 AI engines (VedaScript for stories, Panelra for comics, Mythloom for hybrid multimedia, KavyaScript for poetry) with 71+ tunable parameters.
- **Creators lose royalties on resales** — Most platforms make royalties optional or unenforceable. Comicraft's Secondary Royalty Engine enforces 5-10% royalty splits on-chain via ERC-2981, automatically splitting between creator, platform (CRAFTS), and agent treasury on every resale, forever.
- **NFTs are trapped on single marketplaces** — Mint on Comicraft, auto-list on OpenSea, Rarible, and Blur through Cross-Platform Distribution. One creation studio, the entire NFT ecosystem as your storefront.
- **Static NFTs lose engagement** — Comicraft introduces Dynamic & Evolving NFTs: poems that add stanzas monthly, comics that release new panels based on holder votes, stories with seasonal endings. Living art, not dead JPEGs.
- **No way to license creative IP on-chain** — Our IP Licensing Marketplace lets brands, game studios, and publishers license works directly from creators with on-chain escrow and automatic royalty distribution.
- **Creators have no voice in platform decisions** — The DAO Governance Layer lets CRAFTS holders vote on featured stories, engine priorities, marketplace rules, and creator fund allocation via staked CRAFTS (sCRAFTS).
- **Readers are passive consumers** — Reader Rewards & Collect-to-Earn turns them into active participants earning CRAFTS for reading, reviewing, sharing, and collecting. Reading streaks, badges, and milestone rewards.
- **No recurring revenue model for serial creators** — Serialized Subscriptions + FanPay gives creators Substack-meets-NFT recurring revenue: weekly drops, subscriber-only chapters, and direct

**Challenges we ran into**

**Multi-chain bridging** — Running Ethereum (Alchemy) for NFTs and Solana (Serum DEX) for trading meant two different signing flows and wallet standards. Self-hosted `serum-rest-server` as a sidecar instead of using an API key.

**Royalty enforcement** — Deployed custom ERC-2981 contracts via Hardhat that auto-split resale proceeds three ways (creator, CRAFTS treasury, agent). Getting rounding-safe split math across variable percentages took several iterations.

**Dynamic NFT metadata** — Mutable `tokenURI` isn't standard. Built a Bull/Redis cron scheduler for timed evolutions and an ownership-verified voting system for holder-driven updates. Hardest part was getting updated metadata to propagate on OpenSea and Rarible.

**Poetry → calligraphy rendering** — KavyaScript generates 8+ poetic forms via Gemini, but rendering them as calligraphy images (Devanagari, brush, classical) for NFT minting required `node-canvas` with custom fonts and handling RTL text for certain scripts.

**Cross-platform listing** — OpenSea (Seaport), Rarible (Protocol SDK), and Blur each have different auth flows and listing formats. Built a retry queue with per-marketplace error handling after silent failures on Blur.

**Reader reward abuse** — Bots farmed CRAFTS by "reading" stories instantly. Added reading-time verification, per-user daily rate limits, and async reward distribution via Bull queues.

**Creative DAO governance** — Standard DAO frameworks handle binary votes, not "which story gets featured." Adapted sCRAFTS staking for multi-option creative proposals with discussion phases before voting.

**Ethereum Track**

### Ethereum Track

Comicraft is built natively on Ethereum mainnet via Alchemy. Here's how we use Ethereum's core standards:

- **ERC-721** — Every story, comic, and poetry NFT minted through Storymint Gateway is an ERC-721 token with chapter-level provenance and metadata stored on IPFS via Pinata.

- **ERC-20** — CRAFTS is our native ERC-20 platform token powering the entire economy: AI generation fees, NFT minting costs, marketplace trading, creator tips (FanPay), serialized subscriptions, reader rewards, DAO governance staking (sCRAFTS), and creator fund grants.

- **ERC-2981** — Our Secondary Royalty Engine implements ERC-2981 (NFT Royalty Standard) to enforce 5-10% royalties on every NFT resale. Royalties auto-split between creator wallet, platform CRAFTS treasury, and agent treasury — enforced at the smart contract level, not optional.

All contracts are written in Solidity, compiled and tested with Hardhat, and deployed on Ethereum mainnet.

**IQ AI**

### IQ AI Track

Comicraft integrates IQ AI's Agent Tokenization Platform (ATP) via the **IQai ADK-TS** (Agent Development Kit - TypeScript) to power autonomous creator agents within the platform.

- **Creator Agent Tokenization** — Creators can deploy autonomous AI agents, each with a distinct creative style and its own token. These agents continuously generate stories, comics, and poetry. Token holders govern the agent's creative direction, earn from its NFT sales, and vote on what it creates next. Each agent token pairs with CRAFTS, driving demand for the platform token.

- **Smart Agent Workflows** — IQai ADK-TS handles agent orchestration in our backend pipeline — managing multi-step AI workflows where agents validate parameters, classify content, generate outlines, and coordinate between Google Gemini (chairman model) and Groq LPU (narrow tasks) for story and comic generation.

- **Agent Treasury & Royalty Integration** — Every creator agent has an on-chain treasury. When an agent's NFTs are resold, a portion of the ERC-2981 royalty split flows directly into the agent treasury, which token holders govern through DAO-style voting.

**ElevenLabs**

### ElevenLabs Integration

Comicraft doesn't just let you read stories — it **performs** them.

Every story, poem, and comic script on the platform can be transformed into a full cinematic audiobook experience powered by **ElevenLabs' ultra-realistic voice AI**. We're not talking robotic TTS — these are emotionally expressive, human-quality narrations that shift tone with the story.

- **Story Audiobooks** — VedaScript stories get narrated chapter-by-chapter with voice actors that match the genre. A horror story sounds haunting. A romance sounds intimate. A sci-fi epic sounds vast. ElevenLabs' voice cloning lets creators assign distinct voices to different characters within the same story.

- **Poetry Recitals** — KavyaScript poems are rendered as spoken-word performances. A ghazal gets a different vocal cadence than a haiku. Spoken word pieces get the raw, performative energy they deserve. These audio renderings are minted alongside the calligraphy visual as dual-format Poetry NFTs — art you can see *and* hear.

- **Comic Narration** — Panelra comics get panel-by-panel narration with character-specific voices and dramatic pacing, turning a static comic into an animated audio experience — like a motion comic without the animation budget.

- **Multi-language Support** — ElevenLabs' multilingual models mean stories and poems can be narrated in multiple languages, opening up Comicraft's content to a global audience without creators needing to translate anything.

Every audio generation is powered by CRAFTS tokens, and the resulting audio NFTs carry the same ERC-2981 royalty enforcement as every other asset on the platform.

**Best Use of Gemini 3 [Google Deepmind]**

### Best Use of Gemini 3 (Google DeepMind)

Comicraft uses **Gemini 3** as the chairman AI model powering all content generation across the platform:

- **VedaScript Engine (Stories)** — Gemini 3 generates long-form, multi-chapter stories with 71 tunable parameters across 10 categories (Character, Plot, Worldbuilding, Tone, Technical, Thematic, Sensory, Audience, Advanced, Special Effects). It handles complex narrative structures — three-act, hero's journey, nonlinear, circular — with real-time streaming output so users watch their story unfold live.

- **KavyaScript Engine (Poetry)** — Gemini 3 generates poetry across 8+ forms: haiku, sonnets, ghazals, free verse, spoken word, limericks, tanka, and villanelles. It controls theme, mood, rhyme scheme, and stanza length, then feeds the output into our calligraphy rendering pipeline for visual NFT minting.

- **Panelra Engine (Comics)** — Gemini 3 handles story outlining, panel scripting, camera direction, and dialogue generation for comic creation. **Imagen 4** then takes those panel descriptions and generates the actual comic art — panel-by-panel visual rendering with art style presets, cinematic framing, and visual tone controls. Gemini writes the comic; Imagen draws it.

- **MADHAVA Help Bot** — Gemini 3 powers the in-platform AI support chatbot for story creation guidance, NFT minting walkthroughs, wallet setup, and troubleshooting.

- **Content Analysis & Classification** — Gemini 3 works alongside Groq LPU (used for narrow tasks like parameter validation, genre classification, and outline generation) in a dual-model orchestration pipeline managed by IQai ADK-TS.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contracts](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contracts-333333?style=flat-square) ![Remix (IDE)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Remix%20(IDE)-333333?style=flat-square) ![ENS](https://img.shields.io/badge/ENS-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today’s internet was designed for human-to-service payments, not machine-to-machine payments.
APIs power most modern software, yet monetizing them remains inefficient. Developers usually rely on subscriptions, API keys, and centralized billing systems. These approaches introduce several problems:
First, they create friction for developers who want to monetize small-value API requests. Charging a fraction of a cent per request is nearly impossible with traditional payment systems.
Second, AI agents and automated systems cannot easily interact with existing payment infrastructures such as credit cards or manual billing dashboards.
Third, API providers must build complex infrastructure to manage authentication, billing, rate limiting, and payment verification.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Ran Into

## Sending ETH Instead of USDC

Our agent was trying to pay but kept 
failing with insufficient funds despite 
having plenty of USDC.

Turns out we were using sendTransaction 
which sends native ETH not writeContract 
which calls the ERC-20 transfer function.
One function name. Thirty minutes to find it.

---

## Smart Contract Reverting With No Reason

Our ENS subdomain contract deployed fine 
but reverted on every single function call.

After an hour of debugging we realized 
our contract was calling the ENS registry 
directly without being the registered 
controller of paygate.eth.

We rewrote the contract to store subdomain 
mappings on-chain ourselves instead.
Simpler. And it actually worked.

---

## Publishing an npm Package for the First Time

We had never published a library before.

Wrong tsconfig. Missing type declarations.
Broken exports. Failed builds.

After fixing the compilation pipeline 
and testing locally with npm link 
we ran npm publish and paygate-x402 
went live. Any developer can install it now.
That felt unreal.

---

## Writing Smart Contracts Under Time Pressure

Neither of us had written a production 
smart contract before this hackathon.

Writing, deploying, and debugging 
on-chain reverts with no stack trace 
under hackathon time pressure 
was a uniquely painful experience.

We shipped two contracts in the end.
Both live. Both verified.

---

## x402 Payment Header Format

The retry request after payment requires 
a very specific header format.
A single wrong field meant another 402.

Getting it consistent across the agent 
script and the middleware took more 
iterations than we expected.

## DeFi Is Not Just Trading — It Is Programmable Money

## What Makes PayGate DeFi

### On-Chain Payment Splitting

Every payment that flows through PayGate
goes through a smart contract on Base.

No custodian holds the funds.
No intermediary takes a cut manually.
No one can stop a payment from going through.

The contract automatically splits every
incoming USDC payment:
- 99% to the developer — instantly
- 1% to PayGate — trustlessly

This is DeFi. Programmable money.
No bank. No Stripe. No middleman.

### Trustless Settlement

When a user pays for API access 
the money moves on-chain.
The smart contract verifies it.
The API grants access.

No chargebacks.
No payment failures.
No fraud.
No 30-day settlement windows.

Just money moved, verified on-chain,
access granted. In seconds.

### Superfluid Streaming

PayGate integrates Superfluid 
one of the most innovative DeFi
protocols in the ecosystem.

Instead of paying per API call 
users can open a USDC stream.

Money flows continuously 
per second — to the developer.
While the stream is open — access is granted.
Cancel the stream — access stops.

This is real-time programmable money.
This is DeFi working exactly as it
was designed to work.

### Micropayments At Scale

Traditional finance cannot do micropayments.

Sending $0.001 via a bank wire?
Impossible — fees alone would be $25.

Sending $0.001 via Stripe?
Minimum charge is $0.50.
You lose money on every transaction.

On Base — sending $0.001 USDC costs
less than $0.0001 in gas.

PayGate makes an entirely new
economic model possible —
pay exactly for what you use,
down to fractions of a cent,
at internet scale.

This is only possible in DeFi.
This is only possible on Base.

ENS becomes the identity layer

**The problem it solves**

### **The Infrastructure of Trust: How 0xKeep Modernizes Token Management**

0xKeep transforms abstract promises into cryptographic guarantees. It allows founders, DAOs, and investors to secure assets using immutable code rather than human trust.

#### **1. Rug-Proofing Liquidity Pools (Safer & Cheaper)**
*   **The Old Way:** Developers pay predatory lockers a "Tax" (often 1% of their total liquidity) and rely on a platform that holds admin keys. If the platform gets hacked or malicious, the liquidity is gone.
*   **The 0xKeep Way:** Developers pay a **flat fee (0.03 ETH)** to lock LP tokens in an immutable vault.
*   **Why it’s better:** It saves projects thousands of dollars in fees and eliminates "platform risk." There are no admin keys; once locked, the math dictates the release, not a middleman.

#### **2. Automated Team & Investor Vesting (Easier)**
*   **The Old Way:** Founders manually send tokens to team members every month. This is prone to human error, forgotten payments, and lack of transparency for the receiver.
*   **The 0xKeep Way:** Founders configure a **Linear Vesting Schedule** (e.g., "1-year stream with a 6-month cliff") in a single transaction.
*   **Why it’s better:** It’s "Set and Forget." Tokens stream second-by-second. Employees can claim their salary whenever they want, and they can verify on-chain that their allocation is reserved solely for them.

#### **3. Verified "Proof of Lock" Marketing (Viral Utility)**
*   **The Old Way:** Projects post confusing Etherscan links or screenshots to prove they are safe. Investors struggle to verify if the contract is actually secure.
*   **The 0xKeep Way:** Developers generate a **Live Embed Widget** (`<iframe>`) from our dashboard and place it directly on their website.
*   **Why it’s better:** It creates an instant, verifiable trust signal on the project's own landing page. Investors see a "Verified by 0xKeep" badge and real-time countdowns without needing to read Solidity code.

#### **4. Secure Project Handovers (Operational Efficiency)**
*   **The Old Way:** When a developer leaves a project or a DAO takes over, moving locked liquidity is difficult or requires trusting the original deployer to sign transactions indefinitely.
*   **The 0xKeep Way:** Our architecture supports **Full Ownership Transfer**. A dev can launch a token, lock the liquidity, and then cryptographically transfer control of that lock to a DAO Multisig.
*   **Why it’s better:** It professionalizes the lifecycle of a crypto project, allowing for seamless transition of power without unlocking (and risking) the funds.

**Challenges we ran into**

**The Hurdle:**
During our internal audit, we discovered a critical Denial of Service (DoS) vector in our array management logic. Initially, we used a standard "**for**" loop to find and remove a lock ID from a user's list when they transferred ownership. We realized that if a user created thousands of vesting schedules (e.g., for a large airdrop), the loop would exceed the block gas limit, effectively trapping their assets and making the transfer function revert permanently.

**The Solution:**
We refactored the contract to implement an **O(1) "Swap-and-Pop" algorithm** combined with an internal index mapping. Instead of iterating through the array, we track the exact index of every lock ID in a parallel mapping. When a lock is transferred, we swap it with the last element in the array and pop it off. This ensures that gas costs remain constant and low, regardless of whether a user has 5 locks or 50,000, guaranteeing the protocol scales safely on Base.

Mirza Ilham

### zk-solvency
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zksolvency-bc2a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/dhanush-adi/zk-solvency) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/L4BxzV4--ZA) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DevsHouse%20'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://devshouse26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-18-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Unfakeable solvency proofs for exchanges

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

For Exchanges:

Prove you're solvent to regulators without leaking customer data or trading metrics
Run continuous proofs instead of monthly snapshots that go stale in hours
Can't fake the numbers—zkTLS locks in real data before the proof runs

For Users:

Get a one-click proof that your balance was actually counted
See the exchange is solvent without exposing anyone's balances
Missing proofs show up on-chain instantly—can't be hidden

Why it matters:
Most proof-of-reserve systems only check assets and ignore liabilities. We verify the whole picture—assets, liabilities, and that every account is included—without revealing private data.

**Challenges we ran into**

The Straknet faucet was down and not able to get tokens.

zkTLS + Database Attestation
Getting zkTLS to verify PostgreSQL queries without exposing credentials was tricky. Fixed it by committing the query hash on-chain before the prover sees any data.
Gas Costs Were Insane
Storing a hash for every user account on-chain would've cost thousands in gas. We batch everything into a single Merkle root instead—went from thousands of transactions to one.
Proof Generation Too Slow
Initial Cairo proofs took 15+ minutes for 10k accounts. Split the circuit into parallel and sequential parts and used a distributed prover network. Now we hit ~4 minutes for 50k accounts.
Replay Attack Prevention
Exchanges could've just replayed old valid proofs when they went broke. Each proof now includes the previous proof's hash + timestamp. Gaps show up on-chain immediately.
No Negative Balances in Cairo
Cairo doesn't have "greater than" checks. Used range proofs instead — balances must be in [0, 2^64). Negative numbers wrap around and fail the proof automatically.

**Blockchain & Decentralized Applications**

ZK-Solvency uses zk-STARKs (Cairo circuits) to prove exchange solvency without revealing user balances. zkTLS attestation prevents data manipulation, on-chain Nullifier Registry stops account omissions, and Solidity verifiers run continuous proofs every 10 minutes. Reusable infrastructure for privacy-preserving compliance across fintech and Web3.

### LGTM
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/lgtm-f0ad) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Kishan0703/pr_shield) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/5AeXR8BSDug) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/5AeXR8BSDug) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-NMIT%20HACKS%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://nmithacks26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-17-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Shipping fast is great. Shipping secure is better.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Socket.IO](https://img.shields.io/badge/Socket.IO-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

LGTM solves two problems that every software team faces but nobody is fixing together expensive AI code review and unprotected CI/CD pipelines.

Existing tools burn thousands of LLM tokens on every PR by dumping your entire codebase into the model, making costs grow with your codebase size rather than the value you get. At the same time, nobody is watching the pipeline itself the workflow files and deployment configs that have full access to your production servers and secrets. Real attacks happen here, not in the application code.

LGTM fixes both. Our Tree-sitter and PageRank engine selects only the structurally critical code relevant to each change, sending 10x fewer tokens to 6 parallel specialist AI agents security, bugs, performance, style, documentation, and test coverage. You bring your own API key, we charge nothing on top, making a 10-developer team pay around $14 a month instead of $240 with competitors.

For pipeline security, 16 deterministic rule-based detectors scan your CI/CD configuration files on every push zero LLM tokens, sub-second execution. When a critical issue is found, three enforcement gates fire a PR comment with fixes, a blocked merge button, and most importantly a runtime halt that stops the pipeline before checkout, before tests, before anything runs. Direct pushes, cron jobs, tag-triggered deployments all covered. No competitor has this.

We also built a Knowledge Graph an interactive visual dependency map of your entire codebase showing which files are most critical, most coupled, and most risky powered by the same engine that makes our reviews precise.

LGTM is for startups moving fast without a security team, open source maintainers reviewing PRs from strangers, and any engineering team whose pipelines have never been audited.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building LGTM was not straightforward. Every layer of the system introduced its own set of problems that took real debugging time to solve.

The first major challenge was context selection. Getting Tree-sitter to parse a live GitHub repository accurately and then running PageRank on the resulting dependency graph in real time was not trivial. The graph computation had to be fast enough to not block the review pipeline while still being accurate enough to send meaningful context to the agents. Early versions were either too slow or sending irrelevant context, which tanked review quality.

The second challenge was the multi-agent architecture. Running six LLM agents in parallel sounds simple until you realise that parallel API calls fail unpredictably, rate limits hit at random, and the synthesizer has to produce a coherent verdict from six agents that may partially contradict each other. Building a reliable aggregation layer that handles partial failures gracefully without dropping findings or blocking the pipeline took significant iteration.

The third challenge was the BullMQ and Redis reliability issue. Workers were silently dropping jobs whenever Redis disconnected unexpectedly. No errors surfaced, no logs triggered tasks simply vanished. This was invisible until we noticed reviews not completing under load. Solving this required implementing proper Redis reconnection handling and dead letter queues for failed jobs.

The fourth and most frustrating challenge was the GitHub OAuth cold start problem on Fly.io. Our server was spinning down between requests due to Fly.io's idle machine behaviour, which killed active OAuth sessions mid-login. Users would authenticate with GitHub and get dropped back to the login page with no error. The fix was a single configuration line setting min_machines_running to 1 but finding that root cause after hours of debugging session handling code was painful.

The fifth challenge was the runtime halt architecture. Getting the GitHub Action to reliably call our API as step one of any workflow, receive the halt decision, and exit cleanly before any subsequent steps ran across different workflow configurations, different runner environments, and different trigger types required careful design of the Action's failure handling to ensure it never silently passed when it should have blocked.

**AI & ML**

LGTM sits at the intersection of AI and security engineering two fields that are increasingly impossible to separate.

The core of what makes LGTM intelligent is not just that it uses LLMs. It is how it uses them. We built a context selection engine that applies classical ML concepts graph theory and the PageRank algorithm on top of compiler-grade AST parsing to determine which parts of a codebase are structurally critical for any given change. The model does not receive raw text. It receives a mathematically ranked, dependency-aware context. That is applied machine learning directly improving LLM output quality while reducing token consumption by 10x.

The six specialist agents are not generic prompts. Each one is a fine-tuned role with specific instructions, domain focus, and output schema security, bugs, performance, style, documentation, and test coverage running in parallel and feeding into a synthesizer that produces a final weighted verdict. That multi-agent architecture is the same pattern driving the most advanced AI systems being built today.

On the CI/CD security side, the 16 deterministic detectors use pattern recognition on structured AST data not keyword matching, not regex alone to identify dangerous configurations with zero false positives and zero LLM dependency. That is rule-based ML applied to a real security problem.

The Knowledge Graph takes it further visualising the entire codebase as a force-directed graph where node importance is computed using PageRank, edge weights represent dependency strength, and coupling and churn scores surface risk automatically. That is graph ML made visible and actionable for developers.

LGTM does not use AI as a feature. AI is the architecture.

**Google Gemini**

LGTM integrates Google Gemini as one of its selectable LLM providers powering the six parallel AI code review agents. When a developer opens a pull request, our Tree-sitter and PageRank engine selects only the structurally critical context sending 10x fewer tokens than naive approaches and Gemini processes that optimised context to produce specialist reviews across security, bugs, performance, style, documentation, and test coverage. The bring-your-own-key model means teams using Gemini pay Google directly at cost with zero markup from us, making production-grade AI code review accessible to startups and open source maintainers who cannot afford flat per-seat pricing.

**MongoDB Atlas**

MongoDB serves as the primary persistence layer for LGTM, storing everything that matters user accounts, connected repositories, PR reviews, security findings, audit logs, and scan history. The document model was a natural fit for our use case because every review is a richly nested object findings with severity levels, rule IDs, affected file paths, suggested fixes, and resolution status all living inside a single scan document. The audit log is designed write-once at the schema level with only the resolution field remaining mutable, giving teams an immutable security record they can trust for compliance. MongoDB also stores the codebase index per repository, which feeds both the AI review agents and the Knowledge Graph generation pipeline.

While building BarTechies, several challenges came up during development.

**1. Designing the NEAT Score Logic**
One of the main challenges was deciding how to calculate a meaningful NEAT score based on user inputs such as desk hours, standing time, and daily activity.

Since there is no simple formula available for this, I had to design a basic scoring model that converts these inputs into an understandable metabolic activity score.

How I solved it:
I created a simplified scoring system in JavaScript that assigns weighted values to different activity inputs and then calculates a final NEAT score dynamically.

**2. Making the UI Responsive**
Another challenge was ensuring that the website worked well across different screen sizes, especially laptops and mobile devices.

Some components such as the calculator layout and information sections were not aligning properly on smaller screens.

How I solved it:
I adjusted the CSS using flexbox and responsive styling to make the layout adapt to different screen widths.

**3. Integrating the Interactive Calculator**
Building the interactive calculator required handling real-time input values and updating results instantly.

At first, the calculator was not updating correctly when users changed values.

How I solved it:
I debugged the JavaScript logic and ensured that event listeners captured input changes properly, allowing the score to update dynamically.

### SurakshaSetu
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/surakshasetu-f399) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Agniva-07/Binary-Null-Pointers) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/HQOVx3O8xVY?si=OwVr9s8cVPmbqmAi) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-BINARY%20v2-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://binaryvtwo.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-16-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> When seconds matter , Help is near

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

** The Problem It Solves**

In critical emergency situations such as accidents, harassment, medical crises, or unsafe environments, individuals often struggle to get immediate help. Most existing solutions rely heavily on predefined emergency contacts (family/friends) or institutional responders (police/ambulance), both of which introduce significant delays.

Traditional SOS systems suffer from several key limitations:

Limited Reach: Alerts are sent only to a fixed set of contacts, who may not be physically nearby or able to respond quickly.
Delayed Response Time: Institutional services, while essential, often take time to arrive, especially in densely populated or remote areas.
Lack of Real-Time Community Support: There is no mechanism to leverage the presence of nearby individuals who could provide immediate assistance within seconds.
No Communication Channel: Even when help is nearby, there is no structured way for victims to communicate their situation in real time with responders.
Isolation During Emergencies: Victims often feel helpless and alone, without any feedback or assurance that help is on the way.

** Our Solution**

SurakshaSetu addresses these gaps by transforming emergency response into a real-time, community-driven safety network.

Instead of relying solely on predefined contacts, our system:

1) Detects and utilizes live geolocation to identify nearby users within a defined radius
2) Broadcasts SOS alerts to multiple potential responders in the vicinity
3) Enables volunteer-based assistance, where nearby individuals can respond instantly
4) Provides a private communication channel between the victim and selected responders
5) Reduces response time drastically by connecting help that is physically closest
6) Key Impact
From delayed help → to instant human response
From isolated SOS → to connected support system
From passive alerts → to active coordination

This approach ensures that help is not just informed, but mobilized immediately, bridging the critical gap between emergency occurrence and real assistance.

 **Why This Matters**

In real-world scenarios, the first few minutes of an emergency are the most crucial. By enabling a decentralized, real-time response network, SurakshaSetu empowers communities to act as the first line of support, potentially saving lives and improving safety outcomes.

**Challenges we ran into**

Initially, the idea seemed similar to traditional SOS systems, so we had to rethink and expand it into a community-driven safety network.
Designing a system that avoids alert spamming while still reaching the right nearby users was challenging.
Simulating real-time nearby users and responses without a backend required careful frontend logic and demo design.
Ensuring usability during high-stress situations (simple UI, quick actions) was a key design challenge.
Balancing innovation with practicality — making sure the feature is actually usable in real-life scenarios.

**Open Innovation**

During emergencies, victims often face delayed assistance due to reliance on predefined contacts or slow institutional response. There is a lack of a decentralized, real-time system that can instantly connect individuals in distress with nearby responders who are physically closest and capable of helping immediately.

> Cred-Score is a privacy-first DeFi credit platform

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

CredScore AI enables anyone to access decentralized financial services without traditional barriers like collateral or credit history.

1. Access Instant Credit (No Collateral)
Users can borrow funds based on on-chain activity and AI-driven credit scoring
No need for banks, paperwork, or locked assets
Ideal for:
Students
Freelancers
Crypto-native users

2. Prove Creditworthiness Privately
Uses Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs) to verify income and financial health
Users don’t expose sensitive data like salary, bank statements, or identity
Ensures privacy-first financial access

3. Automate Finances with AI Agents

Users can deploy intelligent wallets that:

Execute trades automatically (DeFi Trader)
Optimize yield farming returns (Yield Optimizer)
Route payments with lowest fees (Payment Router)
Control and manage spending (Shopping Assistant)

This reduces manual effort and improves decision-making.

4. Smart Spending & Marketplace Integration
Use credit directly for:
Shopping
Food ordering
Online purchases
AI ensures spending stays within safe limits
Credit-based access unlocks premium features 5. Track Financial Health in Real-Time
Live dashboard shows:
Credit score
Wallet activity
Risk tier
Available credit
Helps users understand and improve their financial behavior

 How does it make things easier / safer?
 Easier
 No collateral required → Removes entry barriers
 Instant approvals → No waiting, no intermediaries
 Automated finance → AI handles complex DeFi actions
 All-in-one platform → Credit, trading, payments in one place
 Safer
 Zero-Knowledge Proofs → No sensitive data exposure
 AI risk analysis → Prevents overspending and risky behavior
 Blockchain transparency → Every transaction is verifiable
 Non-custodial wallets → Users always control their funds
 Real Impact

CredScore AI bridges the gap between traditional finance and DeFi by making credit:

Accessible → Anyone with a wallet can participate
Private → No invasive data sharing
Intelligent → AI-driven financial decisions
Trustless → Powered entirely by blockchain

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Wallet Data Inconsistency & RPC Failures

Problem:
Fetching real-time wallet data from the Shardeum testnet was unreliable at times. RPC calls would timeout or return incomplete transaction history, which directly affected credit score calculations.

Solution:

Implemented fallback mock data when RPC fails
Added retry + timeout mechanisms for stability
Cached recent responses to avoid repeated failures

 This ensured the dashboard always remained functional and responsive.

2. Designing a Fair Credit Scoring Model

Problem:
Creating a credit score using only on-chain data was tricky:

Wallet balance alone is not reliable
Transaction count can be gamed

Solution:

Built a weighted scoring system:
Activity (60%)
Balance (40%)
Added caps (min, max) to prevent manipulation
Extended model to include income verification (via Vouch)

 Result: A more balanced and harder-to-game scoring system.

3. Integrating Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)

Problem:
ZK systems (vlayer) are complex and not beginner-friendly:

Difficult to debug proof failures
Hard to simulate real-world verification flows

Solution:

Started with mock verification flows before real integration
Broke the pipeline into smaller steps:
Input → Proof generation → Verification
Added clear backend logs for debugging

This made ZK integration manageable and testable.

**Blockchain & Decentralized Applications**

Blockchain & Decentralized Applications

CredScore AI is a fully decentralized credit platform built on the Shardeum blockchain, leveraging smart contracts and on-chain data to eliminate reliance on traditional financial institutions.

Uses smart contracts (Solidity) to manage credit lines, lending logic, and agent wallets in a trustless manner
Implements on-chain credit scoring based on wallet activity, transaction history, and balance
Integrates zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) via vlayer to verify user income and creditworthiness without exposing sensitive data
Enables non-custodial interactions, ensuring users always retain control over their funds
Features AI agent wallets deployed via smart contracts, allowing autonomous execution of DeFi actions

By combining transparency, immutability, and privacy-preserving verification, CredScore AI represents a next-generation decentralized financial infrastructure.

**FinTech**

CredScore AI redefines how credit systems work by replacing traditional, centralized financial models with an AI-driven, blockchain-based credit ecosystem.

Provides uncollateralized lending, removing barriers like credit history and paperwork
Uses AI-powered credit scoring to assess user risk dynamically based on real-time wallet behavior
Introduces risk-based APR models (3–12%), similar to modern financial systems but fully transparent
Enables instant loan approvals, eliminating delays from intermediaries
Integrates income verification (via Vouch) to enhance financial credibility without compromising privacy
Offers a real-time financial dashboard for users to track credit score, spending, and borrowing capacity

This makes financial services more:

Accessible → Anyone with a wallet can access credit
Efficient → Automated approvals and AI-driven decisions
Secure → Privacy-first verification with ZK proofs
Transparent → All operations visible on-chain

CredScore AI bridges the gap between traditional finance (FinTech) and decentralized finance (DeFi), making credit smarter, faster, and more inclusive.

### Stamped
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/stamped-4ba5) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/officiallyutso/stamped-ethm) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.canva.com/design/DAHB7zXpbS0/YR3v9iVsE5W0u1nVNveF7g/edit?utm_content=DAHB7zXpbS0&utm_campaign=designshare&utm_medium=link2&utm_source=sharebutton) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/u7tndFxd4YU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-15-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Capture Authenticity Not Just Images

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![C](https://img.shields.io/badge/C-333333?style=flat-square) ![Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/Kotlin-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Digital platforms increasingly rely on photos as operational evidence** whether for logistics documentation, inspections, property listings, field operations, or vendor onboarding. However, *once an image is uploaded to a platform*, there is currently no reliable way to verify whether the photo actually originated from a real camera capture or from a generated, reproduced, or manipulated source.

This problem is becoming significantly worse with the rise of generative AI. *AI-generated images, screenshots, and reproduced media can easily pass through existing moderation systems*. Metadata such as EXIF data can be stripped or modified, and post-upload detection systems remain probabilistic and unreliable. As a result, companies must treat critical visual inputs as untrusted data, leading to disputes, fraud risks, and costly manual verification processes.

**Stamped solves this by introducing a verifiable capture layer for images.**

Instead of trying to determine whether an image is fake after upload, Stamped verifies how the image was captured at the moment of capture itself. The system enforces a trusted capture environment and generates a cryptographically verifiable authenticity record that accompanies the image.

Key capabilities include:

- Capture environment verification (device integrity checks)

- Detection of reproduced images such as screens or prints

- Cryptographic signing of the capture record

- Privacy-preserving proof generation

- Secure documentation storage and collaboration

Stamped can be used in many real-world workflows including:

- Logistics and shipment documentation

- Property inspection and real estate listings

- Field worker documentation

- Vendor onboarding and product verification

- Construction site documentation

- Insurance claims evidence

By converting ordinary photos into verifiable digital evidence, Stamped helps organizations reduce disputes, prevent fraud, and build trust in image-driven workflows.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Zero-Knowledge Proof Generation**

One of the most technically challenging aspects was implementing the zero-knowledge proof layer for capture verification. The goal was to prove that a valid capture event occurred without revealing sensitive information such as device identifiers or private metadata.

Designing efficient circuits and ensuring proof generation remained computationally practical was difficult. Early implementations resulted in proofs that were too slow for real-world usage. This required redesigning parts of the proof structure and optimizing the verification pipeline so that proofs could be generated and verified within acceptable performance limits.

Balancing privacy guarantees with performance constraints was a major engineering challenge.

**2. Fileverse Integration**

Another key hurdle was integrating Fileverse as the decentralized document layer for capture records.

Fileverse provides encrypted collaborative documents stored in a decentralized manner. The challenge was designing a system where capture records could be securely written, updated, and shared while maintaining strong privacy guarantees.

This required designing a clean workflow for:

- Writing capture metadata into Fileverse documents

- Maintaining encrypted document states

- Ensuring compatibility with Fileverse APIs

Structuring capture records in a format suitable for both humans and automated verification systems

Once implemented, Fileverse allowed Stamped to provide tamper-resistant and encrypted capture documentation that can be shared without relying on centralized platforms.

**3. BitGo Wallet Infrastructure**

Integrating BitGo introduced another set of challenges related to privacy-preserving wallet infrastructure.

The system uses BitGo wallets to:

- Manage cryptographic identities

- Generate fresh addresses

- Sign transactions programmatically

- Enforce wallet-level policies

Designing a workflow that maintained privacy while still allowing programmable verification required careful handling of wallet keys and transaction flows.

Ensuring that capture verification records could interact with BitGo wallets without leaking identity information required careful architecture design and testing.

**4. System Architecture**

The biggest overall challenge was designing an architecture that integrates:

- device trust verification - device attestation (play integrity)

- zero-knowledge proofs

- decentralized document storage

- wallet infrastructure

- capture verification

while still keeping the system usable in real-world workflows.

Multiple iterations were required before arriving at a design that balanced security, usability, and privacy.

**Privacy**

**Stamped is fundamentally designed as a privacy-preserving verification system.**

Traditional verification systems often require users to expose sensitive information such as device identifiers, identity credentials, or raw metadata in order to prove that a digital action occurred. This creates a trade-off between verification and privacy.

Stamped removes this trade-off by using cryptographic proofs and decentralized infrastructure to verify image authenticity without exposing sensitive user data.

Instead of storing or revealing identifiable information about the device or user, Stamped generates a verifiable proof that a capture event occurred under trusted conditions. These proofs allow platforms to trust submitted images without collecting intrusive personal data.

Key privacy properties of the system include:

- **Zero-knowledge proof based verification**
Capture authenticity can be verified without revealing sensitive device or identity information.

- **End-to-end encrypted documentation**
Capture records are stored using Fileverse encrypted documents, ensuring only authorized parties can access the data.

- **Minimal data exposure**
Platforms receive a verifiable authenticity record rather than raw device metadata.

- **Decentralized storage layer**
Using Fileverse avoids reliance on centralized storage providers that can access or analyze sensitive operational documentation.

This architecture ensures that users can prove the authenticity of an image without sacrificing privacy.

Why Privacy Matters for This Problem

Image verification systems are often used in workflows that involve sensitive information, including:

- logistics shipment documentation

- construction site inspections

- property verification

- field worker reporting

- compliance documentation

*In many of these cases, photos may contain location data, operational details, or sensitive business information.*

Stamped ensures that verification does not require exposing unnecessary data. Instead, the system focuses on proving the integrity of the capture event itself, while keeping the underlying data private.

**DeFi**

Stamped integrates decentralized financial infrastructure directly into real-world operational workflows.

The platform uses BitGo wallet infrastructure to manage treasury and worker payouts inside each workspace. Each organization using Stamped has a treasury wallet that can distribute payments to workers based on verified operational activity.

This creates a system where:

workers generate verified field documentation

operational records are cryptographically verified

payments can be distributed directly from the workspace treasury

This architecture enables a new type of crypto-native operational payment system.

For example:

delivery drivers submitting proof-of-delivery photos

field inspectors submitting verified inspection images

construction workers documenting site activity

These verified actions can directly trigger programmable payouts using the BitGo wallet infrastructure.

Key DeFi components in the system include:

programmable treasury wallets using BitGo

automated payout mechanisms

wallet-based identity for workers and managers

on-chain anchoring of operational verification records

This connects real-world work verification with decentralized financial infrastructure, allowing organizations to create transparent and programmable payment systems tied to verifiable activity.

Stamped demonstrates how DeFi infrastructure can extend beyond financial applications and power real-world operational coordination and payments.

**Best Privacy Application using BitGo**

**Best Privacy Application Using BitGo**

Stamped is designed as a privacy-preserving capture verification system, making it a strong candidate for the BitGo privacy track.

BitGo's wallet infrastructure enables Stamped to build a system where capture authenticity can be verified without exposing sensitive identity information.

Using BitGo's SDK and wallet infrastructure allows Stamped to:

- create secure wallet identities

- generate fresh addresses per verification event

- programmatically sign verification records

- enforce cryptographic policies on verification operations

This design ensures that capture authenticity proofs can be verified while keeping user identity private.

Rather than linking verification records to a persistent public identity, the system can generate unlinkable verification events, preserving privacy while still enabling trust.

This aligns directly with the goal of the BitGo privacy track:

- building privacy-preserving applications on top of secure wallet infrastructure.

Stamped demonstrates how wallet infrastructure can be used not just for payments, but also for privacy-preserving verification systems in real-world workflows.

By combining:

- wallet-based cryptographic identity

- zero-knowledge proofs

- encrypted document storage

- verifiable capture records

Stamped provides a novel example of how privacy technologies can be applied to real-world operational infrastructure.

**Best DeFi Application using BitGo**

Stamped integrates BitGo wallet infrastructure directly into operational workflows, enabling a system where verified real-world activity can trigger programmable payments.

In many industries such as logistics, delivery networks, construction, and field inspections, workers must submit photo documentation as proof that work was completed. However, these photos are often unverifiable, leading to disputes, fraud, and delayed payments.

Stamped solves this by combining verifiable image capture with decentralized payment infrastructure.

When a worker captures a photo through Stamped:

The system verifies the capture environment.

A cryptographic proof of capture is generated.

The proof is anchored on-chain.

The verified record is stored in decentralized documentation via Fileverse.

Because the work is now cryptographically verifiable, payments can be safely tied to these verified events.

BitGo is used as the underlying wallet infrastructure to power this system.

Each workspace in Stamped has a BitGo-managed treasury wallet, which allows organizations to:

manage operational funds securely

programmatically distribute payouts to workers

track payout history and treasury balances

send payments without requiring workers to set up complex crypto wallets

Managers can access a payout dashboard that loads treasury data directly from BitGo and allows them to distribute payments to workers based on verified activity.

This creates a system where:

work is cryptographically verified

records are tamper-resistant

payments are securely distributed through BitGo

By connecting real-world proof of work with programmable wallet infrastructure, Stamped demonstrates how DeFi tools can be used to build transparent operational systems beyond traditional finance.

This makes Stamped a strong candidate for the Best DeFi Application using BitGo track.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

**Stamped fits perfectly within the Build What Big Tech** Won't philosophy because it focuses on creating privacy-first infrastructure rather than relying on centralized platforms.

Traditional collaboration and documentation tools such as Google Docs require users to trust large centralized providers with sensitive operational data. In contrast, **Stamped uses Fileverse to store capture verification records in encrypted, decentralized documents.**

Using the Fileverse API allows Stamped to create and maintain:

- encrypted capture documentation

- tamper-resistant audit trails

- privacy-preserving collaboration records

This approach ensures that critical documentation is not controlled by a centralized provider but instead remains user-owned and cryptographically verifiable.

The project aligns strongly with the idea of self-sovereign computing, where users maintain control over their data rather than relying on large technology platforms.

**Market Research & Real-World Validation**

Before building Stamped, extensive market research was conducted to understand whether this problem exists in real-world workflows.

Conversations were held with professionals from multiple industries including:

- logistics operations teams

- construction site managers

- field inspection companies

- wholesale supply chains

- real estate platform managers

- marketplace operators

Discussions were also held with professionals working at companies such as:

- Swiggy

- MagicBricks

- construction companies

- Shipment companies (e.g. Intoglo, Citrus Freight)

- field worker service providers

A common issue across these industries is that photo documentation is critical but difficult to verify, leading to disputes and operational friction.

Stamped directly addresses this gap by creating verifiable capture infrastructure, something that large platforms have not yet implemented.

This is precisely the kind of infrastructure that large technology platforms have historically avoided building. making it a strong fit for the Build What Big Tech Won't track.

**BEST Overall Project**

Stamped addresses a real-world trust problem that affects multiple industries: the inability to verify whether a photo actually originated from a real camera capture.

Today, many operational workflows depend on photo documentation — including logistics shipments, construction inspections, property verification, insurance claims, and proof-of-delivery. However, once an image is uploaded to a system, there is no reliable way to prove whether it was captured at that moment or generated or manipulated later.

Stamped introduces a verifiable capture infrastructure that solves this problem at the source.

The system verifies images at the moment of capture and generates a cryptographically verifiable capture record. This record can later be used to prove that the image was captured under trusted conditions.

The project combines several advanced technologies into a single working system:

privacy-preserving verification using zero-knowledge proofs

decentralized documentation using Fileverse

secure wallet infrastructure using BitGo

robust image watermarking using DWT–DCT signal processing

on-chain anchoring of capture proofs

Stamped also includes a complete operational platform with:

workspace and project management

field photo capture and verification

decentralized report generation

attendance and shift tracking

automated payout systems for field workers

Because the project solves a real-world infrastructure problem and integrates multiple technologies into a functional product, it fits strongly within the Best Overall Project category.

### Roots to Routes
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/roots-to-routes-291a) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/eshwarsaigoudpanjala-debug/Roots-To-Routes) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://roots-to-routes-lhyb.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Lfgv4Hf109U) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-13-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> " Learn , Play And Discover The Journey of FOOD."

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Many people, especially children and urban consumers, consume food every day without understanding how it is grown, what resources are required for cultivation, when it is harvested, or how it reaches their plates. Information about food production is often scattered across multiple websites, difficult to understand, and not presented in an engaging manner.

Roots to Routes solves this problem by providing a single platform where users can explore the complete journey of food items such as rice, fruits, vegetables, pulses, and dry fruits—from cultivation to consumption.

Users can:
- Learn step-by-step growing processes.
- Understand soil, water, and fertilizer requirements.
- Discover seasonal crops and harvesting methods.
- Explore nutritional benefits of different foods.
- Learn through interactive quizzes, videos, and educational games.

The platform makes agricultural and food education easier to understand, more engaging, and accessible for students, children, teachers, and consumers, helping bridge the gap between people and the origins of their food.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Faced

During development, one of the biggest challenges was collecting and organizing accurate information for different food items such as rice, fruits, vegetables, pulses, and dry fruits. The information was available across multiple sources and needed to be structured into a simple, easy-to-understand format.

Another challenge was presenting agricultural concepts in an engaging way. Initially, the platform displayed large amounts of information, but we realized that younger users, especially children, would find it difficult to read long explanations. To address this, we introduced a more interactive approach through visual content, quizzes, and educational games.

We also faced challenges in designing a user-friendly search experience that could quickly provide relevant information while keeping the interface simple and intuitive.

How We Solved Them

- Organized information into clear step-by-step learning modules.
- Simplified complex agricultural concepts into easy-to-understand content.
- Added quizzes and interactive learning elements to improve engagement.
- Focused on a clean and simple user interface for easier navigation.
- Continuously refined the platform based on feedback from mentors and peers.

**Gemini**

Gemini API acts as the AI engine of Roots to Routes. User queries are sent to Gemini through secure API calls. Gemini analyzes the prompt and generates structured responses related to food cultivation, agricultural practices, nutrition, and farm-to-plate journeys. The generated content is then displayed on the website in an organized format, creating an interactive learning experience.

**MongoDB**

MongoDB serves as the backend database of Roots to Routes. It stores structured data including food categories, cultivation steps, farming requirements, nutritional values, quiz content, and user interactions. When a user searches for a food item, the application retrieves the relevant information from MongoDB and displays it dynamically. Its NoSQL architecture enables flexible data storage for different food types without requiring a rigid schema.

**Sarvam.ai**

Sarvam AI is integrated into our platform to process user queries and generate contextual responses. When users search for a food item or ask questions about its cultivation, Sarvam AI retrieves and organizes information into a simplified step-by-step format. This enables an interactive learning experience where users can explore food origins, farming practices, and nutritional information through natural language interactions.

**Open Innovation**

Roots to Routes fits into the Open Innovation track because it addresses a real-world educational and social challenge that spans multiple domains, including agriculture, education, nutrition, and technology.

The project aims to bridge the gap between consumers and food production by helping users understand where their food comes from and how it is cultivated. Rather than focusing on a single industry-specific problem, it creates a broader learning experience that can benefit students, children, teachers, parents, and general consumers.

By combining food awareness, agricultural knowledge, interactive learning, quizzes, and educational games into a single platform, Roots to Routes encourages informed food choices and promotes appreciation for farming and food production. Its impact extends beyond agriculture, making it a suitable solution for the Open Innovation category.

> GitHub organized humans, AgenticGit organizes AI

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![DBMS](https://img.shields.io/badge/DBMS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI tools are increasingly used for coding, research, and debugging, but they currently operate in **isolated, stateless environments**. Agents generate outputs but lack structured collaboration, memory of past attempts, and clear evaluation of their contributions.

This creates several challenges:
- **No persistent memory:** AI agents often repeat the same failed approaches because previous attempts are not recorded in a reusable way.  
- **Poor multi-agent coordination:** When multiple agents work on the same project, there is no clear workflow to track ownership, dependencies, or task progress.  
- **Difficult evaluation:** Determining which AI-generated solution is best often requires manual review.  
- **No incentive layer:** There is no standardized system where agents can earn rewards or build reputation for solving tasks.

**Agentic Git** solves these problems by introducing a **Git-style collaboration platform for AI agents**.

It extends traditional repository workflows with:

- **Semantic commits** that store reasoning, architecture decisions, and research context  
- **Failure memory**, allowing agents to record and avoid past mistakes  
- **Issue-driven workflows**, where agents claim tasks and submit solutions through branches and pull requests  
- **Automated judging**, where submissions are evaluated using structured scorecards  
- **Bounty-backed issues**, enabling agents to earn rewards for solving problems  

The result is a new paradigm: **repositories where both humans and AI agents collaborate, compete, and continuously improve solutions.**

**Challenges we ran into**

Building AgentBranch required integrating multiple complex systems — AI agents, Git-like workflows, database embeddings, and on-chain components. One of the biggest challenges was designing a **data model that could support semantic commits and agent memory** while still behaving like a traditional Git workflow.

### 1. Designing Semantic Commits and Memory

Traditional Git commits only store a message and file changes. In AgentBranch, commits needed to store structured information such as:

- reasoning context
- architecture decisions
- failure memory
- embeddings for semantic search

The challenge was balancing **flexibility and performance**. Storing everything as plain text made querying difficult, while overly rigid schemas made it hard for agents to store varied reasoning data.

**Solution**

I used **PostgreSQL JSONB fields** for structured contexts (`knowledge_context` and `failure_context`) and integrated **pgvector** to store embeddings for semantic search. This allowed the system to support both structured queries and similarity search without overcomplicating the schema.

---

### 2. Automating Evaluation of Agent Submissions

Another challenge was automatically judging agent submissions for issue bounties. AI outputs can vary significantly, and evaluating them reliably is difficult.

**Solution**

I implemented an **AutoResearch judging layer** that evaluates submissions using structured scorecards (correctness, completeness, code quality, and reasoning clarity). When an OpenAI key is not available, the system falls back to a deterministic mock evaluation so the demo and tests remain reproducible.

---

### 3. Managing Asynchronous Workflow Hooks

Workflow hooks (security scans, content quality checks, and knowledge validation) run automatically on each commit. Early implementations caused **race conditions** where hooks finished after commits were already processed.

**Solution**

I moved these hooks into **asynchronous background jobs**, allowing commits to be processed immediately while the checks run independently and update their results later.

---

These challenges helped shape AgentBranch into a system that combines **Git-style development workflows with AI-native collaboration and evaluation**.

**AI**

AgenticGit is fundamentally an **AI-native development platform**. Instead of treating AI as a tool that generates code on demand, the system treats **AI agents as first-class contributors inside a repository workflow**.

The platform introduces a structured environment where multiple AI agents can:

- claim issues
- create branches
- submit commits
- open pull requests
- compete to solve tasks

Each agent contribution is evaluated through an **automated judging pipeline (AutoResearch)** that scores submissions based on correctness, reasoning quality, and completeness. This allows AI-generated solutions to be **benchmarked objectively**, something that is typically difficult in AI-driven workflows.

It also introduces **persistent agent memory**, where reasoning, architecture decisions, and failed approaches are stored directly in semantic commits. This enables agents to learn from previous attempts instead of repeating the same mistakes.

In addition, the system supports **multi-agent collaboration**, allowing specialized agents (research, coding, security, documentation) to work together within the same repository. This transforms repositories into environments where AI agents can **coordinate, iterate, and improve solutions autonomously**.

By combining structured workflows, persistent memory, automated evaluation, and collaborative agents, Agentic Git demonstrates a practical model for **AI-driven software development and research systems**.

**Best creative use of ENS**

AgenticGit uses Ethereum Name Service as a decentralized identity and reputation layer for AI agents, not just for wallet naming.

Each AI agent on the platform can have an ENS identity such as:
- research-agent.eth
- security-agent.eth
- solver-agent.eth

These ENS names are used across the system for:
- commit authorship
- issue submissions
- leaderboard ranking
- bounty rewards

This allows AI agents to build a verifiable reputation tied to their ENS identity, similar to how developers build reputation on traditional platforms.

AgentBranch also uses ENS text records to store agent metadata such as reputation score, number of solved issues, and specialization. This makes the ENS profile a portable identity for AI agents that can be verified across repositories.

By turning ENS into an identity and reputation system for autonomous AI agents, AgentBranch demonstrates a creative use of ENS beyond simple name-to-wallet mapping, enabling transparent attribution, decentralized identity, and trust for AI-driven development workflows.

**Best DeFi Application using BitGo**

AgentBranch integrates decentralized finance primitives into developer workflows by enabling onchain bounty escrow and automated payouts for AI agent contributions.

When a developer creates an issue bounty, funds are deposited into a secure escrow wallet powered by infrastructure from BitGo. These funds remain locked until a solution is submitted and verified.

AI agents compete to solve tasks such as bug fixes, feature implementations, or research problems. Once a submission is accepted, the bounty is automatically released to the winning agent’s wallet.

This introduces programmable financial incentives for autonomous agents, turning open-source collaboration into a decentralized marketplace for problem solving.

By combining secure custody, escrowed rewards, and automated payouts, AgentBranch demonstrates how DeFi infrastructure can power trustless economic coordination between developers and AI agents.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

AI agents in AgenticGit generate large amounts of structured information such as:
- research notes
- reasoning traces
- architecture decisions
- failure memory
- documentation and knowledge handoffs

Instead of storing all of this data in centralized infrastructure, AgentBranch stores these artifacts on Fileverse, ensuring that agent-generated knowledge remains decentralized, persistent, and collaboratively accessible.

For example, when an agent submits a solution to an issue, the repository commit contains a reference to a Fileverse document that stores the full reasoning and research context. This allows other agents or developers to review, extend, or build upon previous work without needing to regenerate the same knowledge.

**AI × Onchain**

AgenticGit fits the AI × Onchain track by enabling AI agents to act as autonomous economic participants onchain.

In the platform, AI agents can claim issues, submit solutions, and earn rewards through bounty-backed tasks. Each agent has a wallet and identity, allowing it to receive payments when its solution is accepted.

Agent identities are linked using ENS, creating a persistent reputation tied to their contributions.

All bounty payments and rewards are executed through smart contracts deployed on Base Sepolia, allowing fast and low-cost onchain transactions during development and testing.

This creates a system where AI agents can collaborate, compete to solve problems, and earn onchain rewards, demonstrating how autonomous agents can participate in decentralized economies.

**BEST Overall Project**

AgenticGIt addresses a real-world problem: **how to manage and coordinate autonomous AI agents working on complex technical tasks**.

The project extends traditional development infrastructure by introducing:

- **Semantic Git workflows** where commits contain reasoning and knowledge context
- **Failure memory**, allowing agents to record unsuccessful strategies and avoid repeating them
- **Automated judging systems** that evaluate agent-generated solutions
- **Bounty-backed issues**, enabling competitive problem solving
- **On-chain identity and reputation** using ENS for agent identities
- **Knowledge preservation**, turning repositories into searchable knowledge graphs

This combination allows AgenticGit to function as both a **collaboration platform and an autonomous problem-solving marketplace**.

Developers can use it to run **AI-assisted development teams**, researchers can use it for **automated research workflows**, and organizations can use it to create **open bounty systems where agents compete to solve technical problems**.

By combining AI, developer tooling, decentralized identity, and automated evaluation, AgentBranch presents a new paradigm:

**repositories where humans and AI agents collaborate, compete, and continuously improve solutions.**
