> Real-Time Threat Intelligence for Smart Contracts.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Machine Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Machine%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Webhook](https://img.shields.io/badge/Webhook-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Kaizen solves the critical latency gap in smart contract security.
Most security systems are reactive exploits are detected only after transactions are finalized and funds are already lost. Protocol teams lack real-time behavioral visibility to identify coordinated attacks such as flash-loan exploits, oracle manipulation, or liquidity drains before execution.

Kaizen provides real-time threat detection and autonomous mitigation within the same block window. By continuously analyzing on-chain behavioral signals and scoring contract risk using machine learning, it can trigger conditional defensive actions like kill-switch transactions or access enforcement. This shifts security from post-incident monitoring to proactive execution-time defense, reducing financial loss, response time, and operational overhead for on-chain protocols.

**Challenges we ran into**

A key challenge while building Kaizen was maintaining consistent real-time monitoring during periods of high on-chain activity.
The initial pipeline processed block data synchronously fetching logs, deriving behavioral features, sending them for scoring, and then triggering alerts. This worked under normal conditions but became slow and unreliable during stress testing when blocks contained a large number of contract interactions. Sequential RPC calls created noticeable delays in scoring and alert generation.
To fix this, I refactored the system into a simple event-driven pipeline where block events are queued and processed by independent workers in parallel. I also optimized RPC usage by batching and parallelizing requests. This improved responsiveness and made the monitoring flow more stable during activity spikes.

**DeFi**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/12ff92a5140e419ebb2f5a2d2aab6f30/76b06f31-0e8f-47f4-a991-2318869a554f.png)

DeFi protocols operate in a paradox: once deployed, the code that secures user funds is completely static, but the attack surface is not.
Kaizen solves this by treating smart contract security as a continuous runtime problem, not a one-time audit. Every block, we extract behavioral signals from your contract including outflow patterns, caller anomalies, governance spikes, and admin activity, then score them against a protocol-specific baseline and respond autonomously if a threat is confirmed.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**On-chain auctions have no privacy.**

On a public blockchain, every bid is visible to everyone in real time. This creates three critical issues:

**1. Bid manipulation: **later bidders can see existing bids and only outbid by the minimum, suppressing the true price
**2. Identity exposure: ** bidder addresses are public, linking financial activity to real-world identities
**3. Front-running: ** bots and other participants can exploit visible bid data before it's finalized

Traditional sealed-bid auctions (common in government bonds, real estate, spectrum allocation) solve manipulation, but no one had made them work privately on-chain.

Penumbra brings sealed-bid auctions to Ethereum using ZK proofs, bid amounts and bidder identities never appear on-chain, not even after the auction ends. The winner claims tokens by proving knowledge of a secret, not by revealing who they are.

Penumbra solves the transparency problem of on-chain auctions, bids, amounts, and winner identities stay private end-to-end using zero-knowledge proofs.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. ZK proofs on a hackathon timeline**
Generating and verifying ZK proofs server-side, then submitting them from a burner wallet so the winner's real address never touches the claim transaction. Getting the circuit, proof generation, and on-chain verifier to agree took significant iteration.

**2. The off-chain/on-chain split**
The whole point is that bids never appear on-chain, but Ethereum needs something to verify. Designing the nullifier scheme (bidders commit a hash on-chain, the backend knows the preimage, the winner proves knowledge without revealing it) required careful architecture so neither side could cheat.

**3. Stealth address key derivation**
Deriving spending and viewing keypairs deterministically from wallet signatures — without ever sending private keys to a server. The secp256k1 point multiplication needed to generate real uncompressed public keys is not natively available in the browser.

**4. BitGo custody for private ETH deposits**
Each bidder gets a unique deposit address so their ETH can't be correlated on-chain. Integrating BitGo's wallet API to generate these addresses, track confirmations, and route payouts to stealth addresses added a whole backend layer that most Ethereum projects don't need.

**5. Auction phase state machine**
Five phases (commit → settle → ended → claimed / cancelled) each with different UI, different allowed actions, and live on-chain polling. Keeping the frontend consistent across all states without race conditions was genuinely fiddly.

**Privacy**

## Core Thesis
Penumbra is privacy infrastructure for on-chain commerce. Every architectural
decision, from bid commitment to winner claim, is made to eliminate
information leakage at every step of the auction lifecycle.

## End-to-End Privacy Guarantees

### 1. Private Bids (ZK Commitments)

Bidders never post their bid amount on-chain. Instead, they submit a
zero-knowledge commitment, a cryptographic hash that proves they have a valid
bid without revealing what it is. The actual amount only exists off-chain,
encrypted in the backend.

### 2. Anonymous Deposits (Stealth Addresses)
Each bidder receives a unique, one-time ETH deposit address via BitGo custody.
This breaks the on-chain link between a bidder's wallet and their deposit,
chain analysis cannot correlate who bid on what.

### 3. Private Winner Declaration (Nullifiers)
The winner is declared on-chain using only their **nullifier**, a
cryptographic identifier with no link to their wallet address or bid amount.
No one watching the chain can determine who won.

### 4. Private Claims (ZK Proofs)
The winner claims their tokens by generating a ZK proof that they know the
secret behind the winning nullifier. The proof is submitted from a **burner
wallet**, so even the claim transaction reveals nothing about the winner's
real identity.

### 5. Private Seller Payouts (Stealth Addresses)
The seller receives their ETH payout at a **stealth address** derived from
their registered viewing and spending keys, not their public wallet, so the
payment cannot be linked to them on-chain.

## What Makes This Different from Existing Privacy Tools
Most privacy tools (Tornado Cash, Railgun, etc.) are **mixers**, they
anonymize existing transactions after the fact. Penumbra builds privacy
**into the auction primitive itself**. There is no "before" state where
information was ever public.

## Why This Matters Beyond the Hackathon
Sealed-bid auctions are the standard format for:
- Government bond issuances
- Real estate portfolio sales
- Spectrum licensing
- High-value NFT drops

None of these can move on-chain today because public bids destroy price
discovery and expose participants. Penumbra removes that blocker.

**DeFi**

# Why Privacy is a Natural Fit for DeFi
## The Core Problem with Transparent DeFi
DeFi runs on public blockchains, every transaction, every position, every
wallet balance is visible to everyone, forever. This is great for auditability
but catastrophic for financial privacy.
In traditional finance, your brokerage account is not broadcast to the world
in real time. In DeFi, it is.
## How Transparency Actively Harms DeFi Users
### Front-Running & MEV
When a trader submits a large swap, bots see it in the mempool and
insert their own transactions ahead of it, extracting value directly
from the user. This is only possible because everything is public.
### Whale Watching
Large wallets are tracked obsessively. When a known address moves funds,
the market reacts before they finish, making it impossible to execute
large positions without moving the market against yourself.
### Liquidation Hunting
Lending protocols expose every collateral position publicly. Attackers
deliberately manipulate prices to trigger liquidations on specific wallets
they've identified as vulnerable.
### Bid Manipulation in Auctions
In any on-chain auction without privacy, bidders can see all existing bids
and game their strategy accordingly, suppressing true price discovery and
disadvantaging honest participants.
## Privacy is Not Optional for Serious DeFi
For DeFi to serve institutional players, DAOs managing treasuries, or any
user transacting at meaningful scale, **financial privacy is a baseline
requirement**, not a nice-to-have.
Privacy in DeFi means:
- Strategies cannot be front-run
- Positions cannot be targeted
- Identity cannot be linked to on-chain activity
- Market participants compete on information, not surveillance
## Where Penumbra Fits
Penumbra addresses the auction layer of DeFi, one of the most
information-sensitive operations in any financial system. Sealed-bid
auctions are the gold standard for fair price discovery precisely because
no participant can see what others are bidding.
By bringing ZK-based sealed-bid auctions on-chain, Penumbra makes a
class of DeFi activity, token sales, liquidation auctions, DAO asset
disposals, viable for participants who cannot afford to have their
strategies exposed publicly.
**Privacy isn't anti-DeFi. It's what DeFi needs to grow up.**

**Best creative use of ENS**

# How Penumbra Uses ENS
## The Problem with Auction Identities
In a sealed-bid auction, the seller needs to be discoverable and
trustworthy. A raw `0x` address tells bidders nothing. It provides
no reputation, no identity, and no assurance that the seller is
who they claim to be.
Penumbra integrates ENS to solve this.
## ENS as the Seller Identity Layer
When a seller creates an auction, they can attach their **ENS name**
to the listing. This gives bidders:
- A human-readable identity tied to the auction (`vitalik.eth` vs `0x1234...`)
- On-chain reputation linked to a real identity
- Confidence that the seller is accountable
This is especially important in a **private auction** where bid amounts
are hidden and trust in the seller is the only signal bidders have before
committing funds.
## ENS + Privacy = Accountable Anonymity
Penumbra's design creates an intentional balance:
| Party | Privacy Level | Identity |
|---|---|---|
| Bidder | Fully anonymous | No on-chain trace |
| Seller | Publicly accountable | ENS name attached |
The seller is **known via ENS**, providing trust and accountability.
The bidder is **fully private via ZK**, protecting their strategy.
Auctions require sellers to be trustworthy and discoverable.
ENS makes that possible on-chain without centralised identity infrastructure.
## The Bottom Line
ENS transforms Penumbra's auction listings from anonymous contract
addresses into **trusted, human-readable storefronts**, making
private auctions safe enough for real participants to commit real funds.

**Best Privacy Application using BitGo**

# How Penumbra Uses BitGo
## BitGo as the Core Privacy Layer
Penumbra uses BitGo as the **core custody layer** for its ZK sealed-bid
auction protocol, not as an optional add-on, but as a load-bearing
component without which the privacy guarantees collapse entirely.
## Private Deposits via Unique BitGo Addresses
When a bidder places a bid, they receive a **unique BitGo-generated deposit
address** completely isolated from their on-chain wallet identity.
This breaks the correlation between:
- A bidder's Ethereum address
- Their ETH deposit amount
- Their participation in the auction
A naive on-chain deposit would immediately link a bidder's wallet to their
bid amount on the public ledger, destroying privacy. BitGo's programmable
wallet infrastructure is what makes this separation possible.
## Full Money Movement Through BitGo
BitGo handles every step of the financial layer:
| Step | BitGo's Role |
|---|---|
| Bid placement | Generates unique deposit address per bidder |
| Deposit tracking | Detects and confirms incoming ETH |
| Auction settlement | Routes payout to the winning seller |
| Seller privacy | Sends proceeds to a stealth address |
## Why BitGo Makes Penumbra Possible
Without BitGo, Penumbra cannot exist. The entire auction lifecycle, 
from private deposit to anonymous payout, depends on BitGo's
programmable custody infrastructure running in parallel with the
on-chain ZK proof system.
**BitGo handles the money. ZK handles the truth. Neither works without
the other.**

**Best DeFi Application using BitGo**

# How Penumbra Uses BitGo for DeFi
## A New DeFi Primitive, Private Sealed-Bid Auctions
Penumbra is a **ZK-powered sealed-bid auction protocol** built on Ethereum.
It enables token sales, DAO treasury disposals, and asset auctions where
**bid amounts and bidder identities are never revealed on-chain**, a class
of DeFi activity that was previously impossible without privacy infrastructure.
BitGo is the financial backbone that makes this work.
## How BitGo Powers the DeFi Flow
### Private Bid Deposits
Every bidder receives a **unique BitGo wallet address** to deposit their ETH.
This decouples their on-chain identity from their bid, chain analysis cannot
link who bid, how much, or on what auction.
### Trustless Settlement
After the auction closes, BitGo confirms all deposits, and the backend
settles the auction off-chain, determining the highest bid without ever
posting amounts on-chain. The winner is declared using only a ZK nullifier.
### Stealth Payouts to Sellers
The seller receives their ETH payout routed through BitGo **directly to a
stealth address**, so even the final payout cannot be linked to their
public wallet.
## Why This is DeFi Infrastructure
| DeFi Need | Penumbra + BitGo Solution |
|---|---|
| Fair price discovery | Sealed bids prevent sniping and manipulation |
| Participant privacy | BitGo deposit addresses break on-chain correlation |
| Trustless execution | ZK proofs enforce winner validity on-chain |
| Private settlement | Stealth address payouts via BitGo custody |
## The Bottom Line
Penumbra uses BitGo to bring **institutional-grade sealed-bid auctions**
to DeFi, the same auction format used in sovereign debt and spectrum
licensing, now available on Ethereum with full privacy guarantees.

**DeFi 2.0 - New Primitives**

## Why Sealed-Bid Auctions are a Missing Primitive
DeFi today has:
- Public AMM swaps
- Public order books
- Public liquidation auctions
- Public token launches
Every single one of these leaks information. Bids, strategies, and
positions are visible to everyone in real time, enabling front-running,
MEV extraction, and market manipulation.
The sealed-bid auction, the gold standard for fair price discovery in
traditional finance, has never existed on-chain. Until now.
## What Penumbra Adds to the DeFi Stack
Penumbra is a composable auction primitive that any protocol can use for:
- **Token launches** where early bid visibility would allow manipulation
- **DAO treasury sales** where whale strategies must stay private
- **Liquidation auctions** where front-running destroys fairness
- **NFT drops** where bid sniping undermines true price discovery
- **On-chain M&A** where deal terms cannot be public before closing
## The Technical Stack that Makes it New
| Layer | Technology |
|---|---|
| Bid privacy | ZK commitments, amounts never on-chain |
| Deposit privacy | BitGo custody, wallets unlinked |
| Winner privacy | Nullifier-based declaration |
| Claim privacy | ZK proof via burner wallet |
| Payout privacy | Stealth addresses |
## The Bottom Line
Penumbra is not a DeFi app built on existing primitives.
It is a new primitive that makes an entirely new category of
on-chain financial activity possible, one that traditional
finance has relied on for decades and DeFi has never had.

**Privacy**

# Why Penumbra Fits the Base Privacy Track
## Privacy as a First-Class Citizen on Base
Penumbra is a **ZK-powered sealed-bid auction protocol** that delivers
end-to-end privacy for on-chain commerce. Every layer of the system is
designed to eliminate information leakage, making it a natural fit for
Base's privacy track.
## What Penumbra Protects
### Bidder Privacy
Bid amounts are never posted on-chain. Bidders commit a ZK hash, send
ETH to a unique deposit address, and are identified only by a nullifier.
No one watching the chain can determine who bid or how much.
### Winner Privacy
The winner is declared using only their **ZK nullifier**, not their wallet
address. They claim tokens by generating a ZK proof server-side, submitted
from a burner wallet. Their real address is never revealed.
### Seller Privacy
Auction proceeds are routed to a **stealth address** derived from the
seller's registered keys, so even the final payout cannot be linked to
their public wallet.
## Privacy at Every Step
| Auction Step | Privacy Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Bid submission | ZK commitment, amount never on-chain |
| ETH deposit | Unique custody address, wallet unlinked |
| Winner declaration | Nullifier only, no address revealed |
| Token claim | Burner wallet + ZK proof |
| Seller payout | Stealth address |
## The Bottom Line
Penumbra does not add privacy as a feature on top of an existing protocol.
Privacy is the protocol. Every architectural decision exists to ensure that
participants in an auction reveal nothing they do not choose to reveal.

Individuals and businesses often subscribe to storage plans from providers such as **Dropbox**, but only use a fraction of their allocated capacity. The remaining storage sits idle, effectively wasting a digital resource that has already been paid for.*

At the same time, many users, startups, and small teams require **affordable and flexible storage solutions**, yet they are forced into fixed subscription models offered by centralized providers. These services often come with rigid pricing structures, limited customization, and no way for users to monetize unused storage capacity.

This creates two major inefficiencies:

- **Underutilized Resources** – Large amounts of paid cloud storage remain unused.
- **Centralized Control** – Storage markets are dominated by centralized platforms with limited transparency and user ownership.

## How Rentabyte Solves This

**Rentabyte** introduces a decentralized storage rental marketplace that transforms unused cloud storage into a valuable, tradable resource.

With Rentabyte:

- Users can **contribute their unused cloud storage** and earn income from it.
- Buyers can **rent storage on demand** without committing to expensive subscription plans.
- All transactions are secured through **smart contracts** on the polygon network.

By enabling peer-to-peer storage sharing, Rentabyte:

- Improves **global storage utilization**
- Reduces **storage costs for users**
- Introduces **transparency and trust through blockchain**
- Creates a **decentralized marketplace for cloud storage**

In short, **Rentabyte turns idle cloud storage into an economic opportunity while making storage more accessible and decentralized.**

### 1. Invisible Transaction Feedback
When users paid POL for storage, **no visual feedback appeared**.  
The issue was caused by toast notifications using a .alert class that had display: none.

### 2. Raw Blockchain Errors Shown to Users
Errors from MetaMask and ethers.js v6 (e.g., RPC error codes) were displayed directly to users.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

**The $0.90 problem that almost broke everything.** Our first implementation used simple yield calculation: $1,000 at 6% for 6 months equals $30 of yield, so send $970 to Morpho and $30 to the position. But $970 earning 6% for 6 months returns $999.10, not $1,000. That $0.90 gap seems tiny until you scale it. On a $10 million deposit that is $9,000 missing. You cannot call something "principal protected" when thousands of dollars are unaccounted for. We spent hours debugging this before realizing TradFi solves it with the zero coupon present value formula: PV = FV / (1 + r)^t. This gives the EXACT amount that grows to EXACTLY the deposit. No approximation. No gap. Once we switched to this formula, the math became airtight at any deposit size, which our 12.5 million simulation backtest confirmed with 100.0000% principal protection.

**Real estate liquidation scanning was way harder than crypto.** For crypto assets, checking if a position got liquidated during a holding period is straightforward because you have hourly or minute level price data. Real estate indexes from Parcl Labs update once per day. A position could appear safe at the daily close but might have breached the liquidation level intraday if we had finer data. We solved this conservatively by checking every daily data point during the entire holding period, not just the entry and exit price. This means our backtest slightly overestimates liquidation rates for real estate (because a daily close below liquidation triggers a liq even if the intraday low was only briefly there), but it ensures our principal protection claim is honest and defensible.

**Yield rates kept changing on us.** We initially hardcoded yield rates at 5 to 6% based on what Morpho historically paid. Midway through building, we pulled live rates from DeFiLlama and discovered current rates were 2.46 to 3.63%. This completely changed the product economics. Exposure budgets shrank, returns got more modest, and strategies that worked at 6% didn't work at 2.5%. We had to rebuild our backtest engine to pull live APYs from DeFiLlama's API on every run and recalculate everything. The silver lining is this forced us to find strategies that work at TODAY's rates, not theoretical ones, making our backtest results genuinely honest.

**Making 5 sponsor SDKs work together in one flow was a nightmare.** The WhatsApp shield activation touches Twilio for messaging, OpenAI for intent parsing, HeyElsa x402 for wallet analysis (paying real micropayments on Base mainnet), BitGo SDK for custodial wallet creation on Base testnet, our smart contracts on Base Sepolia for the actual deposit, ENS NameWrapper on Ethereum Sepolia for subname registration, and Fileverse agents on Sepolia with Pinata storage for encrypted document creation. That is 7 different services across 3 different chains in a single user flow triggered by a WhatsApp message. Getting the async orchestration right, handling failures gracefully at each step, and making sure the user gets a clean confirmation message even when one service is slow took more debugging than building the actual PPN math.

**CoinGecko rate limits during backtest runs.** Running 12.5 million simulations requires fetching historical price data for multiple assets. CoinGecko Pro has a 500 calls per minute limit. Our first backtest run hit the limit, got throttled, and returned incomplete data that silently corrupted thousands of simulations. We solved this by building a local cache layer that fetches historical data once, saves it to disk, and reuses it across all subsequent runs. This also made iteration dramatically faster since we could rerun the full backtest in minutes instead of waiting for API calls.

**Privacy**

## Why PPN.fi is the Best Privacy Project

**Your financial strategy is the most sensitive data you own, and every existing platform exposes it.** When you open a leveraged position on Aave or trade on GMX, your wallet address, position size, asset choice, leverage level, entry price, and liquidation threshold are all publicly visible on chain. Anyone with a block explorer can see exactly what you are betting on, how much, and where you get liquidated. MEV bots front run your trades. Competitors copy your strategy. Your entire financial life is a public broadcast.

**PPN.fi is the first DeFi derivatives protocol where your position details are end to end encrypted by default.** Every shield and perp position created on PPN.fi generates an encrypted document via **@fileverse/agents** stored on **IPFS through Pinata**, with on chain anchoring on Sepolia. The Fileverse Agent uses a **Pimlico** powered smart account with the user's viem account as signer, meaning only the position owner can decrypt and read their shield details: deposit amount, asset, leverage, entry price, duration, projected returns, ENS subname. Not us. Not other users. Not block explorers. Nobody.

**BitGo adds the second privacy layer at the custody level.** Users who interact through our WhatsApp flow never expose a personal wallet address at all. **BitGo custodial wallets** created via `@bitgo/sdk-api` on Base testnet (tbaseeth) mean the user's identity is completely separated from their on chain activity. There is no public wallet to trace back to a phone number. The BitGo enterprise manages key shards through MPC, so no single party, not even us, holds a complete private key. The user's financial positions exist behind two layers of privacy: BitGo MPC custody for identity separation and Fileverse encryption for position data.

**ENS subnames provide pseudonymous financial identity without exposing real wallets.** Each position gets a subname like `gold-71af.hml.eth` registered on chain via our custom NameWrapper integration on Sepolia. The leaderboard shows ENS names, not hex addresses. Users build financial reputation under a pseudonym without ever linking to their real identity or primary wallet.

**The WhatsApp channel itself is a privacy feature.** Traditional DeFi requires connecting a browser wallet to a frontend, creating an on chain trail from IP address to wallet to every transaction. Our Twilio powered WhatsApp flow means users interact through an encrypted messaging channel, never visit a website, never connect a wallet publicly, and never leave a browser fingerprint. Their instructions go through OpenAI for intent parsing with no PII stored, and execution happens through BitGo custodial wallets that are not linkable to their personal address.

**Four privacy layers working together:** Fileverse encrypted position documents on IPFS so nobody can read your strategy. BitGo MPC custodial wallets so nobody can link your identity to your positions. ENS pseudonymous subnames so you can have reputation without exposure. WhatsApp as the interface so you never connect a wallet to a public frontend.

> **Every other DeFi protocol treats privacy as an afterthought or a compliance checkbox. PPN.fi treats it as architecture. Your positions are encrypted. Your identity is custodied. Your reputation is pseudonymous. Your interface is a private chat. That is what financial privacy looks like when you build it from the ground up instead of bolting it on.**

**Best creative use of ENS**

## Why PPN.fi Wins "Best Creative Use of ENS"

**We turned ENS from a name for your wallet into a name for your financial strategy.**

Every ENS integration in DeFi does the same thing: resolve alice.eth to 0x742d... and display it in a navbar. That is address mapping. We went further. On PPN.fi, **every principal protected note gets its own ENS subname** that encodes the financial position itself, creating a human readable on chain identity layer for structured financial products.

When a user activates a Gold shield with 5x leverage for 365 days, our `server/services/sponsorService.js` calls the **NameWrapper contract** on Sepolia using `setSubnodeRecord` with ethers v6 to register `gold-71af.hml.eth` under our parent domain `hml.eth` (resolver `0x8FADE66B79cC9f707aB26799354482EB93a5B7dD`). That subname is not just a label. It IS the position's on chain identity. The leaderboard doesn't show 0x addresses. It shows `gold-71af.hml.eth` versus `miami-b3c2.hml.eth` versus `sol-9d4e.hml.eth`. Users build financial reputation under ENS subnames without ever exposing their real wallet.

**Here is where it gets creative.** The subname encodes the asset class directly in the name. When you see `charlotte-5f2a.hml.eth` on the leaderboard, you know that user has a Charlotte real estate position without querying any contract. The naming convention becomes a **human readable financial position identifier** across 25 real world asset markets. Gold shields, Miami real estate perps, Solana leveraged positions, all identified by ENS subnames that tell you what the position is, not just who owns it.

**The subnames also enable composability that raw addresses cannot.** Any protocol on Base can resolve `gold-71af.hml.eth` and know this is a PPN.fi gold shield position. Future integrations could store position metadata (leverage, duration, entry price) in ENS text records, making the subname a fully self describing financial instrument that any on chain application can read and compose with. A DAO treasury could hold `us-national-dao1.hml.eth` as a principal protected position identified by its ENS name, not a contract address nobody can parse.

**This is not name to address mapping. This is ENS as a financial identity and position discovery layer for structured products.** Every position is named. Every name encodes meaning. Every leaderboard entry is human readable. That is a creative use of ENS that no other project has attempted.

**Pool prize**

```

## Why PPN.fi is Eligible for the ENS Pool Prize

**ENS is deeply integrated into PPN.fi across every user facing surface, not as a cosmetic feature but as core infrastructure for identity and position management.**

Our integration uses **no ENS npm packages**. We built a custom implementation directly against the **NameWrapper contract** on Sepolia using ethers v6 with `ethers.namehash`, `ethers.JsonRpcProvider`, and a custom ABI containing `setSubnodeRecord` and `setSubnodeOwner`. The parent domain `hml.eth` is registered on Sepolia with a dedicated registrar wallet (`ENS_REGISTRAR_PRIVATE_KEY`) that programmatically creates subnames for every shield and perp position opened on the platform.

**Where ENS appears in PPN.fi:**

Every shield activation triggers real on chain subname registration. The portfolio page displays ENS subnames on every position card instead of position IDs. The leaderboard ranks traders by their ENS subnames, creating pseudonymous competition (`gold-71af.hml.eth` at +17.8% versus `miami-b3c2.hml.eth` at +6.3%). The WhatsApp flow includes the ENS subname in confirmation messages so users see their position identity even on mobile. The shield success screen prominently displays the registered subname as proof of on chain identity.

**The integration is real and verifiable.** When `ENS_SEPOLIA_RPC`, `ENS_REGISTRAR_PRIVATE_KEY`, and `ENS_REGISTRAR_ADDRESS` are configured, every subname registration is an actual on chain transaction on Sepolia that anyone can verify through the ENS app at sepolia.app.ens.domains. We register subnames programmatically through smart contract calls, not through a frontend UI, demonstrating that ENS can serve as infrastructure for automated financial product identity at scale.
```

**Best DeFi Application using BitGo**

## Why PPN.fi Wins "Best DeFi Application using BitGo"

**PPN.fi doesn't just use BitGo as a wallet. BitGo is the infrastructure layer that makes a $7 trillion TradFi product accessible to people who have never touched a crypto wallet.**

We integrate BitGo's SDK at two distinct levels through `@bitgo/sdk-api` and `@bitgo/sdk-coin-eth`, each solving a different problem that traditional DeFi applications ignore.

**Level 1: Institutional Audit and Identity.** Our `server/services/bitgoService.js` initializes `BitGoAPI` with enterprise credentials, calls `bitgo.me()` to verify the authenticated entity, and maintains an in memory audit log via `logTx()` for every vault operation. Every P&L settlement, every LP withdrawal, every shield activation that flows through the relayer wallet is logged against the BitGo enterprise identity. This is the same audit infrastructure that institutional funds require before allocating capital to DeFi. When an LP asks "who controls the vault relayer and can I verify every transaction it signed," the answer is BitGo's enterprise audit trail, not a private key in a .env file.

**Level 2: Custodial Wallets for the Unbanked.** This is where BitGo transforms the product. Our `server/services/bitgoCustodyService.js` uses `BitGoAPI` with `registerEthCoins` from `@bitgo/sdk-coin-eth` to programmatically create MPC wallets on Base testnet (tbaseeth via `BITGO_CUSTODY_COIN`). When a user in Mumbai texts our WhatsApp number "I want to protect 50,000 rupees on gold," they don't have MetaMask. They don't have a seed phrase. They have WhatsApp. Our agent calls BitGo's SDK to generate a wallet using `coin.wallets().generateWallet()` with enterprise passphrase, or falls back to BitGo Express REST at `/api/v2/{coin}/wallet/generate` when the SDK coin module isn't available for Base. The wallet is created, funded, and managed entirely through BitGo's MPC infrastructure. No single party holds a complete key. The user's funds are secured by institutional grade multi party computation from the moment they deposit.

**The DeFi composability layer:** These BitGo custodial wallets don't just hold funds. They interact with our entire DeFi stack on Base Sepolia. The wallet deposits H-USDC into the HedgeVault smart contract. The shield engine splits the deposit using zero coupon bond math and opens a leveraged position on gold, real estate, or crypto. The vault routes yield through Morpho and Aave. At settlement, P&L flows back to the BitGo wallet. The user receives a WhatsApp message: "Your gold shield matured. $10,000 deposited, $10,847 returned. Funds in your wallet." All of this happened through BitGo's programmatic transaction building and signing, with enterprise policy controls governing every step.

**Why this matters for the BitGo track specifically:** The prize description asks for multi sig or MPC wallets, programmatic transaction building and signing, policy rules, and DeFi protocol connectivity. We use MPC wallets via BitGo's enterprise SDK for every WhatsApp user. We build and sign transactions programmatically through BitGo Express at `/api/v2/{coin}/wallet/{id}/sendmany` for vault deposits and withdrawals. Enterprise passphrase and wallet policies govern spending limits on the custodial wallets. And the wallets connect directly to our DeFi protocol (HedgeVault, Morpho yield routing, perp engine) on Base. This is not a demo integration. This is BitGo as the custody backbone of a production DeFi application that serves users who could never use DeFi without it.

**What we actually built on Base Sepolia:**

A perpetual derivatives engine with **25 real world asset markets** including gold, silver, crude oil, natural gas, Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and **19 US real estate city indexes** (NYC, Miami, Charlotte, Tampa, Nashville, Las Vegas, San Diego, LA, Chicago, Brooklyn, Atlanta, Boston, Denver, Pittsburgh, San Francisco, Austin, Washington DC, Miami Beach, and a US National composite). That alone qualifies as an RWA perpetual primitive for Base.

**But the new primitive is what sits on top of the perp engine.**

We implemented the **exact zero coupon present value formula** that banks use to construct Principal Protected Notes: `PV = FV / (1 + r)^t`. When a user deposits $10,000 with a 365 day duration at 3.63% Morpho APY, the protocol calculates the precise present value ($9,649.72), routes that to the yield vault, and uses the exact remainder ($350.28) as margin for a leveraged position on the user's chosen real world asset. The yield portion grows to exactly $10,000 at maturity. The exposure portion trades with leverage. **The user's principal is mathematically guaranteed to return in full regardless of what happens to the leveraged position.** This is not an approximation. This is not a promise. This is the same bond math that Goldman Sachs uses, implemented as a composable DeFi primitive on Base.

**We proved it works with the largest backtest in hackathon history.**

12,523,401 individual simulations across 25 assets, 3 real yield protocols (Aave V3 2.46%, Morpho 3.63%, Moonwell 3.43% from live DeFiLlama data), 11 leverage levels, 7 duration windows, and every possible entry date in the historical dataset. **Principal protection held in 100.0000% of simulations. Zero failures.** Charlotte real estate at 10x leverage had zero liquidations across 1,462 simulations. Solana at 1x delivered 44.6% annualized returns with zero liquidation risk. Gold at 5x returned 5.8% annualized with under 10% liquidation. These are not projections. These are results from real price data.

**Why this is a genuinely new DeFi primitive and not just a product:**

Principal Protected Notes in TradFi require a bond desk, an options desk, a custody bank, a legal team, KYC infrastructure, and a minimum of $100,000. The entire pipeline is closed, permissioned, and extractive (2 to 5% hidden fees). We collapsed all of that into a composable on chain primitive where the "bond" is a Morpho deposit, the "option" is a leveraged perp position, the "custody" is a smart contract, and the "minimum" is $100. Any protocol on Base can integrate this primitive. Any vault can offer principal protected yield. Any frontend can plug into our engine. **This is not a product. It is infrastructure.**

**And DeFi yield makes it fundamentally better than the TradFi version.** Banks build PPNs on 4% Treasury yields. We build on 3.63% Morpho yield today, with the architecture supporting any yield source. When yield bearing stablecoins, restaking yields, or points farming vaults push rates to 8 to 15%, the exposure budget doubles or triples, making the same structure dramatically more profitable. **DeFi doesn't just replicate this TradFi primitive. DeFi makes it structurally superior because DeFi yield is higher, composable, and permissionless.**

The LP vault that backs all positions follows the GMX/GLP counterparty model with epoch based withdrawals to prevent sandwich attacks, creating a **yield bearing stablecoin native financial product** where LPs earn base Morpho yield plus trading fees plus profit from liquidated positions across 25 diversified real world asset markets.

> **The prize track asks for RWA perpetuals and new DeFi primitives. We built both. 25 real world asset perp markets on Base including US real estate city indexes that don't exist on any other chain. And on top of that, the first ever on chain implementation of Principal Protected Notes, the $7 trillion TradFi instrument that no protocol has ever brought to DeFi. > Less Weighing Collaborative Malware Analysis Env.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Analyzing a virus or "malware" is usually a slow, dangerous, and complicated process. Zeus-Cont makes
  it fast, safe, and easy for everyone.

  1. It creates a "Digital Cage" for Viruses
   * The Problem: You can’t just open a suspicious file on your laptop to see what it does—it could steal
     your data or break your computer.
   * Our Solution: We provide a safe, isolated container (a "sandbox"). You can run the virus inside this
     cage, and it can’t escape to hurt your actual computer or the internet.

  2. It Translates "Matrix Code" into Plain English
   * The Problem: Malware generates thousands of lines of confusing technical logs. It takes a human
     hours to read through them all.
   * Our Solution: We use Gemini AI to read all that "boring" data for you. In seconds, it writes a
     simple report explaining exactly what the virus was trying to do.

  3. It’s a "GPS" for Security Training
   * The Problem: Most hacking tools are very intimidating and hard to learn.
   * Our Solution: We integrated a Voice Assistant (using Sarvam AI). It actually talks to you and guides
     you through the app, making advanced security research as easy as following a GPS.

  4. No More Working Alone
   * The Problem: Usually, security experts work in silos. If they find something, they have to take
     screenshots and send emails.
   * Our Solution: Our platform is collaborative. Multiple people can jump into the same session to hunt
     a threat together in real-time, just like a shared Google Doc.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Container Orchestration: Making the backend "talk" to Docker to create and destroy isolated sandboxes on demand.
2. Network Isolation: Building a "fake internet" so malware stays trapped but still tries to execute its code.
3. Real-Time Streaming: Pushing file, network, and process events to the browser instantly without any lag.
4. Noise Reduction: Automatically hiding normal system processes so the analyst only sees the malicious activity.
5. AI Data Management: Condensing thousands of raw log lines so Gemini can generate a smart, human-readable report.
6. Forensic Tooling: Packaging heavy-duty security tools (like Radare2 and Volatility) into a lightweight, fast-loading image.

**Gemini**

The Gemini API is the project's "Intelligence Layer." While the sandbox and C agent collect raw data, Gemini acts as the Senior Malware Researcher who interprets that data.

  Its involvement is broken down into three key roles:

  1. Automated Forensic Synthesis
  The most significant involvement is in the Report Generation Engine. When an analyst finishes a session, the backend sends a massive volume of telemetry logs (Process trees, File changes, Network packets) to
  Gemini. 
   * The Task: Gemini parses thousands of lines of raw logs into a structured, professional ANY.RUN-style Malware Analysis Report.
   * The Value: It saves analysts hours of manual work by identifying the "needle in the haystack"—such as distinguishing a normal system file edit from a malicious persistence attempt.

  2. Contextual Intelligence & IOC Extraction
  Gemini is used to identify and categorize Indicators of Compromise (IOCs). It scans the telemetry to extract:
   * Malicious Hashes: Identifying suspicious files dropped during execution.
   * C2 Infrastructure: Spotting Command & Control domains or IP addresses hidden in network traffic.
   * Threat Scoring: Based on the activity patterns, Gemini calculates a "Threat Score" (0-100), helping the analyst prioritize the risk level of the sample.

  3. MITRE ATT&CK Reasoning
  While the system can detect what happened, Gemini explains why it matters. It analyzes the sequences of events to confirm MITRE techniques. For example, if it sees a process modifying ~/.bashrc, Gemini maps
  this to T1546.004 (Persistence via Unix Shell Configuration), providing the technical rationale for why that specific action is a security risk.

  Technical Implementation Details:
   * Models Used: Optimized for gemini-2.0-flash for high-speed analysis and long context windows (to handle large log files).
   * Prompt Engineering: Uses a high-precision system prompt with explicit rules to ensure reports are professional, monochromatic, and free of AI "hallucinations."
   * Determinism: Set to a very low temperature (0.1) to ensure that the same malware activity always results in the same technical conclusion.

**Sarvam.ai**

The Sarvam API serves as the "Voice of Zeus," providing the narrative layer for the platform's onboarding and tactical guidance. While the Gemini API handles the "brain" (logic and reporting), Sarvam provides
  the "voice" (audio and communication).

  Its specific involvement includes:

  1. Indic-Specific Tactical Assistance
  The project uses Sarvam’s Text-to-Speech (TTS) capabilities (specifically the bulbul:v3 model) to provide a localized, natural-sounding audio guide. 
   * The Persona: It powers the "Zeus Tactical Assistant," which speaks to the analyst in high-fidelity Indian dialects/accents.
   * The Goal: This makes the platform more accessible and provides a modern "Mission Control" feel, where the system talks to you while you perform high-stakes analysis.

  2. Interactive Guided Onboarding (Walkthrough)
  The Walkthrough Application is entirely driven by Sarvam. As the user moves through the platform's different zones (Terminal, Telemetry, Intel Column), Sarvam generates real-time audio instructions:
   * It explains complex cybersecurity concepts (like MITRE mapping) through spoken word.
   * It reduces the cognitive load on the analyst, allowing them to keep their eyes on the telemetry feeds while receiving audio cues about the environment.

  3. Real-Time Instruction Proxy
  Technically, the project implements a FastAPI Proxy for Sarvam to ensure security and performance:
   * Security: The API keys are kept on the server side, preventing exposure in the frontend.
   * Speed: It uses Sarvam's low-latency endpoints to ensure that when an analyst clicks "Next" in the walkthrough, the audio response is nearly instantaneous.
   * Hybrid Fallback: The system is designed to check for Sarvam’s availability and fallback to standard Web Speech APIs if the network is disconnected, ensuring the "Assistant" never goes silent.

**CyberSecurity**

Zeus-Cont is a modular Dynamic Malware Analysis Sandbox designed for high-performance threat research. It maps directly to several critical cybersecurity operations:

   1. Isolated Threat Detonation (Sandboxing): The core of the project is the secure execution of suspicious binaries. By using Docker-based isolation and a custom "Fake Internet" gateway, analysts can observe
      malware behavior in a 100% contained environment, preventing any risk to the host system or external networks.
   2. Advanced Behavioral Telemetry: Unlike static analysis, Zeus-Cont captures real-time system behavior. This includes:
       * Process Tree Visualization: Identifying process hollowing, spawning chains, and stealthy execution patterns.
       * Network Forensics: Monitoring DNS queries and C2 (Command & Control) callbacks to identify malicious infrastructure.
       * File System Auditing: Detecting unauthorized modifications to sensitive system configurations.
   3. Framework Alignment (MITRE ATT&CK): The project integrates a real-time mapping system that translates technical telemetry into standardized tactics (e.g., Discovery, Persistence, Exfiltration). This aligns
      analysis with global industry standards used by SOC (Security Operations Center) teams.
   4. Collaborative Incident Response: By supporting multi-user shared sessions and synchronized terminals, the project facilitates collaborative threat hunting. This mirrors modern "War Room" scenarios where
      multiple researchers must coordinate to dissect a high-priority threat.
   5. AI-Augmented Forensics: Through Gemini AI integration, the platform automates the generation of structured forensic reports. This solves the "Documentation Gap" in cybersecurity, allowing analysts to move
      from detection to mitigation significantly faster.

> Passwordless, seedless, phishing-proof wallet

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![RPC Solana API](https://img.shields.io/badge/RPC%20Solana%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solana Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solana%20Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![solana/web3.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/solana/web3.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![SolanaSDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/SolanaSDK-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem It Solves**
Imagine you want to send $5 to a friend using crypto.
First, you're told to write down 12 random words and store them somewhere safe forever. Then you're told you need to buy a separate token just to pay for the transaction. Then the app crashes.
Your friend never got the $5. You never came back.
**This is the reality for every new user entering Web3 today. **The technology is powerful, but the experience is broken. Wallets feel like they were built for engineers, not people.

**Lazorkit flips this.**
You open the app. You use Face ID. You're in — with a real Solana wallet, no seed phrase, no gas fees, no confusion.
Sending crypto feels like sending a Venmo payment. Your balance is right there. You pick a token, enter an amount, hit send. Done. The fee? We cover it.

This is what Lazorkit is built for **making blockchain invisible, so the experience is all that's left.**
Developers get a production-ready starting point. Users get something they'll actually use twice.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Gasless Transactions Were Lying to Us**
SOL transfers worked. USDC didn't. Same code, different token — no useful error. After hours of logging raw transaction bytes, we found the paymaster expected a specific account ordering in the instruction that our ATA derivation wasn't producing. One reordering. Fixed.

**The Wallet Would Forget Who You Were**
Refresh the page and the app would sometimes boot you back to login — not because you were logged out, but because AuthGuard was checking connection state before the SDK finished rehydrating the session. Classic race condition. Fixed by adding an isReconnecting flag that makes the guard wait before making any routing decision.

**Devnet RPC Has Trust Issues**
getBalance succeeds. getSignaturesForAddress times out. On the same connection. We stopped trusting RPC to be consistent and added retry logic with exponential backoff — plus decoupled balance and history fetching so one failure doesn't nuke the whole dashboard.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

## 1. ENS Privacy Leak (Critical)
**The Problem:**  
Early in development, our mentors pointed out a major flaw: resolving `bob.phoneno.eth` returned his main wallet address directly. This meant anyone could view his entire transaction history on Etherscan. **We were doxxing users by design.**

**The Solution:**  
We built a **Privacy Forwarding Contract**.
- Users deploy a lightweight forwarder contract.
- ENS records point to the *contract address*, not the main wallet.
- Funds received auto-sweep to the main wallet internally.
- **Result:** Public sees only the contract. Main wallet stays hidden.

---

## 2. x402 Payment Interception
**The Problem:**  
Integrating HeyElsa's x402 API wasn't just a normal HTTP request. Every call returned `HTTP 402 Payment Required`. Our initial code crashed because it didn't know how to sign and attach the USDC payment proof automatically.

**The Solution:**  
We wrote a custom **axios interceptor** using `viem`:
- Detects 402 responses.
- Parses payment requirements (amount, recipient).
- Signs payment locally with user's wallet.
- Retries request with `X-Payment-Token` header.
- **Result:** Seamless micropayments ($0.001 per data call) without user friction.

---

## 3. Network Mismatch Errors
**The Problem:**  
During testing, transactions failed with:  
`Error: network changed: 1 => 11155111`  
The wallet was on Mainnet, but our agent tried to execute on Sepolia/Base. Ethers.js refused to sign across mismatched networks.

**The Solution:**  
Added a **network validation hook** before execution:
- Checks current wallet chain ID.
- Prompts user to switch networks if mismatched.
- Forces provider alignment before signing.
- **Result:** Reliable execution across multiple chains.

---

## 4. AI Agent Decision Making
**The Problem:**  
Our first version used hard-coded rules for route selection. It wasn't actually using OpenClaw/AI. We risked missing the HeyElsa bounty criteria.

**The Solution:**  
Refactored the orchestrator to call `agent.execute()`:
- Sends route options to OpenClaw.
- AI analyzes gas, speed, and security.
- Returns structured recommendation with reasoning.
- **Result:** Genuine AI-powered routing, not just scripted logic.

## How We Use x402 (Micropayments)

### Every AI Data Call Pays via x402

| Data Call | Endpoint | Cost | Payment Method |
|-----------|----------|------|----------------|
| Chainlink Price | `/api/get_token_price` | $0.002 | x402 USDC on Base |
| Pyth Price | `/api/get_token_price` | $0.002 | x402 USDC on Base |
| Gas Prices | `/api/get_gas_prices` | $0.001 | x402 USDC on Base |

**Total per transaction: ~$0.015 USDC**

## How We Use OpenClaw Skills 

## OpenClaw Agent Flow:

1. **User initiates payment**  
   → `"Send $20 to +91-98765-43210.phoneno.eth"`

2. **OpenClaw agent activates**  
   → Connects to gateway: `ws://127.0.0.1:18789/gateway`

3. **Agent calls tools (with x402 payments)**  
   → `resolve_ens`: Get recipient preferences  
   → `get_token_price`: Fetch 3 price feeds (x402)  
   → `get_swap_quote`: Compare routes (x402)  
   → `analyze_wallet`: Security check (x402)

4. **Agent makes decision**  
   → **Route**: Arbitrum → Base via USDC  
   → **Confidence**: 87%  
   → **Reasoning**: Lowest gas + fastest settlement

5. **User confirms → Agent executes**  
   → `execute_transfer` (optional tool, requires allowlist)

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![SHA-256 Hashes](https://img.shields.io/badge/SHA--256%20Hashes-333333?style=flat-square) ![Keccak256](https://img.shields.io/badge/Keccak256-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![EIP-4788](https://img.shields.io/badge/EIP--4788-333333?style=flat-square) ![SSZ](https://img.shields.io/badge/SSZ-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most cross-chain applications still rely on relayers, bridges, or oracle networks to tell one chain what happened on another. **Anyware** removes that trust assumption.

Using [**EIP-4788**](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788) beacon roots, it allows EVM networks to verify recent Ethereum state directly onchain through cryptographic proofs instead of externally signed messages.

**The demo use case is exploring trustless lending:**
1. a user locks ETH on Ethereum Sepolia
2. a proof of that vault state is generated
3. Base Sepolia verifies the proof onchain
4. demo USDC is issued without trusting a bridge or relayer

**The same primitive can power:**
cross-chain lending | governance verification | proof-of-reserves | attestations | generalized Ethereum state reads

**Challenges we ran into**

A major hurdle was proving that an execution payload header truly belonged to a beacon block trusted through [**EIP-4788**](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788), while also resolving the correct destination-chain beacon-root timestamp window.

**We solved this by building a prover pipeline that:**
1. scans beacon blocks
2. matches execution payloads
3. constructs SSZ inclusion proofs
4. resolves the correct EIP-4788 anchor timestamp for onchain verification

**Ethereum Core**

Anyware builds directly on top of Ethereum consensus infrastructure using [**EIP-4788**](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788).

We demonstrate via PoC how Ethereum beacon roots can become a native trust anchor for cross-chain verification without relying on bridges, relayers, or oracle committees.

**It combines:** EIP-4788 beacon roots | SSZ verification | execution state proofs | Ethereum Merkle-Patricia Trie verification; into a working trust-minimized interoperability primitive.

**Anyware improves:** security by reducing external trust assumptions, transparency through fully onchain verification, and interoperability across EVM networks.

**Network Economy**

Anyware enables trustless cross-chain economic interactions without relying on bridges, relayers, or oracle networks.
Using [**EIP-4788**](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4788), the project allows EVM networks to verify Ethereum state directly through cryptographic proofs anchored to Ethereum consensus.

**The demo shows this through cross-chain lending:**
1. a user locks ETH on Ethereum
2. another chain verifies that state onchain
3. credit is issued without trusting an intermediary


**Our library enabled developers to explore use-cases like:**
- cross-chain lending
- proof-of-reserves
- governance verification
- attestations and reputation
- shared liquidity systems

The project puts user control and protocol-level verification first by replacing externally trusted middleware with direct onchain proof verification.

### PoisonGuard
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/poisonguard-c32b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Altaria-hackathon-teams/cybersecurity-three-engineers) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/shorts/-wVVMq83cjA?feature=share) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Altaria-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://altaria.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-8-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> cybersecurity+AI

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Several Companies are integrating their websites with chatbots, that are built on a RAG pipeline. RAG pipelines often use external documents to produce resources for the chatbot to supply the user answers. When a user asks a chatbot for an image, the chatbot tests the metadata against the user's request to give an output. Attackers can take advantage of this and edit the metadata using misaligned information, hence providing the user with a variation of the request. Our PoisonGuard aims to solve this very problem by comparing the metadata of the image to the description of the image produced by an LLM. If there's an anomaly the answer is withheld from the user thereby preventing the user from getting misinformation.

**Challenges we ran into**

We got inspiration for our idea, from a research paper published in the month of February, 2026. Considering the novelty of the paper we ran into trouble finding trustworthy dataset as well as getting a clear idea of the workflow.

**Cybersecurity + Artificial Intelligence**

Our project focuses on protecting the LLM output, by removing the poisoned documents while retrieving the documents through RAG pipeline. We trained our own ML model that was able to detect whether the document was poisoned (attacker changed the metadata) or not, based on the title and description of the image.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Alchemy API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Alchemy%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Viem](https://img.shields.io/badge/Viem-333333?style=flat-square) ![Coinbase Onchainkit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Coinbase%20Onchainkit-333333?style=flat-square) ![Farcaster Frames v2](https://img.shields.io/badge/Farcaster%20Frames%20v2-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Base ecosystem is exploding, but the tools to navigate it are fundamentally fractured. Right now, Web3 power users and builders are forced to juggle multiple disconnected platforms just to get a clear picture of what is actually happening onchain.

Base Analytics solves three critical pain points in the current Web3 landscape:

1. The Fragmentation of Social and Financial Data
Currently, financial data (token prices, volume) lives on heavy trading terminals, while social signal and reputation data live separately on Farcaster. There is no unified command center that links the Base financial ecosystem with decentralized social identity. Users have to switch between tabs and apps to connect the dots.

2. The Noise-to-Signal Ratio
The Base network never sleeps. Humans cannot manually monitor real-time token shifts, protocol updates, and social sentiment 24/7. Users constantly miss critical ecosystem movements and alpha because they simply have to step away from their screens.

3. Opaque Decentralized Reputation
Farcaster is the heartbeat of Web3 social, and reputation metrics dictate visibility, trust, and airdrop eligibility. Yet, the average user has no clean, accessible way to visualize their actual on-chain social quotient, Neynar score, or Ethos credentials without querying raw APIs themselves.

The Solution:
Base Analytics acts as the ultimate autonomous command center. We bridge the gap by providing a unified dashboard where users can instantly track top BASE network assets while simultaneously visualizing their exact Farcaster reputation. To solve the attention problem, we deployed an autonomous AI agent that ingests raw market data, synthesizes the noise, and broadcasts native ecosystem insights every 6 hours—completely removing the need for manual monitoring.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an autonomous, real-time command center for the Base ecosystem sounded straightforward on paper, but wiring together decentralized social protocols, live financial data, and AI agents introduced several major hurdles:

1. The Web2 API Paywall & The Farcaster Pivot
Our original architecture had the AI Agent broadcasting its Base market insights to X (Twitter). However, we immediately ran into X's newly enforced, strict 402 Payment Required API paywall, which blocks automated posting for free-tier developer accounts. Instead of fighting Web2 infrastructure, we executed a hard pivot to Web3. We re-engineered the agent's voice to cast natively directly to Warpcast using a Neynar Signer UUID. This not only bypassed the paywall but actually resulted in a much better product—keeping the agent entirely native to the Base and Farcaster ecosystem.

2. LLM Cost Optimization & Compatibility Routing
Running an autonomous agent that fires every 6 hours can get expensive quickly. We initially built the agent's "brain" using the OpenAI SDK (gpt-4o-mini). When we ran into API billing constraints, we engineered a clever routing workaround. Instead of rewriting the entire AI logic, we utilized Google's Gemini API Compatibility Mode. By simply swapping the base URL and pointing the existing OpenAI SDK to gemini-2.5-flash, we kept the agent lightning-fast and highly capable while dropping our inference costs to zero.

3. Securing the Autonomous Cron Job
Because our AI agent lives on a Next.js serverless API route, we faced the challenge of preventing random users (or malicious bots) from finding the endpoint and spamming the Farcaster timeline. We solved this by implementing a strict verification handshake. The route now checks for a specific, heavily encrypted CRON_SECRET Bearer token that is only known to the secure Vercel Cron server, ensuring the agent only wakes up exactly when it is scheduled to.

4. Taming Live Financial Data with Strict TypeScript
Ingesting live market data from CoinGecko meant dealing with highly dynamic, constantly changing JSON objects. Early on, this caused our Next.js build to fail due to strict ESLint rules rejecting any types. We had to architect custom, strict TypeScript interfaces (CoinMarketData) to define the exact shape of the incoming Base token data, ensuring the app was completely type-safe from the initial data fetch all the way to the final AI prompt.

**The problem it solves**

## About
NFT Battle Arena is a cross-collection NFT battle game on Base where any NFT from any collection becomes a playable fighter with real combat utility.

V2 brings strategic depth: players build full loadouts — pick a Fighter, equip an Item buff, and choose an Arena modifier — creating thousands of tactical combinations. Your entire wallet inventory is scanned for team synergies, rewarding long-term collectors with passive stat boosts.

All PvP matches are cryptographically secured. Players authenticate via SIWE (Sign-In with Ethereum), and combat is resolved entirely server-side using Vercel KV with atomic operations. A custom seeded PRNG engine (mulberry32 + FNV-1a hashing) ensures every battle is 100% deterministic and reproducible for replays and anti-cheat verification.

Key features:
• Universal stat normalization across 12+ Base NFT collections
• Multi-NFT loadouts (Fighter + Item + Arena) with diminishing returns
• 5 passive abilities with cooldown-based trigger systems
• Cinematic battle renderer with particles, screen shake, and damage numbers
• Server-authoritative PvP with SIWE + JWT authentication
• Deterministic seeded PRNG for reproducible battle outcomes
• Anti-drift snapshot hashing (SHA-256) for mutable NFT protection
• Live balance configuration via CDN for real-time meta-tuning
• V2 analytics pipeline tracking loadouts, battles, and results
• Farcaster and Base Mini App native integration


## The Problem it Solves
Most NFT collections become static PFPs with zero utility after minting. NFT Battle Arena solves this by giving every NFT on Base real combat utility through metadata normalization — no matter the collection, no matter the traits.

V2 goes further by solving three critical problems:

1. Single-NFT Boredom: Players now deploy full strategic loadouts (Fighter + Item + Arena), making every battle a tactical decision rather than a coin flip.

2. Client-Side Cheating: All PvP combat is resolved server-side via Vercel Serverless Functions. Players authenticate with SIWE, stats are snapshot-hashed at challenge time, and battles run on a deterministic seeded PRNG — making manipulation impossible.

3. Balance Stagnation: A live balance config system fetches stat cap overrides from a CDN, allowing real-time meta-tuning without redeployment. No more waiting for a code push to fix a broken build.

**Challenges we ran into**

• Metadata normalization across 12+ collections with wildly different trait structures — each collection needed custom mapping logic while keeping the system extensible via a data-driven collection profiles architecture.

• Balancing combat stats so no single collection dominates — implemented stat caps, floors, diminishing returns on buff layers (Items: 100%, Arena: 80%, Team: 60%), and configurable guardrails.

• Making battles feel cinematic in vanilla JavaScript without heavy game engines — built a custom animation system with CSS keyframes for screen shake, crit bursts, dodge ghosts, floating damage numbers, and particle effects.

• Deterministic replay system — implemented a seeded PRNG (mulberry32 + FNV-1a) to ensure the same battle inputs always produce identical outputs for server-side verification and future spectator mode.

• Server-side PvP without WebSockets — built an atomic challenge/fight system using Vercel KV hash operations to prevent race conditions during concurrent challenge acceptance.

• SIWE authentication flow — integrated Sign-In with Ethereum using the `siwe` npm package with `jose` JWT tokens (1h expiry, 5min nonce TTL) for stateless, secure API authentication.

• Browser compatibility — replaced Node.js crypto with Web Crypto API (SHA-256) for stat snapshots, and handled Farcaster miniapp connector nuances across Base and Warpcast hosts.
