### AgentBazaar
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agentbazaar-3189) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ritiklakhwani/agent-marketplace) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://agentbazaar.oceandev.xyz/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/srJ5h69g1Bw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-SCBC%20Hackathon%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://scbc-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-8-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> From prompt to portfolio, bridged cross-chain.

![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most AI agent marketplaces are glorified chatbots. They return text. They do not hold money, do not compose across agents, and cannot be held accountable when they are wrong. A portfolio rebalance becomes a ChatGPT screenshot, not a filled position. A cross-border payment stays a conversation, not USDC landing on another chain.

AgentBazaar replaces that pattern with a real marketplace where agents bid, pay each other, settle on-chain, and are insured against failure.

What you can do today
Rebalance a portfolio in one prompt. "Maintain 40% AAPL, 30% TSLA, 30% NVDA with $500." A Router LLM parses intent. Two Portfolio Agents compete in a live Dutch auction streamed over SSE. The winner hires an Oracle agent for Pyth-style prices and a Swap agent for each trade leg. Every call is paid in real USDC over x402 on Solana.

Move USDC cross-chain without wrapped tokens. Circle CCTP V2 runs in both directions. Arc testnet to Solana funds the user's wallet, and Solana to Ethereum Sepolia sends the remittance. Native burn and mint, no IOU tokens.

Buy insurance on agent failure. A 0.5% premium routes the task to a lower-reputation agent. If they fail, a Solana Anchor program refunds the user's ATA automatically and slashes that agent's on-chain reputation.

Why it's safer than anything else in this category
Every payment is a signed SPL transfer, so Solana Explorer shows exactly where every USDC went, per edge.

Reputation lives on-chain (Anchor Registry program), so winner picks are explainable by a simple fee ÷ reputation formula.

Delegation is explicit and capped. The user approves 20 USDC once. The marketplace cannot spend more, cannot spend from any other mint, and cannot drift to mainnet by accident.

Failures are priced, not unknown. The Insurance program makes bad agents pay for being bad, programmatically.

Why it composes
Every agent route is a tiny microservice behind the same x402 middleware. Swap out our Oracle or Swap for any third party that accepts a signed X-PAYMENT header and the marketplace keeps working. The whole thing is an open protocol dressed up as a product.

Where it goes next
V1 swaps mock stock mints for real Backed xStocks via Jupiter, adds a fiat offramp via Dodo Payments for INR settlement, and moves x402 to a per-task user-signed model. The pattern (compose, pay, reputation-gate, insure) generalizes to any marketplace of specialist agents.

**Challenges we ran into**

The single hardest thing was getting Circle CCTP V2's receive_message working on Solana devnet end-to-end for the Fund-from-Arc flow. It is the flow that qualifies us for the Circle track, and Circle's Solana side programs (CCTPV2Sm4AdWt5296sk4P66VBZ7bEhcARwFaaS9YPbeC and CCTPV2vPZJS2u2BBsUoscuikbYjnpFmbFsvVuJdgUMQe) had essentially no TypeScript reference for the EVM to Solana direction. We had to reverse engineer the account order and PDA seed encoding from live on-chain data. Four separate traps, each one ate a demo-day hour.

1. The used_nonce PDA seeds changed between V1 and V2
Our first guess, by analogy to V1, was ["used_message", source_domain_BE, nonce]. It failed with AnchorError: ConstraintSeeds. The actual V2 seeds are [b"used_nonce", nonce_32_bytes]. The prefix string changed, and source_domain is not a seed at all.

2. remote_token_messenger and token_pair use ASCII-encoded domains
We initially encoded source_domain as a 4-byte big-endian u32 (the standard Rust to_be_bytes() convention). It failed with AccountNotInitialized. On-chain inspection revealed that Circle encodes the domain as ASCII bytes. Domain 26 becomes [0x32, 0x36] (the string "26"), not [0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x1A]. That choice is not documented anywhere we could find.

3. V2 added a fee_recipient_token_account that every V1 example is missing
CCTP V2 inserted a new account slot between token_pair and recipient_ata in the remaining_accounts forwarded to handle_receive_finalized_message. V1 did not have it, so every reference implementation online was silently wrong. Worse, the fee recipient's pubkey is not a well-known constant. It is stored inside the token_messenger account at byte offset 109 (after owner, pending_owner, paused_by, a u32 version field, and a u8 bump). We wrote a small Node script that walked byte offsets, called getAssociatedTokenAddress for each possible 32-byte chunk, and checked which USDC ATAs actually existed on-chain. That pinpointed the real fee_recipient in about 30 seconds. Now the route fetches token_messenger at call time and parses the layout by hand.

4. The full transaction was 66 bytes over Solana's 1232-byte limit
Combining create_ata and receive_message in one tx exceeded Solana's hard cap. We split into two transactions. An idempotent ATA creation first, then receive_message alone. Only the latter is the real mint, so the user still sees a single on-chain mint event.

The meta-lesson
Six failed attempts burned around 15 USDC on Arc before we got it right. Each iteration was a real on-chain burn that cannot be "un-burned". But the reverse engineering pattern we developed is transferable. Fetch a known-good account, diff its byte layout against what Anchor expects, and iterate on the Anchor error codes until every constraint validates. That pattern is what turned a flow we thought would never ship into the cleanest segment of our demo.

This is the only Arc and Solana CCTP V2 cross-chain flow we have found running end-to-end on a hackathon project in this cycle. It is also why the Circle track qualifier is a fully live demo rather than a bullet point on the README.

**Programmable Money for Humans & Agents**

The track asks for USDC that behaves like more than money. It asks for money that rules can be written into, by humans and by agents. AgentBazaar uses Circle CCTP V2 and Solana together to do exactly that, in both directions, with Arc as a first-class source chain.

Two CCTP V2 flows live in one codebase. The Remittance Agent burns USDC on Solana and mints on Ethereum Sepolia. A separate Fund from Arc flow burns on Circle's Arc testnet (CCTP domain 26) and mints on Solana. Arc is not a mention, it is the live qualifier running end-to-end in the submitted demo. Every mint is native USDC. There is not a single wrapped token anywhere in the flow.

Programmable money for agents. Every agent to agent call carries a signed X-PAYMENT header (x402) wrapping a real USDC SPL transfer on Solana. A rebalance fires four edges. The user pays the Portfolio agent, the Portfolio agent pays the Oracle, and the Portfolio agent pays the Swap agent three times, once per leg. Each edge is a distinct USDC transaction visible on Explorer. On top of that, an on-chain Solana Insurance program (a PDA-owned USDC vault) programmatically refunds failed agent tasks and slashes reputation in the same atomic flow. USDC here is not just transferred. It is the primary integration point for accountability.

Programmable money for humans. A single approve(delegate = marketplace, 20 USDC) lets the user authorize the marketplace to spend on their behalf. The allowance is capped, revocable, and scoped to a single mint. Every downstream agent payment shows up on Explorer as a direct user_wallet to agent_wallet transfer, not from a hidden admin key. The human signs once, and the money rules itself after.

Technical depth as qualifier. Circle's Solana side CCTP V2 programs had no published TypeScript reference for the EVM to Solana direction. We reverse engineered the PDA seeds from live on-chain data, including the ASCII encoded domain bytes, V2's new fee_recipient_token_account slot, and the used_nonce prefix change. The Arc to Solana mint working reliably is earned work, not a stub.

One USDC primitive, three chains, two user modes. Arc, Solana, and Ethereum Sepolia. Humans delegating it, agents spending it, a program refunding it. That is programmable money in the shape Circle asked for.

**Best Use of Solana**

Solana is not a deployment target for AgentBazaar. It is the substrate the whole marketplace architecture depends on. Every piece of the product leans on a primitive that Solana does better than any other chain.

Two live Anchor programs on devnet carry the accountability layer. A Registry program stores per-agent reputation in a PDA keyed by the agent's owner pubkey. Reads are free, updates are gated by a trusted signer, and the winner picker is a one-line fee ÷ reputation formula a judge can verify on Explorer. An Insurance program holds a USDC vault PDA and programmatically refunds failed tasks via CPI. Failure is priced on-chain, not handled by a backend.

SPL token delegation turns the x402 layer from an API pattern into a wallet pattern. The user signs one approve(delegate = marketplace, 20 USDC) and from that moment every agent payment shows up on Explorer as a direct user_wallet to agent_wallet transfer, not from an opaque admin key. Each agent to agent call also carries a signed X-PAYMENT header wrapping a real SPL transfer, so every edge in the composition graph is a real Solana transaction. Four agents firing in sequence produce four Explorer rows, not four mock txs.

Circle CCTP V2 on both sides uses Solana's CCTP programs natively. MessageTransmitterV2 and TokenMessengerMinterV2 are called directly to mint native USDC, with no wrapped tokens and no trust bridges. That unlocks Arc to Solana funding and Solana to Ethereum remittance inside the same UI.

Solana's real strengths are what make agent to agent commerce feasible here. The per-transaction cost is negligible, native program composability means CPI can fire the insurance refund in one instruction, and SPL semantics give us delegation, approvals, and real accounts out of the box. On an EVM chain the fee per edge would dominate the economics. On Solana it is rounding error. The auction animates at roughly 1.5 seconds per bid because Solana confirmation is that fast. We did not pick Solana and port a pattern onto it. We built a pattern Solana specifically enables.

🌟 Core Concept
Medora creates a unified ecosystem connecting all stakeholders: Manufacturers, Distributors, Retailers, and Customers. Every medicine batch is meticulously tracked, verified, and secured, ensuring authenticity and transparency throughout its lifecycle.

Medora integrates cutting-edge technologies to deliver a secure, transparent, and intelligent medicine supply chain. Here's how each core feature is realized:

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem: A 30 Billion Dollar Broken Industry

Traditional insurance claim processing is plagued by three systemic failures:

1. Crippling Processing Delays: Claimants wait anywhere from 14 to 45 days for manual paperwork reviews, adjuster site visits, and back-and-forth email verifications.
2. Astronomical Fraud Overhead: Insurance fraud costs the global industry upwards of 30 Billion dollars annually. To combat this, insurers deploy armies of manual adjusters, driving up administrative overhead by 20 to 30 percent and forcing honest policyholders to pay higher premiums.
3. The Black Box Trust Deficit: Claimants have zero visibility into why their claim was delayed or rejected. Funds remain locked in corporate bank accounts, creating an inherent conflict of interest where insurers profit by delaying or denying payouts.


The Solution: ClaimChain Autonomous Escrow Protocol

ClaimChain completely replaces slow, manual insurance processing with an autonomous multimodal AI agent and trustless blockchain smart contracts on Polygon Amoy.

Instead of waiting weeks for human adjusters, users submit their incident narrative, payout request, and photo evidence. In seconds, ClaimChain executes an automated 3-stage protocol:

1. Multimodal AI Risk Verification
Google Gemini 1.5 Flash simultaneously analyzes the incident description and photo evidence through 5 specialized neural reasoning nodes: Vision Damage Analysis, NLP Semantic Cross-Validation, Risk Scoring Engine, Oracle Signer, and Central Gemini AI Agent. It detects metadata anomalies, lighting inconsistencies, timeline contradictions, and stock image fraud to generate an objective Fraud Risk Score from 0 to 100.

2. Code-Enforced On-Chain Escrow Payouts
Smart contracts deployed on Polygon Amoy hold claim funds in trustless escrow.
For Low Risk below 40, the smart contract instantly auto-executes payout directly to the claimant wallet in under 5 seconds.
For High Risk 40 or above, the smart contract locks escrow funds on-chain and flags the claim for transparent admin verification.

3. Transparent On-Chain Auditability
Every claim verdict, risk score, and transaction hash is recorded immutably on-chain on amoy.polygonscan.com, eliminating insurer-claimant trust deficits and providing 100 percent auditability.


Key Innovations and Real-World Impact

- 99.9 Percent Faster Settlement: Reduces claim processing time from 45 days down to 5 seconds.
- Zero-Trust Escrow: Payouts are enforced by open-source smart contract code ClaimEscrow.sol, not corporate promises.
- 90 Percent Reduction in Administrative Overhead: Eliminates first-level manual adjuster backlogs through automated multimodal AI filtering.
- Dual Demo Infrastructure: Built-in Instant Demo Sandbox Mode for zero-gas presentation testing alongside full Polygon Amoy Testnet live contract verification.


Who Can Use ClaimChain?

1. Micro-Insurance Platforms: Instant automated claims for flight delays, electronics damage, and small asset protection.
2. DeFi and Web3 Escrow Protocols: Automated decentralized oracle payouts for peer-to-peer insurance pools.
3. Traditional Enterprise Insurers: Pluggable AI risk oracle middleware to automate first-notice-of-loss FNOL triage.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into and Technical Solutions


1. Multimodal AI Schema Determinism and Structured Risk Output

Hurdle: Large Multimodal Models like Google Gemini 1.5 Flash often generate natural language conversational responses, which can introduce variance when automated smart contract systems require exact integer risk scores from 0 to 100.

Solution: We engineered strict JSON schema instructions and system prompts within the Express backend SDK. We implemented fallback sanitization parsers that validate output structure, extract explicit numerical scores, and format detected risk signals into deterministic arrays before passing telemetry to the oracle pipeline.


2. Off-Chain AI Oracle Integration with On-Chain Smart Contracts

Hurdle: Connecting off-chain AI risk evaluation with on-chain EVM smart contract execution on Polygon Amoy created security and synchronization challenges, particularly ensuring unauthorized accounts could not submit fake risk scores.

Solution: We implemented a cryptographic Oracle architecture using Ethers.js v6. The Solidity smart contract ClaimEscrow.sol enforces an access-controlled onlyOracle modifier. When Gemini computes a low risk score, the backend oracle signs the payload with its private key to execute automated claim releases securely.


3. Testnet RPC Rate-Limiting and Presentation Resilience

Hurdle: Public blockchain testnet RPC nodes on Polygon Amoy can experience block latency or rate limits during live demonstrations, which could cause presentation bottlenecks for hackathon judges.

Solution: We designed a dual-mode execution architecture. We built an Instant Demo Sandbox Mode that activates when CONTRACT_ADDRESS is set to demo_mode. This simulates smart contract state transitions locally without gas costs, while maintaining full compatibility with live Polygon Amoy contracts when deployed.


4. React SSR Hydration and CSS Variable Theme Synchronization

Hurdle: Developing a text-first developer UI in Next.js 14 with instant Dark and Light mode toggling caused Flash of Unstyled Content FOUC and React server-client hydration mismatches.

Solution: We built a client-side ThemeProvider context wrapper and tokenized all colors into CSS variables on root and html.light. This decouples component styling from hydration states, ensuring instantaneous 60fps theme switching across all inputs, cards, and modal HUDs.

**AI For Society**

ClaimChain uses Artificial Intelligence and blockchain technology to address a real-world societal and financial problem: slow, opaque, and potentially fraudulent insurance claim processing.

The platform allows users to submit an insurance claim along with an incident description and photo evidence. A multimodal AI verification pipeline analyzes both textual and visual information to identify inconsistencies, evaluate supporting evidence, and generate a fraud risk assessment.

Based on the AI-generated risk score, claims follow a hybrid decision workflow. Low-risk claims can proceed toward automated settlement through a smart-contract escrow system, while high-risk claims are flagged for human administrator review. This ensures that AI improves efficiency without completely replacing human judgment in sensitive financial decisions.

Blockchain technology adds transparency and accountability by recording important claim and settlement actions through an auditable on-chain workflow. Smart-contract escrow also helps ensure that funds are handled according to predefined rules rather than opaque manual processes.

ClaimChain demonstrates how AI can be applied to create a more efficient, transparent, and accessible insurance infrastructure. By combining multimodal AI analysis, human-in-the-loop decision-making, smart-contract automation, and blockchain auditability, the project aims to reduce claim-processing delays, improve fraud detection, and increase trust for both claimants and administrators.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into

Building this project was much more than just connecting an AI model to a map. One of our biggest challenges was making the entire experience feel seamless for users while handling multiple moving parts behind the scenes.

The first hurdle was location accuracy. Different devices sometimes returned slightly different GPS coordinates, which occasionally resulted in inaccurate doctor recommendations. We solved this by improving our location handling logic, adding proper validation, and introducing fallback mechanisms to ensure users still received relevant nearby results.

Another challenge was combining AI with location-based search. The AI could understand a user's symptoms, but converting those symptoms into the correct medical specialty and then finding nearby doctors required careful prompt engineering and structured mapping. We refined our prompts and built a layer that translates natural language into meaningful healthcare categories before searching for nearby medical facilities.

We also faced issues with API response times and data synchronization. Since the application relies on multiple services, loading everything at once sometimes caused delays. We optimized API calls, improved loading states, and reduced unnecessary requests so the interface remained responsive even when external services were slower than expected.

During development, we encountered several frontend issues related to state management. After adding or updating data, the UI sometimes continued showing older information until the page was refreshed. We fixed this by improving our data-fetching strategy, updating application state immediately after successful operations, and ensuring the latest information was always displayed without requiring manual refreshes.

Another important challenge was creating an interface that remained simple during stressful situations. Healthcare applications are often used when people are anxious or in a hurry, so we continuously simplified the user journey, reduced unnecessary steps, improved button placement, and focused on making the most important actions accessible within a single screen.

Finally, integrating all the different components—AI assistance, location services, healthcare information, and a responsive frontend—while working within a hackathon timeline required constant testing, debugging, and collaboration. Every issue we solved helped us make the application more reliable and user-friendly.

These challenges taught us that building a useful healthcare solution isn't just about writing code—it's about creating an experience people can trust when they need it the most.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves

Imagine it's late at night. A family member suddenly falls sick. You don't know which doctor to visit, which hospital is open, or whether you should see a physician, cardiologist, or orthopedic specialist. In moments like these, people often waste valuable time searching Google, opening multiple apps, reading reviews, calling hospitals, and asking friends for suggestions. During a medical emergency, every minute matters.

This is the problem we wanted to solve.

Our AI Nearest Doctor Assistant is designed to make finding medical help as simple as having a conversation. Instead of searching through dozens of websites, users can simply describe what's happening—for example, "I have severe stomach pain" or "My child has a high fever"—and the AI helps them understand which type of doctor they should consult while instantly suggesting nearby hospitals, clinics, and specialists based on their location.

The goal isn't to replace doctors or provide medical diagnoses. The goal is to help people reach the right healthcare professional faster, especially when they are stressed, confused, or unfamiliar with the healthcare system.

This is useful not only during emergencies but also in everyday situations. Students living away from home, travelers in a new city, senior citizens who are not comfortable using multiple apps, and families looking for nearby specialists can all benefit from one intelligent assistant that brings everything together in one place.

Our platform reduces the time spent searching for healthcare by combining AI-powered symptom guidance with location-based doctor discovery. Instead of switching between Google Search, Maps, hospital websites, and review platforms, users receive relevant recommendations in one simple interface.

We also believe healthcare should be accessible and easy to understand. That's why the assistant communicates in a natural, conversational way rather than expecting users to know medical terminology. It guides them step by step, helping them make informed decisions without feeling overwhelmed.

At its core, this project is about one simple idea:

When someone needs medical help, finding the right doctor should take seconds—not precious minutes.

If our solution can help even one person reach the right healthcare professional faster during a critical moment, then we believe it has achieved its purpose.

> Securing Land Ownership through Smart Contracts.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Etherscan](https://img.shields.io/badge/Etherscan-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today, land records are still managed using paper documents and different government offices. This makes the process slow and sometimes confusing. Fake documents, duplicate registrations, and ownership disputes are common problems. Buying or selling land can take a long time because every document has to be checked manually.

Bhoomi helps solve these problems by creating a secure digital land registry using blockchain technology. Every verified land is given a unique digital ownership record, making it difficult to change or fake the information.

People can use **Bhoomi** to:
- Register land digitally.
- View verified ownership records.
- Check the history of a property before buying it.
- Transfer land ownership more securely.
- Store important land documents safely.
- Fractional deal of NFT land

Bhoomi makes the land registration process faster, more transparent, and easier for landowners, buyers, and government authorities. It reduces paperwork, helps prevent fraud, and builds trust by keeping ownership records secure and easy to verify.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was deploying and managing our smart contracts on the Ethereum Sepolia testnet. We encountered issues related to RPC configuration, account management, gas estimation, contract verification, and maintaining consistent contract addresses across deployments. Since every contract update required redeployment, keeping the frontend synchronized with the latest deployed addresses and ABIs was an ongoing challenge. We streamlined this process using Hardhat deployment scripts, environment-based configuration, and modular contract testing.

Another challenge was designing a secure land minting workflow. We needed to ensure that land NFTs could only be minted after verification by an authorized government authority, rather than allowing unrestricted minting. To solve this, we implemented role-based access control in our smart contracts, ensuring that only authorized authority accounts can approve land records and execute the NFT minting process.

We also had to carefully decide what data belonged on-chain and what should remain off-chain. Storing property documents directly on Ethereum was impractical due to storage costs, so we adopted a hybrid architecture where legal documents are stored on IPFS while only immutable document hashes and metadata references are recorded on-chain. This approach maintains data integrity while keeping the system scalable and cost-efficient.

These challenges gave us valuable experience in smart contract deployment, secure access control, decentralized storage, and building a practical Web3 application that balances transparency, security, scalability and clean system design.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Twilio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Twilio-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygon-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Udhaar - Blockchain-Powered Trust Lending for Bharat 🇮🇳

Problem Statement

In India, ₹5 trillion worth of informal credit flows through kirana stores and local communities annually. These "udhaar" transactions are unrecorded (written in notebooks), untraceable (no credit history), risky (no reputation system), and inefficient (requires physical presence). Traditional banking excludes 190M+ Indians, while existing fintech demands smartphones, credit scores, and digital literacy that rural communities lack.

Our Solution

Udhaar digitizes informal lending with blockchain immutability and zero Web3 complexity. It's a phone-first platform where users authenticate via OTP, and every loan agreement is recorded on Polygon blockchain through custodial wallets—no MetaMask, no gas fees, no jargon.

Key Innovation: Dual OTP Trust Flow
- Loan Creation: Lender enters borrower's phone → OTP sent to borrower → Borrower confirms → Recorded on blockchain
- Repayment: Borrower initiates → OTP sent to lender → Lender shares OTP verbally → Borrower enters OTP → Settled on blockchain

This mimics real-world trust (verbal confirmation) while providing cryptographic proof.

ML-Powered Reputation: Every user gets a 0-100 credit score computed by an ensemble model (Gradient Boosting + Random Forest + Ridge) trained on 15 features: repayment rate, default rate, loan velocity, recency, and more. Scores update automatically after each transaction (+10 for settled loans, -30 for defaults).

Chain-or-Fallback Architecture: When blockchain is unavailable (low gas balance, network issues), transactions save to Turso database and queue for automatic retry. Users never see errors—just "pending blockchain confirmation." This ensures 100% availability.

Impact: Udhaar builds portable credit history for the unbanked, reduces lending risk through transparent reputation, and enables financial inclusion without requiring users to understand blockchain technology. The platform scales to millions via custodial wallet derivation and distributed SQLite, targeting 10,000 users and ₹50 crore loan volume in Year 1.

**Challenges we ran into**

Almost Everything.. Heres the deal - 
1) The Target audience - they dont know whats web3, nor do they need to know. to abstract web3 enough so that it doesnt feel more than a non-negotiable witness was indeed a challange
2) Wallet management - Creating a custodial account and managing funds for every user, defining the scalability , deciding the tradeoffs between ease of use and freedom to user, AP vs CP (Turso as cache) and actually making sure that user does not feel alien to it.
3)Two-Party Verification Without Physical Presence - How to verify both parties agree remotely using dual OTP flow
4)Reputation System Design - Linking phone numbers to blockchain addresses while preventing Sybil attacks and preserving privacy
5)Gas Fee Economics & Sustainability - Making custodial gas payments economically viable at scale
6)Real-Time State Synchronization - Keeping DB and blockchain in sync without race conditions
7)Testing Blockchain Interactions - Testing time-dependent logic and fallback scenarios

> Blockchain Based Blue Carbon Registry System

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Imagine a small coastal village in India.

A farmer plants mangrove trees near the shoreline. These trees protect his village from storms, prevent coastal erosion, and absorb carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.

In fact, mangroves can capture four times more carbon than regular forests.

But here is the problem.

Even though this farmer is helping the planet fight climate change, he earns nothing for it.

At the same time, companies across the world are desperately trying to reduce their carbon footprint. They are willing to pay for verified carbon credits to offset their emissions.

So we have two sides of the same story:

Farmers restoring nature but earning nothing

Companies searching for trusted carbon credits

Governments planting mangroves through MISHTI Scheme but lacking systems to measure their impact

The missing piece is trust and verification.

Today, verifying carbon credits is extremely expensive and slow. International certification systems can take 18 months and cost up to $80,000 per project. Small farmers and local communities simply cannot afford that process.

As a result, millions of mangrove plantations across developing countries never become carbon credits, even though they are capturing carbon every day.

Our platform solves this gap.

We built a digital blue carbon registry that connects farmers, local governments, and companies into one transparent system.

When a farmer plants mangroves, they can register their project using a simple mobile interface. The system records GPS location, plantation area, species type, and supporting evidence such as geo-tagged images.

Artificial Intelligence then estimates the carbon captured by those trees using environmental data and species-specific models.

Local panchayat officers (hence this needed by the GOV) verify the plantation on the ground, and the government performs the final approval (where we are giving the AI confidence score for the details entered by the farmer and panchayat based on it the GOV can decide weather to accept or reject ).

Once verified, the carbon captured by that plantation is converted into blockchain-secured carbon credits. Each credit is recorded permanently on the blockchain, ensuring that it cannot be altered, duplicated, or falsely claimed.

Companies can then purchase these verified credits through a transparent marketplace to offset their emissions.

This creates a powerful cycle of impact:

Farmers earn income for restoring nature

Companies reduce their carbon footprint responsibly

Governments gain a transparent national carbon registry

And coastal ecosystems receive the protection they urgently need

Instead of planting trees without recognition, communities now participate in a global climate economy.

The trees are already being planted.
The science already exists.
The market for carbon credits is already growing.

The only thing missing was a system that connects them all together.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building BlueCarbon Ledger involved integrating several complex systems  AI models, blockchain infrastructure, geospatial verification, and a multi-role web platform. One of the biggest challenges was connecting these components into a reliable workflow that non-technical users could operate easily.

**Blockchain Integration Challenges**

One major hurdle was integrating the Ethereum smart contract with the Django backend. While the smart contract worked correctly on Ganache, the backend initially failed to connect to the blockchain node due to network configuration issues and RPC connectivity errors. This caused transaction failures when attempting to mint carbon credits.

To resolve this, I carefully debugged the Web3 connection, verified RPC endpoints, adjusted gas configurations, and implemented proper transaction signing using private keys. After stabilizing the connection, the platform was able to mint carbon credits directly from the government approval workflow.

**Designing for Rural Accessibility**

A different type of challenge was usability for rural farmers. Many potential users may not be comfortable with English or complex digital interfaces.

To address this, I redesigned the registration flow to include multilingual support and voice-guided assistance, allowing users to understand each step through audio instructions. This ensured the platform could be used even by individuals with limited literacy.

> Next-Gen Supply Chain Verification

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The global supply chain is fractured. 
- The Transparency Gap: Most "tracking" only knows where a box is, not what’s Inside or if it's been tampered with.
- The Counterfeit Crisis: Counterfeit goods cost the global economy billions annually and put lives at risk (fake medicines).
- Centralized Vulnerability: Traditional databases can be edited. A corrupt actor can alter records to hide theft or substitution.

---

🟢 Our Solution: The Tracely Protocol

Tracely introduces a three-layer trust architecture:

1.  Digital Identity (QR Provenance): Every batch is assigned a unique, cryptographic QR identity that serves as its digital twin.
2.  AI Guardian (TIS Score): Our proprietary Trust Integrity Score (TIS)uses an ensemble of Gemini 1.5 Flash models and classical CV (OpenCV) to detect micro-variations in packaging, seal lift, or digital tampering.
3.  Blockchain Anchor (Ethereum): Every custody transfer is anchored on the Sepolia testnet, creating an immutable history that can be verified by anyone, anywhere.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The "Gemini Ensemble" Strategy
We discovered that a single AI model can produce hallucinations in specialized forensic tasks. We implemented a *consensus-based ensemble architecture* where two Gemini models independently analyze the images. If their confidence or detection types mismatch, a classical Computer Vision (OpenCV) filter is triggered to normalize result, ensuring high precision.
2. The macOS SSL & Auth0 Hurdle
During development on macOS, we encountered significant SSL certificate verification issues connecting to MongoDB and Auth0. We resolved this by implementing a robust certificate injection layer in the Python backend (certifi) to ensure secure, compliant connections in production environments.

3. State Syncing across 3 Layers
Managing state between *MongoDB (User Metadata), **Ethereum (Logs), and **IPFS (Images)* required a custom middleware to ensure transactions are atomic. We learned to prioritize blockchain confirmation before committing metadata to the local cache.

**Ethereum Track**

Tracely is a "best use" of Ethereum because it solves the Trust Gap in global logistics a problem that a standard centralized database (like SQL or MongoDB) simply cannot solve.

Here are the four "Killer Reasons" why Ethereum is essential for Tracely, which you should definitely mention in your pitch:

1. Immutability vs. "Admin Privileges"
In a traditional database, an "Admin" or a corrupt employee can go back and change a record (e.g., delete a log of a damaged package to hide liability).

Ethereum's Value: Once a custody transfer is logged on-chain, not even the developers of Tracely can delete it. It creates a "Permanent Forensic Timeline" that judges and insurance companies can trust 100%.
2. Cryptographic "Non-Repudiation"
In standard tracking, a worker might say "I didn't sign that."

Ethereum's Value: Every event in Tracely is signed by a private key (MetaMask). This provides mathematical proof of who handled the goods at every step. You aren't just trusting a username; you are trusting a cryptographic signature that cannot be forged.
3. Decentralized Verification Power
Usually, a consumer has to trust "Company X's" website to tell them a product is authentic.

Ethereum's Value: Tracely allows any third-party regulator or consumer to verify the data directly from the blockchain (the "Public Ledger"), bypassing the need to trust the manufacturer's own internal servers.
4. Anchoring the "Physical-Digital" Link
Our AI (Gemini) generates a Trust Integrity Score (TIS) and stores the photo on IPFS.

Ethereum's Value: By pushing the IPFS Hash (the digital fingerprint of the photo) into an Ethereum transaction, we "lock" the physical state of the box at a specific point in time. If someone tries to swap the photo later, the blockchain hash won't match, instantly exposing the fraud.

**Electrothon 8.0 Winners**

Solves a real problem: Counterfeit products cost industries billions. Tracely provides a reliable way to verify product authenticity.

Blockchain-powered trust: Immutable records ensure transparent and tamper-proof supply chains.

Scalable & cost-efficient: Built using Layer 2 technology to keep costs low and adoption easy.

Real-world impact: Helps manufacturers, regulators, and consumers verify products instantly.

**Requestly Track**

Requestly was utilized as a middleware traffic controller to bridge the gap between decentralized latency and production-grade reliability.

1. Network Resiliency & Failover
IPFS gateways can be volatile. We used Requestly Redirect Rules to ensure that even if the public IPFS gateway (ipfs.io) is slow, the Tracely UI remains responsive by instantly failing over to high-speed cached assets.

2. Advanced Stress Testing (The "Broken Seal" Scenario)
To verify our AI's ability to detect tampering without damaging physical goods, we used Modify Response rules. This allowed us to inject compromised data and "damaged" baseline images into the app in real-time, validating that our Trust Integrity Score (TIS) correctly flags and blocks suspicious handoffs.

3. Accelerated Developer Velocity (Zero-Redeploy)
Requestly eliminated the "Code-Build-Deploy" bottleneck. By intercepting API calls and redirecting them to local mocks, we could test new UI states and complex backend logic instantly, ensuring a highly polished final product.

**Best Use of Gemini 3 [Google Deepmind]**

AI Innovation: The Gemini Consensus Ensemble
Tracely moves beyond standard image recognition by implementing a Forensic Ensemble Architecture powered by Google Gemini 3 Flash and pro.

1. Beyond "Hotdog/Not-Hotdog": Forensic Vision
While standard AI identifies objects, Tracely's Gemini implementation detects micro-variations in physical state. It analyzes texture consistency, seal reflection anomalies, and structural integrity between "Baseline" and "Current" states to identify tampering that is invisible to the human eye.

2. The Consensus Strategy (Zero-Hallucination)
To meet institutional-grade security standards, we don't rely on a single AI inference. Tracely utilizes an ensemble approach where two independent Gemini models analyze the package from different logical perspectives. A custody event only proceeds if there is a statistical consensus, virtually eliminating AI "hallucinations."

3. Quantitative Trust (The TIS Score)
Gemini transforms qualitative visual data into a quantitative Trust Integrity Score (TIS). This score is direct-coupled with the Ethereum smart contract—if the TIS falls below the threshold, the blockchain transaction is aborted, creating a hard-link between AI intelligence and decentralized enforcement.

### MeshSearch
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/meshsearch-7294) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/WhyAsh5114/MeshSearch) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-7-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Search privately. Pay anonymously. Trust no one.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

**Every web search you make is a data exhaust trail.** Google, Bing, and most AI search tools log your IP, your queries, and your patterns — building a profile that's sold, subpoenaed, or breached.

MeshSearch makes private web search practical for both humans and AI agents:

- **AI agents that search the web leak their user's intent.** MeshSearch gives Claude, Cursor, and any MCP-compatible agent a search tool where queries are ZK-committed before leaving the device — the relay network never sees the plaintext query.
- **Anonymous micropayments instead of surveillance.** Instead of paying with your attention and identity, you pay per-search with USDC via x402 — no account, no tracking, just a wallet signature.
- **Auditable routing, not a black box.** Traffic routes through 3 ENS-named relay hops. Every result shows which relay operators handled your traffic — you can verify it on-chain.
- **Your history, under your key.** Search history is AES-256-GCM encrypted with your wallet key and stored on Fileverse. Only you can decrypt it. No server ever sees plaintext.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

**1. Getting the x402 payment flow to actually fire**
The MCP tool was returning results without triggering payment — the 402 response was being swallowed silently. The fix was separating the payment gate into its own `/api/paid-search` endpoint on the Next.js side and ensuring the client re-sent the request with the signed USDC authorization attached.

**2. ENS resolution was fake**
The relay routing code was pattern-matching strings like `relay1.meshsearch.eth` instead of actually resolving them on L1. Swapped in `@ensdomains/ensjs` v4 with `ensPublicActions` on a viem client — now relays do real forward/reverse resolution at startup and each routing decision.

**3. Using the wrong Fileverse product entirely**
First pass used Fileverse's low-level Storage V2 IPFS API (UCAN tokens, multipart uploads, Contract/Invoker/Chain headers). The hackathon integration was actually the **dDocs API** — a completely different product with simple REST + API key auth (`POST /api/ddocs`, `GET /api/ddocs/:ddocId`). Rewrote the storage service from scratch once the hackathon docs clarified the correct endpoint surface.

**4. ZK proof generation being synchronous in tests**
Semaphore v4 Groth16 proof generation blocked the event loop long enough to cause test timeouts. Moved proof generation to a worker and added `vi.setSystemTime` mocking in tests to avoid flakiness.

**Privacy**

## ETHMumbai — Privacy

MeshSearch is private by construction — not by policy. Every layer of the stack replaces a trust assumption with a cryptographic guarantee, so no single party ever sees a user's plaintext query, traffic pattern, or search history.

**How it qualifies:**
- **ZK query commitment** — Every search is committed with a Semaphore v4 Groth16 proof before leaving the device. The relay network sees only the commitment, never the plaintext query.
- **Nullifier registry on-chain** — The `NullifierRegistry` contract on Base Sepolia prevents proof replay attacks, giving each search cryptographic uniqueness.
- **3-hop onion routing** — Traffic routes through ENS-named relay nodes; no single node knows both the origin and destination.
- **Encrypted history on Fileverse** — Search results are AES-256-GCM encrypted with the user's wallet key before storage. Not even the storage layer sees plaintext.
- **No accounts, no emails, no KYC** — A wallet signature is the only identity. x402 USDC micropayments settle on Base Sepolia without linking a user profile to a query.

**AI**

## ETHMumbai — AI

MeshSearch ships as an **MCP server** — the native tool-calling protocol for AI agents. Any MCP-compatible agent (Claude, Cursor, etc.) can call `private_search` and get the full privacy stack automatically, with zero additional integration.

**How it qualifies:**
- **MCP server for AI agents** — Claude, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible agent can call `private_search` and get privacy guarantees that no existing search tool provides.
- **Agent-driven payment** — The AI agent's wallet signs a USDC EIP-3009 authorization; the x402 payment settles on Base Sepolia before the query executes. The agent handles the entire payment flow autonomously.
- **Streaming results with provenance** — Search results stream back to the agent with a `Routing:` field showing the ENS names of the relay operators and a Base Sepolia transaction hash — full auditability inside the chat context.
- **Encrypted research reports** — The `compile_report` MCP tool aggregates multiple search dDocs into a single encrypted research report stored on Fileverse, letting agents build long-running research workflows with persistent, private memory.
- **Core thesis** — When an AI agent searches the web on your behalf, it creates the same surveillance surface as you searching yourself — unless the protocol is private by construction. MeshSearch is that protocol.

**Best creative use of ENS**

MeshSearch uses ENS as **infrastructure identity**, not user profiles. This is a genuinely novel application: relay nodes in a private routing network are named, discovered, and held accountable via ENS.

**How it qualifies:**
- relay1.meshsearch.eth, relay2.meshsearch.eth, relay3.meshsearch.eth are the canonical identifiers for the relay network — resolved on L1 at startup via @ensdomains/ensjs v4.
- Every search result includes a Routing: field showing the ENS names of the relay operators who handled the traffic — an **auditable privacy trail** anchored to ENS identity.
- The NodeRegistry contract maps ENS names to node public keys, ports, and reputation scores. Relay operators stake their ENS reputation on correct behaviour.
- x402 payment splits are distributed to relay operators identified by their ENS names — ENS becomes a payment routing identity, not just a username.

ENS here replaces DNS, certificate authorities, and operator registries simultaneously — all in a privacy-preserving routing network.

**Best Privacy Application using BitGo**

## BitGo — Privacy-Preserving Wallet Infrastructure

MeshSearch uses BitGo wallets as the disbursement layer for relay operator payments. The integration is live on Holesky testnet with 4 self-custody MPC hot wallets.

**How it qualifies:**
- **Stealth-address pattern** — for every private_search, generateFreshAddress() is called on each relay operator's BitGo wallet. Each operator receives funds at a new, unlinkable address. An observer cannot correlate relay1's payment from search A with relay1's payment from search B.
- **Self-custody MPC hot wallets** — all four wallets (treasury + 3 relay operators) use walletVersion: 3 on the hteth (Holesky ETH) coin. Key material never leaves BitGo MPC; no single point of compromise.
- **BitGo Express** — local key management via docker run bitgo/express:latest. The MCP server communicates with Express at http://localhost:3080 for transaction signing.
- **Policy engine** — velocity limits and address whitelists applied server-side via setupTreasuryPolicies(). The treasury wallet cannot be drained even if the MCP server is compromised.
- **Webhooks** — POST /webhooks/bitgo handler with HMAC-SHA256 signature validation (x-signature-sha256 header). Confirmed disbursements create an immutable audit trail.
- **Live browser UI** — the chat interface shows a pulsing **BitGo MPC** status badge in the header that polls /health every 15 seconds. Before payment, a card explains the stealth-address flow. After a successful search, a full disbursement visualisation shows USDC → Treasury (0x…) → relay1.eth → 0xABC… | relay2.eth → 0xDEF… | relay3.eth → 0x789… with fingerprint icons marking each fresh address. The actual stealth address generated for the search is shown when available.

**Wallets (Holesky testnet):**

| Wallet | ID prefix | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Treasury | `69b5a463…` | Receives x402 payments, disburses to relays |
| Relay 1 | `69b5a473…` | `relay1.meshsearch.eth` operator |
| Relay 2 | `69b5a483…` | `relay2.meshsearch.eth` operator |
| Relay 3 | `69b5a492…` | `relay3.meshsearch.eth` operator |

**Key files:**

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| apps/mcp-server/src/bitgo/client.ts | SDK wrapper, generateFreshAddress(), sendTransaction(), isBitGoEnabled() |
| apps/mcp-server/src/bitgo/stealth-disbursement.ts | Fresh-address fan-out to relay wallets |
| apps/mcp-server/src/bitgo/webhooks.ts | HMAC-validated webhook handler |
| apps/mcp-server/src/bitgo/policies.ts | Velocity limits, address whitelists |
| apps/web/src/app/chat/page.tsx | useBitGoStatus hook, StealthDisbursementCard, payment card pre-flight info |
| apps/web/src/app/api/health/route.ts | BitGoHealthInfo proxy — status, env, coin, walletId, relay count |

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

## Fileverse

MeshSearch uses the Fileverse **dDocs API** as the persistence layer for encrypted search history:

- After every private_search, the encrypted query commitment + result hash is stored as a dDoc via POST /api/ddocs
- The ciphertext (AES-256-GCM) is the dDoc content — Fileverse stores it without ever having the key
- get_history MCP tool: fetches dDocs, decrypts with wallet key, returns readable history
- compile_report MCP tool: aggregates multiple search dDocs into a single encrypted research report dDoc
- Sync status is polled until synced before returning the shareable link — full lifecycle implemented

This makes Fileverse the **anti-Google search history** — decentralised, content-addressed, user-key-encrypted, and accessible only to the wallet that created it.

**AI × Onchain**

## Base — AI × Onchain

The `private_search` MCP tool is a direct bridge between AI agents and on-chain infrastructure:

- AI agent calls private_search → triggers x402 payment gate → agent's wallet signs USDC authorization → payment settles on Base Sepolia → ZK proof verified against NullifierRegistry → search executes through ENS-named relays → encrypted result stored to Fileverse dDocs
- The **entire pipeline is on-chain-gated**: an AI agent literally cannot run a search without an on-chain USDC transaction
- Works natively with Claude via MCP — the agent handles the payment, proof, routing, and storage autonomously
- Streaming results with Routing: provenance and Base Sepolia transaction hash returned to the agent

**DeFi 2.0 - New Primitives**

## Base — DeFi 2.0

MeshSearch introduces a **micropayment incentive layer for decentralised search infrastructure**:

- PaymentSplitter contract receives x402 USDC payments and distributes shares to the 3 relay operators pro-rata
- Relay operators earn USDC per search routed through their node — a real economic incentive to run privacy infrastructure
- Payment splits are configurable; operators are identified by ENS name and tracked by NodeRegistry
- This is DeFi applied to a non-financial primitive: instead of yield farming, operators are paid for privacy routing work
- The x402 protocol (@x402/core, @x402/evm) handles EIP-3009 authorized transfers — no approve/transfer two-step, no gas paid by the server
- When BitGo is enabled, disbursement flows through MPC wallets with fresh stealth addresses per relay per search — the on-chain payment trail shows N unique, unlinked addresses, making relay income invisible to chain analysis

**Privacy**

## Base — Privacy

MeshSearch deploys its entire contract suite to **Base Sepolia** and settles all payments there:

- NullifierRegistry — prevents ZK proof replay; each search produces a unique on-chain nullifier
- AccessControl — ENS-verified subscriber list for the relay network
- NodeRegistry — relay operator registry with reputation tracking
- PaymentSplitter — distributes x402 USDC payments to relay operators
- x402 payment flow: 402 → USDC EIP-3009 authorization signed by client → settled on Base Sepolia before query executes
- No account, no email, no KYC — a wallet signature is the only identity

**BEST Overall Project**

## Best Overall

MeshSearch is the only hackathon project that ships a **complete, trust-minimised search stack** — from ZK proof generation in the browser, through ENS-named onion routing, to on-chain micropayments and decentralised encrypted storage — all wired together as an MCP server any AI agent can use out of the box.

Every layer replaces a trusted intermediary with a cryptographic guarantee:

| What you'd normally trust | What MeshSearch does instead |
|---|---|
| Search provider not logging queries | ZK commitment before query leaves device |
| VPN provider not logging traffic | 3-hop onion routing through ENS-named relays |
| Payment processor not linking identity | x402 USDC micropayment — wallet signature only |
| Payment linked to relay operator | BitGo MPC fresh address per disbursement — stealth-address pattern |
| Cloud storage not reading your history | AES-256-GCM encrypted Fileverse dDocs — only your key decrypts |
| DNS / PKI not being compromised | ENS L1 resolution for all relay identities |

It's not a demo of one privacy primitive — it's a production-ready system where **six independent prize tracks' technologies work together as a coherent product**.

The browser UI surfaces every layer in real time: a live **BitGo MPC** status badge in the header, a payment card explaining the stealth-address disbursement before you sign, and a full visualisation of the USDC → Treasury → unique per-relay addresses after every successful search.

> Give your agents memory they can't leak

![Cryptography](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cryptography-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS / Filecoin](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS%20/%20Filecoin-333333?style=flat-square) ![plugins](https://img.shields.io/badge/plugins-333333?style=flat-square) ![Cursor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Cursor-333333?style=flat-square) ![Fileverse](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fileverse-333333?style=flat-square) ![Claude Code](https://img.shields.io/badge/Claude%20Code-333333?style=flat-square) ![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-333333?style=flat-square) ![Agentic frameworks](https://img.shields.io/badge/Agentic%20frameworks-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem

AI agents are stateless by default. Every conversation starts from zero , no memory of past decisions, no context from other tools, no continuity across sessions. Teams hack around this with plaintext files, vector databases, or cloud-hosted memory services, all of which share the same fundamental flaw: **your data is readable by the storage provider.**

This matters because agentic memory isn't just chat history. It's architecture decisions, security audit findings, API keys and rotation schedules, customer-specific context, incident postmortems, and strategic plans. As agents become more capable and autonomous — writing code, managing infrastructure, triaging alerts — the memory they accumulate becomes increasingly sensitive and increasingly valuable to attackers.


### What exists today is broken in three ways:

**1. No privacy.** Cloud memory services (Mem0, Zep, LangMem, etc.) store plaintext or server-side encrypted data. The provider holds the keys. One breach, one rogue employee, one subpoena — and every customer's agentic context is exposed. This is the same trust model we rejected for passwords a decade ago, yet we're repeating it for AI memory.

**2. No access control.** When you give an agent access to memory, it's all-or-nothing. A junior dev's Cursor instance sees the same memories as a principal engineer's Claude Code session. There's no way to say "this agent can read `/engineering/decisions` but not `/finance/runway`." Teams either over-share sensitive context or don't use shared memory at all — both are bad outcomes.

**3. No portability.** Memory is locked to one platform. Context built in Cursor doesn't carry to Claude Code. Knowledge captured in one agent framework dies when you switch to another. Every tool reinvents its own storage format, its own sync mechanism, its own context window stuffing strategy. There's no shared substrate.

### What rok does differently:

rok is an **end-to-end encrypted, hierarchical memory layer** for AI agents built on a dual-key cryptographic architecture.

**How it works under the hood:**

- A **spend key** (Ed25519) is the root of trust. The owner holds this. From it, a **root read key** (X25519) is deterministically derived via HKDF with domain separation (`rok-v1-spend-to-root-read`). Child read keys are further derived per scope path — `/engineering`, `/engineering/decisions`, `/finance/q1` — forming a cryptographic hierarchy.

- When a memory is written, it's encrypted with **X25519 ECDH + ChaCha20-Poly1305** using an ephemeral key pair, signed with the spend key, and serialized into a compact binary envelope (`ROK\x01` header). The storage backend (currently Fileverse decentralized documents) receives only opaque base64 ciphertext. It never sees plaintext, scope structure, or key material.

- **Scope-based access** means a read key for `/engineering` can automatically derive child keys and decrypt anything under `/engineering/*`, but cryptographically cannot access `/finance` or any sibling scope. This is enforced by HKDF derivation paths - not ACLs, not permissions tables, not policy engines. Math, not trust.

- Agents receive **scoped read keys only**. They can decrypt and read memories within their scope, and **propose** new memories — but cannot write directly. Proposals are staged as plaintext that the owner (spend key holder) reviews and accepts. This limits blast radius: a compromised agent can't corrupt the memory store, and a leaked read key only exposes one scope subtree.

- **Batch sync with deduplication**: at session end, the agent extracts new knowledge and calls `rok_memory:sync`. The system reads existing entries, compares content, and skips unchanged memories — avoiding unnecessary re-encryption, signature generation, and HTTP round-trips.

- **Post-quantum ready**: optional hybrid mode combines X25519 with ML-KEM-768 (NIST FIPS 203) for forward security against quantum adversaries.

**How it's delivered:**

rok ships as an MCP server with 9 tools (read, write, list, grant, propose, sync, etc.) that plug into any MCP-compatible environment: Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, or custom agent frameworks. Session hooks auto-load memories at conversation start and prompt sync at conversation end. The StorageBackend trait is pluggable: Fileverse today, any HTTP-compatible store tomorrow.

One encrypted memory layer. Scoped cryptographic access control. Zero trust in storage. Works everywhere MCP works.

**tl;dr: rok gives AI agents persistent, end-to-end encrypted memory with hierarchical access control enforced by key derivation, not permissions. Think 1Password meets agentic context, if the vault were decentralized and every agent got exactly the keys it needs and nothing more.**

**The problem it solves**

Most small businesses are ran by non-technical people - and their entire online presence is on Airbnb, Instagram, or a Google listing and have no website of their own. They know they need one - it drives direct bookings (no platform fees), helps them rank in search, and makes them look legit - but actually getting one is a slog.

Normally you'd have to write code, push it to GitHub, deploy to Vercel, buy a domain from GoDaddy, and spend hours hunting for photos, writing copy, and laying out the page. Most homestay owners, cafés, and tradesmen are never going to do that - so they just don't, and leave money on the table.

Rowbo collapses that entire stack into a single conversation. We take a link from your existing social media profiles, and the agent scrapes your photos and details, builds you a real site, then lets you tweak it, and puts it live on your own custom domain - hosting subscription and domain both paid for - in the same platform. No code, no accounts, no juggling five providers.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest one was getting a Prava payment to actually complete after approval. We'd set up the mandate, the owner would approve with their passkey… and then nothing - the site never went live and no charge landed.

We were polling the session's payment-result to detect success, which is the right call for a one-off checkout. But for a mandate the session just sits at authorized forever - approval only authorises the mandate, it doesn't move any money. We only worked that out by pulling the Vercel logs (which surfaced a CHARGE_NOT_REPORTABLE error) and then hitting the Prava API directly to watch the session state stay stuck at "authorized" with no credentials issued.

The unlock was realising the money moves when you charge the mandate: POST /v1/mandates/{id}/charge issues the virtual-card credentials, and then you report the outcome to get visaConfirmation: SUCCESS. Prava's webhooks aren't live yet either, so we built the completion as a poll: after the card is sent, the agent watches for the freshly-approved mandate, charges it, reports it, and only then flips the site live - plus a tweak to handle the sandbox auto-settling the charge instantly. Once that clicked, the whole thing ran end to end: approve → charge → site live → confetti.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

Rowbo is an AI agent initiating a real transaction on a user-approved, controlled Visa credential that buys domains and subscribes to hosting for websites. 

Prava mints a Visa virtual-card credential (token plus dynamic CVV) that the agent uses to complete the purchase on the owner's behalf. The result is verifiable rather than self-reported - a completed charge returning visaConfirmation: SUCCESS - which means our backend can continue with a domain purchase / deployment of their website.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Rowbo is a real working product that scrapes and generates users websites from their existing social media links. This is perfect for non-technical users like homestay owners, cafe's or even tradesmen - who want a site to portray their work, take direct bookings or even just boost their site rankings.

Now, we are getting ready to cold outreach to these businesses, with the subject line of "I built you a free website" - and they will just need to pay the £30/month hosting and any domain they choose to purchase. 

The underlying engine we built - multi-tenant site generation, real Stripe subscription billing at £30/mo, a self-serve editor, and automated custom-domain provisioning — is running today at rowbo.dev, and the hackathon layer adds the part that makes it a company worth scaling: an AI that can acquire and activate a customer entirely over text, collapsing "find lead → build site → close sale → go live" into a single conversation. 

We proved the whole path tonight end to end: a real owner (Chris) got a generated site, paid through Prava, and is now live on a genuine registered custom domain, chrishomestay.top (DNS provisioned, SSL issued, serving) - all from an iMessage.

**OpenAI**

The rowbo agent is built on OpenAI function-calling (gpt-4o). It runs the whole conversation and decides what to do at each step - when to scrape the listing from airbnb, build the site, send the preview, change the look, take the payment, and buy a domain - all through a set of tools we gave it.

It remembers the conversation, so a quick "yes" or "make it blue" always does the right thing without asking twice. From one inbound text, OpenAI takes the owner the whole way to a paid, live website - no forms, no dashboard, just the agent making the calls.

**iMessage Agent**

The rowbo agent lives entirely inside a iMessage thread over Linq - and allows users to build, deploy and buy domains all from a text. An owner texts us that they'd like a website, the agent asks for their Airbnb link, and from that single message it scrapes their listings, generates a real site, sends it back as a tappable rich-link card, takes edits by text, sells the subscription with a Prava checkout card, and puts the site live - all in Messages. 

We lean into Linq's native surface to make it feel alive: rich-link cards for the preview and the payment, tapback polls to choose a custom domain, confetti when the payment lands and fireworks when the domain goes live, typing indicators while it works, and HMAC-verified inbound webhooks driving the whole loop.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

Usually to create a website, you have to code, upload your code to github, deploy your codebase to vercel, buy a domain from GoDaddy, and spend hours alone finding the right photos, typing the right copy, and laying out your page how you like it. 

Imagine you could do all of that stack with one provider, through one iMessage conversation. That's how easy it is with rowbo.dev

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/voltshield-b3d4) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Akshay-coder17/VoltShield) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/zWfLNasRdwE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-6-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> voltzz

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

VoltShield AI solves the multimillion-dollar problem of industrial "silent killers"—microsecond power anomalies like voltage sags and harmonic distortions that easily bypass traditional fuses but silently destroy the sensitive logic boards of automated factory machinery (such as CNC units or robotic lines). By replacing slow, reactive manual troubleshooting with a high-frequency, multi-agent digital twin, the system utilizes an autonomous Plan-Act-Reflect loop running at 60Hz to detect electrical anomalies, calculate the mathematical inverse wave, and simulate a corrective power injection to stabilize the grid before equipment damage occurs. Plant managers can visually track this stabilization through a fluid, cyberpunk-inspired, dark-mode HUD optimized to render real-time telemetry at 60FPS without system lag, while an integrated GenAI agent eliminates days of administrative overhead by instantly translating millisecond-level telemetry logs into formal, engineering-grade insurance and utility compliance reports.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was ensuring that the autonomous agent could effectively stabilize the power system after anomalies such as voltage sag, harmonic distortion, and phase imbalance were introduced. Initially, the correction algorithms often overcompensated, causing instability in the balanced waveform. To overcome this, we implemented a feedback-based reflection mechanism that continuously measured residual error and adjusted the agent’s response dynamically. Another challenge was maintaining smooth real-time communication between the simulator and dashboard through WebSockets. We optimized the data streaming process and telemetry structure to achieve reliable real-time performance and consistent visualization across the system.

**Gen AI&ML**

VoltShield aligns with the Generative AI and Machine Learning track by demonstrating an autonomous AI agent capable of perceiving, reasoning, acting, and learning within a simulated power-grid environment. The system continuously monitors three-phase electrical signals, analyzes disturbances such as voltage sag, harmonic distortion, and phase imbalance, and decides the most appropriate corrective action without human intervention.

The project follows an Agentic AI architecture consisting of Plan, Act, and Reflect stages. The agent analyzes incoming telemetry data, evaluates system health, applies corrective strategies, and learns from previous disturbances to improve future responses. This mimics the decision-making workflow of modern AI agents.

From a Machine Learning perspective, VoltShield provides a foundation for training anomaly detection and predictive maintenance models using data generated by its digital twin environment. The simulator can create labeled datasets representing different grid conditions, enabling the development of classifiers and forecasting models for real-world applications.

By combining digital twins, adaptive learning, autonomous reasoning, and future ML-driven anomaly detection, VoltShield demonstrates how AI can move beyond simple prediction to intelligent decision-making and self-correcting system management.
