**The Problem NexusPay Solves**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/12037b7fa4fd4be69a4202e157816284/6d009ed7-9859-4801-8c4e-2f78ace16527.png)
x402 is powerful. It's also painful to integrate.

The protocol is promising but getting it production ready means handling cryptographic verification, on-chain transaction validation, real-time price checks, and middleware wiring yourself. Most developers give up and fall back to Stripe  which means account approvals, webhook management, subscription tiers, and billing dashboards that AI agents fundamentally cannot use.
Neither option was built for the agentic web. NexusPay is.

How Exactly we solve it?

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/12037b7fa4fd4be69a4202e157816284/63fa335c-89f8-42d1-a8e8-1cba6fa08bb8.png)
**- Monetize Any API in 3 Lines of Code**

No Stripe account. No x402 boilerplate. No infrastructure overhead. Drop in the paygateNext middleware, set a price, set a wallet  and you're live. Any AI agent that hits your endpoint gets a 402, pays in USDC on Base, and retries with proof. The whole handshake is handled for you.
You ship. You earn. That's it.
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/12037b7fa4fd4be69a4202e157816284/576481d6-601a-4733-b039-81edc27fca57.png)

**- Two Sided Marketplace where AI Agents Hire Humans. Humans Hire AI.**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/12037b7fa4fd4be69a4202e157816284/f6fa1499-678a-4032-b5f5-7b81437d61c0.png)

Not every task belongs to an agent. Not every task belongs to a human. NexusPay brings both sides together in one marketplace. AI agents hire humans for what machines can't do, and humans hire AI agents for what would take them hours. Both sides transact seamlessly, on-chain, in real time.
The right worker for every job. Every time.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/12037b7fa4fd4be69a4202e157816284/0d115784-684f-4dc4-8af9-dfe9c93506f2.png)





**- One Marketplace. Every API Your Agent Will Ever Need.**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/12037b7fa4fd4be69a4202e157816284/55ec873d-90d1-4631-84f7-3fa4ebba678d.png)

Once your API is live, it doesn't sit in a void. NexusPay lists it in a curated marketplace of 100+ monetized APIs all x402-compatible, all instantly callable by any AI agent. Agents stop being hardcoded to single providers and start discovering the right tool, at the right price, on demand. For builders, it's instant distribution. For agents, it's a catalogue of superpowers.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/12037b7fa4fd4be69a4202e157816284/f3d13c46-276f-401d-b773-198d3d54a2c9.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

****1.  x402 Payment Retry Race Condition****

When an agent got a `402` and retried with payment, the middleware was checking the transaction too fast  before the blockchain had actually confirmed it. So valid payments were being rejected and agents kept retrying forever.

Fixed it by waiting for **2 block confirmations** before accepting any payment as valid.

**2. **USDC Approval Silently Killing Transactions****
 

USDC needs a one-time `approve` before any contract can spend it. What we didn't realize is that allowance gets used up over time — so mid-workflow, agent payments started silently failing with a vague error and no clear reason why.

Fixed it by checking the remaining allowance before every payment and topping it up automatically when it runs low.

Most Web3 projects fail because they make users deal with the hard parts upfront: buying crypto, setting up wallets, understanding gas fees. People leave before they even see what the product does. LapLogic flips that. You connect your wallet, you get GameCoin instantly, and you're playing. No friction, no prior crypto knowledge needed.
The game itself is built around the 2026 Formula 1 season. You act as a team principal : picking 3 drivers and 1 constructor under a 60 million GameCoin cost cap. Since driver prices reflect real-world performance, you can't just pick the obvious names. You have to think smart, spot undervalued picks, and back your F1 knowledge. Before each race, an AI integration generates fresh prediction challenges based on real conditions like weather, track history, and championship standings , so every weekend feels different.
The core mechanic that makes it unique is what you do with your remaining budget. Whatever GameCoin is left after building your team, you can invest into the race pool. Your return depends on how well your strategy performs against other players. Better knowledge, better picks, better return. (Skill is directly tied to reward)
Everything runs on a smart contract on Polygon, so payouts are automatic, transparent, and go straight to your wallet. Your earnings are yours : no platform holding them, no approval process, no delays. F1 is booming globally and Web3 adoption is accelerating. LapLogic sits right at that intersection, at exactly the right time.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest part was Solidity. Writing smart contracts is one thing but getting deployment right on Polygon, making sure the contract logic actually synced with the backend, and debugging on-chain errors without straightforward error messages took way more time than expected. Web3 development has a very unforgiving feedback loop compared to normal backend work.
Working in the Web3 space also meant we could not test with real money at any stage. Everything had to run on testnet, which adds a layer of uncertainty because you are never fully sure how things behave until there is actual value on the line.
On the AI side, the prediction generation currently runs on a local 8 billion parameter Llama model. It works, but the quality and depth of the predictions is something we know can be much better. It is one of the clearest things we want to improve going forward.

**The problem it solves**

#  Problem It Solves

Modern campuses generate a significant amount of waste daily, yet there is **no effective system to track, incentivize, or reward responsible disposal behavior**. Students often lack motivation to segregate or properly dispose of waste because:

*  No immediate benefit or feedback
*  No accountability for individual contribution
*  Existing systems rely on manual effort (QR scans, reporting, etc.)
*  Sustainability efforts feel invisible and unrewarding

---

#  How BIN2COIN Solves This

BIN2COIN transforms waste management into a **smart, automated, and rewarding system** using IoT and Blockchain.

##  Key Improvements

###  1. Eliminates Manual Effort

* No need for QR scans or manual input
* Students simply:

  * Tap RFID card
  * Drop waste
* System automatically:

  * Identifies user
  * Measures weight
  * Logs data

---

###  2. Creates Accountability & Transparency

* Every waste deposit is:

  * Tracked per user
  * Stored in database
* Enables:

  * Individual contribution tracking
  * Fair measurement of impact

---

###  3. Introduces Gamification

* Converts waste into **points and tokens**
* Encourages:

  * Healthy competition
  * Consistent participation
* Makes sustainability **engaging and fun**

---

###  4. Real Reward System (Token Economy)

* Points are converted into **GC tokens**
* Tokens can be:

  * Redeemed for food/items
  * Used in campus ecosystem
* Adds **real value to sustainable behavior**

---

###  5. Secure & Trustless System (Blockchain)

* Rewards are:

  * Transparent
  * Tamper-proof
* Ensures:

  * No fake entries
  * Fair distribution

---

#  Impact

BIN2COIN turns passive sustainability into an **active, measurable, and rewarding experience**.
 Students are no longer just “throwing waste”
 They are **contributing, earning, and competing**

---

#  Final Outcome

> **“From Trash to Tokens — making sustainability visible, measurable, and rewarding.”**

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

Building BIN2COIN involved integrating **hardware (IoT), backend systems, and blockchain**, which introduced several real-world challenges.

---

##  1. Arduino Upload & Hardware Issues

**Problem:**
While setting up the Arduino Nano, I faced repeated errors like:

* `not in sync`
* `unable to open port`

**Cause:**

* Wrong processor selection (ATmega168 vs ATmega328P)
* Faulty USB cable / port conflicts

**Solution:**

* Identified the correct processor (**ATmega168**)
* Reinstalled Arduino IDE and drivers
* Used proper reset timing during upload

---

##  2. Load Cell (HX711) Calibration & Inconsistent Readings

**Problem:**
The weight readings were inconsistent or not showing correctly.

**Cause:**

* Raw values from HX711 without calibration
* Wiring issues

**Solution:**

* Verified wiring connections carefully
* Switched to `read_average()` for stable readings
* Treated raw values for hackathon demo instead of full calibration

---

##  3. Arduino → Backend Communication

**Problem:**
Arduino cannot directly send HTTP requests using Arduino Nano.

**Cause:**

* No WiFi module on Arduino Nano

**Solution:**

* Built a **Serial → Node.js bridge**
* Used `serialport` in Node.js to read Arduino output
* Sent data to backend API using Axios

---

##  4. Managing Real-Time IoT Logic

**Problem:**
Continuous RFID scanning caused multiple triggers and duplicate entries.

**Cause:**

* No session control logic

**Solution:**

* Implemented a **state machine system**:

  * RFID Scan → Timer → Weight → Send → Reset
* Added cooldown period to prevent repeated scans

---

##  5. Backend Data Consistency

**Problem:**
Handling cases where:

* User exists vs does not exist
* Dustbin capacity overflow

**Solution:**

* Added validation logic:

  * Check user by UID
  * Allow waste logging even if user not found
  * Prevent deposits if dustbin is full

---

##  6. Blockchain Integration Complexity

**Problem:**
Understanding how to:

* Convert points → tokens
* Send tokens via smart contract

**Solution:**

* Simplified logic:

  * **1 Point = 1 Token**
* Used `ethers.js` to interact with contract
* Created a backend function to call `rewardStudent()`

---

## 7. Token Transfer vs Approval Confusion

**Problem:**
Initially confused between:

* `transfer`
* `transferFrom`
* `approve`

**Solution:**

* For hackathon simplicity:

  * Used direct `transfer` approach
  * Avoided complex approval flow

---

#  Key Learning

> Integrating hardware + backend + blockchain is not just about coding —
> it requires **debugging real-world systems, handling edge cases, and simplifying complex flows**.

---

#  Final Takeaway

Despite multiple challenges, each issue helped improve the system’s reliability and design.
The result is a **fully working end-to-end solution combining IoT, backend, and blockchain**.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In peer-to-peer (P2P) online marketplaces and shipping contracting, **trust is the biggest bottleneck.**
- **Buyers** are afraid of paying upfront and never receiving the promised goods or services.
- **Sellers** hesitate to ship products or deliver work without guaranteed payment.
- Traditional escrow services charge exorbitant fees (often 5-10%), hold funds for agonizingly long periods (3-5 business days), and rely on opaque, centralized dispute resolution processes that are prone to human bias and error.

Additionally, international transactions are plagued by high currency conversion fees and slow wire transfer speeds.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building decentralized legal frameworks involves overcoming systemic barriers:

### 1. Smart Contracts are not Recognized Legally Everywhere
* **Challenge:** Code is not always recognized as "law" in traditional jurisdictions. If an on-chain arbitration occurs, one party might attempt to sue off-chain in a local court, creating legal friction.
* **Mitigation:** TradeVault requires users to sign an explicit "Terms of Use" that designates the smart contract and subsequent arbitration results as legally binding arbitration under the New York Convention (or local equivalents). We bridge the gap by combining cryptographic signatures with formatted, printable PDF legal agreements generated upon deal creation.

### 2. Lack of Awareness / Web3 Friction
* **Challenge:** Non-crypto-native users are intimidated by wallets, gas fees, and token names.
* **Mitigation:** We utilize Account Abstraction and user-friendly wallets (like Lute Wallet via email login). The UI abstracts away "MicroAlgos" and "Teal" and simply shows terms in familiar USD equivalents. Our onboarding focuses entirely on the P2P safety benefits rather than the underlying blockchain tech.

### 3. Oracles bridging "Real-World" Delivery Status
* **Challenge:** Blockchains cannot intrinsically know if a physical item was delivered.
* **Mitigation:** We utilize trusted backend oracles bridging carrier APIs (UPS, FedEx, DHL) to write tracking verification hashes to the blockchain. We also support "Instant Handover" cryptography involving QR-code scanning for in-person local deals.

### 4. AVM Foreign Asset & Account Access
* **Challenge:** The Algorand Virtual Machine requires all foreign assets (e.g. USDC ASA ID) and foreign accounts (e.g. seller's wallet) to be explicitly declared in the outer transaction before inner transactions can reference them.
* **Mitigation:** All contract calls include `foreignAssets: [USDC_ASSET_ID]` and `accounts: [sellerWallet]` in the transaction payload, ensuring the AVM has full context for every inner transfer it needs to execute.

**Web3**

**Trustless custody.** No company holds the money — a smart contract does.

**Permissionless access.** No bank account, no KYC, no institution required to participate.

**Immutable agreements.** Contract terms written on Algorand cannot be altered by either party after signing.

**Cryptographic acceptance.** Karim's wallet signature is mathematically verifiable proof of agreement — stronger than any wet signature.

**On-chain proof of shipment.** Tracking hash stored permanently on Algorand — nobody can claim delivery was never submitted.

**Automatic trustless settlement.** Payment releases by code, not by a human decision.

**Permanent reputation.** Trade history lives on-chain forever — unfakeable, undeletable, publicly verifiable.

**Algorand**

Algorand fits TradeVault for five reasons that are not interchangeable with any other chain.

USDC is native. Circle issues USDC directly on Algorand — no wrapping, no bridging, no additional risk layer. The contract holds and releases real USDC.

Fees are flat and near-zero. Every transaction costs $0.002 regardless of trade size. On Ethereum the same escrow flow costs $15–60 in gas — economically impossible for sub-$5,000 trades. Algorand makes the target market viable.

Atomic transactions are a protocol feature. Karim's acceptance signature and USDC transfer are grouped atomically — both succeed or neither does. This is not application logic. It is guaranteed at the protocol level.
Finality is 4 seconds. No confirmation waiting periods, no chain reorganisation risk. Funds lock or release instantly in user-visible time.

The AVM is constrained by design. The contract is 120 lines, 7 methods. Algorand's execution environment limits complexity, eliminates reentrancy by default, and makes the class of exploits that caused the DAO hack structurally impossible here.

> Your password is how you move.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Passwords, OTPs, and 2FA codes can be stolen, phished, or coerced out of people, yet most authentication systems have no way to detect or respond to these scenarios.
VAULTLESS solves this by replacing static credentials with a behavioural biometric profile built from how you naturally type and move. It captures **keystroke rhythm, mouse dynamics, touch patterns, and device motion, signals unique to you that can't be lifted from a database or handed over under pressure.**
It specifically addresses three gaps existing systems ignore:

**Stolen credentials:** no password means nothing to steal or phish
**Coercion:** if someone forces you to log in, VAULTLESS detects the stress in your typing pattern and silently redirects the attacker to a decoy session while alerting your security contact
**Audit gaps:** every authentication event (success, failure, or duress) is permanently logged on an Ethereum smart contract, giving you a tamper-proof record

No specialist hardware. No shared secrets. Works on **PC, Android, and iOS**- using touch and motion sensors on mobile for an even richer behavioural signal.
Built for anyone who needs **security that protects people, not just accounts.**

**Challenges we ran into**

*Scoring consistency:* Early on, the same user would get different scores across attempts due to minor typing variations. Fixed it by averaging three enrollment samples and weighting hold times 3× so the dominant signal carried more influence.
*Tuning the duress zone:* Deciding where "stressed but plausible" should sit took a lot of trial and error. Too tight and real users got flagged. We added a second condition, rhythm variance must exceed 2.5× the enrollment baseline, so both signals had to fire together.
*Mobile sensor fallbacks:* Different browsers expose different APIs, and iOS requires a permission prompt most users dismiss. Built the engine to fuse whatever signals are available so it never fails hard, keystrokes carry the full weight when motion data is absent.

**Ethereum Track**

VAULTLESS is built on **Ethereum Sepolia** as its trust layer - not as an afterthought, but because the **core security guarantee of the system depends on it.**
Every enrollment, authentication, duress event, and failed attempt is permanently logged on-chain via **VaultlessCore.sol**, a **custom Solidity contract** deployed on **Sepolia**. The contract stores a **keccak256** commitment hash of the user's biometric vector - meaning the actual behavioural data never leaves the browser, but a cryptographic proof of it *lives on Ethereum forever*. This makes authentication records honest, tamper-evident, and user-owned rather than controlled by any server.
We used **Remix IDE** to write and deploy the contract, **MetaMask** as the injected wallet provider, **Ethers.js** **v6** to interact with the contract from the frontend, and **Sepolia Etherscan** to verify and monitor transactions in real time.
The contract also implements **nullifier-based** replay protection - each successful authentication burns a unique **keccak256(vectorHash + walletAddress + timestamp) nullifier on-chain**, so a captured transaction can never be reused to impersonate a user.
The duress protocol goes further: when coercion is detected, a *DuressActivated event is emitted on-chain before silently loading a decoy session*. This creates a permanent, timestamped, public record of the coercion attempt that no attacker can erase - something no traditional auth system can offer.
***Ethereum is the core of our trust model***. Without it, authentication records are just logs on a server someone controls. With it, every enrollment, every login, every duress event is a permanent, user-owned, **cryptographically verifiable** fact that no company, no admin, and no attacker can alter or delete.

**The problem it solves**

## The Broken Ad Economy

Traditional online advertising is fundamentally broken:

- **Publishers** get pennies while platforms take 70%+ of ad revenue
- **Viewers** see thousands of ads yearly and earn exactly $0
- **Advertisers** pay middlemen, not the people actually seeing their ads
- **Privacy** is sacrificed — every click, scroll, and view is tracked and sold

### Web3Ads Fixes This

**Fair Revenue Distribution:**
| Stakeholder | Traditional Ads | Web3Ads |
|-------------|-----------------|---------|
| Publishers | ~30% | **50%** |
| Viewers | 0% | **20%** |
| Platform | ~70% | 30% |

**For Viewers — Get Paid to Browse:**
- Install the Chrome extension, link your wallet once
- Earn ETH automatically every time you see an ad
- Withdraw anytime with **$0 gas fees** — we pay the gas
- Your data stays private via zkProof identity (Semaphore)

**For Publishers — Better Revenue, Zero Friction:**
- One React component: `<Web3Ad publisherId="0x..." slot="banner" />`
- 50% of ad spend goes directly to you
- Gasless withdrawals to any wallet
- Real-time analytics on impressions and earnings

**For Advertisers — Pay For Real Engagement:**
- Funds go to actual viewers and publishers, not middlemen
- Smart contract transparency — see exactly where your budget goes
- Target by category (DeFi, NFT, Gaming) with CPM pricing

### Unique Innovations

1. **AI Agent Payments (x402 Protocol):** Users can spend their ad earnings through AI agents. Your Claude can pay for APIs using funds you earned viewing ads — completely gasless.

2. **Privacy-Preserving Tracking:** Semaphore zkProofs prove "this viewer saw this ad" without revealing WHO they are. No cookies, no fingerprinting, no surveillance.

3. **True Gasless UX:** Viewers never need ETH to withdraw. Backend signs EIP-712 messages and pays all gas fees. Web3 without the friction.

4. **MCP Server for AI Integration:** AI agents can create campaigns, check balances, and make payments programmatically via Model Context Protocol.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

**1. Semaphore WASM in Chrome Extensions**
Service workers block WebAssembly blob URLs. Solved by generating Semaphore identity in the client web app and sending it to the extension via postMessage — extension becomes lightweight storage only.

**2. CSP Blocking Extension Detection**
Inline script injection fails on strict CSP sites. Switched to DOM attributes which content scripts can set regardless of CSP policy.

**3. Gasless Withdrawals Without Full Account Abstraction**
Full ERC-4337 paymasters are complex. Implemented simplified EIP-712 signature flow where backend signs authorization and pays gas directly when calling the withdraw function.

**4. USDC Faucet Reliability**
Base Sepolia USDC faucets were unreliable. Migrated to V2 contract using native ETH, requiring updates across smart contracts, frontend hooks, and all payment flows.

**5. Ad Earnings as x402 Payment Source**
Standard x402 requires direct transfers. Built custom "web3ads-balance" payment method that deducts from user's pending earnings — enabling AI agents to pay for APIs without any wallet interaction.

**Privacy**

**How it fits:** Viewers generate Semaphore identities (zkProof) to prove ad views without revealing identity. Nullifiers prevent double-counting while maintaining anonymity.

**Code Implementation:**
- Viewer.tsx — Semaphore identity generation
- index.ts — Nullifier generation per ad view
- index.ts — Proof relay between SDK and extension
- ads.ts — Server-side nullifier verification

## How Web3Ads Fits

AI agents execute real on-chain transactions via MCP server. Claude can withdraw user earnings, create campaigns, and make payments — all settled on Base Sepolia with the backend paying gas fees.

## Transaction Flow

```
AI Agent (Claude) → MCP Server → Backend API → Smart Contract (Base Sepolia)
     │                  │              │                │
     │  "withdraw my    │  HTTP POST   │  Sign & submit │
     │   earnings"      │  to API      │  transaction   │
     ▼                  ▼              ▼                ▼
  User prompt      Tool call      Backend signer    On-chain tx
                                  pays gas fees     executed
```

| `web3ads_create_campaign` | `createCampaign()` | Campaign created, ETH deposited |
| `web3ads_fund_campaign`   | (via API)          | Additional budget added         |

**The problem it solves**

Managing crypto trading and on-chain transactions requires constant monitoring, technical knowledge, and manual execution. OctoHive simplifies this by letting users deploy autonomous AI agents that analyze markets, find optimal routes and exchange rates, and execute transactions automatically — all monitorable from a unified wallet dashboard. Every agent is assigned its own ENS subdomain, giving it a verifiable on-chain identity complete with personality, avatar, and strategy stored as ENS profile records. The platform also features an** Agent Arena, where agents from different users compete head-to-head based on trading performance**, adding a gamified, competitive layer to automated DeFi.

**Challenges we ran into**

Integrating multiple systems like BitGo wallets, AI agents, market analysis tools, and on-chain transaction automation was complex — we solved this by orchestrating the workflow using the Hey Elsa automation layer.
Another challenge was enabling secure autonomous transactions — we addressed this by using Elsa’s x402 framework to safely authorize and execute on-chain actions.

**DeFi**

We built a platform for characterized autonomous AI agents with real on-chain identities that trade on behalf of users without manual intervention.

When a user joins, the system automatically creates a secure BitGo vault wallet and deploys one or more AI trading agents assigned to that vault. Each agent is given controlled wallet access plus a stealth address for executing transactions in the open market, preserving privacy while remaining verifiable on-chain.

🧠 Agent Identity Layer (ENS-based)

Every AI agent is not just a bot — it has a persistent identity.

The platform assigns each agent an ENS subdomain of the user’s domain, creating a readable identity instead of a raw wallet address. This identity contains:

Name

Personality & trading style

Tagline

Historical performance & reputation

Strategy metadata

On-chain activity

These profiles are publicly inspectable, allowing:

Humans to choose trustworthy agents

Other AI agents to evaluate counterparties before trading

Fully autonomous agent-to-agent markets

⚔️ BattleArena — Real-World Strategy Testing

To validate performance safely, we built BattleArena, a competitive sandbox where agents trade against each other using real market data.

Users can:

Pit their agents against others

Stake funds on outcomes

Benchmark strategies transparently

Observe decision-making in real time

Train and refine agent behavior

This creates a merit-based ecosystem where agents earn reputation through performance, not promises.

🔐 Key Innovations

Autonomous AI trading with user-owned custody via BitGo vaults

ENS-based identity system replacing unreadable wallet addresses

Stealth transaction layer for privacy-preserving execution

Agent-to-agent trust via public identity profiles

Real-world competitive testing through BattleArena

Fully on-chain, transparent, and composable

🌐 Vision

We are building the foundation for an Agentic DeFi economy — a world where intelligent agents negotiate, trade, compete, and collaborate on behalf of humans, using verifiable identities instead of anonymous wallets.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem

Every DeFi frontend today has a dirty secret: **it's centralized**.

The smart contracts are on-chain. The tokens are yours. But the website
you use to interact with them? It runs on AWS, Vercel, or Cloudflare
servers controlled by a company that can be hacked, subpoenaed, or simply
decide to pull the plug.

This has already caused real damage:
- **Curve Finance, Uniswap, Balancer** frontends hijacked via DNS attacks
  to drain user wallets
- **Tornado Cash** OFAC pressured the frontend offline within hours
- **Compound, dYdX** geo-blocked entire regions via their hosting provider
- **Hundreds of smaller protocols** taken offline the moment their Vercel
  free tier expired or their domain registrar received a complaint

The smart contract is trustless. The frontend is not. **That gap kills people.**

---

## What Deploy.eth Solves

Deploy.eth makes your entire stack trustless — not just the contracts.

### 🌐 For DeFi Protocol Teams

**Ship a frontend that cannot be taken down.**
```bash
web3deploy push
# ✓ Site live on IPFS (content-addressed, immutable)
# ✓ myprotocol.eth now resolves to your new build
# ✓ No Vercel. No AWS. No domain registrar. No kill switch.
```

Your site lives on IPFS a global peer-to-peer network where files are
addressed by their content hash, not a server location. Nobody can redirect
it, modify it silently, or take it offline. Even if your entire team
disappears, the frontend keeps serving users.

**Store your protocol config on-chain, not in a dashboard.**

Every deploy writes your configuration to ENS text records publicly
auditable, immutable history, readable by your smart contracts:
```
swap.slippage      → 0.5
fee.recipient      → 0x...
fee.bps            → 30
access.policy      → public
monitor.riskLevel  → medium
```

Users can verify exactly what your frontend is configured to do before
they connect their wallet. No more "trust us."

**Require multi-sig approval before any frontend update goes live.**

Malicious frontend updates are one of DeFi's biggest attack vectors.
Deploy.eth lets you require 3-of-5 team signatures before the ENS
contenthash changes making a frontend attack as hard as a smart
contract exploit.

---

### 📊 For DeFi Users

**A live, intelligent frontend powered by Elsa x402 with no backend.**

Because there's no server, there are no API keys to steal, no database
to breach, and no company to subpoena for your transaction history.
Every data call is a direct pay-per-use request:

| What you get | How | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Portfolio across 15+ chains | `elsa_get_portfolio` | $0.01 |
| Live yield suggestions | `elsa_get_yield_suggestions` | $0.02 |
| Best swap quote across 20+ DEXs | `elsa_get_swap_quote` | $0.01 |
| P&L report | `elsa_get_pnl_report` | $0.015 |

Your ENS domain becomes your **personal DeFi config** — store your risk
tolerance, preferred chains, slippage limits, and the site respects them
automatically, every time, on any device, without logging in.

**Your site watches your portfolio even when you're not looking.**

ENS monitor records tell the site what to watch for:
```
monitor.alertThreshold  → 0.15   (alert if 15% drawdown)
monitor.autoRebalance   → true
monitor.preferredYield  → 0.08   (suggest moves if APY < 8%)
```

When conditions are met, your ungoverned frontend surfaces the action.
You confirm. Elsa executes. No email. No notification from a company
that knows your wallet address.

---

### 🔒 For DAOs and Governance-Heavy Protocols

**Make frontend deployments a governance action.**

Right now, a DAO can vote on treasury decisions, parameter changes, and
contract upgrades — but a single developer can push a malicious frontend
unilaterally. Deploy.eth closes that gap.

Every frontend update is a proposal. Signers review the CID diff. The
ENS contenthash only changes when the threshold is met. The full deploy
history — who proposed what, when, with which CID — lives on-chain forever.

**Environment routing without a backend.**
```
myprotocol.eth          → production (CID: bafybeig3...)
staging.myprotocol.eth  → staging    (CID: bafybeia7...)
v2.myprotocol.eth       → beta       (CID: bafybeif2...)
```

Each subname is independently owned. Staging can move fast. Production
requires governance. All of it lives in ENS — no DevOps, no infra bill.

---

### 🛠 For Developers

**One command. Everything decentralized.**
```bash
npx web3deploy init    # scaffold config
web3deploy push        # build → IPFS → ENS → done
web3deploy rollback    # one command back to any previous deploy
web3deploy env set swap.slippage 0.3  # update on-chain config
```

No accounts to create. No credit card. No vendor lock-in. If Deploy.eth
shuts down tomorrow, your site keeps running — the files are on IPFS,
the domain is in ENS, the history is on-chain. The platform is optional
infrastructure, not a dependency.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. ENS `contenthash` encoding is not what you think it is

The first wall I hit. ENS doesn't store a raw IPFS CID string in the
`contenthash` field — it stores a binary-encoded value following a
specific multicodec spec. Passing a raw CIDv1 string to the resolver
contract just reverts silently.

The CID has to be encoded as:
```
0xe3010170 + varint(cid-length) + cid-bytes
```

The `0xe3010170` prefix encodes the namespace (IPFS), the version, and
the codec. Miss any byte and the ENS gateway refuses to resolve it —
with no error message, just a blank page.

**Fix:** Used `@ensdomains/content-hash` library which handles the
encoding correctly. But it took hours to diagnose because the ENS
resolver accepts the malformed transaction — it only fails silently
at resolution time, not at write time.
```typescript
import { encode } from '@ensdomains/content-hash';
const encoded = encode('ipfs', cid); // '0xe301017012...'
```

---

### 2. IPFS CIDs change every build even when nothing changes

The second major hurdle. Vite's build output includes chunk hashes in
filenames — `index-BvXk3a91.js` — so every build produces a different
`dist/` tree even if the source hasn't changed. Every different tree
produces a different root CID. This meant every `git push`, even a
README typo fix, produced a new CID, a new ENS transaction, and ~$5-15
in gas fees on mainnet.

**Fix 1:** Switched to deterministic chunk naming in `vite.config.ts`:
```typescript
build: {
  rollupOptions: {
    output: {
      entryFileNames: 'assets/[name].js',
      chunkFileNames: 'assets/[name].js',
      assetFileNames: 'assets/[name].[ext]',
    }
  }
}
```

**Fix 2:** Added a CID comparison step in the deploy script — reads the
current ENS `contenthash`, decodes it, compares with the new CID, and
skips the ENS transaction entirely if they match:
```typescript
const currentCid = await getCurrentEnsCid(domain);
if (currentCid === newCid) {
  console.log('CID unchanged, skipping ENS update');
  process.exit(0);
}
```

Gas saved. Sanity restored.

---

### 3. Elsa x402 payment tokens expire mid-pipeline

The x402 payment flow generates a short-lived JWT-style payment token
before each API call. In a multi-step pipeline —
`get_portfolio` → `get_yield_suggestions` → `execute_swap_dry_run` —
if any step takes longer than expected (slow IPFS pin, RPC congestion),
the token for the next step has already expired by the time you use it.

This caused the swap dry-run to fail silently, returning a `402 Payment
Required` response that I initially mistook for a broken endpoint.

**Fix:** Generate payment tokens lazily — immediately before each
individual API call rather than upfront for the whole pipeline:
```typescript
// ❌ Wrong — tokens generated upfront, may expire
const tokens = await generateTokens(['portfolio', 'yield', 'swap']);
await getPortfolio(tokens[0]);
await sleep(3000); // tokens[1] may already be stale
await getYield(tokens[1]);

// ✅ Correct — token generated fresh per call
await getPortfolio(await generateToken('portfolio'));
await getYield(await generateToken('yield'));
await executeDryRun(await generateToken('swap'));
```

---

### 4. ENS text record updates require a separate resolver transaction

I assumed updating the `contenthash` and updating text records could
be batched into one transaction. They can't — at least not on the
standard public resolver. Each `setText` call is a separate transaction,
and with 8 text records to update per deploy (CID, timestamp, framework,
env, tx hash, version, build command, node version), the deploy script
was firing 9 transactions sequentially.

At ~15 seconds per transaction confirmation and gas for each, a full
deploy was taking 3+ minutes and costing more in gas than the hosting
was worth.

**Fix:** Used ENS's `multicall` on the resolver contract, which batches
multiple `setText` and `setContenthash` calls into a single transaction:
```typescript
const resolver = await provider.getResolver(domain);
await resolver.multicall([
  resolver.interface.encodeFunctionData('setContenthash', [node, encoded]),
  resolver.interface.encodeFunctionData('setText', [node, 'deploy.cid', cid]),
  resolver.interface.encodeFunctionData('setText', [node, 'deploy.timestamp', ts]),
  // ... all 8 records
]);
```

One transaction. One gas fee. Deploy time dropped from 3 minutes to
under 30 seconds.

---

### 5. IPFS gateway resolution lag breaks the "instant deploy" experience

After updating the ENS contenthash to a new CID, there's a propagation
delay before IPFS gateways (ipfs.io, cloudflare-ipfs.com, eth.limo)
actually serve the new content. The CID is correct in ENS immediately,
but visiting `myapp.eth.limo` still shows the old version for anywhere
from 30 seconds to 5 minutes.

Users opening the site right after a deploy would see the old version
with no indication that a new one exists — confusing and undermining
trust in the platform.

**Best creative use of ENS**

Our project treats ENS as a programmable deployment and coordination layer for Web3 apps, not just a wallet alias.

What we built

We let builders deploy directly from a GitHub repo to IPFS, then bind that deployment to an ENS-linked subname.
Every new deploy updates onchain metadata so the ENS name becomes a live pointer to the latest decentralized frontend.
This turns ENS names into versioned, human-readable app endpoints instead of static identity labels.

Why this is a creative ENS use

ENS as decentralized hosting: We use ENS-linked content addressing so the name resolves to a decentralized website, not a centralized server.
ENS as programmable app registry: Subnames act like app namespaces for teams, environments, and products.
ENS as trust surface: Users can interact with DeFi interfaces through memorable names, reducing copy-paste risk from raw addresses and random URLs.
ENS as composable state: Deployment metadata can be attached and resolved through ENS-compatible records, enabling wallets, explorers, and dapps to consume the same canonical app identity.

**Software**

**CoEvolve Sandbox** fits strongly within the Open Innovation track by addressing an emerging challenge at the intersection of Generative AI, autonomous software development, and cybersecurity. As AI coding agents become increasingly capable of writing and modifying software, ensuring that their outputs remain secure is a continuously evolving problem. Our project proposes an innovative, self-improving security framework that allows coding agents to learn from verified failures without retraining their underlying models.

The system creates a continuous attacker–developer co-evolution loop: an Attacker LLM generates adversarial coding tasks, a Developer LLM attempts to solve them, and a Hybrid Judge validates vulnerabilities using both static analysis (SAST) and dynamic exploit replay (DAST). Confirmed failures are transformed into natural-language security rules and incorporated into the developer agent's system prompt. This creates a non-parametric alignment mechanism where defensive capabilities evolve while model weights remain frozen.

The project demonstrates innovation through adaptive Elo-based difficulty, hardened Docker isolation, regression guarding, Git-backed prompt evolution, and portable security rules. It already supports multiple LLM providers, three programming languages, 29 SAST rules, and 19 vulnerable applications for DAST validation.

Therefore, CoEvolve is not simply another cybersecurity scanner; it is an **adaptive innovation platform for continuously improving the security of autonomous AI coding systems**, with potential to evolve alongside new models, attack techniques, and software environments.

> Autonomous AI Position Manager for DeFi Options

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![options](https://img.shields.io/badge/options-333333?style=flat-square) ![Thetanuts Finance SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Thetanuts%20Finance%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

DeFi options are useful for hedging, but managing them is still difficult. A user has to watch spot prices, expiry, liquidity, dealer positioning, and the changing options book, then decide whether to buy protection, hold, close, or roll a position. That is a lot to monitor manually, especially when market conditions move quickly.

> **The problem:** options protection is valuable, but interpreting the market and acting safely is too manual for most users.

GammaShield turns this into a **guarded workflow**, not an open-ended trading bot.

It reads the live Thetanuts OptionBook for BTC and ETH on Base, combines it with live spot-market data, and explains the market's dealer-gamma and liquidity conditions in a single dashboard. The user can review a real options quote and make a normal wallet-signed trade. For autonomous hedging, the user first creates a dedicated ERC-4337 policy account and signs a mandate with clear limits: asset, maximum loss, trade size, allowed actions, risk thresholds, persistence, cooldown, expiry, and pause/revoke controls.

The agent monitors the market, but it cannot spend outside those signed rules. Before any action, GammaShield rechecks the market, confirms that a fresh eligible quote exists, and applies the on-chain policy guard. This makes options protection easier to use while keeping the user in control of the money and the rules.

In practice, GammaShield helps users:

| What a user needs | How GammaShield helps |
| --- | --- |
| Understand a fast-moving options market | Translates the live Thetanuts book, spot prices, dealer gamma, liquidity, and expiry into an understandable risk view. |
| Review a potential options trade | Surfaces real Thetanuts OptionBook opportunities and fresh SDK-built quotes. |
| Automate cautiously | Lets the user set bounded hedging rules instead of handing a private key to a bot. |
| Stay in control | Supports pause and revoke controls before any later policy-account fill. |
| Learn safely | Provides a complete Base Sepolia policy-account flow before using Base mainnet. |

**Challenges we ran into**

| Challenge | What we did | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Making autonomous execution safe instead of simulated** | Replaced fixed application-level guards with owner-signed EIP-712 mandates and ERC-4337 policy accounts. | The policy account enforces signed limits, pause state, revocation, risk evidence, persistence, and cooldown—not a backend private key or hardcoded cap. |
| **Separating a live quote from an executable order** | Kept RFQ estimates advisory and enable trades only after a fresh SDK preview validates a listed order. | The agent cannot treat a price estimate, synthetic contract, or stale order as executable. |
| **Testing without misrepresenting a testnet as Thetanuts mainnet** | Built `ShadowOptionBook` on Base Sepolia for policy signing, funding, UserOperations, execution receipts, and positions. | Users can test the guarded flow without real funds, while the UI clearly distinguishes Shadow positions from Thetanuts positions. |
| **Operating under real RPC and upstream limits** | Narrowed and paged chain-log queries, added bounded retries and fallbacks, and cached short-lived snapshots. | The dashboard handles rate limits and upstream failures clearly instead of silently showing mock data. |
| **Making AI useful without letting it override the user** | Treated AI as a policy-drafting and second-opinion assistant; deterministic logic and the signed policy remain the final gate. | An unavailable or malformed AI response cannot bypass the user's limits or create a trade. |

**BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK**

Thetanuts is GammaShield's live options venue. We use the SDK server-side to read and normalize the Base OptionBook for BTC and ETH, power the risk dashboard, construct fresh quotes, and generate exact approval/fill calldata for eligible listed orders. A connected wallet signs a mainnet fill. GammaShield then uses the live book to calculate dealer-gamma and market-structure risk, show per-contract risk and trade impact, and gate policy decisions on a fresh eligible quote.

**AI × OPTIONS**

GammaShield uses AI where it helps most: converting a complex live book and risk model into a policy draft and readable second opinion. It does **not** give AI unrestricted execution. AI cannot raise signed limits, bypass risk checks, invent an executable order, or send funds. Every autonomous action still requires live market checks, a fresh SDK-safe quote, deterministic logic, and the user's on-chain policy.

GammaShield combines AI assistance with verifiable user controls. The result is a more understandable and safer way to use DeFi options—not a black-box trading bot.

**AI For Society**

GammaShield uses GonkaRouter to build a high-public-value Multi-Model Market Rumor & Narrative Fact-Checker. It cross-examines viral claims across independent models on the Gonka Network, scores their factual and structural threat (0–100% Truth Score), exposes transparent reasoning traces and verifiable Gonka Request IDs, and equips the public with actionable financial protection.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nuttyduoduel-c9fc) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/POTATO0826/MUBA.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://taygood-project.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ezUYEzhZRFE?si=skrsCG6fN87KmW0Q) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Options trading as a 1v1 game

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chainlink](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chainlink-333333?style=flat-square) ![sepolia](https://img.shields.io/badge/sepolia-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![bun](https://img.shields.io/badge/bun-333333?style=flat-square) ![Thethanuts sdk](https://img.shields.io/badge/Thethanuts%20sdk-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The problem it solves

Anyone can read a betting slip. Almost nobody can read an options chain.

Sports betting took $167B in wagers in the US last year and 51% of active accounts belong to 21–34 year olds — people already comfortable taking a position, who never sat a course to do it. Options ask for strike, delta, implied volatility and moneyness before your first trade, so that audience never arrives. The liquidity isn't the bottleneck. The interface is.

THETADUEL puts two familiar game formats on top of Thetanuts Finance's live options book on Base, so a first-time user takes a real options position without being taught the vocabulary first.

Parlay. The game deals you a few cards. Each is up or down on a coin, and how far you think it moves. Every card is a real option bought off Thetanuts' order book. Under the hood a "tier" is a delta band queried against live resting orders, not a difficulty setting we invented — so the "70% chance" a beginner reads and the "delta 0.70" a trader reads are the same number, and there is no second vocabulary to unlearn later. A card only exists if a real order backs it; when the book has nothing in that band, the card renders as a dead slot rather than a number we made up.

Draw a box. Drag a price band and an expiry on a chart. That box is a four-strike zone option: it pays maximum if the price lands inside your band at expiry, decays through the wings either side, and is worth nothing outside them. If the box matches a zone a market maker has already listed, it fills straight off the OptionBook as a RANGER. If it doesn't — which is most boxes, since the book carries only about three zones per asset-expiry — it goes to the OptionFactory's sealed-bid RFQ as a CALL_CONDOR, where the player names their own max bid and market makers answer.

Why the reward is honest. Draw a tighter box, or pick a bigger move, and the contract is cheaper to buy — so the same payout divided by a smaller premium is a bigger multiple. We never wrote a payback rate. Every multiplier on screen is derived from a real premium off the book, and because every position is a bought option, max loss is the premium and it's printed above the upside on every card.

Two players stake to enter, lock blind, and the better position takes the pool. The duel scores in minutes on mark-to-market return on premium — so it isn't a size contest — while the option itself settles at its own expiry, on chain.

How we built it
Thetanuts SDK @thetanuts-finance/thetanuts-client 0.3.0 on Base — live order book, MM pricing, greeks, previewFillOrder / fillOrder, and the OptionFactory RFQ path (buildCondorRFQ, requestForQuotation, settleQuotationEarly).
Chainlink price feeds on Base for the chart history behind the box grid, so the chart reads the same oracle the option settles against.
React + TypeScript + Bun, wagmi / viem / RainbowKit for wallets.
DuelEscrow.sol — stake, winner-takes-pool, with an unconditional refund path so a duel that never resolves returns both stakes without anyone signing.
An EIP-712 attestor that re-derives the winner from committed picks and its own market snapshot — it never signs a winner a client claims.
Market data sits behind one MarketSource interface, so every live feature degrades to a frozen fixture and the seeded game runs fully offline.

We also ran three measurements against Base mainnet before building the RFQ path

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges we ran into

The docs and the shipped SDK disagree in ten places. We built a probe harness and verified every claim against the live chain, committed at tnuts-test/FINDINGS.md. Example: the docs cap the MM fee adjustment at 3e-4; the shipped code uses 4e-4 and live data agrees. We treat our measurements as the source of truth, not the docs.

RANGER looked like the perfect instrument and isn't mintable. It has exactly the payoff our box needs and Thetanuts calls it unique to them — but client.ranger exposes only payout, close, split and transfer. There is no create method anywhere in the SDK. So the box fills a listed RANGER off the book, and mints a CALL_CONDOR through RFQ when nothing matches.

The book is not a ladder. Real strikes cluster ~$20 apart near spot and $100+ in the wings, and expiries are tomorrow, the day after, then weeklies. An evenly spaced grid would have promised instruments that don't exist, so the box snaps to strikes that actually carry orders and the grid is irregular by design.

Settlement is terminal, not path-dependent. We initially assumed a box meant "price stays in the band." It doesn't — the price has to land there at expiry. Every line of copy on that screen had to change.

There is no testnet for Thetanuts. It's Base mainnet only, so every rehearsal of a fill costs real money. We put a $2 cap in code above the network — checked per leg and against the slip sum — rather than in the UI.

Connecting deployed smart contracts to thethanuts frontend to make sure it works on mainnet and testnet

**BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK**

THETADUEL is built on the Thetanuts SDK end to end, and uses both execution venues rather than one.

OptionBook. fetchOrders and getMarketData drive every number on screen — strikes, greeks, MM pricing, depth. Our parlay cards are delta bands queried against live resting orders, so a card only exists when a real order backs it; previewFillOrder and fillOrder execute the picks, with ensureAllowance sized exactly per leg and never MaxUint256.

OptionFactory RFQ. A drawn box that matches nothing listed is minted as a CALL_CONDOR through the sealed-bid auction — buildCondorRFQ, validateRFQRequest, requestForQuotation, settleQuotationEarly — with calculateReservePrice suggesting a bid the player can override, and client.rfqKeys handling the ECDH keypair so offers decrypt.

We also use client.ranger to identify listed zones, client.utils.calculatePayout and validateCondor for payoff math, and chainConfig.optionImplementations to type every order by product.

**AI × OPTIONS**

AI webscrapes news to help in option trading during parlay game and helps translate live option details into simplified terms for users

### FortiFi
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/fortifi-44af) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/edda1011/FortiFi) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/agt_rEnapqs) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Financial Firewall Between Information and Action

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS3​](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3​-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The problem it solves

Financial information can move markets quickly, but users often have to make decisions based on claims, headlines, or articles that may be misleading, incomplete, or difficult to verify. Even when a claim is identified as risky, users may not have a clear way to understand how that risk could affect their ETH holdings or what protection options are available.

FortiFi addresses this by combining multi-model AI verification with evidence gathering, portfolio risk assessment, and live options protection. It helps users evaluate financial claims before acting, understand potential downside exposure, and discover suitable ETH protection strategies through Thetanuts. The system also provides an auditable record of its analysis and completed protection actions through Sui, making the decision-making process more transparent and verifiable.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges we ran into

One of our biggest challenges was our team's background. We are all cybersecurity students rather than software engineering students, and most of us had limited experience building a complete application involving AI, blockchain, frontend, backend, and smart-contract integrations.

This was also the first or second hackathon for everyone on the team, so we had to learn how to work with unfamiliar technologies while developing the product under a strict time constraint. Integrating multiple external technologies such as Gonka, Thetanuts, Base, and Sui required us to understand APIs, wallet interactions, blockchain transactions, and different development environments simultaneously.

Testing the blockchain components presented another practical challenge. We did not have sufficient funds in our wallets to freely test every on-chain operation, particularly automated contract interactions on Sui. As a result, we had to be careful with testing and work within the available testnet resources while ensuring that the core functionality could still be demonstrated.

Despite these limitations, the challenges forced us to simplify our architecture, divide responsibilities across the team, and focus on delivering a working end-to-end prototype rather than attempting to build every feature to production scale.

**AI × SUI**

FortiFi uses Sui to create tamper-evident records of AI-assisted financial analysis and subsequent protection actions. Financial claims are assessed by multiple AI models through Gonka Router, and users can authorize anchoring a report hash through a Move contract on Sui testnet. After an options purchase on Base, a separate protection record links the analysis report hash to the associated Base transaction. The contract prevents duplicate report hashes, while the backend sponsors the Sui transaction. This gives users a traceable connection between the assessment and the recorded action, allowing saved reports to be checked for changes without publishing their full contents on-chain.

**BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK**

FortiFi integrates the Thetanuts SDK into a guided ETH protection workflow, from live option discovery to wallet-confirmed purchase on Base mainnet. It retrieves OptionBook orders and market data, filters eligible ETH puts, and presents Basic, Balanced, and Strong protection choices based on the user's budget and preferences. Users can compare strike prices, expiry dates, estimated costs, and settlement types before selecting an option. Before execution, FortiFi refreshes the selected order and checks for material changes in price or quantity. The SDK then handles USDC allowance and order execution through the user's wallet, making options protection more accessible through a single interface.

**AI × OPTIONS**

FortiFi connects AI-assisted financial claim assessment with actionable ETH options protection. Through Gonka Router, multiple AI models evaluate submitted claims against retrieved evidence and provide assessments of credibility, potential market impact, and missing context. Connected users can review their ETH exposure and estimated losses under hypothetical price declines. Claim-impact assessments and ETH allocation inform an initial protection preference, which users can adjust alongside their budget. FortiFi then uses live Thetanuts data and rule-based selection to suggest eligible ETH puts. Users review the terms and confirm purchases through their own Base wallet, bringing evidence review, risk awareness, and options execution into one workflow.

**AI For Society**

FortiFi helps users assess potentially misleading financial information before making decisions that could affect their savings or crypto holdings. It uses Gonka Router to compare assessments from multiple AI models alongside retrieved news evidence and available article content. Results present model verdicts, confidence, reasoning summaries, and missing context, helping users understand uncertainty and identify what needs further verification. A faster mode uses two successful model responses, while an optional mode waits for all three. By combining accessible claim assessment with ETH downside scenarios and user-controlled protection choices, FortiFi aims to support financial literacy and more informed decisions when users encounter uncertain or conflicting information.

### PreFlight
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/bold-name-service-or-bns-8c78) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://bafybeib34kld4dhyejv2zxzixen3taalianypy3t7azatlhlan2j5xqyi4.ipfs.inbrowser.link/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/_gXAKlvX8NI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Dora%20Hack%202.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://dora-hack.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> A Browser extension that prefly's every URL

![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vite](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Sandbox Isolation](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sandbox%20Isolation-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most people only discover a site is malicious after it has already loaded, by which time trackers have fired, cookies are set, or a steganographic payload may already be executing.
Preflight flips that model. It acts as a pre-click safety layer:

Intercepts every URL (typed, clicked, or redirected) before the real browser ever resolves the host.
Executes the page in a disposable sandbox with zero network egress and no persistent storage, so even if the site is malicious, only the sandbox is affected.
Delivers a clear, plain-language report that surfaces trackers, fingerprinting scripts, security misconfigurations, known vulnerable libraries, and hidden steganographic data inside images.
Lets the user decide in one tap: Visit (one-time), Leave, Greenlist, or Redlist the domain forever.

In short, it turns the risky act of “clicking a link” into a controlled experiment. Users stay in control, phishing and drive-by threats are stopped before they reach the real browser, and the cognitive load of constantly second-guessing links is dramatically reduced.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest technical hurdles was building a true zero-egress sandbox that still produces a useful scan report under Manifest V3 constraints.
Manifest V3 severely restricts remote code execution and network access inside extensions. Getting a headless/isolated environment that could:

Load an arbitrary URL,
Intercept every network request and API call at the boundary,
Analyse images for LSB / trailing-byte / EXIF steganography,
…and then safely tear itself down with zero residual state

required careful use of sandboxed pages, service-worker coordination, and strict isolation boundaries. Early versions either leaked network requests or couldn’t extract enough signal from the page.
I solved it by treating the sandbox as a completely disposable “crash-test dummy”: the real browser never touches the target origin until the user explicitly chooses to Visit. All analysis happens inside the isolated context, results are postMessaged back, and the sandbox is destroyed. This kept the security model clean while still delivering the depth of scanning (including the steganography decoder) that makes Preflight useful.

### Argus
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/argus-2efe) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Samarth208P/Argus) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://tryargus.netlify.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Road%20To%20Devcon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://road-to-devcon-iitr.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The lie detector for Ethereum RPCs — one endpoint

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

## 1. Honest nodes kept "lying" (client diversity)
Geth, Erigon and Reth return different extra fields for `eth_getBlockByNumber`, so comparing full objects flagged honest nodes as deviant.
**Fix:** compare only the consensus-critical tuple `(hash, parentHash, stateRoot, transactionsRoot)` — false positives gone.

## 2. The "latest" tag made truth subjective
Honest nodes legitimately disagree about `latest` due to propagation delay, which would have caused false accusations.
**Fix:** pin every canonical query to an explicit **finalized block hex**. This made "lying" objectively definable — and made every piece of evidence reproducible forever via curl.

## 3. The router recommended the worst node
Our first "Best RPC" widget read `scores[0]`, but the query was sorted by timestamp — so it recommended whichever provider *finished polling last*, even a score-20 node.
**Fix:** dedupe to the latest row per provider, sort by score, and add safety thresholds (min score 50, score freshness, flagged fail-open instead of silent recommendation).

## 4. "Why should we trust YOUR server?"
Our first architectures kept failing this question. We iterated from client-side → federated observers, and finally landed on **"server is a reporter, not a judge"**: publish raw evidence, commit Merkle roots on-chain, and let a `/verify` page recompute the math in the skeptic's browser. That turned our biggest weakness into the product's core feature.

**The problem it solves**

Every wallet and dApp silently trusts a single RPC provider. If that provider serves stale balances, mutated state, or quietly censors your transaction (published research shows ~46% of mainnet blocks have been produced by censoring builders), you would never know — no receipt, no proof, no recourse.

**Argus is a lie detector and failover router for Ethereum RPCs.**

## What people use it for

- **Devs & wallets:** paste one endpoint (`/api/rpc`) into any dApp or wallet. Argus pools the major free public RPCs plus any paid ones you add, routes every request to the highest-integrity live provider, and auto-fails-over the instant one degrades.
- **Auditors & skeptics:** click any flag to see raw evidence — expected-vs-got diffs, a reproducible `curl` frozen at a finalized block, explorer links, and an on-chain attestation. The `/verify` page re-runs our open-source math in *your* browser and checks it against on-chain Merkle roots: `browser math == server verdict == on-chain hash`.
- **The ecosystem:** a public, tamper-evident reputation ledger for RPC providers — accuracy, uptime, latency, censorship flags, and improving/degrading trends over time.

## How it makes things safer

- Cross-examines 8+ providers every 20s at pinned finalized blocks, reaches an independence-weighted consensus, and classifies deviations as `DEVIANT / STALE / CENSORING / DOWN`.
- A dedicated probe EOA detects write-path censorship that read-only checks can never see.
- The server is a **reporter, not a judge**: raw evidence is public, hourly Merkle roots are committed to Sepolia, and anyone can recompute every verdict. A server that cannot lie undetectably.

**Censorship Resistance**

Argus implements both directions of this track — a consensus-driven decentralized RPC aggregator and a verifiable routing layer — as one shipped product.

**Consensus mechanism among providers (aggregator):** Every 20s Argus fans out identical canonical queries to 8+ RPC providers, pinned to a *finalized* block, normalizes and hashes the responses, and selects truth via an independence-weighted majority vote (one operator = one vote, so a single company running many endpoints cannot fake a majority). If no group holds >50%, the poll is marked INCONCLUSIVE instead of guessing.

**Accurate data selection:** Outliers are retried before accusation and classified as `DEVIANT / STALE / CENSORING / DOWN`. A dedicated probe EOA runs differential write-path tests to catch silent transaction filtering — the censorship mode read-only checks can never see.

**Load balancing:** A single `/api/rpc` endpoint routes every request to the highest-integrity live provider (integrity → uptime → latency), with automatic failover and hot-swap the instant a provider is flagged.

**Verifiable routing infrastructure:** Every accusation ships with independently checkable evidence: expected-vs-got diff, a reproducible `curl` frozen at the pinned block, explorer links, and an on-chain attestation. Hourly Merkle roots of all polls are committed to Sepolia so history can never be rewritten. The `/verify` page re-runs the open-source math in the user's own browser: `browser math == server verdict == on-chain hash`.

The tool itself practices what the track preaches: no trusted center — the server is a reporter, not a judge, observers are replaceable, and Ethereum holds the log.

### x402-prava-bridge
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/xpravabridge-d4f1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/predgeAI/x402-prava-bridge) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://data.predge.io/.well-known/x402) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/2C0CaqXD0iM) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Agentic%20Commerce%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://agentic-commerce.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-4-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Card-only AI agents pay any wallet-only x402 API

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![x402](https://img.shields.io/badge/x402-333333?style=flat-square) ![prava](https://img.shields.io/badge/prava-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Since then the bridge grew into a full agent. Its brain is OpenAI — function/tool calling decides which paid endpoint to buy (100% routing accuracy across 120 eval cases). 

The same agent also lives in iMessage via Linq: you text it, it buys Predge data over x402 and replies in the bubble. And Predge itself is published as verified, machine-discoverable citeables via Senso (signed ed25519 outcomes, live on cited.md) with GEO monitoring across ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini. 

One card-only agent — on the web, in iMessage, and across the agentic web.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Two payment rails that don't share a language.** x402 speaks EIP-3009 USDC authorizations; Prava speaks cards + passkeys. 
The bridge had to read an x402 '402' challenge, translate the amount into a Prava payment session, complete the card charge, *then* settle the crypto leg — and keep the human in control on the expensive path.

**Passkey in a cross-origin iframe.** The card leg first ran with Prava's embedded SDK, but WebAuthn passkey creation is blocked inside a cross-origin iframe and kept failing ("Security Check Failed" / "Authentication couldn't be completed"). Fix: switch to Prava's **hosted 'full_checkout'** mode so the passkey runs same-origin on Prava's own page. Sandbox auth is also flaky — retrying the passkey/OTP a couple of times clears it.

**Keeping the demo honest and free.** Rather than spend real mainnet USDC on every test, I pointed the x402 leg at **Base Sepolia** so the settlement is a real on-chain transaction that costs nothing — while the same code path settles real USDC on Base mainnet against the live Predge API.

Publishing honestly: the Senso onboarding can auto-generate case studies, but Predge has no real named customers — so we deliberately withheld fabricated case studies and published only factual, source-grounded content.

**Best Visa Intelligent Commerce Implementation**

The transaction flows through Visa's rails via Prava: a single-use, network-tokenized Visa credential, authorized by the cardholder with a **Visa Payment Passkey** (biometric WebAuthn) on Prava's hosted checkout. That is the whole point of the bridge — it lets a card-only AI agent pay a crypto-native, wallet-only x402 API using a tokenized Visa card instead of a private key.

We map directly to the track's judged axes — **permissions, trust, controls**:
- **Permissions / controls:** a spend-policy gate sits in front of every 402. Small machine calls run autonomously under a standing Prava mandate; anything above the cap **escalates to a passkey**, so the human explicitly approves expensive spend. The limits are set by the human, not the agent.
- **Trust:** the card is never exposed to the agent or the merchant — it's a single-use Visa network token. Every bridged payment is audit-logged, and the paid data carries a machine-readable 'outcome_verified' trust flag.
- **Intelligent commerce:** this widens the buyer market for every x402 seller from "agents holding USDC" to "any agent with a Visa card" — the agent decides it needs data, pays with a card, and gets the data, end to end.

Evidence in the demo: the Prava hosted checkout (VISA ···· 2465), the passkey approval, "Payment Successful", the bridge reporting the charge APPROVED, and the paired on-chain USDC settlement.

**Most Startup-Ready Product**

Not a hackathon toy — this is shippable today:

- **Live seller:** Predge is already an x402 API in production on Base mainnet, with real paid routes ($0.005–$0.03/call), on-chain settlement, and an audit trail.

- **The unlock:** today x402 sellers can only be paid by the tiny set of agents holding USDC on the right chain. The bridge lets ANY agent with a card pay them — a crypto-native niche becomes a mass market.

- **Already shipping** across web, iMessage, and discoverable feeds.

Ready to onboard paying agents now, not "someday".

**Participation Credits (Already Claimed)**

We genuinely used our OpenAI participation credits to power the agent's brain — gpt-4o-mini via function/tool calling (planning, trust audit, and reply generation), including a 120-case eval (100% routing accuracy) and the live iMessage demo. 144+ real API calls, visible in the usage dashboard.

**OpenAI**

The agent's brain is OpenAI (src/brain.mjs, gpt-4o-mini) at three points:

- **Plan (tool calling):** two buy-tools — buy_whales_latest and buy_wallet_history({wallet}) — with tool_choice=required. The model's tool call IS the purchase decision: which paid Predge x402 endpoint, which wallet.

- **Trust audit:** a call reads the outcome_verified flag and states what to act on vs discount.

- **Answer:** a final call writes the reply over the bought data.

`npm run eval:brain` measures the planner at 100% routing accuracy across 120 labeled cases. Without a key it falls back to regex — so OpenAI is doing the real commerce decision.

Code: github.com/predgeAI/x402-prava-bridge/blob/main/src/brain.mjs

**iMessage Agent**

A real two-way iMessage agent on Linq's Partner API:

- Inbound message.received webhook → OpenAI plans the query
- The agent BUYS Predge whale data over x402 (pays per query)
- Replies via /chats/{id}/messages — right in the iMessage bubble

Live demo: text the Linq number, get back a verified whale-trade answer. It's genuine agentic commerce inside a text thread — not a chatbot; the agent pays on-chain for what it sends.

Repo: github.com/predgeAI/predge-imessage

**Agent Commerce Discovery & Trust**

We used Senso to make Predge discoverable and trusted by AI.

Via the Senso CLI we built a knowledge base grounded in predge.io:

- 7 folders, 12 sourced docs, brand kit, 40 tracking prompts
- 40 drafts generated
- **3 verified citeables published live on cited.md** — e.g. cited.md/article/what-proof-does-predge-give-that-a-track-record-is-real
- GEO monitoring across ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini

That's the track exactly: **Discovery** (machine-findable feeds) + **Trust** (signed, ed25519-verified outcomes).

No fabricated content — case studies withheld since Predge has no named customers yet.

**Best Agentic User Experience**

The UX is the spend-control surface:

- **Frictionless when cheap:** small machine payments run autonomously under a standing Prava mandate — no interruptions.
- **Human-approved when it matters:** anything above a threshold escalates to a passkey (biometry), so the person stays in control of expensive spend.
- **Accountable:** every call is audit-logged.

And the agent meets users where they already are — in an iMessage thread (via Linq):

- You text a question in plain English
- It plans (OpenAI), buys the data (x402), and replies in the bubble
- With a trust flag: win rate verified, PnL modelled

Frictionless when cheap, human-approved when it matters, conversational throughout.

**Agentic Commerce Hackathon**

Agentic commerce at its core: a card-only AI agent buying from a wallet-only x402 API — a transaction that couldn't happen before.

The gap:

- Sellers of machine data (like Predge, a live x402 API) accept only USDC on-chain.
- Most agents only have a card, not a funded crypto wallet.

What the bridge does:

- Reads the HTTP-402 challenge
- Charges the agent's card via Prava
- Settles the USDC leg on-chain
- Returns the paid data — with an OpenAI brain deciding what to buy

It ships across three surfaces — web, iMessage (Linq), and discoverable feeds (Senso) — turning "agents that can pay" from a crypto-native niche into any agent with a card.

Real merchant, real prices ($0.005–$0.03/call), real on-chain settlement.
