### DRaffle – Decentralized Raffle System
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/draffle-decentralized-raffle-system-657e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sathwikraminedi/DRaffle-Decentralized-Raffle-System.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1NpNE3CbS2OkPEW6VWbNNJE9FJP3hZcKf/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=107714882685270986394&rtpof=true&sd=true) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-INNOVAT3-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://innovat3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> ''Fair Raffles. Powered by Blockchain.''

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![npm](https://img.shields.io/badge/npm-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional raffle and lottery systems are usually controlled by a central organizer. Participants must trust that the organizer will record all ticket purchases correctly, select a winner fairly, and distribute the prize honestly. However, this process often lacks transparency, making it difficult for participants to verify whether the raffle was conducted fairly. In many cases, users may face issues such as manipulated results, hidden participant lists, delayed payouts, or even fraud.

DRaffle addresses these problems by using blockchain-based smart contracts to automate and secure the entire raffle process. Instead of relying on a centralized authority, the raffle logic is executed on-chain, meaning all actions are transparent, verifiable, and tamper-proof.

When users participate in a raffle on DRaffle, their ticket purchase is recorded on the blockchain, creating a permanent and publicly verifiable record of participation. The smart contract stores all participants and manages the prize pool automatically. When the raffle ends, the contract selects a winner using on-chain logic and automatically transfers the prize directly to the winner’s wallet.

This approach removes the need for trust in an organizer and ensures that the system operates fairly, securely, and transparently.

What People Can Use DRaffle For

DRaffle can be used in many real-world scenarios where fairness and transparency are important:

Online raffles and giveaways for communities or events

Gaming tournaments where the prize pool is distributed fairly

Community reward systems for Web3 projects

Fundraising raffles for charities with transparent prize distribution

Event-based lucky draws where participants can verify results on-chain

By leveraging blockchain technology, DRaffle simplifies the raffle process while making it more secure, transparent, and trustworthy for everyone involved.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into

During the development of DRaffle, several challenges arose while integrating blockchain logic with the frontend application.

1. Smart Contract Deployment Issues

One of the initial hurdles was compiling and deploying the Move smart contract on the Aptos blockchain. Incorrect address configurations in the Move.toml file caused deployment errors. This was resolved by carefully configuring the contract address and recompiling the project using the Aptos CLI tools.

2. Wallet Integration

Connecting the frontend to the user's wallet was another challenge. Ensuring that the application could properly detect the wallet and handle transaction signing required correct configuration of the wallet adapter and handling asynchronous responses from the blockchain.

3. Managing On-Chain Data

Storing and retrieving participant data from the smart contract required understanding how Move handles resources and vectors. Debugging transaction failures and ensuring that participant entries were recorded correctly took several iterations.

4. Synchronizing Frontend with Blockchain State

Another challenge was updating the UI after blockchain transactions. Since blockchain operations are asynchronous, the frontend had to wait for transaction confirmations before reflecting updated raffle data. This was solved by implementing proper transaction status handling and refreshing the state after successful confirmations.

Through debugging, documentation research, and testing different configurations, these issues were resolved, leading to a stable decentralized raffle application.

SATHWIK RAMINEDI

### Q Chain
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/q-chain-32c7) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Jiyansh-2006/qchain2) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://www.q-chain.xyz/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtube.com/watch?v=cWVzL5h_DiE&feature=youtu.be) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-INNOVAT3-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://innovat3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Unbreakable Today. Unstoppable Tomorrow.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MetaMask](https://img.shields.io/badge/MetaMask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Zero--Knowledge%20Proofs%20(ZKPs)-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Core Problem: Classical Blockchain Cryptography is Quantum-Vulnerable
Modern blockchains — including Ethereum and Algorand — rely on ECDSA / Ed25519 elliptic-curve cryptography for signing transactions. These are mathematically vulnerable to quantum computers running Shor's Algorithm, which can derive private keys from public keys, potentially allowing:

Theft of wallet funds at scale
Forgery of transaction signatures
Undermining the trust model of all existing blockchain infrastructure

This is not a theoretical risk — NIST finalized three PQC standards in August 2024 (CRYSTALS-Dilithium, Falcon, SPHINCS+), and regulators like the NSA's CNSA 2.0 framework are already mandating quantum-safe migration timelines. Algorand itself executed the first mainnet Falcon-1024 transaction on November 3, 2025, signaling the urgency of this transition.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/990a6c5930474e4bb66b2d37f31934aa/f5a1015f-44d2-4aa9-9ac3-3b89011b07b8.png)


In short: Q-Chain solves the gap between the emerging quantum threat and practical blockchain usability, making PQC-enhanced blockchain interaction accessible to developers and students through a real application, not just theory.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenge A: Algorand Pera Wallet — Web Integration via Deeplink
This was a genuinely hard engineering problem that very few developers have tackled cleanly.
The core difficulty: Pera Wallet is fundamentally a mobile-first wallet. It does not have a browser extension like MetaMask. To use it on a web app, you must:

Generate a WalletConnect deeplink or use the @perawallet/connect SDK
Display a QR code or redirect URL that opens Pera on mobile
After the user approves the connection on their phone, the web app must listen for the session approval event and receive the connected account address
When submitting transactions, the web must construct the unsigned transaction, send it over the WalletConnect bridge, wait for the user to sign it on mobile, and receive the signed transaction back
Then broadcast the signed transaction to the Algorand node

What went wrong / the challenge:

The WalletConnect v2 bridge and Pera SDK have inconsistent behavior between environments — sessions would drop, reconnect events wouldn't fire reliably, and the web app would lose track of wallet state after mobile approval
Mobile redirect flow: After deeplink approval, returning to the browser didn't always trigger the correct state update — requiring careful event listener management and session persistence
Transaction monitoring after approval: The web dashboard needed to track transaction IDs and poll the Algorand indexer (or node) to confirm when a transaction submitted from mobile had settled on-chain — this polling loop had to be built manually since there's no native push from Pera to web
PQC layer integration: Algorand's PQC support (Falcon-1024) is currently opt-in via CLI-generated keys and not yet natively exposed in the standard AlgoSDK for dApps, making it extremely non-trivial to layer PQC signing into a web transaction flow — your team had to either simulate this layer client-side or use experimental SDK features

Technical resolution path:

Use @perawallet/connect with persistent WalletConnect session storage
Implement polling against the Algorand Indexer REST API (/v2/transactions/{txId}) to confirm settlement
For PQC: generate Falcon key pairs client-side using a WASM-compiled library (e.g., liboqs-js) and embed the PQC signature as a note field or ARC-2 metadata on the Algorand transaction, since native AVM PQC verification isn't yet web-accessible

Challenge B: NFT Minting on Both Algorand Testnet and Sepolia Ethereum Testnet
On Algorand:

NFTs on Algorand are ASAs (Algorand Standard Assets) created via the AssetCreateTxn
Minting requires the creator account to have sufficient ALGO for the minimum balance requirement (0.1 ALGO per ASA created)
Testnet faucet limitations and opt-in requirements (receivers must opt-in to receive the ASA) created friction
If Pera wallet was used to sign the asset creation transaction via the web bridge, the multi-step flow (create → opt-in → transfer) had to be choreographed carefully, with each step waiting for the previous transaction to confirm
ARC-3 / ARC-69 metadata for NFT URI pointing to off-chain storage (IPFS) required careful JSON construction and IPFS pinning in the flow

On Ethereum Sepolia:

Deploying an ERC-721 contract to Sepolia via MetaMask or a web3 provider is straightforward in theory, but using a pre-deployed contract address requires ensuring the ABI matches and the safeMint() function is exposed correctly
Sepolia faucets have rate limits and are often congested, causing insufficient funds errors during testing
Gas estimation failures: If the minting function had any revert path (e.g., duplicate token IDs, access control), the transaction would silently fail at the estimation stage, which is hard to debug without good error handling
If you were also trying to attach PQC metadata to the Ethereum NFT (e.g., in the tokenURI or as on-chain data), the gas cost became significant and sometimes caused out-of-gas errors on testnet with limited ETH

Cross-chain coordination challenge: Your dashboard needed to display minting status from both chains simultaneously, meaning you had to manage two different provider instances (AlgoSDK + ethers.js/viem), two different transaction lifecycle models (Algorand's round-based finality vs Ethereum's block confirmation), and two different wallet connection states — all in a single coherent UI.

[Jiyansh Kushwah](https://github.com/Jiyansh-2006)

Recruiters check verified skills on-chain.

Solidity smart contracts

**Challenges we ran into**

Wallet Authentication Issues

One challenge was integrating wallet authentication using MetaMask. Sometimes the connection failed or the wrong network was selected.
Solution: I added network checks and prompts asking users to switch to the Polygon network before interacting with the smart contract.

Smart Contract Verification Logic

Designing a secure verification system was difficult because mentors should only verify skills once.
Solution: I added mappings in the Solidity contract to track verified mentors and prevent duplicate validations.

Storing Project Proof Securely

Storing project files directly on the blockchain was expensive.
Solution: I used IPFS for decentralized storage and stored only the IPFS hash inside the smart contract.

Skill Graph Visualization

Displaying verified skills in a dynamic graph was challenging.
Solution: I used a JavaScript visualization library to create an interactive skill graph based on verified skills from the blockchain.

Blockchain Transaction Delays

Blockchain transactions sometimes took time to confirm, affecting user experience.
Solution: I added loading states and transaction status indicators to inform users while the verification was recorded on chain.

> Trustless Escrow on Chain for the workforce

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contract](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contract-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![foundry](https://img.shields.io/badge/foundry-333333?style=flat-square) ![Sepolia Testnet](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sepolia%20Testnet-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

****Problem Statement****
**Escrow on Chain** resolves to solve a fundamental dilemma faced by freelancers, contract workers, and clients. In many cases, for a given project, the Freelancers, or the contract workers does not want to start the project until they are either paid some amount or full amount for the project. Similarly the Clients do not wish to pay until the project is completed. 

****Solution****
**Current Solution:**
To combat this, current solutions require involving a third party, such as a bank, or a lawyer. These third parties would hold on to the funds until the end of the project, and resolve disputes in case. 

However, they charge a hefty fee and can be biased in case of a dispute. 

**Our Solution**
Escrow on Chain allows a sender (Client) to lock their funds in the smart contract until the duration of the project. Once the receiver sees that the funds are locked in they can start working. 

Once the project is completed, the sender can release funds, and they would be sent to the receiver. The sender cannot call the funds back. 

In case of failure in delivery, the receiver has the option to refund the funds locked in the smart contract back to the sender.   

The sender can Create an Escrow.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/125343d8a10b45f4945b4751ac51ad49/8e60da16-e76d-4566-8024-cac8c1519858.png)

The Sender can see all their escrows, including the released, refunded, and have the option to release funds from a locked Escrow. 

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/125343d8a10b45f4945b4751ac51ad49/881f3750-96e6-49f2-8a07-87314557819d.png)

Similarly the Receiver can see all the escrows related to them as well, and have the option to refund a pending escrow.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/125343d8a10b45f4945b4751ac51ad49/8cbf0561-3e3f-47a6-8f76-91b70aec55e9.png)

> DeFAI YieldGuard — Global AutoYield Agent

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most DeFi users leave yield on the table — not because they don't care, but because
optimizing across protocols like Aave V3 and Morpho Blue requires constant monitoring,
DeFi expertise, and manual transactions. APYs shift every few hours, and no one has
time to watch a dashboard all day.

**Vatiin AI solves this by giving every user a personal on-chain AI agent.**

- **Set it in plain English.** You write one sentence — "Maximize yield with low risk
  on stablecoins" — and the agent understands your intent, risk tolerance, and goals.
  No DeFi knowledge required.

- **It runs 24/7 without you.** Powered by Qwen 3 235B (235-billion parameter MoE model)
  via Alibaba DashScope, the agent continuously evaluates yield opportunities and decides
  when and where to rebalance — autonomously.

- **Fully on-chain execution.** Every rebalance is a real transaction on Base. The agent
  calls Aave V3 or Morpho Blue directly through auditable smart contracts. You can verify
  every action on BaseScan.

- **Non-custodial by design.** Your funds never leave your control. The agent only moves
  assets between whitelisted yield protocols — it cannot withdraw to arbitrary addresses.

- **Dual automation guarantee.** Chainlink Automation triggers the agent on-chain every
  6 hours. A cron fallback on the backend ensures execution even if Chainlink is delayed.
  You get true 24/7 uptime.

In short: Vatiin AI turns passive DeFi participation into an active, intelligent yield
strategy — without requiring the user to do anything after the initial setup.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. Chainlink Automation + Custom Logic Contract Integration

Getting Chainlink's `AutomationCompatibleInterface` to correctly trigger our
`YieldOptimizerCore` was non-trivial. The `checkUpkeep` / `performUpkeep` pattern
requires the contract to be registered on the Chainlink Automation registry with
sufficient LINK balance, and the ABI encoding of `performData` had to match exactly
what our consumer contract expected. We debugged this by writing a local simulation
script that replayed the upkeep call before deploying to Base Sepolia.

### 2. Qwen 3 235B JSON Schema Validation

The LLM occasionally returned reasoning text wrapped around the JSON payload, or
used slightly different key names. This caused silent failures in the yield execution
pipeline. We solved it by adding a strict JSON extraction step with regex fallback,
and a Zod schema validator that rejects malformed responses before they reach the
on-chain execution layer.

### 3. SSR + Wagmi / RainbowKit on Astro

Astro's server-side rendering conflicted with Wagmi's client-side wallet hooks.
Components using `useAccount` or `useConnect` would throw hydration mismatches.
The fix was isolating all wallet-dependent components as Astro islands with
`client:load`, and wrapping them in a custom `WagmiProvider` that only initializes
on the client.

### 4. Auto-redirect Loop on Landing Page

After fixing the wallet connect flow, users who were already connected would get
silently redirected to `/dashboard` within 2–3 seconds of landing on the homepage.
The bug was in `WalletConnect.tsx` — a `useEffect` watching `isConnected` was
triggering `window.location.href = '/dashboard'` on every render. We removed the
auto-redirect entirely and replaced it with a visible "Dashboard" button that appears
when the wallet is connected, giving users full control.

### 5. IndexedDB Persistence Across Dashboard Pages

Each dashboard page is a separate Astro route with its own HTML shell. Sharing
IndexedDB state (transaction history, risk profile) across pages required a
consistent DB schema and careful versioning. We centralized all DB access in
`src/lib/db.ts` with a single `openDB` call and versioned object stores, ensuring
no migration conflicts between page navigations.

**The problem it solves**

Blockchain wallets are completely opaque to regular users. 
When someone sends you a wallet address — is it safe? Is it 
a scammer? A whale? A bot? Without deep technical expertise, 
there's no way to know.

**WalletIQ solves this** by instantly analyzing any Ethereum 
wallet and returning a human-readable intelligence report:

- 🔍 **Risk Score (0-100)** — AI-powered danger assessment
- 🤖 **AI Summary** — plain English explanation of wallet behavior
- 💬 **AI Chat** — ask anything about the wallet in plain English
- 📊 **Transaction Visualization** — chart of activity over time
- 🚩 **Red Flag Detection** — automatically spots suspicious patterns
- 🏷️ **Wallet Profiling** — tags like DeFi User, NFT Trader, Whale
- ⚖️ **Wallet Comparison** — compare two wallets side by side
- 📄 **PDF Report Export** — download full intelligence report
- 🦊 **MetaMask Integration** — connect your own wallet instantly
- ⚡ **MongoDB Caching** — repeat lookups are instant

Anyone can use WalletIQ — investors checking if a wallet is 
safe to send funds to, traders analyzing whale wallets, or 
anyone curious about on-chain behavior.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/4bed2ff88e62462299ff72276e1d3fa3/2b7d6bbb-a7e3-402a-877b-66a349701dfb.jpeg)

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Etherscan API Rate Limiting**
Etherscan V2 has strict rate limits. We solved this by 
implementing MongoDB caching — once a wallet is analyzed, 
results are stored and served instantly on repeat lookups, 
reducing API calls by ~80%.

**2. AI Prompt Engineering**
Getting Groq AI (llama-3.3-70b) to return consistent, 
structured risk scores was tricky. We solved this by 
carefully crafting prompts that force the model to analyze 
specific on-chain patterns and return structured JSON data.

**3. MetaMask Web3 Integration**
Injecting window.ethereum and handling account changes 
required careful async handling. We implemented auto-wallet 
detection with live account change listeners.

**4. CORS & Deployment**
Connecting Vercel frontend to Render backend required 
careful CORS configuration and environment variable 
management to keep API keys secure.

**5. AI Chat Context Management**
Building conversational AI on top of live wallet data 
required passing full wallet context to Groq on every 
message. We solved this by fetching cached wallet data 
from MongoDB and injecting it as system context, giving 
the AI full knowledge of the wallet before answering.

### Axion
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/axion-f6ba) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/advikdivekar/axion-innovat3-hackathon) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://aexion.vercel.app) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-INNOVAT3-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://innovat3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> The Operating System for DAOs

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Framer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Framer-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![alchemy](https://img.shields.io/badge/alchemy-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Decentralized governance is broken not because DAOs lack of participation, but because they lack **visibility**. 

Currently, decentralized decision-making suffers from several critical blind spots:
* **Governance Apathy:** Proposals often pass with less than 1% voter participation, and coordinated whale clusters can pass contentious changes without broad community awareness.
* **Invisible Treasuries:** DAO treasuries manage billions in community funds, yet are monitored via manual Etherscan refreshes rather than live P&L dashboards. Treasury movements are effectively invisible until it's catastrophically too late.
* **Silent Security Threats:** Sybil attack clusters, flash loan governance attacks, and delegate capture manipulate outcomes, yet no tool actively monitors for them in real-time.
* **Unrecognized Contributors:** The people building DAOs have no feedback loop to visualize their impact, reputation, or standing within the network.

Teams currently stitch together Snapshot, Etherscan, Dune, Discord, and Tenderly five separate tools with no shared context or AI synthesis. 

**The Solution: Axion**
Axion is a real-time 3D intelligence platform that acts as a single command center for DAOs. It renders the entire DAO governance proposals, treasury flows, contributor networks, and security threats as a living neural network in 3D space. 

It solves the visibility problem by integrating:
1. **Four Specialized AI Agents** (powered by Gemini 2.0 Flash) that act as 24/7 domain experts for governance, treasury, security, and operations.
2. **Live Blockchain Data** connected via Alchemy to Ethereum mainnet, providing real-time intelligence on votes, tokens, and events.
3. **Active Threat Detection** using heuristic analysis across six threat categories to flag risks before they execute.
4. **A Multiverse Simulator** that forecasts branching timelines and survival runways for various governance scenarios (e.g., market crashes, exploits).

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a platform that sits at the intersection of Web3, 3D WebGL, and Generative AI presented several complex technical hurdles:

* **Managing 3D State with React:** Rendering a massive, real-time "living neural network" using `Three.js` and `React Three Fiber` required intense optimization. Ensuring the UI layer (sidebar, status bars) remained responsive while particles traveled between 3D nodes in the background meant carefully managing re-renders and abstracting the WebGL canvas from the React DOM tree.
* **Orchestrating Multiple AI Agents:** Implementing four distinct AI agents (HERMES, ATLAS, AEGIS, NEXUS) meant creating a unified router that could dynamically dispatch prompts based on context. Handling the token-by-token streaming from the Gemini 2.0 Flash API via `ReadableStream` and decoding it incrementally in the UI without jank was a major synchronization challenge.
* **Real-time Web3 Data Aggregation:** Fetching live data from the Ethereum mainnet (Uniswap Governor Bravo, UNI token, and Treasury multisigs) using the Alchemy SDK and Ethers.js required aggressive caching strategies. We had to ensure we didn't hit rate limits while keeping the dashboard truly "real-time." 
* **Database Syncing:** Setting up Supabase PostgreSQL with real-time subscriptions for high-frequency events (like live votes or treasury transfers) required writing composite indexes on hot query paths to maintain sub-second latency for the frontend.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Nodejs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Nodejs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

In the digital era, certificates and professional credentials are widely shared online in the form of PDFs or images. However, these documents are **easy to manipulate, duplicate, or forge**, making it difficult for recruiters, institutions, and organizations to verify their authenticity. Current verification processes are often **manual, slow, and dependent on centralized authorities**, requiring emails or direct communication with issuing organizations.

**ProofChain** solves this problem by providing a **decentralized credential verification system powered by blockchain**. Instead of relying on trust in documents, certificates are converted into **cryptographic hashes and recorded on-chain**, ensuring they cannot be altered once issued.

### What People Can Use It For

ProofChain enables **instant and tamper-proof verification** of digital achievements. It can be used for:

- **Academic certificates** issued by universities
- **Hackathon and competition credentials**
- **Professional certifications and training programs**
- **Internship and employment verification**
- **Online course completions**

### How It Improves Existing Systems

ProofChain improves credential verification by making it:

- **Tamper-proof** – Certificates cannot be modified after being recorded on the blockchain.
- **Instantly verifiable** – Anyone can verify authenticity in seconds without contacting the issuer.
- **Transparent and trustless** – Verification does not rely on a central authority.
- **Fraud-resistant** – Prevents the use of fake or altered credentials.

By combining **IPFS storage with blockchain-based verification**, ProofChain introduces a **secure and decentralized trust layer for digital credentials**, making the verification of achievements faster, safer, and globally accessible.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

One of the main challenges we encountered while building **ProofChain** was ensuring that the certificate verification process remained **consistent and tamper-proof** across the entire pipeline — from file upload to blockchain verification.

### File Hash Consistency

Since ProofChain verifies certificates by generating a **SHA256 hash of the uploaded file**, we initially ran into an issue where the same certificate sometimes produced **different hashes**. This happened because small differences in file encoding or metadata could change the hash value, even if the visual content of the certificate was the same.

**How we solved it**

We standardized the hashing process by always generating the hash directly from the **binary file buffer received by the backend**, ensuring that the same file always produces the same cryptographic fingerprint. This eliminated inconsistencies during verification.

### Blockchain Integration

Another hurdle was connecting the backend with the deployed smart contract. Interacting with the contract using **ethers.js** required careful handling of environment variables such as the private key, RPC URL, and contract address. Incorrect configuration initially caused failed transactions and contract call errors.

**How we solved it**

We modularized the blockchain interaction logic into a dedicated service layer, making it easier to manage wallet connections and contract calls while keeping the backend code clean and maintainable.

### IPFS Storage

Uploading certificate files to IPFS also required handling asynchronous responses and ensuring the returned **CID** was properly stored alongside the blockchain record.

By structuring the backend into clear modules (IPFS service, blockchain service, and controllers), we were able to build a **reliable pipeline that securely stores and verifies certificates** across decentralized infrastructure.

## ✨ Core Features

🪙 Milestone-based funding  
🗳 DAO voting mechanism  
🔒 Smart contract escrow  
🏆 NFT milestone achievements  
🔍 Fully transparent on-chain records

ProofFlow is a decentralized platform that enables **transparent milestone-based funding for projects**.
Funds are locked in smart contracts and released **only when milestones are approved by contributors or governance participants**.

The system also **mints NFT achievements** as proof that milestones were successfully completed.

Built as a Web3 prototype for decentralized funding ecosystems.

---

# 🌍 Overview

Traditional crowdfunding releases funds upfront, which can lead to:

* Missed deliverables
* Lack of accountability
* Limited transparency

ProofFlow introduces **milestone-based escrow funding powered by blockchain**.

Funds are **locked on-chain** and only released after milestone verification.

---

## 🎯 Hackathon Alignment

ProofFlow aligns with several Web3 innovation themes:

• DeFi & Payments  
• DAO Governance  
• NFT Creator Economy  
• Web3 Open Innovation  

By combining these technologies, ProofFlow demonstrates how decentralized systems can improve funding transparency.

---

## ⭐ Why This Project Matters

Decentralized ecosystems depend on trustless collaboration.

However, many funding platforms still rely on **trust rather than verifiable delivery**.

ProofFlow introduces a transparent milestone-based funding mechanism where:

• Funds are locked in smart contracts  
• Milestones must be verified before payments  
• Progress becomes visible and immutable on-chain  

This model encourages **accountability, transparency, and trust in decentralized innovation.**

---

# ❗ Problem

Many projects receiving grants or crowdfunding face issues:

| Problem                      | Impact                              |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| Upfront funding              | Reduced accountability              |
| Lack of transparency         | Contributors cannot verify progress |
| Centralized decision making  | Limited trust                       |
| No verifiable delivery proof | Hard to track project progress      |

---

# 💡 Solution

ProofFlow solves this using smart contracts:

✔ Escrow-based funding
✔ DAO-style milestone approval
✔ Automated payment release
✔ NFT achievement proof
✔ Transparent on-chain funding history

---

# ✨ Features

## 🪙 Milestone Funding

Projects define funding milestones with specific amounts.

## 🗳 Decentralized Voting

Funders vote to approve milestone completion.

## 🔒 Smart Contract Escrow

Funds are locked in the smart contract until approval.

## 🏆 NFT Achievement Badges

Creators receive NFT badges when milestones are completed.

## 🔎 Transparent Blockchain History

All funding and voting events are recorded on-chain.

---
# 🔄 How It Works

```
Creator creates project
        ↓
Investors fund project
        ↓
Funds locked in smart contract
        ↓
Creator submits milestone
        ↓
Investors vote
        ↓
Milestone approved
        ↓
Payment released
        ↓
Milestone NFT minted
```

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenge 1: Hardhat Version Conflicts

**Problem**

There were compatibility issues between **Hardhat v3 and several required plugins**. Additionally, the project ran into **ESM vs CommonJS conflicts**, causing scripts and deployments to fail.

**Fix**

* Removed `node_modules`
* Set `"module": "commonjs"` in `tsconfig.json`
* Installed compatible versions of Hardhat plugins (`hardhat-toolbox`)

**Lesson Learned**

Always check **plugin compatibility with the Hardhat version** before starting development.

---

### Challenge 2: RPC Connection Failures

**Problem**

Public RPC endpoints failed during contract deployment with errors like:

* `ENOTFOUND`
* `Invalid Project ID`

**Fix**

* Tested multiple RPC providers
* Switched between **Infura and public RPC endpoints**
* Used `curl` to verify RPC connectivity before deployment
* Maintained **backup RPC URLs**

**Lesson Learned**

Always keep **multiple RPC providers** available when deploying smart contracts.

---

### Challenge 3: Wallet Connection & MetaMask Integration

**Problem**

Users sometimes faced issues connecting their wallet or switching networks when interacting with the dApp.

**Fix**

* Implemented better wallet connection handling using **Ethers.js**
* Added **network checks for Sepolia**
* Improved error handling in the frontend

**Lesson Learned**

Web3 UX requires **clear error messages and network validation**.

---

### Challenge 4: Smart Contract State Synchronization

**Problem**

Frontend state did not always reflect the latest blockchain data immediately after transactions.

**Fix**

* Used **event listeners and contract reads** after transactions
* Implemented **refresh logic for project and milestone data**

**Lesson Learned**

Blockchain data must be **explicitly fetched again after transactions** to keep UI in sync.

---

### Challenge 5: Milestone Voting Logic

**Problem**

Designing a **fair milestone voting mechanism** was tricky. The contract needed to ensure:

* Only funders could vote
* No double voting
* Majority approval before releasing funds

**Fix**

Implemented:

* A **mapping to track voter addresses**
* Voting validation checks
* Majority approval logic before payment release

**Lesson Learned**

DAO-style governance requires **careful validation and edge-case handling**.

---

### Challenge 6: Frontend Layout & Web3 UX

**Problem**

Balancing a **clean dashboard UI** with complex Web3 interactions (funding, voting, NFTs) was challenging.

**Fix**

* Used **React + TailwindCSS**
* Built reusable components for stats, forms, and project actions
* Improved layout with **sidebar navigation**

**Lesson Learned**

Good Web3 apps require **simple UI for complex blockchain actions**.

---

**The problem it solves**

Cryptocurrency markets move 24/7, and prices change constantly. 
Users often miss important price targets while sleeping, working, 
or doing other things. 

CryptoAlert Pro solves this by:
- Tracking prices in real-time (every 30 seconds)
- Allowing users to set custom price alerts for any crypto
- Sending instant browser notifications when prices hit targets
- Keeping an alert history so users never lose track

This means users can focus on their day without worrying about 
missing critical price movements. They get instant alerts exactly 
when they need them.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Real-time Price Synchronization
   - Challenge: Keeping prices updated across all user screens simultaneously
   - Solution: Used Firebase Firestore for real-time data sync and CoinGecko API for live prices

2. Alert Triggering Logic
   - Challenge: Efficiently checking thousands of alerts against live prices
   - Solution: Implemented client-side checking with Firestore listeners to avoid unnecessary API calls

3. Firebase Security
   - Challenge: Ensuring users can only access their own alerts
   - Solution: Implemented Firestore security rules that enforce userId-based access control

4. Mobile Responsiveness
   - Challenge: Making the app work well on both desktop and mobile
   - Solution: Designed with mobile-first approach using CSS media queries

5. Deployment & Environment Variables
   - Challenge: Managing API keys securely on Vercel
   - Solution: Used environment variables in Vercel dashboard (not committing .env files)

> Where Academic Credentials Meet Trust.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![SHA-256 Hashes](https://img.shields.io/badge/SHA--256%20Hashes-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tesseract OCR](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tesseract%20OCR-333333?style=flat-square) ![axios](https://img.shields.io/badge/axios-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3.py](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3.py-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### The Problem it Solves

Academic certificates today are mostly stored and shared in **digital formats**, which makes them vulnerable to **editing, duplication, and forgery using common software tools**. Because of this, employers and institutions often struggle to determine whether a certificate is **authentic or manipulated**.

At the same time, the **verification process is slow and inefficient**. Recruiters typically have to contact universities manually through emails or official requests to confirm a candidate’s credentials. This process can take **days or even weeks**, delaying hiring decisions and creating administrative overhead for educational institutions.

Another major challenge is the **lack of a centralized and trusted verification system**. Most universities maintain their own isolated databases, making it difficult for employers to verify certificates across multiple institutions in a reliable and standardized way.

These issues create opportunities for **fake degrees and altered certificates to enter the job market**, undermining trust between **students, employers, and academic institutions**.

**TrueDegree solves this problem** by enabling a **secure, tamper-proof verification system** where academic certificates can be instantly validated without relying on slow manual processes. This makes credential verification **faster, safer, and more reliable** for everyone involved.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges I Ran Into

While building **TrueDegree**, we encountered several technical and integration challenges during development.

**1. Smart Contract Integration with the Backend**
One of the initial hurdles was connecting the backend application with the blockchain smart contract. Ensuring that certificate hashes were correctly generated and stored on the blockchain required careful handling of **Web3 interactions and transaction confirmations**. We resolved this by restructuring the backend logic and thoroughly testing the API calls that interact with the smart contract.

**2. Generating Reliable Certificate Hashes**
Another challenge was ensuring that the **same certificate always produces the same cryptographic hash**. Even a small change in formatting or metadata could generate a different hash, making verification fail. To solve this, we standardized the certificate processing pipeline and implemented consistent **SHA-256 hashing** before storing the hash on the blockchain.

**3. Document Processing Dependencies**
Setting up tools for document processing, such as OCR and PDF utilities, was another hurdle. Some dependencies required proper installation and environment configuration before the system could correctly extract data from certificates. After troubleshooting PATH configurations and testing multiple setups, we were able to successfully integrate these tools.

**4. Ensuring Fast Verification**
Since blockchain transactions can sometimes take time, we needed to ensure that the verification process for users remained smooth. We addressed this by separating the **certificate issuance process (blockchain write)** from the **verification process (blockchain read)** so that employers could verify certificates almost instantly.

Overcoming these challenges helped us build a more **robust, secure, and scalable certificate verification system.**

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/proofchain-transperent-donation-network-b3c5) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://proofchain-pied.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/ngM_GfR5yL4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-INNOVAT3-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://innovat3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Track every rupee. Prove every impact

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ProofChain is a transparency-focused digital donation platform engineered to eliminate trust issues in traditional charity systems by introducing verifiable, tamper-resistant donation tracking. The platform allows users to discover active fundraising campaigns, contribute to verified NGOs, and monitor the lifecycle of their donations through a secure and traceable transaction framework. When a user submits a donation, the system generates a globally unique Donation ID and computes a cryptographic hash using a blockchain-inspired hashing mechanism, creating a tamper-evident digital fingerprint of the transaction. This hash is derived from key parameters such as the donation amount, timestamp, donor identifier, and campaign ID, ensuring that any modification to the data would invalidate the hash. The transaction is recorded in the backend database as an immutable entry, while the system updates campaign funding metrics and logs the event in a real-time activity dashboard. A dedicated Donation Verification Engine enables users to independently validate their contributions by entering the Donation ID, which retrieves the stored transaction record and recomputes the hash to confirm data integrity. Additionally, the platform integrates an Impact Transparency Module that publishes structured reports detailing how collected funds are allocated across real-world initiatives such as education support programs, emergency medical aid, disaster relief operations, and animal welfare activities. From a system architecture perspective, the platform is built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the client-side interface, while the backend is implemented with Node.js and Express.js, exposing RESTful APIs for secure transaction handling, verification services, and campaign management. SQLite is used as the lightweight transactional database to store donation records, campaign data, and verification logs. By combining cryptographic verification, transparent reporting mechanisms, and real-time transaction tracking, ProofChain establishes a trust-driven donation ecosystem where donors gain full visibility into their contributions, enabling them to confidently track every rupee and verify every impact.

**The problem it solves**

***AgentForge*** solves the problem of ***discovering, deploying, and monetizing AI agents*** in a single decentralized marketplace.

Today, using AI for specialized tasks requires *technical setup, API knowledge, and infrastructure*. **AgentForge removes this complexity** by allowing users to instantly access ready-to-use AI agents while creators can deploy and monetize their own agents.

Users can:
- *Discover AI agents* for analytics, automation, and content generation  
- **Execute agents on-demand** without building infrastructure  
- *Pay per execution* using secure blockchain payments  

Creators can:
- **Deploy AI agents to a global marketplace**
- *Earn revenue automatically* from agent usage
- ***Scale AI services without managing servers or payment systems***

In short, ***AgentForge makes AI agents as accessible as apps in an app store***.

**Challenges we ran into**

While building ***AgentForge***, several technical challenges emerged:

• *Frontend–Backend Integration*  
The biggest challenge was ensuring the **Next.js frontend communicated reliably with the FastAPI backend** without breaking existing API contracts. This was solved by strictly centralizing endpoints in **`config.ts`** and maintaining consistent request payloads.

• *Wallet Authentication & Payments*  
Integrating **Solana wallet adapters** while keeping the UI responsive required careful handling of *client components and hydration issues* in Next.js.

• *Merge Conflicts & Deployment Setup*  
During repository integration, there were **Git merge conflicts between local and remote package files**. These were resolved by prioritizing the local dependency tree and completing the merge safely.

• *UI Performance*  
Maintaining a ***minimal yet premium interface*** while keeping the application performant required optimizing components and limiting client-side rendering.

Each challenge improved the architecture, resulting in a ***scalable and production-ready AI agent marketplace***.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

MandiConnect solves one of India's biggest agricultural problems — 
the middleman exploitation of small farmers.

🌾 **For Farmers:**
- Small-scale farmers in regions like Nipani, Karnataka are forced 
  to sell produce to local middlemen at 30-50% below market price
- They have zero bargaining power and no direct access to buyers
- Existing platforms are too complex and require high-speed internet

💡 **MandiConnect fixes this by:**
- Letting farmers LIST their own crops and SET their own price
- Connecting them DIRECTLY to retailers — zero middlemen, zero commission
- Working OFFLINE FIRST — built for low-connectivity rural areas
- Sending real-time mandi price alerts via SMS to basic phones
- Providing AI-powered crop advisory, disease detection, and demand prediction
- Integrating UPI payments (PhonePe, GPay, Paytm) directly to farmer's account

📊 **Impact:**
- Farmers earn 30-50% more per kg
- Retailers save 20-30% vs buying through middlemen
- Platform fee = ₹0 always (hardcoded, never changes)
- Works on 2G internet and offline via Progressive Web App (PWA)

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Offline-First Architecture**
Building a marketplace that works without internet was the hardest 
challenge. We solved it using PWA Service Workers and localStorage 
as a local database, with background sync when connection returns.

**2. Real-Time Price Updates**
Implementing live mandi price updates across 500+ mandis required 
Socket.IO with efficient room-based broadcasting. We used crop-specific 
rooms so farmers only receive relevant price updates.

**3. Bulk Order Splitting**
When a retailer places a 500kg order but no single farmer has that 
quantity, the system needed to auto-split across multiple farmers by 
distance, price, and availability simultaneously.

**4. Low-Bandwidth SMS Integration**
Many farmers in rural areas don't have smartphones. We integrated 
Twilio and MSG91 so all critical alerts (new orders, price changes, 
weather warnings) are delivered as plain SMS to any basic phone.

**5. Farmer-Set Pricing**
The core feature — ensuring the platform NEVER changes a farmer's 
price — required careful backend validation. We hardcoded platformFee = 0 
at the database schema level, making it impossible to override.

**6. Time Constraint**
Built the complete frontend + backend in 24 hours at the hackathon. 
We prioritized core features first, used localStorage as a mock backend 
initially, then connected the real Node.js + MongoDB backend.

### FinSentry
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/finsentry-76e0) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ullasdewangan09/Fin_Sentry) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://fin-sentry-frontend.onrender.com/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-INNOVAT3-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://innovat3.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Auditing on Auto-Pilot

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![NetworkX](https://img.shields.io/badge/NetworkX-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Traditional enterprise financial auditing is a slow, manual, and reactive process. Human auditors spend hundreds of hours sifting through thousands of disparate records—employee directories, vendor lists, invoices, and payment ledgers—trying to piece together complex trails of fraud, embezzlement, or policy violations. Often, by the time anomalies are flagged, the financial damage has already been done.

**FinTwin (Financial Digital Twin)** solves this by shifting corporate auditing from reactive sample testing to proactive, 100% automated continuous monitoring. 

**How it works & what it makes easier:**
1. **The Digital Twin Graph:** It ingests flat CSV/database records and builds a multi-dimensional graph database (NetworkX) mapping every entity (Employee, Vendor, Invoice, Payment). This allows the system to instantly see hidden relationships—like an employee approving an invoice for a vendor they secretly created.
2. **Automated Risk Detection:** It runs complex graph-traversal algorithms to catch sophisticated fraud patterns (like invoice splitting to bypass approval limits, or rapid vendor creation-to-payment loops) that traditional scalar rule-engines miss.
3. **AI-Powered Explanations:** Instead of handing risk analysts a spreadsheet of flags, FinTwin uses an autonomous LangGraph AI Agent to act as a Forensic Investigator. The AI traces the entire graph pathway, tests related transactions, and generates a human-readable executive narrative explaining the exact mechanism of the fraud and recommending remediation steps.

Ultimately, it empowers risk analysts and compliance officers to catch internal collusion instantly, saving enterprises millions in fraud loss and drastically reducing audit cycle times.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a complex, two-agent AI graph pipeline within a hackathon timeframe presented several distinct technical hurdles:

**1. Connecting Disparate Data Structures into a Cohesive Graph**
Initial datasets were flat tables (employees, vendors, approvals). The biggest challenge was figuring out how to build a directed causal graph where nodes had different types and schemas.
* **How we got over it:** We normalized the data and used `NetworkX` in Python to map structural dependencies (Employee -> created -> Vendor -> submitted -> Invoice). We realized we needed "Decision Nodes" (like `vendor_creation` or `approval_decision`) to serve as the connective tissue between entities, allowing our risk-detection algorithms to traverse the exact chain of events.

**2. Taming the LLM Context Window**
When we first built the AI Forensic Investigator, we fed it the entire graph state. Naturally, it hallucinated connections or timed out because the context window was flooded with irrelevant, un-flagged transactions.
* **How we got over it:** We implemented a two-agent `LangGraph` supervisor approach. The *Detection Agent* first runs deterministic network algorithms to isolate the *exact subgraph* (a compromised pathway of 4-5 nodes). This tiny, highly-relevant subgraph is the only thing passed to the *Investigation Agent* (using `Langchain` and `Groq`), resulting in incredibly fast, hallucination-free executive summaries.

**3. Visualizing a Complex Network in React**
We needed the dashboard to actually *look* like a digital twin, meaning we had to render the network graph in the browser. Initial attempts with basic chart libraries failed to handle the node gravity and relationship edges properly.
* **How we got over it:** We integrated interactive flow/graph libraries on the frontend (React/Vite). We built a dedicated API endpoint (`/graph/data`) on the FastAPI backend specifically to serialize the complex NetworkX python objects into lightweight, JSON-safe node-edge pairs that the React UI physics engine could accurately render.

### Provium
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/provium-1622) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Rohansingh3001/Prhttps://github.com/Rohansingh3001/Proviumovium) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/zxoyE4AdAJw) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/zxoyE4AdAJw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Comply without exposure.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![WalletConnect](https://img.shields.io/badge/WalletConnect-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Wagmi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wagmi-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In 2025, OFAC fined ShapeShift $750,000 - not for laundering money, but for failing to prove compliance without exposing their users. Tornado Cash, BitMEX, ShapeShift - all fined, none had a way to satisfy regulators without handing over raw user data.

That's the impossible choice DeFi faces today: expose your users to prove you're compliant, or protect privacy and get fined. The GENIUS Act now mandates that stablecoin issuers and DeFi protocols prove solvency - but says nothing about how.

Provium eliminates that choice. It's an autonomous AI compliance agent that generates zero-knowledge proofs of protocol solvency every hour - proving every position maintains 150%+ collateral ratio without revealing a single user's balance, address, or position size.

Three AI agents (Watcher, Analyst, Reporter) powered by Groq's LLaMA 3.3 monitor a live DeFi lending protocol on Base Sepolia, assess risk in real time, and generate Noir ZK proofs bound to a Poseidon2 Merkle tree committed on-chain. Every proof is verified by a real UltraHonk verifier deployed on Base -not a mock.

Proof submissions are signed through BitGo's 2-of-3 multisig custody, so no single compromised key can forge a compliance report. After each proof lands on-chain, Fileverse packages a full compliance dossier - proof metadata, agent reasoning, protocol snapshot, transaction links - into a permanent document regulators can access with a single URL.

The regulator story ties it together: any regulator can call RegulatorPortal.requestComplianceProof() specifying a jurisdiction and target block. The agent detects the request, generates a fresh ZK proof, and fulfills it on-chain within 30 minutes - with both a cryptographic proof and a plain-English AI explanation of why the protocol is or isn't compliant.

The agent's identity is verified via ENSIP-25 -its ENS name is cryptographically bound to its ComplianceRegistry entry using ERC-7930 cross-chain addressing. Anyone can verify the agent is legitimate with a single ENS lookup.

No phone calls. No subpoenas. No quarterly audits that arrive months too late. Verifiable compliance on demand - without exposing a single user.

**Challenges we ran into**

**ZK Circuit Constraints** - Noir requires fixed-size arrays at compile time, so the circuit is hardcoded to 16 positions with zero-padded slots. Poseidon hashing was the real challenge -the circuit uses `std::hash::poseidon2_permutation` over BN254, and the Python Merkle tree builder must produce byte-identical hashes or witness generation fails silently. Matching the Python `poseidon-hash` library to Noir's internal implementation took multiple rounds of debugging field arithmetic edge cases.

- **LLM Reliability** - The first architecture used Agno's team delegation, where a coordinator LLM passed data between agents. The coordinator summarized the positions JSON instead of forwarding it verbatim, corrupting Merkle tree inputs downstream. The fix: a deterministic Python orchestrator where LLMs handle reasoning and decision-making, but Python handles all data wiring. No LLM touches raw position data.

- **BitGo Testnet** - No Python SDK existed. We built a minimal REST client against BitGo API v2 from scratch - Bearer auth, wallet passphrase handling, and 2-of-3 multisig transaction construction. The challenge was sending zero-value contract calls (pure calldata for proof submission), not token transfers, which is an uncommon BitGo use case.

- **On-Chain Gas for Reasoning Strings** - Each compliance report stores the full LLM reasoning in contract storage permanently. We accepted the cost as a feature — an immutable, human-readable audit trail is the entire point. A regulator shouldn't need to decode ZK circuits to understand why a protocol passed or failed.

- **ENSIP-25 with Cross-Chain Addressing** - ERC-7930 encoding for Base Sepolia (chain ID 84532 = 3-byte big-endian) had no reference implementation. We built the encoder from the raw spec in both Python and TypeScript, then verified they produce identical output.

**Privacy**

Provium proves DeFi solvency to regulators using zero-knowledge proofs — no individual position, balance, or user address is ever revealed on-chain or to the regulator. The ZK circuit (Noir/BN254) verifies aggregate collateral ratios are above the GENIUS Act threshold while the Poseidon2 Merkle commitment binds the protocol to its full position set without disclosing it. Compliance without exposure — that's the entire product thesis.

**Pool prize**

Provium implements ENSIP-25 (AI Agent Registry ENS Name Verification) to give its autonomous compliance agent a verifiable, human-readable identity. The agent's ENS name (provium-agent.eth) carries a parameterized text record that binds it to its ComplianceRegistry entry on Base Sepolia via ERC-7930 cross-chain address encoding. Any protocol or regulator can verify the agent's legitimacy with a single ENS resolver lookup — no third-party trust needed. The dashboard includes a live ENSIP-25 verification badge (React hook + wagmi useEnsText) that resolves the text record on mainnet and shows real-time verification status. This is not cosmetic ENS usage — it's ENS as the identity layer for autonomous AI agents operating across chains.

**Best DeFi Application using BitGo**

Provium routes all autonomous agent transactions through BitGo's 2-of-3 multisig wallet on Base Sepolia. Every ZK compliance proof submission and regulator request fulfillment requires BitGo approval before reaching the chain. This prevents a compromised agent key from forging solvency reports — the exact attack vector that made FTX possible. BitGo isn't holding funds here; it's guarding regulatory truth. The integration uses BitGo REST API v2 with testnet (tbaseeth), and every transaction is logged with its BitGo tx ID for full audit trail.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

After each ZK compliance proof is submitted on-chain, Provium packages a full compliance dossier — proof metadata, on-chain tx references, agent reasoning snapshot, protocol health data, and jurisdiction tags — and uploads it to Fileverse. This creates a permanent, addressable "regulator packet" that a compliance officer can retrieve with a single URL, without needing to parse on-chain calldata or decode ZK proofs. The dossier includes a SHA-256 content hash for tamper detection. The dashboard links each proof row directly to its Fileverse dossier. Fileverse is the bridge between cryptographic truth (on-chain) and human-readable evidence (regulator's desk).

**Privacy**

All 6 smart contracts are deployed on Base Sepolia — ComplianceRegistry, RegulatorPortal, UltraVerifier, LendingProtocol, MockWETH, MockUSDC. The ZK verifier runs natively on Base EVM, verifying Noir/BN254 UltraHonk proofs in a single verify() call. Compliance reports, regulator requests, and proof verification all happen on Base. The privacy angle: individual DeFi positions never touch the chain — only the ZK proof and aggregate compliance status are stored. Base gets GENIUS Act compliance infrastructure that protects user privacy by default.

### SettleX
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/settlex-b65c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vrajparikh01/SettleX-alpha-contracts) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://settle-x-alpha-frontend.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/khLx6wIW1YU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> OTC & Premarket Trading with Onchain Settlement

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![AWS](https://img.shields.io/badge/AWS-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vercel](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vercel-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Early token trading and private allocations often happen off-chain through informal agreements or centralized brokers, which introduces several issues:
- Counterparty risk between buyers and sellers
- Lack of transparency in OTC deals
- Manual settlement processes that can fail or be manipulated
- Limited infrastructure for premarket trading before token launches
- No standardized way to manage early investor allocations

Because of this, early-stage deals and token allocations frequently rely on trusted intermediaries, which contradicts the decentralized ethos of Web3.

**SettleX solves this by creating an on-chain infrastructure for OTC deals and premarket token trading, enabling transparent commitments and automated settlement through smart contracts.**

Key Features:

- Premarket Token Offers
 Users can create buy or sell offers for tokens before the official launch.

- Collateralized Participation
 Participants lock collateral to ensure commitments are honored.

- On-chain Settlement Logic
 Smart contracts automatically manage token and fund transfers when settlement conditions are met.

- OTC Deal Creation
 Users can create direct over-the-counter agreements for token trades.

- Transparent Contributions
 All contributions and allocations are visible on-chain.

- ENS-Based Identity
 Human-readable identities using Ethereum Name Service instead of raw wallet addresses.

**Challenges we ran into**

During development, several challenges emerged:
- Designing a fair settlement mechanism for both buy and sell offers.
- Handling multiple contributors while ensuring secure token distribution.
- Managing collateral locking and refund scenarios when offers fail.
- Implementing time-based settlement logic tied to the token generation event.
- Handling edge cases such as partial fills and expired offers.

Additionally, debugging the premarket flow across both the smart contracts and frontend interaction layer required careful testing to ensure correct state transitions.

**DeFi**

SettleX is a decentralized infrastructure for OTC and premarket trading of digital assets, bringing early-stage token markets on-chain. Today, private token allocations and OTC trades often occur off-chain through brokers or informal agreements, creating counterparty risk, lack of transparency, and limited accessibility.

SettleX solves this by enabling users to create OTC deals and premarket token offers directly through smart contracts. Participants can lock capital, contribute to offers, and settle trades in a transparent and trustless manner once predefined conditions are met. This transforms early asset trading into a programmable financial primitive within decentralized finance.

By bringing private market activity on-chain, SettleX expands the scope of DeFi beyond traditional AMMs and lending protocols, introducing infrastructure for early token liquidity, capital formation, and peer-to-peer OTC settlements. The protocol demonstrates how decentralized systems can replace intermediaries in private market transactions while maintaining transparency and security.

The protocol is deployed on Base to enable low-cost and scalable decentralized trading infrastructure.

**Best creative use of ENS**

SettleX integrates ENS as a programmable identity layer for decentralized OTC and premarket trading. Instead of relying on raw wallet addresses, traders interact using ENS names, enabling human-readable and reputation-based private market transactions.

I reimagined ENS beyond name resolution. So, created settlex.prefs, a custom ENS text record that stores OTC trading preferences as JSON directly on Ethereum. Traders set it once on app.ens.domains — listing their preferred tokens, deal sizes, and notes. When you type alice.eth in our deal form, her entire on-chain identity loads in real time: avatar, verified checkmark, on-chain reputation score (0–100, computed from ENS profile completeness), social links, and her trading preferences — all pulled live from Ethereum. No API calls. No database. Pure ENS.

This is ENS as infrastructure, not decoration. We created an open standard (settlex.prefs) that any DeFi protocol can adopt. Traders own their identity on-chain forever, portable across all apps that read the same records. The marketplace filters by "ENS only," searches by ENS name, and highlights trades matching your own preferences — all impossible without this creative use of text records. We solved a real, high-value DeFi problem (OTC trust) using ENS as decentralized infrastructure beyond simple naming.

**Pool prize**

SettleX integrates ENS to improve usability and identity within decentralized OTC and premarket trading. Wallet addresses are resolved to ENS names throughout the platform, making deal creation, offer discovery, and settlement interactions human-readable.

Users can create OTC deals and premarket offers using ENS names instead of raw addresses, enabling more intuitive peer-to-peer trading. ENS also serves as a decentralized identity layer where traders can associate metadata such as social profiles or trading preferences through ENS text records.

By integrating ENS across deal creation, counterparty identification, and trader profiles, SettleX demonstrates how human-readable identities can improve the usability and transparency of DeFi protocols.

**DeFi 2.0 - New Primitives**

SettleX can be deployed on Base to provide a low-cost environment for token launch settlements.

Using Base improves:
- lower gas fees
- faster settlement
- better accessibility for retail users

This makes Base an ideal network for scaling decentralized capital formation tools like SettleX.
