### PayPerSecret
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/paypersecret-4498) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/snehaa-eth/eth-mumbai-) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/MY65T3pmuaY) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-2-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Sell secrets. Stay invisible. ZK guarantees it.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**PayPerSecret — Anonymous Information Marketplace**
Sell what you know. Buy what others won't say publicly.

PayPerSecret lets anyone monetize sensitive information without revealing their identity. Powered by Semaphore zero-knowledge proofs, x402 payments, and Fileverse decentralized storage — no accounts, no KYC, no trace.

*The Problem*
Valuable information exists everywhere — but sharing it is risky:

- A DeFi researcher spots a whale about to dump tokens. Posting it publicly on Twitter means everyone front-runs it and the alpha is worthless.
- A security researcher finds a vulnerability in a protocol. Responsible disclosure gets them nothing; selling it is legally grey.
- A company insider knows about an upcoming partnership. They can't tell anyone without exposing themselves.
- A journalist has a leaked document. Publishing it reveals their source.
- Today, people either share alpha for free (losing value) or stay silent (information dies). There's no safe way to sell information anonymously.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/97f2cfce4a8447348fe1f2f4ea8227a1/f1793eff-b1da-4741-a952-ef98b09ad4ea.png)
Real-World Use Cases

Crypto / DeFi Alpha

- Whale wallet movements before they hit CT
- Upcoming token listings, airdrops, or delistings
- MEV opportunities and mempool insights
- Protocol vulnerabilities (responsible disclosure marketplace)

Business Intelligence

- Competitor strategy leaks
- Upcoming M&A or partnership announcements
- Internal metrics that move markets

Journalism & Whistleblowing

- Leaked documents sold to verified journalists
- Government or corporate misconduct evidence
- Source protection through ZK anonymity

Security Research

- Bug bounties for protocols that don't have programs
- Zero-day vulnerability marketplace
- Audit findings sold to affected parties

Sports & Betting

- Insider injury reports before public announcement
- Team strategy leaks
- Transfer news before official confirmation

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/97f2cfce4a8447348fe1f2f4ea8227a1/0c963a82-75a9-43ed-9941-e0fec8441e64.png)

What's NEVER stored on Fileverse or on-chain:

1. Telegram usernames or chat IDs
2. Wallet addresses
3. IP addresses
4. Any personally identifiable information

What IS stored (ZK-safe):

1. Semaphore identity commitments (sem_...)
2. Purchase nullifiers (zkn_...)
3. Encrypted secret content (Fileverse handles E2E encryption)
4. SHA-256 content hashes (tamper-proof)

**Challenges we ran into**

- Semaphore's generateProof() requires the scope to be under 32 bytes. My scope was purchase:{secretId}:{txHash} — way over 32 bytes. The proof generation crashed with bytes32 string must be less than 32 bytes. Fixed by SHA-256 hashing the scope and truncating to 30 characters before passing to Semaphore.

- The biggest architectural challenge: ZK privacy means no raw identities are stored on Fileverse, but the server needs Telegram chat IDs to send notifications. Solution: volatile memory mapping (commitmentToChat Map) that exists only while the server runs. After restart, old sellers/buyers can't receive notifications — this is by design. Privacy > convenience.

**Privacy**

PayPerSecret is built privacy-first — not as a feature, but as the core architecture. Every design decision prioritizes anonymity.

Zero-Knowledge Identity (Semaphore Protocol v4)
Users never register with emails, phone numbers, or wallets. Instead, each user gets a Semaphore identity — a cryptographic commitment that proves "I am a registered user" without revealing which user. Sellers are shown as sem_388600493550... in the marketplace. Buyers prove they purchased a secret using zk-SNARK proofs (Groth16) without revealing their identity. Nullifiers prevent double-actions without linking transactions to a person.

Nothing Personal Touches Storage
Secrets are stored on Fileverse (IPFS + Gnosis chain) as encrypted JSON. Before any data reaches Fileverse, a sanitizer strips all personally identifiable information — Telegram IDs, wallet addresses, usernames. Only ZK commitments and nullifiers are persisted. Raw identities exist only in volatile server memory and are lost on restart — by design.

Stealth Addresses Per Transaction
Each purchase generates a unique stealth address derived from the buyer's wallet + secret ID. Payments can't be linked across different purchases. An observer on-chain sees random addresses, not a pattern of activity tied to one person.

x402 Payments Without Identity
The x402 protocol (HTTP 402) enables pay-per-access without accounts. The server returns a 402 response with payment requirements, the buyer pays USDC from any wallet, and retries with proof. No login, no session, no cookies — just a transaction hash.

**AI**

In an anonymous marketplace, trust is the hardest problem. When sellers are hidden behind ZK commitments and buyers use stealth addresses, there's no reputation system, no reviews, no identity to stake. So how does a buyer know a secret is real before paying?

PayPerSecret uses HeyElsa AI as an automated verification layer. When a buyer purchases a secret, the content is sent to HeyElsa's on-chain intelligence API. If someone sells a secret claiming "whale wallet is dumping 5000 ETH", HeyElsa queries real blockchain data — token balances, recent transfers, price movements — and returns a verdict: LEGIT, PARTIALLY_VERIFIED, UNVERIFIABLE, or FAKE. This verdict is stored with the secret and shown to future buyers during the paid peek ($0.50 via x402).

The AI doesn't just flag scams — it creates a trust signal in a trustless system. A buyer can peek at the AI verdict before committing to the full purchase. A seller with verified secrets gets more sales without ever revealing who they are. The verification is objective (on-chain data), automated (no human moderators), and privacy-preserving (HeyElsa never sees the seller's identity, only the claim content).

This solves a problem that traditional AI applications don't face: verification without identity. Most AI trust systems rely on user profiles, history, or reputation scores. PayPerSecret can't use any of that — everyone is anonymous. HeyElsa fills this gap by shifting trust from "who said it" to "is it true on-chain", making AI the neutral arbiter in a zero-knowledge marketplace.

**Best Privacy Application using BitGo**

BitGo's Multi-Party Computation (MPC) wallet serves as the escrow layer — holding buyer funds until AI verification completes, then releasing to sellers without either party knowing each other's wallet.
A smart contract escrow would expose the logic on-chain — anyone could see the seller's payout address by watching contract events. BitGo MPC keeps the release as a normal wallet-to-wallet transfer. On-chain it looks like a regular USDC send, not an escrow release. No contract address to monitor, no events to index, no seller address leaked through transaction traces.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

Big tech profits from identity. Their business model requires knowing who you are, what you buy, and who you talk to. PayPerSecret inverts this - the marketplace works precisely because nobody knows who's selling or buying. The math guarantees it, not a privacy policy that can change tomorrow.

There is no MongoDB, no PostgreSQL, no Firebase. When a seller lists a secret, the content is stored as a Fileverse document via the @fileverse/api local server. On startup, the app loads all documents from Fileverse into an in-memory cache, rebuilding the entire database from decentralized storage. The server is stateless — you can wipe it and everything reloads from Fileverse.

Before any document reaches Fileverse, a ZK sanitizer strips all personally identifiable information (Telegram IDs, wallet addresses, usernames). Only ZK commitments, nullifiers, and encrypted content are persisted. Fileverse handles end-to-end encryption — we removed our own AES-256 encryption layer because Fileverse already provides it. The result: even if someone reads the IPFS data, they see encrypted content with anonymous identifiers.

**Best Use of Elsa x402 and Elsa OpenClaw skills**

Every paid action uses x402's native HTTP flow: request a resource → get a 402 response with payment requirements → pay USDC on Base Sepolia → retry with the X-Payment header. Peeking at secret metadata costs $0.50 via x402. Buying a secret uses x402 with dynamic pricing set by the seller. No MetaMask popups for "approval" — the USDC transfer IS the x402 payment. No accounts, no sessions, no payment processors. Just HTTP status codes and on-chain transfers.

In an anonymous marketplace, how do you trust the seller? You can't check their reputation — they're anonymous. HeyElsa solves this by verifying secrets against on-chain data. When a buyer purchases a secret claiming "whale wallet 0xd8dA is dumping UNI", HeyElsa's API can checks:

Does that wallet actually hold UNI?
What are the token's current price movements?
Is there on-chain evidence supporting the claim?
The AI returns a verdict — LEGIT, PARTIALLY_VERIFIED, UNVERIFIABLE, or FAKE. This verdict is shown to future buyers in the peek metadata, creating a trust score without requiring seller identity.

**BEST Overall Project**

PayPerSecret is a fully anonymous information marketplace where users sell secrets and buy alpha — with zero identity exposure. It combines five technologies that don't normally work together into a single, working product accessible through Telegram.

What makes it different:
There is no traditional database — Fileverse (IPFS + Gnosis chain) is the sole storage layer, replacing MongoDB entirely. Payments happen through the x402 protocol (HTTP 402) — no accounts, no payment processors, just USDC and status codes. User identity is protected by Semaphore v4 zk-SNARKs — sellers and buyers are represented by cryptographic commitments, not usernames or wallets. HeyElsa AI verifies secret claims against on-chain data, creating automated trust in a system where no one knows who anyone is. BitGo MPC handles escrow with split-key signing so no single party controls the funds.

Why it matters:
Today, valuable information is either shared for free (losing its value) or kept silent (wasting its value). There's no safe way to monetize what you know without revealing who you are. PayPerSecret solves this — a DeFi researcher can sell whale movement alerts, a security researcher can sell vulnerability findings, a whistleblower can sell evidence — all without ever exposing their identity. The privacy isn't a feature toggle, it's the architecture. ZK proofs, decentralized storage, and HTTP-native payments make it mathematically impossible to trace a secret back to its seller.

Built and tested end-to-end: Sell → Browse → Peek ($0.50 x402) → Buy (dynamic x402) → AI Verify → Decrypt — all through Telegram, all anonymous, all on-chain verifiable.

**The problem it solves**

Right now:

1. Sharing your wallet address means copy-pasting an ugly 0x1a2b3c... string.

2. Your ENS profile data (bio, socials, avatar) exists on-chain but is invisible to most people.

3. There's no easy way to view or update your ENS identity without navigating complex blockchain tools.

ens.card solves this by making ENS text records human-readable, visually stunning, and shareable with a single link like a Web3 business card or a decentralized Linktree.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Public RPC reliability: Free Ethereum RPC endpoints are rate-limited and sometimes go down. Solved by implementing a fallback chain of multiple RPC providers.

2. Writing text records: ENS setText calls require knowing the correct resolver contract address per name, and the user must be the owner. Added proper error handling for rejected transactions and missing resolvers.

3. ENS Avatar formats : ENS avatars can be stored as ipfs://, ar:// (Arweave), or HTTPS URLs. Had to handle each format and convert to a browser-displayable URL.

**Best creative use of ENS**

My project is built entirely around ENS text records  going far beyond simple name-to-address resolution. It uses ENS as a full decentralized identity layer:

1. Reads 6+ text record types: description, com.twitter, com.github, url, email, avatar

2. Writes text records on-chain via ENS Public Resolver's setText function

3. Creates a shareable profile URL using the ENS name as the identifier

4. Demonstrates ENS as a human-readable identity layer exactly what the bounty describes as "creative use of ENS"

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![circuito.io](https://img.shields.io/badge/circuito.io-333333?style=flat-square) ![Biconomy SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Biconomy%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square) ![Wagmi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wagmi-333333?style=flat-square) ![RainbowKit](https://img.shields.io/badge/RainbowKit-333333?style=flat-square) ![Snarkjs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Snarkjs-333333?style=flat-square) ![groth16](https://img.shields.io/badge/groth16-333333?style=flat-square) ![POSEIDON HASH](https://img.shields.io/badge/POSEIDON%20HASH-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Blockchain transactions on Ethereum are fully transparent. Every transaction publicly exposes the sender address, receiver address, and transaction amount. While this transparency improves trust and auditability, it also creates serious privacy issues. Anyone can analyze blockchain data to track financial activity, link wallets together, and monitor user behavior.

This project solves that problem by enabling private transactions using Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKPs). By using the Groth16 proving system and commitment-based deposits, the protocol breaks the link between deposits and withdrawals. Users can deposit funds into a pool and later withdraw them to a different address without revealing their identity.

**As a result,** observers cannot determine who sent funds to whom. This significantly improves financial privacy, protects user identities, and prevents transaction graph analysis on-chain. The system allows users to benefit from blockchain technology while maintaining control over their financial privacy.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges during development was implementing and verifying Groth16 Zero-Knowledge proofs using Circom and SnarkJS.

While building the circuit, I encountered multiple issues such as circuit assertion failures, incorrect signal wiring, and proof verification mismatches between the generated proof and the on-chain verifier contract. These problems caused the proof verification step to fail during smart contract execution.

To solve this, I carefully debugged the circuit constraints, validated the input signals, and ensured that the public signals generated by the circuit matched the verifier inputs expected by the smart contract. After fixing the constraint logic and re-compiling the circuit, I successfully generated valid proofs and verified them on-chain.

This debugging process helped me better understand the interaction between Circom circuits, Groth16 proofs, and Solidity verifier contracts.

**Privacy**

This protocol enables private transactions on Ethereum using Groth16 zero-knowledge proofs. Users deposit funds into a pool as cryptographic commitments and later withdraw them anonymously without revealing which deposit they own. A Poseidon-based Merkle tree stores commitments, while nullifier hashes prevent double spending and ensure secure, unlinkable transactions.

**Best creative use of ENS**

ShadowPool combines ENS with stealth addresses to enable private and user-friendly transactions. Instead of sharing raw wallet addresses, users can use their ENS name (like alice.eth), which generates stealth addresses for each transaction, protecting the user’s identity and transaction history while keeping interactions simple and human-readable

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/3b9fc3b92e944d378ed45d355cfd2e1a/7d6fda52-30de-4c47-aaf6-3ae7eacbc437.png)

**Pool prize**

ShadowPool integrates ENS to make private crypto finance easier to manage. Users can link their ENS names (like alice.eth) to their private financial vaults, allowing them to send and receive funds without exposing raw wallet addresses. This improves usability while maintaining privacy, making private transactions more human-readable and accessible.

**Best Privacy Application using BitGo**

ShadowPool uses BitGo's MPC wallet as its withdrawal relayer. When a user submits a valid Groth16 ZK proof, the agent calls BitGo's sendMany API to sign and broadcast the on-chain withdraw() transaction — meaning no single private key ever exists in memory. The MPC key shares are split across parties so the relayer cannot be compromised by a single breach. Combined with Flashbots Protect submission (MEV-resistant, private mempool), this gives users both privacy guarantees and institutional-grade custody for the most sensitive operation in the protocol: moving funds to an anonymous recipient.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

Fileverse integration: Every deposit and withdrawal is automatically stored as a decentralized document via the Fileverse local API. Users get a shareable Fileverse link for each transaction — a privacy-preserving audit trail without exposing wallet addresses publicly.

Use case: Prove a private transfer happened, without revealing who sent it.

**DeFi 2.0 - New Primitives**

ShadowPool introduces a new DeFi primitive for private financial management on-chain. Built on Base, it enables users to track and manage crypto finances while preserving transaction privacy using stealth addresses and encrypted receipts. By combining privacy-preserving transactions with secure receipt sharing and human-readable ENS identities, ShadowPool creates a new layer of confidential financial infrastructure for DeFi users on scalable L2 networks like Base.

**Privacy**

ShadowPool uses privacy-preserving techniques on Base to help users manage and move their crypto finances without exposing sensitive transaction details on-chain. By combining Base’s scalable infrastructure with privacy mechanisms, the project enables secure and confidential financial activity on a public blockchain.

**BEST Overall Project**

ShadowPool focuses on privacy-first crypto finance management. It allows users to track, manage, and share financial information such as transaction receipts without exposing sensitive wallet data on public blockchains. By combining privacy techniques, secure storage, and user-friendly identity systems like ENS, the project improves how individuals handle their on-chain finances while maintaining confidentiality.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Centralized AI platforms lock credits (**non-withdrawable, expiring**), require KYC/accounts for access, block anonymous usage, and prevent AI agents from autonomously paying for frontier models (**Claude,GPT, Grok, etc.**). This wastes capital, leaks privacy,and stalls the agent economy.
**Solution: ChainAgent — Decentralized AI Credit Marketplace with x402 Micropayments**
Turn locked OpenRouter (or similar) credits into liquid USDC on Base via a pay-per-use proxy API.

- Sellers run a simple proxy forwarding to top models using their credits.
- Protect it with x402 (HTTP 402 Payment Required) — users/agents pay tiny USDC amounts per request (e.g., $0.01–$0.10).
- Payments settle instantly onchain to seller's wallet → fully withdrawable anytime.
- No KYC, no accounts — pure wallet-based, anonymous access.
- ENS-powered discoverability: Register e.g. chainagent.eth → users/agents resolve it to your proxy URL.
- Creative ENS twist: Text records store metadata (supported models, dynamic pricing per 1M tokens, status like "online / 60% credits left", reputation link) → enables autonomous agent discovery & trust (aligns with ERC-8004 trends).


**How It Works**

1. Seller sets ENS (e.g., chainagent.eth) → points to proxy + text records for models/pricing/address.
2. User/Agent resolves ENS → gets URL + pricing.
3. Requests proxy → gets 402 + payment demand.
4. x402 client (HeyElsa SDK, extension, agent lib) auto-pays USDC on Base → retries → gets AI response.
5. Proxy forwards internally with seller's key → seller earns & withdraws USDC freely.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges I Ran Into
ENS resolution on testnet was trickier than expected. I initially created the ENS provider without specifying the network, and name lookups silently failed. The fix was simple — pass 'sepolia' as the network — but it took a while to figure out because ethers.js doesn't throw, it just returns null. The ENS docs saved me here: "Specify the chain ID to whichever ENS network you're using."

Replay attacks across server restarts. My first replay guard was just an in-memory Set of used tx hashes. Worked great... until the server restarted and every old tx could be replayed. I ended up checking the transactions table in Supabase first (which has a unique constraint on tx_hash), then falling back to the in-memory set for speed.

x402 payment verification timing. When a buyer sends USDC on Base Sepolia and immediately retries with the tx hash, the transaction often isn't confirmed yet. I kept getting "tx not found" errors during testing. The solution was adding clear messaging in the 402 response telling clients to wait for confirmation before retrying.

Race condition in earnings counters. Under concurrent requests, two payments could read total_earned_usdc = 5, both write back 6, and one payment's earnings would vanish. Fixed it with an atomic SQL function (total_earned_usdc = total_earned_usdc + amount) instead of read-increment-write in JS.

API keys leaking through a legacy endpoint. The /api/proxies endpoint correctly masked seller API keys, but I forgot the old /registry endpoint returned raw data — including full API keys. Caught it during a security review and patched both endpoints to strip sensitive fields.

**Best creative use of ENS**

ChainAgent pushes ENS creatively as a dynamic discovery & trust layer for decentralized AI services:

ENS as readable API endpoint: chainagent.eth resolves to your proxy URL — simple, memorable access instead of raw links.
Text records for live metadata: Stores supported models, dynamic pricing (e.g., USDC per tokens), credit status, reputation — agents resolve ENS, fetch data, assess trust, then auto-pay via x402.

This evolves ENS into a protocol for agent-native service discovery in the onchain AI economy — novel, practical, and aligned with ENS's extensible vision.

**Pool prize**

ChainAgent uses ENS creatively as a dynamic, agent-native API discovery layer:

ENS name (chainagent.eth) resolves to proxy URL → easy, memorable access.
Text records store live metadata: supported models, pricing, credit status, reputation → agents resolve ENS, fetch data, trust-check, then auto-pay via x402.

This turns ENS into real-time service discovery + trust primitive for onchain AI — not just a name, but a protocol for autonomous agents.

**AI × Onchain**

ChainAgent.eth is fully built on Base for instant, low-cost USDC micropayments per AI request via x402.

All payments settle onchain on Base → cheap/fast txs make tiny AI queries (e.g., $0.01) viable.
Bridges AI + onchain: Autonomous agents discover proxies (ENS), evaluate metadata, pay USDC on Base, and access frontier models permissionlessly.
Turns AI intelligence into a Base-native primitive for the agent economy.

**Best Use of Elsa x402 and Elsa OpenClaw skills**

ChainAgent.eth is a perfect showcase for HeyElsa’s x402 protocol and OpenClaw skills:

Core mechanic uses x402: Proxy returns HTTP 402 "Payment Required" → clients (including agents) auto-pay tiny USDC amounts per AI request on Base, settling instantly onchain — direct implementation of x402 for micropayments.

**The problem it solves**

# What Can You Use ENSPay For?

---

## Freelancers and Creators Getting Paid in Crypto

Instead of sending clients a long wallet address and explaining "make sure it's on Base, and send USDC not ETH" you just share **yourname.eth**.

Your client types it in, enters the amount, and pays. ENSPay handles the token and chain automatically. No back-and-forth, no wrong-chain mistakes.

> **Easier because:** You set your preferences once. Every future payment just works.

---

## Merchants and Indie Sellers Accepting Crypto

Put your ENS QR code at checkout, physical or digital. Customers scan it exactly like a UPI code. ENSPay resolves your preferences and routes payment to you in your preferred token on your preferred chain.

> **Easier because:** No payment terminal setup, no chain-specific wallets to manage. One QR does everything.

---

## Splitting Bills and Sending Money to Friends

Splitting dinner? Instead of fumbling with wallet addresses, your friend scans your QR from the /receive page and sends their share. Works even if they're holding ETH and you want USDC. ENSPay swaps on the way.

> **Easier because:** Token mismatch is no longer a problem. You get what you want, they send what they have.

---

## Private Payments Without Extra Steps

If you're a journalist, activist, or just someone who values financial privacy, turn on **stealth mode**. Every payment you receive goes to a fresh one-time address. No one on-chain can link payments back to your identity.

> **Safer because:** Your wallet history stays private without requiring the payer to do anything differently. They just scan and pay.

---

## Cross-Border and Cross-Chain Payments

Sending money across chains today means manually bridging, waiting, and hoping nothing breaks. ENSPay integrates **Across Protocol v3** to handle this automatically. The payer pays on their chain; the receiver gets it on theirs.

> **Easier because:** Cross-chain complexity is completely abstracted away. Neither party needs to understand bridging.

---

## DAOs and Teams Paying Contributors

A DAO can set a shared ENS name with team payment preferences. Contributors submit work and get paid to the ENS name. No need to collect wallet addresses from every contributor each cycle, and no risk of paying to the wrong chain.

> **Easier because:** One ENS name, one set of preferences, consistent payouts every time.

---

## Shareable Payment Links

Every ENS name gets a dedicated URL like `/pay/alice.eth`. Share it in your Twitter bio, Discord profile, invoice email, or README. Anyone who clicks it lands on a clean payment page, ready to pay.

> **Easier because:** It works like a payment link (think PayPal.me) but fully on-chain, non-custodial, and chain-agnostic.

---

## TL;DR — The Core Value

| Old Way | ENSPay Way |
|---|---|
| Share wallet address + specify chain + specify token | Share your .eth name |
| Payer sends wrong token — funds stuck | ENSPay swaps automatically |
| Payer on wrong chain — manual bridge | ENSPay bridges automatically |
| Wallet address is public and traceable | Stealth mode gives a fresh address every time |
| Payment links require custodial services | `/pay/alice.eth` is fully on-chain |

ENSPay does not reinvent crypto payments. It makes them feel like they should have felt all along.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Setting ENS Preferences: From Six Transactions to One

The first version of the preference setup sent six separate setText() transactions on the ENS PublicResolver, one for each key (enspay.token, enspay.network, enspay.dex, enspay.slippage, enspay.note, enspay.stealth).

That was a terrible experience. The user had to confirm six wallet popups in a row, pay gas six times, and wait for each one to land before the next could fire. If they rejected or one failed midway, their preferences were left in a half-written state on-chain.

The fix was multicall() on the PublicResolver. ENS's resolver supports batching multiple setText() calls into a single transaction. I encoded each call as ABI-encoded calldata and passed them as an array. One wallet confirmation, one gas payment, all six records written atomically. If it fails, nothing is written. The UX went from painful to seamless overnight.

> The key insight was treating the six records not as six separate writes but as a single atomic preference object that either saves completely or not at all.

---

## Uniswap V3 Integration: Getting the Swap Router Right

Integrating Uniswap V3 inside the smart contract had several sharp edges.

The first issue was using the wrong router address. Base Sepolia uses SwapRouter02 at a specific address, not the same one as mainnet or other testnets. Transactions were silently reverting until I traced the issue down to the router address being wrong.

The second issue was amountOutMinimum. Setting it to zero made swaps pass in testing but is dangerous in production. Setting it too tight caused legitimate swaps to revert due to price movement between quote and execution. The fix was building applyDefaultSlippage() into the contract itself, applying a 0.5% (50 bps) tolerance to the quoted output, giving a realistic minimum without being exploitable.

The third issue was token approval flow. The contract needs the payer to approve it as a spender before calling resolveAndSwap(). Getting the frontend to sequence the approval transaction and then the swap transaction correctly, and handling the case where approval was already sufficient, took several iterations to get right.

---

## Across Protocol: No Hardcoded Addresses

The initial approach to cross-chain bridging hardcoded the SpokePool address for each chain. That broke immediately because Across v3 returns the correct spokePoolAddress dynamically from their quotes API at app.across.to/api/suggested-fees.

The fix was to never hardcode SpokePool addresses. Every cross-chain payment now starts with a getBridgeQuote() call that fetches the fee suggestion and extracts the spokePoolAddress from the response. The frontend then calls depositV3() on that address directly.

This also meant the integration is future-proof. If Across upgrades or migrates their SpokePool, the app adapts automatically without a contract redeployment.

> One hard limitation: Across Protocol only operates on mainnet chains. On testnets, cross-chain attempts return an error. All the bridging logic is fully wired and tested against mainnet parameters, but live end-to-end bridging is a mainnet-only flow.

**Best creative use of ENS**

ENSPay qualifies for Best Creative Use of ENS because it goes far beyond using ENS as a name resolver.

ENS text records were designed to store arbitrary metadata. ENSPay repurposes that capability to encode a complete payment specification, turning a human-readable name into a self-contained payment contract. Six keys on the PublicResolver replace what would otherwise require constant sender-receiver coordination.

The creativity is in the abstraction. The ENS name does not just resolve to an address. It resolves to a token preference, a destination chain, a DEX hint, a slippage tolerance, a personal note, and a privacy setting, all written atomically in a single multicall transaction.

No other payment system uses ENS this way. Most treat it as a glorified address book. ENSPay treats it as programmable payment intent.

**Pool prize**

ENSPay was built around ENS as its core infrastructure, not as an afterthought.

The entire payment layer depends on the ENS PublicResolver. Receiver preferences live on-chain as ENS text records. Payment routing, token selection, chain targeting, and privacy settings are all resolved from those records at payment time. Remove ENS and the product does not exist.

Beyond reading records, ENSPay pushes ENS into new territory. It uses multicall on the PublicResolver to write six preference keys atomically in one transaction, treats a human-readable name as a fully self-describing payment endpoint, and generates stealth addresses keyed to ENS identities so privacy is opt-in without any extra complexity for the payer.

ENSPay is a direct demonstration of what ENS unlocks when you treat text records as programmable state rather than just metadata.

**Best Privacy Application using BitGo**

ENSPay puts privacy directly in the hands of the receiver, with zero added friction for the payer.

When stealth mode is enabled on a receiver's ENS profile, every inbound payment lands on a fresh one-time address generated at payment time. The payer scans a QR, sends funds, and has no idea they are sending to a stealth address. No identity is ever published on-chain. No one can link incoming payments back to the receiver's ENS name or wallet.

BitGo's infrastructure handles the actual asset custody and movement while ENSPay layers programmable privacy on top through ENS text records and one-time address generation. Privacy is not a separate flow or an advanced feature. It is a single toggle in the receiver's preferences.

Most privacy tools ask users to change how they transact. ENSPay makes privacy the default experience without changing the transaction flow at all.

**BEST Overall Project**

**ENSPay deserves Best Overall because it solves a real, unsolved problem end to end.**

Crypto payments have always required coordination between sender and receiver. ENSPay eliminates that entirely by turning an ENS name into a complete payment specification. The receiver sets preferences once. Every payment after that just works, regardless of token, chain, or privacy preference.

It is not a proof of concept. It ships a deployed smart contract on Base Sepolia, live ENS resolution, Uniswap V3 swaps, Across Protocol v3 bridging, stealth payments, a QR payment terminal, and a full transaction dashboard. Every layer of the stack is connected and functional.

The UX ambition matches the technical depth. Multicall batching, dynamic SpokePool resolution, one-time stealth addresses, and automatic route selection are not visible to the user at all. They just type a name and pay.

ENSPay does not add a feature to crypto payments. It removes the friction that has always made them impractical for everyday use.

**The problem it solves**

# AetherGuard — Privacy-First AI Portfolio Guardian

## Overview

**AetherGuard** is a platform that helps users get **AI-powered trading suggestions** while keeping their **investment strategies completely private**.

Instead of sending strategies to AI providers, AetherGuard only shares the **user’s investment goal**. All actual strategies and guardrails remain private, yet **cryptographically verifiable**.

The system leverages:

- **Merkle proofs** to verify strategy compliance  
- **Fileverse encrypted documents** for secure and decentralized storage  

This ensures **AI can assist users** without ever seeing their private strategy.

---

## The Problem

Most AI trading assistants today require users to send:

- Portfolio details  
- Investment strategies  
- Risk and trading rules  

to centralized systems, which creates major risks:

| Problem | Description | Risk |
|---------|------------|------|
| **Strategy Leakage** | Trading logic is visible to AI providers | Intellectual property theft or misuse |
| **Centralized Control** | Platforms store user data in central databases | Users lose ownership and privacy |
| **No Verification** | Users cannot prove AI followed their strategy | Black-box AI reduces trust and transparency |

Even if users want privacy, traditional tools **do not allow strategy confidentiality**.

---

## Real-World Example

A trader manages **$100,000** crypto portfolio with these rules:

| Guardrail | Limit |
|------------|-------|
| Max allocation per asset | 30% |
| Minimum liquidity | 20% |
| Buy only high-volume assets | Yes |

**Without AetherGuard:** AI platforms require sending the rules → full strategy is visible.  

**With AetherGuard:** AI only sees the goal and portfolio state. It can propose trades but cannot access private rules.

Example workflow:

| Portfolio (Before) | AI Suggestion | Portfolio (After Simulation) |
|------------------|---------------|-----------------------------|
| 100% Cash | Buy 20% ETH | 20% ETH, 80% Cash |
| 20% ETH, 80% Cash | Buy 10% BTC | 20% ETH, 10% BTC, 70% Cash |

---

## The AetherGuard Solution

### 1. Strategy Creation

Users define:

- **Investment Goal** → Sent to AI  
- **Private Guardrail Rules** → Stored in **Fileverse encrypted documents**

Rules are converted into a **Merkle tree**, and the **root hash** is used for verification.

---

### 2. AI Market Suggestions

The AI only receives:

- **Current portfolio state**  
- **Investment goal**

It analyzes market data and generates suggestions:

- Example: “Buy 20% ETH with available cash”  

AI **never sees strategy rules**.

---

### 3. Guardrail Verification

Before execution:

- Each AI suggestion is checked against the **Merkle root**  
- Violations trigger **UI warnings**  
- Users can **approve or reject trades on-chain**

---

### 4. Permanent Audit Trail

All strategy and decision data are stored in Fileverse:

| Document | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| Strategy Document | Stores private guardrails |
| Master Document | Aggregates all strategies of a user |
| Decision Log | Records AI proposals, approvals, and executed trades |

This ensures **transparent, tamper-proof auditability**.

---

### 5. Collaborative Multi-Sig

AetherGuard enables **team portfolio management**:

- Teams create a **shared Fileverse document**  
- AI proposals are reviewed by multiple members  
- Execution can require **multi-signature approval**

This is ideal for **DAOs, treasuries, or collaborative trading teams**.

---

## Why AetherGuard

AetherGuard allows users to:

- Maintain **private strategies**  
- Receive **AI market insights**  
- Verify AI suggestions **cryptographically**  
- Approve trades **on-chain**  
- Keep a **permanent decentralized audit trail**  

> It combines AI assistance with **full privacy, security, and user control**, making AI-powered trading safe and trustworthy.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges We Faced

Building AetherGuard involved solving several key challenges around **privacy, collaboration, and portfolio simulation**.

---

## 1. Verifying AI Suggestions Without Revealing Strategy

We wanted the AI to suggest trades **without ever seeing the user’s private strategy**.  
Normally, AI systems require the full strategy to know if a trade is allowed, but sending it to the AI would break privacy.

**Solution:**  
We used **Merkle Root Proofs**:

- Each strategy rule is hashed and stored in a **Merkle tree**.
- The **Merkle root** acts as a fingerprint of the strategy.
- AI suggestions are checked against this root to verify compliance **without revealing the rules**.
- We also show the verification process in the **UI** for transparency.

---

## 2. Collaborative Multi-Signature Trading

For team-managed portfolios or DAOs, multiple people need to review and approve trades.

**Challenge:**  
How to enable **secure team collaboration** while preserving privacy and avoiding a single point of failure.

**Solution:**  
We built **Fileverse-based multi-sig boardrooms**:

- A **team document** stores proposals.
- Members can review suggestions.
- Trades require **multi-signature approval** before execution.

This ensures **no single person—or AI—can move funds independently**.

---

## 3. Portfolio Simulation & Visualization

As students, we don’t have access to real mainnet funds or large testnet portfolios.

**Challenge:**  
How to **demonstrate trading flow** and AI decision-making realistically without risking real assets.

**Solution:**  

- We use a **simulated portfolio**, starting with **100% cash**.
- When AI suggests a trade (e.g., buy 20% ETH), the portfolio updates **virtually**: 20% ETH, 80% cash.
- AI can read this simulated portfolio to propose **strategically meaningful trades**.
- Execution still requires **user approval**, ensuring safety.

This allows us to **show the full AI workflow** in the demo even without real funds.

---

## Summary

The three main challenges we overcame:

1. **Strategy privacy vs verification** — solved with Merkle proofs.  
2. **Collaborative multi-sig trading** — solved with Fileverse team documents.  
3. **Portfolio simulation for demo purposes** — solved with a safe cash-to-simulated-asset system.

These solutions ensure that AetherGuard **maintains privacy, security, and transparency**, while still providing a realistic AI-assisted trading experience.

**Privacy**

# AetherGuard – Privacy-First 

## How AetherGuard Ensures Privacy

### 1. Encrypted Strategy Storage
- **Guardrail rules and private strategy** are never exposed to the AI or any third-party server.  
- Rules are stored in **Fileverse dDocs**, which are **end-to-end encrypted and decentralized**.  
- Only the user (or authorized collaborators) can access these documents.  
- This prevents **any centralized service from seeing or storing sensitive strategy data**.

### 2. Stateless AI Computation
- AI (Groq / Llama 3) analyzes the **portfolio state and investment goals** without storing the user's rules or prior strategies.  
- AI suggestions are **generated in memory** and remain stateless.  
- Ensures **no private data leaks to the AI provider**, fulfilling zero-trust principles.

### 3. Cryptographic Verification
- Each user's guardrail rules generate a **Merkle Root fingerprint** stored on-chain.  
- The AI and collaborators can **verify adherence to rules** without ever revealing the rules themselves.  
- Prevents rule tampering and guarantees **proof of compliance** without compromising privacy.

### 4. Multi-Sig Governance
- Collaborative decisions happen in **Fileverse Boardrooms**, a shared encrypted document space.  
- Multi-signature approval ensures **no single user or AI can act unilaterally**.  
- Maintains **privacy and control** while allowing secure collaboration.

### 5. Immutable Audit Trail
- Every decision, proposal, and execution is logged in a **Fileverse cryptographically signed audit trail**.  
- Audit logs are **tamper-proof and decentralized**, ensuring that private strategies remain secure while still proving compliance.  

### 6. User-Owned Identity
- Users connect via **MetaMask / Ethereum wallets**.  
- Identity is **permissionless and non-custodial**, meaning AetherGuard never stores sensitive personal information.  

### 7. Zero Surveillance, No Middlemen
- Fileverse replaces centralized storage solutions, removing **any third-party monitoring risk**.  
- Users maintain full ownership of data, strategy, and decisions.  
- AI only interacts with **encrypted, anonymized, or public components** of the portfolio, never the private guardrails.

---

## Summary: Why Privacy is Guaranteed
AetherGuard combines **Fileverse encrypted storage, stateless AI, cryptographic verification, and multi-sig governance** to create a system where:

- AI is **fully advisory**  
- User strategies and rules are **never exposed**  
- Collaboration is secure, decentralized, and private  
- All actions are verifiable **without revealing secrets**  

This approach **fully embodies the privacy track** and ensures users retain **complete control over their data and strategies**.

**The problem it solves**

## DarkEarn — Full Pitch With Reverse Bidding

---

## The Problem

Your income is permanently public on every Web3 platform.

Web3 platforms publish transactional details on public ledgers. While this promotes transparency, it makes private financial data visible to everyone — forever.

What that means in practice: you complete a $5,000 bounty on Superteam or Dework. The payment hits your wallet. Now anyone, forever, can go to Etherscan, paste your ENS name, and see:

- Every job you have ever been paid for
- Exactly how much each one paid
- Which company or protocol paid you
- How frequently you work

Your entire income history is a public ledger entry. Employers can lowball you because they already know what you earned last time. Competitors can track your clients. Tax authorities can trivially audit you.

This is not hypothetical. This is the current state of Web3 work.

---

## What DarkEarn Is

**First Dollar but private.** We are what Base built but with a privacy layer that should have existed from day one.

A bounty marketplace where your earnings, your clients, your work history, and your payment destination are completely hidden — mathematically, not just visually.

---

## Three Ways To Work On DarkEarn

### 1 — Standard Bounty (Poster posts, Hunter applies)
Poster locks funds in BitGo. Posts bounty publicly. Hunters apply anonymously as Applicant #1, #2, #3. Poster reveals and accepts. Work submitted via Fileverse encrypted document. Payment goes to stealth address — zero on-chain link to hunter's ENS identity.

### 2 — Reverse Bidding (Hunter posts their rate, Poster comes to them)
Hunter publishes a service listing — "I do Solidity audits. My rate is $3,000 per engagement. Available now." No wallet address shown. No income history visible. Poster browses listings, clicks Hire, locks funds in BitGo, and the engagement begins.

This flips the power dynamic entirely. Instead of 50 hunters competing for one poster's attention — one skilled hunter sets their price and posters compete for their time.

**Why this matters for privacy:** In the current Web3 world, a hunter who posts their rate on any platform immediately reveals their income expectations. Competitors see it. Future clients use it to anchor negotiations. On DarkEarn, the rate is public but the payment is private. Nobody can verify whether you actually got paid that rate, or more, or less. Your negotiating position stays yours.

**Reverse bidding flow:**
```
Hunter creates service listing
  → Title, category, rate, availability
  → No wallet address shown
  → Listed as "Contributor #4721" — anonymous
        ↓
Poster browses listings, filters by skill + rate
        ↓
Poster clicks Hire
  → Locks funds in BitGo
  → Sends private encrypted brief via Fileverse
        ↓
Hunter accepts engagement
        ↓
Same work + payment flow as standard bounty
        ↓
Payment to stealth address — rate paid is never provable on-chain
```

### 3 — Private Bids (Direct headhunting)
Poster finds a contributor in the directory (Band 2+ opt-in). Sends ECIES encrypted private bid directly to their address. Only that contributor can read it. Nobody else knows the offer was made or what it contained.

---

## How Privacy Works — The Technical Stack

**ZK Reputation** — Band 0 to 4 proven using Noir circuits. Your completion count, approval rate, dispute rate are private inputs. Only the band number is public. You cannot fake it. Nobody can reverse-engineer your history from it.

**Anonymous Applications** — You apply as Applicant #3. Poster never sees your name until they choose to reveal. Your ENS and wallet are stored privately in contract storage — never emitted in any public event.

**Encrypted Work** — Deliverables and project briefs stored as Fileverse encrypted documents on IPFS. Only the intended reader's wallet can decrypt. Not Google. Not DarkEarn. Not the blockchain.

**Stealth Addresses (ERC-5564)** — Payment is mathematically derived and announced on-chain. Your ENS wallet and your payment destination have zero on-chain connection. Anyone looking at Basescan sees a fresh address receiving funds. They cannot link it to alice.eth.

**Institutional Custody** — BitGo MPC wallets hold poster funds. Webhook policy verifies ZK reputation credential before co-signing any payment. Two independent privacy enforcement layers.

---

## We Are First Dollar But Better

First Dollar proved the Indian Web3 talent market is real. They showed that builders in India will compete for and complete crypto bounties. They built the demand.

DarkEarn is the infrastructure layer that should have been built alongside it. Same bounty marketplace. Same Base network. Same community.

The difference: on First Dollar your income history is on Etherscan forever. On DarkEarn it is mathematically impossible to trace.

---

**Challenges we ran into**

We started with BitGo for wallet management thinking it would gave us enterprise-grade custody. But the moment we got into it the passphrase handling alone was a rabbit hole.

This was a long internal argument. ENS looked like the obvious choice for identity  it's web3 native, human readable, already adopted. But the more we dug into it the more problems appeared. First, ENS registration costs gas  you're asking a hunter to pay just to sign up, which is terrible UX. Second, ENS is on Ethereum mainnet what if we deploy on a different chain? Third, and most importantly  hunters are supposed to be anonymous. Why would we force them to register a permanent public identity just to apply for jobs anonymously? It was contradictory to our own privacy thesis.
So we made a deliberate decision: ENS is mandatory only for posters because they need to be publicly accountable. Hunters get a deterministically generated codename black-fox-354 derived from their wallet address in the browser. No ENS, no gas, no setup friction. Zero. They connect their wallet and they're in.
That decision cleaned up the entire onboarding flow and made the privacy architecture more honest.

Future Scope
AI Agents competing alongside humans.
AI agents that can autonomously browse bounties, pick up work, complete it, and get paid — fully onchain, no human needed.
A marketplace where both humans and AI agents compete for work side by side. An agent sees a $500 Solidity audit bounty, applies, does the work, submits the deliverable via Fileverse, and receives payment to its stealth address — zero human intervention required.
Reverse bidding extends naturally here too. An AI agent posts its capabilities and rate. Posters hire it directly. The agent's payment history is as private as a human hunter's — the stealth address standard applies identically whether the recipient is a person or an autonomous agent.
This is the endgame: a fully private, permissionless marketplace for work where humans and agents compete on merit, not on publicly visible income history.

**Privacy**

DarkEarn's entire architecture is privacy-first. Every single step of the freelance flow application, brief, submission, payment has a dedicated privacy layer underneath it. 

We used real cryptographic primitives
We didn't just hide data behind a login wall and call it private. We used:

- ZK proofs (Semaphore) for anonymous identity during applications
- Lit Protocol for threshold encryption of work submissions
- ERC-5564 stealth addresses for on-chain payment privacy
- Soulbound NFTs for verifiable reputation without identity leakage

**Best creative use of ENS**

We used ENS as a trust signal, not an identity system
Every other project that uses ENS uses it the same way  replace your wallet address with a readable name. alice.eth instead of 0x1a2b. That is the default, obvious use. DarkEarn does something fundamentally different.

We used ENS as a one-sided trust primitive mandatory for posters, completely absent for hunters. That is a creative architectural decision nobody else has made.

What we did specifically

- Poster must have ENS — their name is permanently attached to every job they post, publicly, on-chain
- Hunter gets a deterministic codename  black-fox-354  generated from their wallet in the browser
- ENS reverse lookup is used to verify poster legitimacy before their job goes live on the board
- Post-reveal, the hunter's wallet address appears not their ENS keeping maximum privacy even after identity is unlocked

**Pool prize**

When a hunter completes work and expects payment, they need to know the poster is a real accountable entity — not a throwaway wallet that disappears after posting. ENS creates that accountability. A poster with base.eth attached to a $5,000 bounty has something to lose reputationally if they behave badly. A random 0x address has nothing.
ENS is what makes the prize pool trustworthy.

**Best Privacy Application using BitGo**

BitGo is not used for hunter wallets. Hunters use MetaMask self-custody, no friction. BitGo is used for one specific and critical function: the escrow vault.
When a poster locks $5,000 into a job's prize pool, that money sits in an escrow wallet until the work is approved. That escrow wallet is managed by BitGo. Here is why that matters for privacy:

- The escrow wallet is not owned by DarkEarn
- It is not owned by the poster
- It is not owned by the hunter
- It is a BitGo multi-sig wallet requiring 2-of-3 keys to move funds poster key, BitGo key, and a DarkEarn policy key

Nobody can unilaterally move the money. Not the poster. Not us. Not BitGo alone.

The traditional escrow problem: if DarkEarn runs the escrow, DarkEarn knows every transaction who paid who, how much, when. That is a centralized privacy leak.
BitGo's architecture solves this because:

Spending policies are enforced at the BitGo SDK level we set rules like "only release to the stealth address generated by ERC-5564" DarkEarn cannot override this
The API token authenticates the transaction policy, not the identity of the recipient BitGo never learns who the hunter is, only that the policy conditions were met
Passphrase-encrypted user key means even if BitGo's servers are compromised, the user key is useless without the poster's passphrase funds are safe

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

Big Tech builds tools that are convenient AND surveilled. Google Docs is free because Google reads everything in it. Notion stores your data on their servers unencrypted. Dropbox can open your files. Microsoft can read your Word documents stored on OneDrive.

This is not a bug. It is the business model. Ad targeting, AI training, data brokering all of it requires reading your content. Big Tech will never voluntarily give that up.
DarkEarn with Fileverse gives that up entirely. By design. By architecture.

Where Fileverse sits in DarkEarn
There are two documents in every DarkEarn job:

1. The private job brief  written by the poster, readable only by the selected winner

2. The work submission written by the hunter, readable only by the poster

Both of these live on Fileverse. Neither can be read by DarkEarn. Neither can be read by Fileverse. Neither can be read by anyone without the cryptographic key which lives in the user's wallet, not on any server.

**Privacy**

DarkEarn is the first freelance platform deployed on Base where every payment is private by default using stealth addresses, ZK proofs, and encrypted storage to bring real financial privacy to real users doing real work onchain.

1. Stealth Addresses on Base

ERC-5564 stealth address standard implemented and deployed on Base. Every payment on DarkEarn goes through this. When a hunter claims their prize, it lands on a one-time address that has never existed before on Base completely untraceable back to their identity. This is live onchain privacy for real payments, on Base, today.

2. ZK Anonymous Applications on Base

When a hunter applies for a job, a ZK proof is generated in their browser and verified by a smart contract on Base. The contract confirms: this person has valid reputation and skills without ever learning which wallet submitted the proof. Anonymous identity verification, verified onchain, on Base.

3. Private Escrow on Base

The entire prize pool lifecycle deposit, lock, release happens on Base via our escrow contract. The release goes to a stealth address. Base never sees a link between the poster's ENS identity and the hunter's payment destination. Financial privacy baked into every single transaction.

**BEST Overall Project**

This is not "imagine if web3 had privacy." Open Etherscan right now, paste any Superteam winner's wallet, and you will see their entire earning history in 10 seconds. The problem is live, it is affecting real people today, and nobody has fixed it. DarkEarn fixes it.

A ZK proof project. An encrypted storage project. A stealth address experiment. DarkEarn is the only submission where all four primitives ZK proofs, Lit Protocol encryption, ERC-5564 stealth addresses, and Soulbound reputation  work together as one product

A hunter connects their wallet. They get black-fox-354. They apply. They work. They get paid privately. They never touched a ZK circuit. They never configured encryption keys. They never thought about stealth addresses. The hardest crypto in the room is completely invisible to the end user. That is the real engineering challenge  and we solved it.

> BitSend. Money that works when nothing else does.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Payments have one fatal flaw – they require the internet.**

There are **2.2 billion people** without access to the internet. In 
conflict zones like Iran, the entire network goes dark overnight. 185 
million transactions were lost overnight. People cannot pay for 
their food. Not because they cannot afford it, but because they 
cannot access the network.

Each app has the same problem. No internet, no payment.


**BitSend solves the problem**

A **hybrid offline crypto payment app**. No internet required.

- Load funds online → stored as secure offline token
- Send via **Hotspot , QR code and Bluetooth**
- Settles on-chain via **BitGo** when the internet is available
- Built on **Base**: fast, cheap, ethereum-grade security
- Send to **ENS names**, rather than long wallet addresses
- Tamper-proof PDF receipts stored via **Fileverse**

Our **Backed Wallet** ensures double-spending is impossible.

**Money that works when nothing else does.**

**Challenges we ran into**

## The core challenge

The biggest challenge wasn't making the single transaction work; the 
challenge was making the **entire offline payment process dependably work**.

Not only do we need to coordinate wallet state, chain selection, transport 
mode, and offline behavior, we need to do this simultaneously. This was 
actually causing real issues in the early days: the UI would incorrectly 
indicate readiness, the wallet might appear funded and ready for handoff 
but not really be ready for handoff, or the transaction might fail 
silently after the user changed networks or transport modes.

I made significant architectural changes to address these issues: I 
centralized logic around clear **state boundaries**, splitting **"prepare 
while online" from "sign and hand off offline"**, and ensuring the UI 
clearly presents the user with the status and recovery options rather than 
allowing them to proceed in an invalid state.

**DeFi**

**BitSend is bringing DeFi to the physical world
 including those parts of the world that have no internet.**

The majority of DeFi today is built on the assumption that users are 
connected. We take that assumption away entirely. With a combination of 
offline token signing, **Base** chain settlement, **ENS** name resolution, 
and **BitGo** custody, we're making decentralized peer-to-peer 
transactions possible in zero-connectivity situations.

DeFi is now possible in conflict zones, rural areas, or during 
infrastructure blackouts – giving access to the 2.2 billion people that 
current DeFi solutions completely ignore.

**Best creative use of ENS**

Every ENS integration works the same way  resolve a name, get an 
address, send a transaction. Online. Always online.

BitSend does something nobody has done with ENS before  it makes 
ENS names work **with no internet connection.**

In a blackout, a conflict zone, or anywhere without signal, users 
can still type **ali.eth** instead of a 42-character wallet address 
and complete a real payment. We built a local ENS resolution cache 
on-device that stores recently resolved names  so the human-readable 
identity layer ENS provides doesn't disappear the moment connectivity 
does.

This matters most for exactly the people ENS was philosophically built 
for  giving everyone a readable, ownable identity in Web3. But until 
now, that identity was useless the moment the internet went down.

BitSend is the first app where your ENS name works in a war zone.

That's the most creative use of ENS we could imagine because it's 
the most human one.

**Pool prize**

BitSend integrates ENS to make offline crypto payments human-readable.

Sending to a wallet address offline is a terrible user experience 
long hex strings are error-prone, especially in high-stress situations 
like conflict zones or emergencies. BitSend lets users send payments 
to **ENS names** instead, making peer-to-peer transfers as simple as 
typing a name.

The key technical challenge was resolving ENS names in a 
zero-connectivity environment. Live ENS lookups require internet  which defeats the entire purpose of an offline payment app. We solved 
this by building a **local ENS resolution cache** on-device, storing 
recently resolved addresses so users can send to human-readable names 
even with no signal.

ENS makes BitSend accessible to real people in real crisis situations not just crypto-native users who memorise wallet addresses. That 
alignment between ENS's mission of human-readable identity and 
BitSend's mission of financial access without internet is exactly why 
this integration matters.

**Best DeFi Application using BitGo**

BitSend uses BitGo as the settlement and custody layer for all offline 
transactions.

When a user makes a payment offline  via Bluetooth, hotspot, or QR 
code  the transaction is signed and stored locally on device. The 
moment internet connectivity is restored, BitSend automatically pushes 
all pending transactions through **BitGo** for on-chain settlement on 
**Base**.

BitGo gives BitSend something no other offline payment app has
**institutional-grade custody and settlement reliability** behind a 
consumer-facing product. Users transacting in conflict zones, rural 
areas, or during infrastructure blackouts can trust that when their 
transactions finally settle, they settle correctly and securely.

BitGo isn't just an integration for us  it's the trust backbone of 
the entire offline-to-onchain flow. Without it, delayed settlement at 
scale would be unreliable. With it, every offline payment eventually 
becomes a verified, immutable on-chain transaction.

That's what makes BitSend the strongest DeFi application built on 
BitGo in this hackathon.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

Big Tech builds payment infrastructure for people who already have 
everything  stable internet, functioning banks, reliable governments.

They will never build for conflict zones. They will never build for 
the 2.2 billion without internet. There's no ad revenue in a blackout. 
No growth metric in a war zone. No quarterly target served by giving 
financial access to people governments are trying to freeze out.

So they don't build it. And they never will.

BitSend does exactly that.

We use **Fileverse** to store every transaction receipt as a 
tamper-proof, decentralized PDF  permanently accessible, censorship 
resistant, and outside the control of any platform that could be 
pressured to delete it. In environments where governments shut down 
the internet specifically to erase financial activity, having an 
immutable paper trail stored on decentralized infrastructure isn't 
a feature. It's protection.

That's what Fileverse enables for BitSend  and that's exactly what 
Big Tech will never touch.

**DeFi 2.0 - New Primitives**

BitSend introduces a primitive that doesn't exist in DeFi today **offline-first payment settlement on Base.**

Every DeFi primitive currently assumes liveness. Swaps, transfers, 
lending  they all require a live RPC connection to function. BitSend 
breaks that assumption by separating transaction signing from 
settlement, allowing fully valid, cryptographically signed transactions 
to be prepared and exchanged offline via Bluetooth, hotspot, or QR 
code  then settled on **Base** the moment connectivity returns.

This creates a new class of DeFi interaction: **asynchronous 
peer-to-peer settlement.** The payment is real and binding at the 
moment of offline handoff. Base just confirms what already happened.

We chose Base specifically for its low fees and fast finality 
critical when batching multiple delayed offline transactions that 
stack up during a blackout and hit the chain simultaneously.

BitSend isn't using Base as a backend. It's using Base to anchor a 
genuinely new DeFi primitive  one that works for the 2.2 billion 
people the rest of DeFi has never been able to reach.

**BEST Overall Project**

**BitSend** is a solution to a problem that no other project in this hackathon is touching what happens to payments when the internet disappears?

It is not a concept. It is a working hybrid crypto payment app that has a 
full end-to-end flow, including pre-loaded token signing, **Bluetooth, 
hotspot, and QR code** device-to-device transfer, ENS name resolution, 
Base chain settlement via BitGo, and tamper-proof Fileverse receipts – 
all without a single byte of internet during the transaction itself.

The tech is not a concept. The problem is. The population it is serving – 
2.2 billion without internet, millions more in active conflict zones – 
has never had a solution like this.

Most hackathon projects optimize an existing flow. BitSend works when 
every other payment app fails.

It is a solution to a problem that matters. Therefore, it should win 
Best Overall.

> Monetising artistry through agentic royalties.

![ENS](https://img.shields.io/badge/ENS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Base Sepolia](https://img.shields.io/badge/Base%20Sepolia-333333?style=flat-square) ![Fileverse](https://img.shields.io/badge/Fileverse-333333?style=flat-square) ![HeyElsa](https://img.shields.io/badge/HeyElsa-333333?style=flat-square) ![Bitgo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Bitgo-333333?style=flat-square) ![Solidity, Hardhat, Ethers.js (v6)](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity,%20Hardhat,%20Ethers.js%20(v6)-333333?style=flat-square) ![ERC-721, ERC-8004, EIP-4906, x402](https://img.shields.io/badge/ERC--721,%20ERC--8004,%20EIP--4906,%20x402-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js%2016,%20React%2019,%20TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Generative AI is currently facing a massive crisis of consent and compensation. AI models and autonomous agents scrape, synthesize, and utilize human creations like UI designs, branding, and art without affording attribution or royalties to the original creators. Designers are losing their creative legacy to the algorithms trained on their work.

**Eidos8004** solves this by turning AI from a threat into a paying customer. It is a decentralized portfolio and royalty platform that bridges the gap between human designers and the agentic economy.

---
How it works:
- Designers upload their work as **Dynamic NFTs**, breaking them down into purchasable "**artifacts**" (e.g., color palettes, layouts, typography) and setting **threshold prices**.
- AI Agents (acting on behalf of clients or development tools) autonomously browse the registry, negotiate pricing via smart contracts, and execute headless **x402** payments to license these artifacts for inspiration.
- The Protocol utilizes **ERC-8004** (Agent Identity) to verify the agents, ensuring transparent, on-chain attribution and direct ETH royalty transfers to the human creator.

Eidos8004 creates a verifiable, fair-trade economy for designs in the age of AI.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a platform that sits at the intersection of AI integration and complex Web3 primitives for the fair designer economy presented following challenges:

- Determining exact percentage of the inspiration taken by a client's agent from different type of designs requires a fine-tuned pre-trained model which is not realistic to develop in the hackathon timeframe. Thus we took the good old NFT approach of splitting the art into artifacts so that the creator will assign cost to each artifact in a way that the total threshold price is equal to the sum of all the costs of artifacts.

- Complex State sync with Ethers v6 & React 19: Managing the asynchronous state of four interconnected smart contracts (AgentRegistry, DesignRegistry, AttributionPayment, ReputationForum) across a modern Next.js 16 App Router was difficult. We overcame this by abstracting the contract instantiations into a centralized getContract utility and wrapping the UI in highly localized, custom React hooks (useAgentRegistry, useWallet) rather than relying on a heavy, monolithic global context provider.

- Dependency Collisions: During the merger of our high-fidelity, framer-motion-powered "glassmorphism" UI with the Web3 backend, We ran into severe npm ERESOLVE conflicts regarding Hardhat v3 peer dependencies and UI libraries on Vercel. I resolved this by enforcing legacy-peer-deps, manually aligning the React versions, and isolating the frontend from the Hardhat build pipeline.

- Simulating Headless Agent Payments (x402): Representing autonomous agent-to-agent negotiations within a hackathon timeframe was conceptually challenging. I abstracted the negotiation logic into Next.js serverless API routes (/api/agents/negotiate), which act as the "AI Client", verifying the designer's on-chain threshold price before returning the x402 payment proof parameters required to unlock the smart contract.

**AI**

**Eidos8004** is fundamentally designed for the burgeoning Agentic Economy. Rather than using AI to generate images, the platform targets the infrastructure of AI development itself. It facilitates Machine-to-Machine (**M2M**) and Agent-to-Human economic interactions. The primary "users" purchasing assets on the platform are autonomous AI agents who must negotiate, verify their **ERC-8004** identity, and execute crypto transactions to "legally" use human-made designs as training data or inspiration.

**Best creative use of ENS**

**ENS** integration is crucial for humanizing the platform. In a system populated by autonomous AI agents and human designers, raw 0x... addresses are unreadable. ENS is used to resolve the addresses of human designers on their portfolio pages and within the **Moltbook-style Reputation Forum**. It establishes verifiable, human-readable trust in an ecosystem heavily populated by programmatic actors.

**Best DeFi Application using BitGo**

In a true production environment, AI agents require programmatic, headless wallets to hold funds and execute x402 payments autonomously. We integrated the **BitGo**'s robust wallet infrastructure to secure these underlying Agent Wallets. BitGo ensures that the AI agents have a **secure sandbox** to programmatically sign attribution transactions and transfer ETH royalties to creators without requiring manual human intervention for every micro-transaction.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

**Fileverse** provided the decentralized collaboration and storage infrastructure necessary to house the high-fidelity design assets (e.g., source code, CSS modules, design files). Instead of using standard, publicly accessible IPFS links, Fileverse's **programmable access control** ensured that the raw, usable design files are encrypted and only unlocked for the AI Agent after the x402 payment and on-chain attribution are successfully verified by the smart contract.

**AI × Onchain**

**Eidos8004** is built entirely on the premise that the future of the internet is **Agentic**. It sits squarely at the intersection of AI development and Onchain infrastructure by providing the missing economic layer for human-to-AI interaction.

Currently, AI models and autonomous agents scrape and utilize human design data without consent or compensation. Eidos8004 leverages **Base Sepolia** to flip this paradigm, turning AI from a data scraper into a verified, paying customer.

---

**How it utilizes Base for AI x Onchain innovation:**

- **Agent Identity (ERC-8004 on Base)**: AI Agents are registered as first-class citizens on the Base network. Their capabilities, reputation, and wallets are verifiable onchain, meaning a designer's smart contract always knows which AI is interacting with their work.
- **Headless Micro-transactions (x402)**: The platform facilitates autonomous M2M (Machine-to-Machine) negotiations. An AI agent can independently discover a human's design, agree to the threshold price, and execute an x402 payment to license the asset.
- **Why Base is Critical**: This economy relies on thousands of programmatic, low-value licensing transactions occurring in the background without human intervention. Base's ultra-low latency, nominal gas fees, and robust Ethereum-equivalent security are the only way to make an automated, agent-driven royalty system financially viable and scalable.

The entire **Eidos8004 protocol suite** (DesignRegistry, AgentRegistry, AttributionPayment, ReputationForum) is deployed natively on Base Sepolia.  Eidos8004 relies on facilitating thousands of headless micro-transactions between AI agents and creators. **Base**'s extremely low fees, robust Ethereum-equivalent security, and fast block times are absolute prerequisites for making this automated, agentic royalty economy financially viable.

**Best Use of Elsa x402 and Elsa OpenClaw skills**

**HeyElsa** serves as the **conversational bridge** between human users and the on-chain protocol. Instead of navigating complex dashboards, a designer can ask Elsa: "Hey Elsa, how much royalty did my 'Dark Mode Dashboard' earn today?" Conversely, a human client can instruct their agent via Elsa: "Find me a minimalist landing page design under 0.05 ETH and negotiate a license." It makes the complex interactions of **ERC-8004** and **x402** payments accessible via natural language.

**BEST Overall Project**

**Eidos8004** tackles one of the most pressing socio-technological issues of our time which is AI copyright and creator compensation; using novel, cutting-edge web3 primitives. It goes beyond a simple NFT marketplace by integrating **ERC-8004** (NFTs as Agents), **EIP-4906** (Dynamic Metadata for artifacts), and the **x402** protocol (Headless Agent Payments). Combined with a production-ready, highly web2-friendly UI/UX and a fully tested Solidity backend, it offers a complete, visionary solution to a real-world problem.
