### DeVault
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/devault-8997) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/GrindingHZ/DeVault) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://devault-marketplace.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.loom.com/share/6a4b2c69841548cba70015307ffdd627) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> A pawn shop with a public order book.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![nestjs](https://img.shields.io/badge/nestjs-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

Most of our hard problems were not the lending logic. They came from the chain's own rules, and from errors that confidently pointed in the wrong direction.

**zkLogin proofs are bound to one network:** A zkLogin signature commits to a maxEpoch, and every Sui network counts epochs separately, so a proof made on mainnet can never verify against testnet. Our API checked against a single network fixed at boot, which locked out anyone whose wallet sat elsewhere. It now tries each allowed network until one accepts the proof, so nobody has to move their wallet just to sign in.
**One line of error handling hid it:** `catch { return false; }` collapsed an expired proof, a wrong network, and a timed-out full node into the same "invalid signature". That is also why it looked intermittent rather than broken: a rate-limited node was being reported to users as a bad signature, so retrying eventually worked. Unreachable now raises something different from invalid, and every attempt logs which network refused it and why.
**A 404 that had nothing to do with the listing:** Buying on the secondary market failed with "That is no longer here", while the listing was plainly still there. The API resolves the buyer's coin before it ever looks at the listing, and throws a not-found when no single coin covers the ask, which our frontend maps to that one message. An error's status code is part of its meaning, and reusing 404 for "you cannot afford this" sent us hunting a phantom.
**You cannot add a Display after publishing:** Showing the item's photograph in wallets needs a Display, which needs a Publisher, which needs a one-time witness that exists only inside `init` at publish time. Our package had shipped without one, and `init` never runs again on upgrade, so there was no route but a full republish under a new package ID.
**Deployment that failed silently:** Our Vercel config sat at the repository root while Vercel read it from the app directory, so the API rewrite was simply absent. Every call returned 404 with nothing in the build log to explain why, and the fix was making the repo carry the config in both places.

**The problem it solves**

Pawnbroking is one of the oldest forms of credit and one of the least changed. If you need short-term cash against something you own, you walk into a shop, accept whatever single rate that shop offers, and walk out with a paper ticket. The shop holds your item, sets the price, and keeps the only record that the item is yours.

DeVault rebuilds that arrangement as a market. The receipt becomes an object in the borrower's own wallet, and lenders compete to fund a loan against it.

**Title you actually hold:** The pawn ticket is a Sui object in the borrower's wallet, not a row in our database. Whoever holds it is the owner of record, and nothing in the system can move it.
**Competition instead of one quote:** The borrower names the amount and the highest rate they will pay. Lenders bid by undercutting each other downward from that ceiling.
**Rules enforced, not promised:** Loan-to-value ceilings by item category, the maximum interest rate, and the grace period before default are all checked on chain at the moment of the transaction, not written into terms and conditions.
**Money held, never custodied:** A lender's offer escrows into a hold that can only fund that loan or return to them. Losing offers refund themselves by reading the listing's own status, needing nothing from us.
**A way out for lenders:** A funded position is a transferable object carrying its own terms, so a lender can sell it mid-loan instead of waiting for maturity. The borrower is not involved and their loan does not change.
**Stablecoin settlement throughout:** Every leg moves in USDC: offer escrow, disbursement, repayment, payoff, and secondary sales.
**No gas, no crypto learning curve:** Transactions are sponsored and sign-in works with a Google account, so a borrower never holds SUI, manages a seed phrase, or sees a wallet prompt they do not understand.

The goal is simple: make a pawn loan behave like a market, and make the ticket something the borrower actually holds.

**PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS**

DeVault is a stablecoin payments product end to end. There is no protocol token
and nothing to speculate on. Every leg of the product is a USDC payment.

**Five distinct payment legs, all in USDC**

1. A lender's offer escrows USDC into a hold.
2. Accepting an offer disburses the principal to the borrower.
3. Repayment parks the payoff back in the loan.
4. The lender pulls that payoff.
5. The secondary market settles a position sale between two strangers.

Settlement is Circle's own USDC on Sui testnet, not a mock coin we mint for
ourselves. The package ships a stand-in coin used only on a local network.

**Money is held, never custodied**

A lender's offer does not send us their money. It goes into a `FundsHold` that
can only be consumed by the borrower accepting that exact offer, or refunded to
the address that funded it. A losing offer refunds itself: the proof is the
listing's own on-chain status, so nobody needs our permission or our uptime to
get their money back. We are never a party that can hold funds hostage.

**Atomic settlement**

Selling a loan position is a swap, not a promise. The seller's note is escrowed
in a shared listing and the buyer's coin and that note change hands in one
transaction, or neither moves. Neither side trusts the other and neither trusts
us.

**Users never touch gas**

Member transactions are sponsored: the operator is the gas owner and co-signs.
A borrower or lender only ever thinks in USDC. That removes the single worst
onboarding step in crypto payments, holding a second asset just to move the
first one.

**Coin-agnostic by construction**

Thirty public entry points across the pledge, escrow and market modules are
generic over the coin type. Moving from our stand-in coin to Circle USDC needed
no republish, only repointing the recorded deployment. Any other stablecoin is
the same one-line change.

**Amounts are handled like money, not like numbers**

Base units as `u64` on chain and `bigint` off it, with no float anywhere near an
amount. Interest is taken in `u128` because principal times rate times elapsed
milliseconds overflows `u64` within days, and the division truncates in the
borrower's favour on purpose. The same arithmetic exists twice, in Move and in
TypeScript, line for line, so the quote a borrower is shown is the number the
chain computes.

### Giam Siap
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/giam-siap-2ca3) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/xinweileow/giam-siap.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/gNl3kPda7ME) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Autonomous purchasing bot for SMEs

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Telegram](https://img.shields.io/badge/Telegram-333333?style=flat-square) ![Qwen](https://img.shields.io/badge/Qwen-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hermes Agent](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hermes%20Agent-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## Problem Statement

Three related pains, one system:

- **Owners waste real time and money just watching prices move.** Ingredient prices shift day to day across vendors, but checking them is manual and unrewarding work — so owners either miss the dip and overpay, or react too slowly and stock out mid-service.
- **SME restaurants and cafes don't have a procurement team to fall back on.** A larger F&B chain has staff whose job is to know what a fair market price looks like and how much stock the business actually needs. A single-outlet SME owner has none of that — they're guessing at both numbers themselves, on top of running the floor, which means the business either overpays for what it buys or over/under-orders against demand it never had time to properly size.
- **Every order today means a negotiation, and every negotiation means friction on both sides.** Owners spend time haggling price and credit terms with suppliers instead of running their business; suppliers spend that same time chasing Net-30/Net-60 invoices instead of getting paid, which strains their cash flow and ties up working capital that should already be theirs.
- **Neither side can safely automate any of this today.** Web2 tooling can't be trusted with real spending authority without either a human re-approving every transaction (which defeats the point of automating it) or a high-fee third-party processor sitting in the middle (which eats the margin automation was supposed to protect).

**Giam Siap's answer, in one sentence: it gives an SME owner the procurement team they can't afford to hire, and replaces the negotiation both sides can't afford to keep wasting time at.** 
The owner doesn't need to arrive with a price and quantity already worked out — they can just state a need (*"I want to procure coffee beans"*), and the agent asks a few follow-ups about their actual business (location, operating days, typical volume, stock on hand), researches the real current market price itself, and proposes both numbers with its reasoning, doing the market research and demand sizing a bigger business would pay a team to do. And because the owner is only ever agreeing to an objective, pre-committed condition — not haggling a deal with a person on the other end — there's nothing left to negotiate: the smart contract, not the agent and not any human, locks the funds the moment the owner confirms and releases them the instant the vendor's own signed price meets that condition, so the supplier is paid instantly and trustlessly, with no invoice to chase and no counterparty risk on either side.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

**No real vendor to test settlement against.** Early on, the biggest blocker to proving the escrow actually worked end-to-end was that we didn't have a real, registered vendor issuing signed price quotes — and the contract's whole trust model depends on verifying exactly that signature before it will release funds. Without one, we couldn't exercise the release path at all, only the lock path. We solved this by standing up a mock vendor endpoint that behaves like a real registered vendor: it signs price quotes the same way a genuine vendor integration would, so `checkVendorPrice` and the watcher's settlement logic could be exercised against something structurally identical to production, not stubbed out. That let us validate the full escrow → price-match → payout flow was technically sound before a single real vendor was ever onboarded.

**Getting owners in is easy — getting vendors in is the hard part.** zkLogin means an *owner* can join in one Google sign-in with no wallet, no gas, no crypto knowledge. Vendors don't get that same free ride: settling a real trade means a vendor has to actually be reachable on-chain, which is a much bigger ask than "log in with Google" for a supplier who's never touched a blockchain and has no reason to care that they're on one. This is really a two-sided cold-start problem — the buyer side of the marketplace is nearly frictionless, but the supply side isn't, and a marketplace with only buyers doesn't work.

Longer-term, our plan is to make joining worth a vendor's while directly: a commission/toll-fee reward for vendors who come on-chain, with the reward gated behind a minimum retention period (e.g. staying active on-chain for 12 months) so we're paying for vendors who actually stick around and keep settling trades, not one-off sign-ups chasing a payout.

**AI × SUI**

## AI x Sui Track Fit

**Ideas:** transaction-executing assistant, workflow automation, agent-to-agent commerce.

- **AI solves a real problem** — an SME owner has no procurement team, so pricing and quantity decisions fall on whoever is already running the floor: they either don't have time to check vendor prices and overpay, or guess at order size without ever properly sizing demand. Hermes' market-search step takes that job over — it asks about the business (location, operating days, volume, stock on hand), researches the real current vendor price itself, and comes back with a sized, priced order proposal instead of leaving the owner to work both numbers out alone. The benefit isn't just saved time: it's an owner who now orders at a fair, researched price and a quantity that actually matches their business, without needing to hire the staff a bigger chain would for exactly this.
- **Why Sui specifically** — the product needs a currency escrow that no one, not even the agent or the team running it, can quietly override once it's locked, and Move's object model gives that for free: the escrowed coin is a resource with one owner and one exit path (`execute_order`'s signature check or a cancel), so there's no shared mutable state for a bug or a rogue call to corrupt mid-flight. zkLogin and sponsored transactions being native Sui/Enoki primitives, not a third-party wallet SDK bolted on top, is what makes it possible to onboard an owner with just a Google login and no gas token in the first place. And PTBs let the whole "source payment coin → lock into escrow" step happen as one atomic transaction, so there's never a half-finished order sitting in limbo.
- **Thoughtful UX** — the interface is Telegram, not a wallet dApp, because that's where the target user already is. SME restaurant and cafe owners aren't crypto-native and won't install a wallet extension or manage a seed phrase just to buy ingredients — they already run their business through a phone and a chat app. So the entire blockchain layer is hidden behind a conversation: sign in with Google (zkLogin), never touch gas (Enoki sponsorship), and start from a bare need like *"I want to procure coffee beans"* instead of a form full of on-chain parameters. The owner experiences "texting a bot," not "using a blockchain."

**Sui features used:** zkLogin (via Enoki) for non-custodial login · sponsored transactions (Enoki gas station) so owners never hold gas · Programmable Transaction Blocks composing coin-sourcing and the `create_order` Move call in one atomic transaction · on-chain ed25519 signature verification gating payout.

### Thetanutty Farm
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/thetanutty-farm-321b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Ong-pogs/thetanutty) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://thetanutty.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/FzNGQrREfgI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> pogs

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![AAVE](https://img.shields.io/badge/AAVE-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![React Three Fiber](https://img.shields.io/badge/React%20Three%20Fiber-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Thetanutty makes selling puts easier to approach through an interactive farming experience.

For crypto users new to options, collecting a premium sounds straightforward, but understanding the commitment behind it is harder. Users must choose a strike and expiry, determine how much collateral to lock, understand potential assignment, and follow their position after opening it.

 Thetanutty brings these decisions into one guided journey powered by Thetanuts:

  - Choose a seed: Browse live offers from market makers to buy physically settled ETH puts.
  - Review before planting: See the premium received, collateral required, expiry, and possible gains and losses.
  - Plant a real position: Confirm the required wallet transactions to sell the put on Base.
  - Follow its growth: Each farm plot represents a real position, with growth tied to its actual time to expiry.

  We focus on puts because our initial user starts with USDC and is willing to acquire ETH at an agreed price. Physical settlement matches that intention: if assigned, the user buys ETH at the strike, even if the market price has fallen below it. Covered calls serve a different
  journey for users who already hold ETH and are willing to sell it.

  The farm makes the position visible and approachable while keeping its real financial obligation explicit

**Challenges we ran into**

** Correctly handling the seller’s collateral**

For the maker-long physical-put orders we integrated, the SDK’s preview returned the premium as totalCollateral. However, the user is selling the put and must supply collateral based on strike price multiplied by contract size. We implemented separate premium and collateral calculations using integer arithmetic and validated the manual execution path with a successful Base mainnet fill.

**  Keeping quotes valid during multiple wallet transactions**

Opening a position can require USDC approval, supplying USDC to Aave, approving aBasUSDC, and filling the option. The original maker quote can expire during that sequence. We refresh the order and simulate the exact fill before the final wallet confirmation, enforcing a minimum acceptable premium.

 ** Handling uncertain transaction outcomes**

A slow confirmation or replaced transaction must not be reported as a failed trade, because that could encourage a duplicate submission. We added transaction reconciliation and a wallet-specific guard shared across browser tabs to distinguish pending, confirmed and failed transactions.

**Making the farm meaningful without obscuring risk**

The visual experience needed to reflect real financial state. Plot growth follows actual expiry time, positions are linked to on-chain records, and the review displays collateral, assignment obligations and payoff scenarios. Premium received is shown separately from realised results so it is not mistaken for profit.

**Constraining the AI farmhand**

We separated model decisions from transaction authority. The model works within deterministically screened candidates, while signed user limits and execution checks control what can actually be traded.

**BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK**

Thetanutty is a consumer options application built directly on the Thetanuts SDK and OptionBook on Base.

  We use Thetanuts’ live order feed to discover maker-long physical ETH put bids. When a user plants a seed, they take the seller side of one of these bids. Our application prepares Aave-wrapped USDC collateral, calculates the seller’s required amount, coordinates approvals,
  refreshes the order, simulates the fill, and executes through Thetanuts.

  After execution, indexed position data connects the trade back to its farm plot, allowing the user to inspect its collateral, premium and expiry.

  Our contribution is a complete manual opening workflow and visual position experience for this specific strategy, including a correction for the seller-collateral mismatch encountered in the SDK preview.

 The manual path has completed a real Base mainnet physical-put fill:

  0xdf3323fefb54cd040a0e86cca3733e4c469a77e33c85a0351e9e987dcfda76f3

Thetanuts supplies the essential liquidity and execution infrastructure behind every planted position.

**AI × OPTIONS**

Thetanutty includes an AI farmhand that translates natural-language preferences into a structured options policy and helps select trades from live Thetanuts pricing.

 Gemini drafts policies and selects from candidates that have already passed deterministic eligibility checks. Users review and sign their limits, including collateral exposure, strike bounds, expiry bounds and trading frequency.

 The model cannot approve its own policy, choose arbitrary position sizes, construct transaction calldata or bypass the signed limits. A separate execution layer validates the selected trade and coordinates the Thetanuts transaction through a dedicated wallet. Decisions and
  refusals are recorded for inspection.

 The manual trading path has been proven on Base mainnet. The autonomous farmhand is implemented, but an end-to-end armed-to-filled run has not yet been demonstrated.

### SuiPay
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/suipay-0990) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/waisumyong/SuiPay) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/G6FWPNJb-AM) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Simple merchant payment platform

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![sui](https://img.shields.io/badge/sui-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Merchants who want to accept digital asset payments often face complex payment flows and a lack of simple tools for managing on-chain payments. SuiPay solves this by providing a simple merchant-focused payment system built on Sui. Merchants can create payment requests, customers can pay directly using their Sui wallets, and transactions can be verified on-chain.

**Challenges we ran into**

A key challenge was integrating Sui wallet functionality and handling on-chain transactions correctly in our Next.js application. We had to learn how to work with the Sui SDK, construct transactions, and handle asynchronous transaction states.

We overcame these challenges through iterative testing on Sui Testnet, checking transaction results on-chain, and refining the payment flow to ensure the UI correctly reflected the transaction status.

**PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS**

SuiPay brings simple and practical on-chain payments to merchants using the Sui network. Merchants can create payment requests and receive payments directly through Sui wallets, while transactions are recorded transparently on-chain. Sui's fast and low-cost infrastructure makes it well suited for everyday digital payments. The MVP currently runs on Sui Testnet, with future plans to expand into stablecoin payments, multi-currency support, invoicing, and merchant payment management.

Team **milo ais** -- [sumyong wai](https://github.com/waisumyong), [Jasper Lim](https://github.com/oktobuoy)

> Decentralized Factual Verification Protocol

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![move](https://img.shields.io/badge/move-333333?style=flat-square) ![sui](https://img.shields.io/badge/sui-333333?style=flat-square) ![Walrus](https://img.shields.io/badge/Walrus-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

**Gonka weather.**
Shared gateway 429s/524s, erratic response times, and silent model-swapping risked commit deadlines. We resolved this with X-Gonka-No-Fallback to fail closed on swaps, 25-second same-model hedging, an immediate commit pump as seats finish, and a two-minute probe queue that halts submissions during bad gateway weather and auto-relaunches failed runs up to three times.

**Jurors answering from memory.** 
Models hallucinated citations without opening sources. We moved all browsing execution to the engine: citations are now strictly verified against stored text from pages the juror actually visited, requiring quotes from two distinct domains and counter-evidence searches, or the vote fails closed to UNSURE.

**Sui randomness rules, then a live draw starvation.** 
Sui’s &Random rules forced us into a private entry function drawing all five seats at the end of a PTB, but a non-backtracking draw starved committees when new stake was added. We fixed it with an eight-rejection resample fallback, stake eligibility guards, a MISSING_COMMITTEE void mechanism, and replay tests across historical randomness states.

**Byte-identical commitments in two languages.** 
A single mismatched byte in blake2b256(BCS(preimage)) between TypeScript and Move invalidates reveals. We unified the state codes into a strict wire contract and pinned six shared test vectors across both codebases to validate edge cases, phases, and BCS length prefixes.

**Running four processes on one operator key.** 
Splitting the app across Railway workers broke database locks via connection pooling, created gas coin race conditions, and caused Walrus-to-Sui epoch mismatches. We switched to transaction-scoped advisory locks (pg_advisory_xact_lock), assigned dedicated gas coins per worker, rebuilt retry factories, and added an explicit epoch converter.

**The problem it solves**

### The problem

Whenever a disputed question is worth money or attention, somebody has to declare the answer. Today that is one AI model, a token-weighted vote, or a private resolution desk. None show their work, all can be wrong or captured, and human fact-checkers are stepping back just as generative AI makes convincing falsehoods free. Asking multiple AIs instead of one changes nothing if their votes live in a server log the operator can edit. Verification has to be a property of the system, not a promise from whoever runs it.

### What OpenVerdict does

Paste a statement or a URL. OpenVerdict turns it into one checkable claim, convenes a jury of five AI jurors, and settles a verdict on Sui that anyone can recompute.

- **A jury, not a chatbot.** Sui's native randomness draws five seats across DeepSeek, Kimi and MiniMax via GonkaRouter, at most two per family. No vendor or operator picks the judges.
- **Research you can watch.** Each juror searches the live web for and against the claim. Every search and page opened appears on the claim page as it happens, and every quote is hashed and stored on Walrus. A YES or NO needs word-for-word quotes from two different sites and a search for counter-evidence, or it fails closed.
- **Secret votes, then a public debate.** Jurors seal their votes on Sui before anyone reveals, so nobody can copy another juror. Four of five matching votes settle the claim in about twelve minutes. A split jury cross-examines in public, citing only evidence already on record, and votes once more under seal. Still split means UNRESOLVED, never a forced answer.
- **A verdict on chain.** An immutable certificate on Sui with a 0 to 100 Truth Score. Budgets escrow in SUI, seats that did valid work are paid, and anyone can stake SUI on a seat.
- **All AI on Gonka.** Every inference runs through gonkarouter.io, and each Gonka Request ID is committed on chain before the vote is revealed, so it can be checked against Gonka's public receipts.
- **Built for agents too.** Any agent can drive and recompute the whole flow with the `ov` command line (weather, board, extract, submit, watch, audit, trace) or the skill at app.openverdict.info/SKILL.md, installable with `npx skills add Marcussy34/OpenVerdict`.

### What people use it for

- **Prediction markets and DAOs.** An oracle for questions no price feed can settle: did the milestone ship, did the grant deliver, did the proposal meet its conditions. Bonded claims finalize free when nobody challenges. A challenge convenes the jury, and the losing bond pays for it.
- **Anyone with a viral claim.** A verdict with the evidence, the dissent and the exact pages the jury read, instead of "an AI said so".

### Why it is safer

Nothing rests on trusting us. Fetch the bytes from Walrus, hash them, compare against Sui, and re-ask the same model through Gonka. The Audit page reruns 15 checks per juror in your browser, and `ov audit` reruns more than a hundred from the terminal. Reveal keys are time-locked with Mysten Seal, so sealed juror work opens after the deadline even if we disappear. The operator can pause but cannot forge: an edited vote, a swapped page or a changed score breaks a hash anyone can check.

**AI × SUI**

OpenVerdict is a decentralized verification protocol for factual claims, and Sui is the court it runs in. Five AI juror seats from three model families (DeepSeek, Kimi, MiniMax, all through GonkaRouter) research a claim on the live web, seal secret ballots, cross-examine a deadlock in public, and the verdict settles on Sui as an immutable certificate anyone can recompute. Disputed questions today are settled by token-whale votes, private resolution desks, or one AI model whose reasoning lives in a log the operator can edit; OpenVerdict gives markets, DAOs and the public a verdict that no single vendor can steer and that the chain acts on. It is live on Sui testnet at https://app.openverdict.info, submitting and reading need no wallet or gas, and a settled certificate with a 5 of 5 jury is here: https://suiscan.xyz/testnet/object/0x42954c917d0b7e34cb4634091a5ece1921a89a931f4872f690971b62fdcee706

Sui is the mechanism, not a logo. sui::random draws the five seats inside a private entry function under diversity caps, Clock enforces every deadline, and Move recomputes each commit-reveal ballot (blake2b256(BCS(preimage))), applies the 4-of-5 quorum, computes the Truth Score and mints the certificate, across 8 modules and 89 Move tests. Jurors are AgentProfile objects controlled by AgentCaps; seats, run approvals, stakes and payout tickets are owned objects, and certificates carry Object Display metadata. Payments run in SUI: claim budgets escrow at creation, valid seats earn jury-reward tickets next to a 5 percent protocol-fee ticket, and anyone can stake 0.1 SUI on a seat and earn its rewards. Every page a juror opened, every evidence manifest and every sealed and revealed run bundle is a Walrus blob hash-pinned on chain, each reveal key is escrowed under a Seal time-lock policy so bundles open after the deadline without us, a Google sign-in (Enoki zkLogin) can stake with gas paid by Shinami Gas Station behind a server-side allowlist, and PTBs compose the phase transitions and the stake atomically. 

Source and PRD: https://github.com/Marcussy34/OpenVerdict

**AI For Society**

OpenVerdict is a public fact checker with a jury inside: a decentralized verification protocol where every piece of AI reasoning runs on the Gonka network through gonkarouter.io. Paste a URL, a tweet or a sentence at https://app.openverdict.info (no account, no wallet, no gas): a Gonka model extracts up to three checkable claims with the quote and the reason, and the one you pick gets a five-seat jury drawn across all three GonkaRouter families (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K2.6, MiniMax-M2.7, at most two seats per family). Each juror researches the live web independently, must run a search for and a search against the claim, open pages on both sides and cite verbatim quotes from at least two sites, then seals a secret YES, NO or UNSURE ballot. Four matching votes settle the claim; a split jury cross-examines in public and debates with each other over the frozen record and votes again; a still-split jury ends honestly as UNRESOLVED. The output is a 0 to 100 Truth Score plus an evidence-linked reasoning trace for every juror (every search, every page, every quote, every prompt and reply), stamped on Sui as a certificate anyone can recompute from start to end. Gonka's decentralized inference is what makes this affordable as public infrastructure.

The Gonka mandate is enforced in code, not policy. The adapter refuses any inference host outside gonkarouter.io, no other AI provider exists in the repository, every call carries X-Gonka-No-Fallback: true, a reply from a different model than the juror's manifest is rejected, and a juror that cannot reach Gonka fails closed instead of falling back. Neutrality is pinned as well, the system prompt requiring evidence for and against with exact citations is hashed into each juror's on-chain manifest, so the instructions are provable and immutable. Every inference shows its Gonka Request ID (the devshard-… response id, the gateway x-request-id, the devshard id and the node fingerprint) per turn, and the request id is committed on Sui inside the run hash before any ballot is revealed, so the receipt is part of what the jury commits to, not an afterthought. One click cross-checks that id against GonkaRouter's public receipts endpoint to confirm the model, node and timing, and anyone can rerun the exact recorded conversation against the same model. Integration write-up for judges: https://github.com/Marcussy34/OpenVerdict/blob/main/docs/GONKA-INTEGRATION.md. 

Settled example with five Gonka request ids across three families: https://app.openverdict.info/claims/0x273220b56d87edea0a6db35f85c0fc8f36591461ee6be6962e86bb4586ee4ac6

### AEGIS
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aegis-ec56) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Aidenthien/muba_hackathon_AEGIS) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://muba-aegis.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1224052815?fl=ip&fe=ec) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Pre-Execution Security Oracle for Sui

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Chrome Extension](https://img.shields.io/badge/Chrome%20Extension-333333?style=flat-square) ![sui](https://img.shields.io/badge/sui-333333?style=flat-square) ![Qdrant](https://img.shields.io/badge/Qdrant-333333?style=flat-square) ![LangGraph](https://img.shields.io/badge/LangGraph-333333?style=flat-square) ![Walrus](https://img.shields.io/badge/Walrus-333333?style=flat-square) ![Enoki](https://img.shields.io/badge/Enoki-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges We Ran Into

1. **Chrome MV3 Worker Dying During Confirmation (30s+ Timeout)**
   * **Challenge:** Chrome kills background service workers after ~30s. If a user hesitated before clicking "Confirm", the worker was already dead, dropping the action and freezing the dApp.
   * **Fix:** Implemented bidirectional `chrome.runtime.Port` connections and an active 8-second heartbeat interval while confirmations are pending, keeping the worker alive and ensuring reliable routing.

2. **Gonka Router 502 Bad Gateway Inconsistency**
   * **Challenge:** Decentralized model calls on Gonka Router occasionally returned `502 Bad Gateway` errors due to network node drops.
   
     ![Gonka Router 502 Bad Gateway Error](https://res.cloudinary.com/dzumvmtzs/image/upload/v1788573104/gonka_router_bad_gateway_lkvued.jpg)
   
   * **Fix:** Built a resilient fallback pipeline in LangGraph: if Gonka Router fails or times out, the agent automatically fallsback to Google Gemini without crashing the stream.

3. **Building a LangGraph AI Agent as Non-AI Students**
   * **Challenge:** Without formal AI backgrounds, orchestrating cyclical state graphs, tool routing, and preventing LLM hallucinations was a steep learning curve.
   * **Fix:** Constrained the LLM's routing decisions using strict Zod schemas (`PlanSchema`) over 3 fixed tools, keeping blockchain dry-runs and risk scoring in 100% deterministic TypeScript.

**The problem it solves**

### The Problem
Blind transaction signing causes massive fund losses in Web3. On Sui, this is critical because:
* **Complex Multi-Step PTBs:** Scammers hide wallet-drainers inside transactions that look normal on the surface.
* **Blind Signatures:** Wallets display raw hex code and technical parameters instead of human-readable outcomes.
* **~400ms Sub-Second Finality:** Sui has no mempool waiting room. Once you sign, funds are gone instantly—post-hack alerts and revoke tools are too late.

---

### What It’s Used For
**AEGIS** is a browser extension and pre-execution security oracle that inspects transactions *before* the wallet signs:
* **Live Deterministic Dry-Run:** Computes exact net balance changes and object mutations against live Sui state.
* **Plain-English Explanations:** Explains what enters/leaves your wallet with zero technical jargon.
* **Dual-Model Consensus (Gonka Router):** Dispatches parallel inference across two models (`DeepSeek-V4-Flash` + `MiniMax-M2.7`) to eliminate hallucinations and compute a calibrated Truth Score.
* **Clear Verdicts:** Delivers instant **Approve**, **Caution**, or **Reject** recommendations.
* **Gasless zkLogin (Enoki):** Allows users to onboard with Web2 logins and transact with sponsored gas.

---

### How It Makes Web3 Safer & Easier
* **Stops Exploits Pre-Signature:** Intercepts threats before execution, not after funds are lost.
* **Zero Custody, Zero Admin Keys:** Never holds user funds or contract capabilities—no central point of failure.
* **Defense-in-Depth:** Automatically enforces the strictest conservative verdict if AI models disagree.
* **Permanent Audit Proofs:** Records cryptographic audit proofs to **Walrus Storage** and **MongoDB**.
* **1-Line dApp SDK:** Any Sui dApp can integrate `aegis.analyze(tx)` with one line of code.

**PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS**

### 💳 SUI Track 1: Payments & Stablecoins
**How AEGIS Fits:**
AEGIS delivers a frictionless, zero-fear financial layer for sending, receiving, and managing stablecoins (USDC) and native assets on Sui.
* **Frictionless Onboarding with zkLogin:** Users log in securely with their existing Google / Apple accounts—no seed phrases or complex wallet onboarding required.
* **100% Gasless Money Movement:** Integrated **Enoki Sponsored Transactions** cover network gas fees automatically, allowing users to send payments even with a $0 SUI balance.
* **Pre-Execution Fraud & Drainer Protection:** Before any payment or PTB settles, AEGIS simulates the transaction, translating complex coin transfers and balance mutations into a human-readable payout breakdown so users never sign blind transfers or malicious drainer scripts.
* **Safe Merchant & Peer Transfers:** Empowers non-crypto-native everyday users with the confidence to transact in stablecoins without the fear of irreversible typos or phishing scams.
* **AI Plain-English Payment Explanations:** Instead of confusing bytecode and technical Move function names, the AI explains exactly what is happening in plain English (who receives the funds, exact amounts, and fee breakdowns) so non-technical users always understand what they are confirming.

**AI × SUI**

### 🤖 SUI Track 2: AI × Sui

**How AEGIS Fits:**
AEGIS is an autonomous AI security agent built specifically for Sui's unique object-centric architecture and Programmable Transaction Blocks (PTBs).

* **The Real User Problem it Solves:** 
  * **The Problem:** In Web3, users are forced to approve unreadable bytecode, raw hex data, and complex multi-command PTBs where drainers hide malicious coin transfers inside benign-looking calls. Once signed, losses are irreversible.
  * **The AI Solution:** AEGIS acts as an active, pre-execution security copilot. It autonomously intercepts, simulates, and translates raw PTB operations into plain human language, warning users of hidden drainers, asset transfer mismatches, and contract risks *before* they click sign.
* **Dual-Model AI Consensus Engine (Defense-in-Depth):** 
  * Unlike single-model tools prone to hallucinations, AEGIS runs parallel multi-model inference (**DeepSeek-V4-Flash** for deep code/PTB reasoning and **MiniMax-M2.7** for independent verification).
  * If models diverge on risk classification, an automated **Defense-in-Depth Consensus algorithm** flags the higher severity to guarantee zero false negatives and protect user funds.
* **Sui as the AI Agent's On-Chain Execution Engine (PTB Deconstruction):** 
  * Rather than generic text generation, the agent operates directly on Sui's **Programmable Transaction Blocks (PTBs)**. It parses batched calls, object inputs, and commands in real time to perform automated security triage and risk scoring (0–100%).
* **Sui RPC/gRPC as the Agent's Ground Truth (Deterministic Fact Layer):** 
  * Sui is integral to the agent's cognition. The AI uses Sui RPC dry-runs as a deterministic factual anchor for its **LangGraph** state graph, eliminating AI hallucinations by verifying exact coin outflows and object mutations against live chain state.
* **AI with Native Sui Identity & Digital Ownership (zkLogin):** 
  * Leverages **zkLogin** for non-custodial agent-user synergy. The AI operates with fine-grained permission boundaries to inspect and simulate actions without ever holding private keys, preserving 100% sovereign user ownership.
* **Gasless Interactions via Sponsored Transactions:** 
  * Integrates **Enoki Sponsored Transactions** to subsidize execution gas fees. Users can interact with the agent, test transaction simulations, and execute safe on-chain actions seamlessly with zero gas barriers or need to hold native SUI first.
* **Walrus as the AI's Decentralized Memory & Audit Layer:** 
  * Fits Sui's decentralized storage stack by archiving every AI consensus verdict, risk analysis, and transaction breakdown permanently on **Walrus Protocol** (`blobId`), providing a transparent, verifiable audit trail for the agent's decisions.
* **Semantic Threat Intelligence via Qdrant Vector DB:** 
  * Vectorizes known Sui drainer signatures, phishing patterns, and Move exploit vectors. When a new transaction arrives, the agent performs high-speed semantic similarity matching to instantly detect zero-day variants and morphing scam templates before passing the context to the LLM.

**AI For Society**

### 🌐 Gonka Router Track: AI for Society (Truth Engine)

**How AEGIS Fits:**
AEGIS serves as a decentralized **Transaction Truth Engine**, protecting everyday Web3 users from scams, phishing, and fake dApps through multi-model AI consensus powered by Gonka Network (`gonkarouter.io`).

* **AI for Society & Public Consumer Protection:**
  * **The Societal Problem:** Everyday internet users lose their hard-earned money to deceptive Web3 sites, fake airdrops, and obfuscated smart contracts because blockchain data is fundamentally unreadable to humans. Centralized security services are opaque, easily censored, and single points of failure.
  * **The Societal Impact:** AEGIS democratizes Web3 security as a transparent public utility. Powered by Gonka Network's decentralized AI inference, it gives everyday users an unbiased, real-time "digital bodyguard" that guarantees consumer safety without relying on centralized gatekeepers.
* **Decentralized Multi-Model Consensus (Unbiased Fact-Checking):** 
  * Claims and transactions are cross-verified in parallel across two independent models on Gonka Network (**DeepSeek-V4-Flash** as Primary Analyzer and **MiniMax-M2.7** as Independent Verifier) to eliminate single-model bias and hallucinations.
* **Objective Truth Score (0–100%) & Evidence Trail:** 
  * Delivers a transparent **Truth & Safety Score (0–100%)** accompanied by neutral, evidence-backed explanations that cite exact contract function calls, balance alterations, and security risks.
* **Defense-in-Depth Consensus Arbitration:** 
  * If the two decentralized models disagree on risk level, AEGIS enforces automated defense-in-depth consensus (prioritizing user asset safety by adopting the stricter safety rating).
 **Transparency Dashboard & Verifiable Proof of Inference:** 
  * Our live **AEGIS Dashboard** features dedicated **Transparency UI Cards** that display the exact cryptographic **Gonka Request IDs** (`x-request-id`, `x-devshard-id`) and latency metrics for both models. This gives users, developers, and auditors verifiable proof that every analysis was computed trustlessly across Gonka's decentralized network rather than faked by a centralized server.
* **Semantic Pattern Matching via Qdrant Vector DB:** 
  * Connects decentralized model reasoning with high-speed vector retrieval across known phishing campaigns and exploit databases to catch emerging scams instantly.

### SuiSure

> U Sure or Not???

**The problem it solves**

## Safer and simpler on-chain merchant payments

QR payments are already familiar to Malaysian users through systems such as DuitNow, TNG and Grab. However, a displayed merchant QR can potentially be covered, replaced or manipulated, causing the customer to pay a different recipient without immediately realizing it.

**On-chain payments introduce an additional challenge:** transactions are irreversible, wallet addresses are difficult for ordinary users to recognize, and making a normal transfer often requires manually copying an address, selecting the correct token and entering the amount.

SuiSure brings the convenience of QR payments to on-chain merchant transactions while introducing two layers of verification:

1. **Before signing**, SuiSure retrieves and cross-checks the merchant credential and payment request from Sui. It verifies the merchant, amount, token, expiry and whether the request has already been paid.
2. **During execution**, the Move contract enforces the checks again and retrieves the payout address from the registered merchant credential; not directly from the QR code.

This means a QR code cannot simply provide or replace the trusted destination address.

Customers can scan a QR, upload a QR image or describe the intended payment using AI assistance. The AI interprets the request, helps calculate and explain its risk score, and presents the result in understandable language. However, it cannot select the trusted recipient, change verified values, sign or approve the transaction.

For merchants, SuiSure provides structured payment requests, QR generation, payment-status tracking and incoming-payment visibility. For customers, it makes paying with stablecoins more familiar, understandable and safer than manually transferring funds to a hexadecimal wallet address.

***SuiSure is inspired by the convenience of DuitNow QR, strengthened by on-chain security.***

**Challenges we ran into**

### Aida: Sui Smart Contracts and Payment Infrastructure
A late security review revealed that Payment Kit checked a coin’s value but not its type, potentially allowing a USDC request to be paid with another token. Fixing this required republishing the Move package and recreating all Testnet data. Differences between the documentation and source code also required direct dependency inspection and custom payment receipts.

### Aidan: AI Safety and On-Chain Merchant Resolution

The main challenge was connecting natural-language instructions to genuine merchant-issued payment requests without allowing the AI to create or manipulate payments. The final design restricts AI to interpretation, while merchant resolution, amount matching and prompt-injection protection are handled deterministically using verified on-chain data.

### Syafieqah: Frontend, Authentication & End-to-End Integration

The frontend needed to support both Google zkLogin and external Sui wallets through one consistent payment flow. End-to-end testing uncovered issues involving production configuration, balance detection, authentication redirects, responsive dialogs and account activity isolation. These were resolved while preserving user approval and on-chain verification.

**Overall**

The largest lesson was that successful compilation was not sufficient evidence that the system was safe or ready. Documentation, model output, generated configuration and cached Testnet assumptions could all be incomplete or misleading. We therefore relied on source inspection, deterministic validation, on-chain verification, automated health checks and repeated end-to-end testing across both wallet and zkLogin users.

**PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c9745a0ea8f34c52ac4b0266e6478246/15849921-a327-4ea1-a104-8a0690f281cf.png)

SuiSure is a non-custodial merchant payment application built on Sui Testnet. Verified merchants and payment requests are represented by on-chain MerchantCredential and PaymentIntent objects. Customers review the canonical on-chain details before paying Circle Testnet USDC through our Move contract and Sui Payment Kit.

Payments settle directly from the customer to the merchant, while the transaction digest provides verifiable proof on Sui Explorer. Users can access SuiSure through Google zkLogin or compatible Sui wallets such as Slush. QR codes contain object identifiers rather than trusted payout addresses, preventing the QR or AI layer from redirecting funds.

**AI × SUI**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/c9745a0ea8f34c52ac4b0266e6478246/4c1fc316-fff9-4a6d-9d42-c28134274720.png)

SuiSure uses Gemini to interpret natural-language, scanned or uploaded payment requests and convert them into structured payment information. The application then retrieves the canonical merchant, amount, expiry and status directly from Sui Testnet before presenting the payment for confirmation.

AI assists with interpretation and explanation but cannot determine the trusted payout address, override on-chain values, sign transactions or control user funds. Sui remains the source of truth and the Move contract enforces the final payment rules. This combines an accessible AI-assisted experience with deterministic on-chain verification.

### Mory
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/morry-72f8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/TenJingYi/MorryWebsiteCompetition.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://morrywebsite.onrender.com/elderly.html) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/LtoT25VXxPM?si=Hl1L4hmy47Hqgiwj) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Remember You, Remember Me, Our Memory

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Gonka Router does not support vision/image inputs**
We initially designed the medicine scanner to send photos directly to vision-capable AI models on Gonka. After deployment, every attempt returned a 400 error — Gonka's current models don't accept image_url content. We rebuilt the pipeline to use Tesseract.js for local OCR first, then send the extracted text to Gonka for structuring and medical knowledge enrichment. This actually improved accuracy for text-heavy labels.

**2. DeepSeek's <think> blocks swallowed the JSON**
DeepSeek V4 Flash generates a long internal reasoning block wrapped in <think>...</think> before outputting the answer. Our original code stripped these blocks before JSON parsing — but for complex prompts like fact-checking, DeepSeek placed the JSON *inside* the think block. Stripping it deleted the answer entirely. We fixed this by returning both the raw and stripped content from every model call, then searching for JSON in three passes: after the last </think> tag, in the stripped text, and anywhere in the raw response.

**3. max_tokens too low caused truncated responses**
Setting max_tokens: 450 for the fact-checker wasn't enough for DeepSeek to finish reasoning AND output JSON. The response was cut off mid-think with no JSON produced. Raising to max_tokens: 1200 resolved this.

**4. False consensus from a single model**
When one model failed, the system calculated scoreDiff as 0 (one model agreeing with itself) and showed "Models agree" — which was misleading. We fixed this by tracking twoModels as a boolean, only computing real consensus when both models respond, and using the tertiary model as a genuine second opinion when needed.

**5. iOS Safari camera bug**
The medicine scanner used JavaScript .click() on a hidden file input to open the camera. iOS Safari silently blocked this when called through a function chain. We fixed it by using a <label for="medicine-photo-input"> element instead, which creates a direct browser-native link to the file input that iOS Safari always respects.

**The problem it solves**

Millions of elderly people in Southeast Asia are cared for by families who live far away and caregivers who lack efficient tools. Three problems go unsolved every day:

**1. Medication confusion** — Elderly users manage multiple medicines with complex instructions in languages they may not read well. Missed doses and misread labels are common and dangerous.

**2. Social isolation and language barriers** — Most AI companions only speak English or Mandarin. Grandparents who speak Cantonese, Hokkien, Hakka, or Bahasa Melayu are left out entirely.

**3. Health misinformation** — Elderly users regularly receive unverified health claims through WhatsApp groups with no way to fact-check them.

MORY solves all three: a voice-first elderly companion in 6 Southeast Asian dialects, an AI-powered medicine scanner that reads labels and explains what each medicine does in plain language, and a Health Fact Checker that uses Gonka's decentralised multi-model consensus to return a verified Truth Score for any health claim — with transparent Gonka Request IDs proving every inference ran on the decentralised network.

Team **Ten out of Ten** -- [SANZY LEE](https://github.com/no), [TEN JING YI](https://github.com/TenJingYi), [Teo Joey](https://github.com/joeginy558-oss)

### TrustHire
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/trusthire-42a6) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Elivius/TrustHire) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://trust-hire-ruddy.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI decides who to trust. Sui enforces it.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Sui Move](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sui%20Move-333333?style=flat-square) ![GonkaRouter](https://img.shields.io/badge/GonkaRouter-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

### The Trust Deficit in the Gig Economy

In today's digital economy, a massive amount of freelance work happens informally. Clients and talent connecting directly through social media, Discord, or WhatsApp. While this bypasses the massive 20% fees of traditional platforms, it creates a severe trust deficit with zero protection for either side:
- **Freelancers** constantly worry about clients defaulting on payments, or ghosting them entirely after the final work is delivered.
- **Clients** worry about hiring fake profiles, encountering fabricated portfolios, or receiving subpar work because they have no formal recourse or arbitration.
- **Pay-to-play barriers:** Even when users try to rely on traditional platforms, freelancers are often forced to buy virtual "tokens" or "connects" just for the privilege of applying to a job, and face manual dispute systems that are easily manipulated.

### How TrustHire Solves This

TrustHire completely removes the need for expensive, subjective middlemen. It replaces them with trustless Web3 infrastructure and unbiased AI, providing institutional-grade safety for independent and direct hires.

People can use TrustHire to securely hire talent or accept freelance work with zero anxiety about getting scammed. It makes gig work radically safer through four core pillars:

1. **Guaranteed Payments (Sui Escrow):** Clients securely lock project funds in an on-chain Sui Move contract *before* work begins. The platform never holds custody of the funds, and the freelancer knows the money is guaranteed the moment they meet the requirements.
2. **Unbiased AI Arbitration (Gonka Router):** Instead of relying on a biased human support agent during disputes, TrustHire routes milestone submissions (like a GitHub PR or Figma link) through a multi-model AI consensus engine. The AI neutrally evaluates the work against the initial project spec, outputs a "Truth Score," and automatically authorizes the release of the escrowed funds. 
3. **Immutable Reputation:** Freelancers build a permanent, on-chain work history that proves their skills and track record, completely eliminating the "fake profile" problem.
4. **Zero-Cost, Walletless Onboarding:** Unlike legacy platforms that charge freelancers just to apply, TrustHire removes all friction. Using **zkLogin** and **Enoki Sponsored Transactions**, talent can sign in with a simple Google account and start working instantly. Gas fees are fully sponsored, meaning freelancers don't even need a crypto wallet or SUI tokens to get started.

By combining Web3 payment guarantees with AI verification, TrustHire makes freelance work fairer, safer, and completely trustless.

**Challenges we ran into**

### 1. The Enoki Gas Sponsorship vs. Coin Splitting Hurdle
**The Challenge:** 
Our goal was to make the platform 100% gasless using Enoki Sponsored Transactions. However, when we attempted to sponsor the `create_escrow` transaction (where a client locks SUI funds into the smart contract), the transaction kept failing. We discovered a core limitation: Enoki gas pools cannot sponsor transactions that involve splitting the primary gas-paying coin itself, which is exactly what happens when you try to extract funds to lock into an escrow.

**The Solution:** 
We had to deeply rethink our transaction architecture. We leveraged **Programmable Transaction Blocks (PTBs)** to elegantly solve this. Instead of a clumsy two-step process, we used a PTB to atomically execute `tx.splitCoins` and pass the newly created coin object directly into the `tx.moveCall` for the escrow in a single execution. We then explicitly restricted Enoki sponsorship to the *freelancer* side (onboarding and milestone submissions), ensuring the talent experience remained 100% frictionless and gasless, while clients handle standard gas for their funding transactions.

### 2. Preventing AI Hallucinations in Financial Decisions
**The Challenge:**
Since our smart contracts release real escrowed funds based on the AI's verdict, relying on a single AI model to verify complex milestone deliverables (like analyzing a GitHub PR) was too risky. A single model might hallucinate or provide a subjective, lenient approval.

**The Solution:**
We implemented a strict **Multi-Model Consensus** mechanism using the Gonka Router. Instead of one model, we cross-reference the milestone proof across multiple distinct models (e.g., DeepSeek and MiniMax). Only when the models reach a consensus on the requirements does the system output a definitive "Truth Score." If the models disagree, the system flags it for manual review, ensuring that no funds are released on a hallucinated verdict.

### 3. Cost-Efficient Hybrid Architecture (Off-chain DB + On-chain Execution)
**The Challenge:**
Storing extensive project requirements, freelancer portfolios, and AI reasoning traces directly on the Sui blockchain would have resulted in astronomically high gas fees. Furthermore, we needed a way to render complex UI data instantly on page load without waiting for wallet connections or slow RPC nodes to hydrate the state.

**The Solution:**
We implemented a hybrid architecture to solve both problems. We use **Supabase** as a lightning-fast off-chain database to store all heavy metadata (project descriptions, profile text, AI analysis). 

When a critical financial action occurs (like creating an escrow or approving a milestone), the transaction is executed on the Sui blockchain. We then capture the resulting **on-chain transaction hash (txDigest)** and store it directly in our off-chain Supabase database as an irrefutable reference. 

This approach drastically minimized gas fees while giving us Web2 load speeds. We render the heavy UI from Supabase instantly, and use the stored transaction hashes to cross-verify the financial state on-chain exactly when needed.

**PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS**

TrustHire perfectly aligns with the Payments & Stablecoins track by building the future of automated, trustless "creator payouts" and escrow.

We built a real-world ready payout workflow that eliminates platform custody risk. By utilizing Sui's **Programmable Transaction Blocks (PTBs)**, clients securely split and lock their project funds into an on-chain milestone escrow in a single click. 

To guarantee a "fast, intuitive UX" for non-crypto native freelancers, we utilized **zkLogin** (Google onboarding) and **Enoki Sponsored Transactions**. This completely removes all Web3 friction—freelancers never have to worry about gas fees, seed phrases, or managing wallets when receiving their payouts.

While our current prototype utilizes the SUI token for escrow funding, our `escrow.move` smart contract is fully built around Sui's generic `Coin<T>` standard. This makes our entire payment architecture natively **stablecoin-ready**. In production, clients will fund the escrow using stablecoins (like USDC), protecting freelancers from crypto volatility while still enjoying automated, AI-verified payouts.

**AI × SUI**

TrustHire is an **AI-powered freelance marketplace** that perfectly intersects AI and Sui to solve the problem of trust and payment fairness in the gig economy. 

**AI acts as the brain:** The Gonka AI Router extracts structured project requirements, intelligently matches freelancers to jobs, and generates Trust Scores based on verified skills and portfolio data. 

**Sui acts as the muscle:** AI alone cannot hold or distribute funds, making Sui absolutely integral to our platform. We use **Programmable Transaction Blocks (PTBs)** to securely fund **On-Chain Escrow** Move contracts. Payments are locked in advance and automatically released upon milestone approval, eliminating platform custody and payment default risks.

Additionally, to ensure a seamless "Web2-like" user experience for non-crypto native freelancers, we heavily utilize **zkLogin** for passwordless Google onboarding and **Enoki Sponsored Transactions** so talent can interact with the blockchain with zero gas fees.

**AI For Society**

TrustHire applies the **Gonka AI Fact Checker** pattern to solve a genuine public value issue: preventing scams and unpaid work in the gig economy. 

When a freelancer completes a job (a milestone), they submit a URL (e.g., a GitHub PR or Figma link) or text snippet. Instead of leaving the client to manually verify, which often leads to disputes or unpaid labor, TrustHire routes the submission through the **Gonka Router** (`gonkarouter.io`) for **Decentralized Verification**.

To guarantee absolute neutrality, we utilize **Multi-Model Consensus**, cross-verifying the submission using at least two different models. The AI analyzes the submitted work against the original project requirements and outputs a **Truth Score (0-100%)** along with a detailed **Reasoning Trace**. This unbiased AI verdict empowers the client to confidently approve the milestone and release the on-chain payment.

For complete transparency, all AI judgments are rendered on the dashboard alongside their specific **Gonka Request IDs**, proving that the verification was untampered and decentralized.

### Thesis.fun

> Say it. Trade it. Real onchain options on Base.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Drizzle](https://img.shields.io/badge/Drizzle-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Wagmi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Wagmi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Viem](https://img.shields.io/badge/Viem-333333?style=flat-square) ![BASE](https://img.shields.io/badge/BASE-333333?style=flat-square) ![bun](https://img.shields.io/badge/bun-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

## The SDK comment about which side the maker is on was backwards

We decoded production fills from Base bytes and pinned the real rule with tests: `isLong` is the maker's flag, so `false` means the taker buys.

## Maker signatures expire in about a minute

The ticket approves first, then re-quotes right before the fill, and refuses to broadcast stale calldata.

## Thetanuts publishes no price history

The market page draws Binance hourly spot and says so on the chart, because Thetanuts settles on a Chainlink TWAP that can differ. No number on a position comes from the chart: every figure is derived from the fill event and the raw order, never from the quote.

## Recording a fill had to fail closed

A mismatched event, an unprovable contract count, or a structure that vanished from the book refuses instead of guessing. The ticket is held while the last fill is still being recorded, and the server re-checks the chain for this wallet's recent fills before it issues another ticket.

**The problem it solves**

## Options on chain are hard to find and harder to talk about

**Thesis.fun makes a trade a post.** Pick any market Thetanuts has liquidity for on Base, take a side with your own wallet, and the position gets its own page with a live P&L card. Say why in a post; link the trade and it unfurls into a card, X-style.

- **Every market Thetanuts has liquidity for.** Assets, strikes and expiries come from live OptionBook orders, never a hardcoded list.
- **Both sides.** Buy an option (loss bounded by the premium) or sell one (lock collateral, receive the premium), each with honest sizing and copy.
- **A social layer built only from onchain fills.** Likes, comments, follows and a leaderboard from real positions, so a track record cannot be faked and a losing thesis cannot be deleted.
- **Every new user gets a name and a face on day one.** Generated names and avatars, editable later.
- **An AI agent that explains any thesis and proposes trades** within a hard loss limit and daily caps. The wallet signs everything; the agent never does.

**BEST PRODUCT BUILT ON THE THETANUTS SDK**

Thesis.fun is built end to end on the Thetanuts SDK: live OptionBook orders drive every market, strike and expiry; quotes, approvals and fills go through the SDK's calldata builders and are recorded from the on-chain `OrderFilled` event; both taker sides ship with sizing derived from decoded production fills. Every quote and fill carries the platform referrer.

**AI × OPTIONS**

An approval-gated AI agent explains any thesis, proposes a trade on a live Thetanuts structure, prepares the real calldata through the same path as the ticket, and hands it to the user's wallet to sign. Hard loss ceiling and daily caps are enforced server-side on the prepared economics; the agent never signs.

### Custodia
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/custodia-393d) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/hmhhmm/Custodia.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://canva.link/c4kmv07ql8u34eh) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/yfxmxRLLGy4) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> On-chain trust for what AI agents do

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Giving an AI agent your wallet to act on your behalf is currently an all-or-nothing choice: either hand over full control and hope it doesn't overspend or pay the wrong party, or supervise every single transaction yourself which defeats the point of automation in the first place.

Custodia gives people a middle ground: a Mandate, a real on-chain spending permit with a hard cap, an expiry, and a fixed list of allowed task categories. An agent can act freely and autonomously within that boundary, and the boundary itself is enforced by a Move smart contract, not by trusting the app's frontend to behave.

What people can actually use it for:
Hiring specialists without micromanaging payment. Ask for something done like a document translated, a contract reviewed, an item picked up and repaired and the agent finds a real specialist, escrows payment, and only releases it once delivery is verified. You never manually wire money or chase an invoice.
Multi-step jobs that need different specialists in sequence. A single request like pick up my broken laptop, get it repaired, send it back gets split into several linked deals which is pickup, repair, return. Each automatically triggering the next once the last one's delivery is proven on-chain, with no manual hand-off required.
Trusting who you're hiring, without a middleman. Specialists are ranked by a reputation score built entirely from real completed-vs-disputed deals, not a profile they wrote themselves, not a platform's opaque rating.
Keeping sensitive job details private. Task briefs and delivered work are encrypted so only the client and the assigned specialist can ever read them, not a backend, not Custodia itself, because there is no backend holding that data.
How it makes things safer, concretely:

Money can never move outside the Mandate's cap, categories, or expiry, enforced on-chain, not just in the UI.
Payment and proof-of-delivery are locked together in one atomic transaction, so there's no window where a specialist gets paid without delivering, or delivers without ever getting paid.
Every reputation score is a real, auditable history of completed and disputed deals, not a number anyone can inflate by hand.

**Challenges we ran into**

Package upgrades broke object lookups silently. When we upgraded our Move package to add a new module, an older module's objects were still typed under the original package id, not the new one but our query used the new id. Transactions succeeded every time; our own code just never found what it created. We found the real cause by pulling the raw transaction JSON via the Sui CLI and reading the object's actual type string.

Seal requires the original package id, always. After that same upgrade, encryption started throwing InvalidPackageError. Turned out Seal's SDK hard-requires the package's version-1 id specifically, even though the function itself works fine on the newer package. We only found this by reading Seal's own SDK source.

A budget check passed, but the real transaction still failed. Our on-screen "Mandate check passed" message and the actual escrow transaction were silently reading two different Mandate objects, one freshly fetched, one cached from earlier in the session. Once a user had two Mandates, the check and the real transaction could disagree.

**PAYMENTS & STABLECOINS**

Custodia is escrow and payout infrastructure for agent driven money movement, settling in stablecoins so payouts are stable, predictable, and instant.

The problem: 
Automated payouts like payroll, creator tips, marketplace escrow, campus payments need money to move the moment work is verified, with no human in the loop and no risk of paying out before the job is actually done, and no exposure to price swings while funds sit in escrow. Custodia's Mandate is an on-chain spending permit with a hard cap, expiry, and allowed categories, enforced by a Move contract nothing on the frontend can bypass. An agent can release stablecoin funds freely inside that boundary and nowhere else.

Why Sui matters here: 
Escrow-lock, delivery verification, and stablecoin payout are one atomic Move transaction like funds and proof-of-work can never drift out of sync, and reputation only grows when a payout genuinely lands. Sponsored transactions mean the person receiving a payout never needs to hold SUI for gas just to get paid, and zkLogin means onboarding a payee is a Google sign-in, not a seed phrase.

The demo: 
A client escrows a stablecoin payment the moment a task is accepted, watches real on-chain checkpoints as the work happens, and the moment delivery is verified, payout fires automatically and atomically to the payee's wallet and no invoice, no manual transfer as well as no waiting on a human to notice the job is done.

**AI × SUI**

Custodia is a trust and settlement layer that lets AI agents hire other agents and actually pay them safely.

The problem: 
Giving an AI agent your wallet key is reckless; supervising every transaction defeats the point of automation. Custodia's answer is a Mandate which is an on-chain spending permit with a hard cap, expiry and allowed categories, enforced by a Move contract the frontend can't bypass. The agent (Envoy) can act freely inside that boundary and nowhere else.

Why Sui matters here: 
Every real state change like escrow, delivery verification, payout, reputation update is a single atomic Move transaction, so money and trust can never drift out of sync. Specialists are ranked by a reputation score that only grows when a deal is genuinely completed and paid. Deliverables are Seal-encrypted and Walrus-stored, readable only by the two parties on that exact deal.

The demo isn't just locked to one workflow. Envoy decomposes whatever the user asks into however many sequential deals it needs, matches each to the right specialist type from six real categories, and chains them automatically. The laptop repair example is just one instance of a general pattern.

**AI For Society**

Custodia verify it's escrow and reputation contracts, repointed at fact-checking instead of task delivery.

The problem: 
Fact-checking has no accountability layer. A model (or a human reviewer) can call a claim true or false and face no consequence if they're wrong. Custodia already has a contract for exactly this shape of problem that pay someone only once their output is verified, and track their track record on-chain that it's just been used for task delivery, not truth verification until now.

What would be built using Custodia's real contracts is a claim that gets checked by at least two independent models via Gonka Router. Custodia's existing Mandate would fund that inference cost per claim, the same way it funds a specialist's payout today. The Truth Score and reasoning trace Gonka returns would be Seal-encrypted and stored on Walrus which is the same storage path Custodia that already uses for a specialist's deliverable, so the reasoning behind a verdict is provenance-anchored, not just displayed and forgotten. And Custodia's Reputation object, the same Move module that already scores a specialist by completed-vs-disputed deals would score each model or verifier by how often its calls hold up over time, using the identical record_completed/record_disputed mechanism.
