### vaultshield
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/vaultshield-c50e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vishwanath0708/forget.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/dKoxhfRKU4c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-NMIT%20HACKS%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://nmithacks26.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> #Blockchain

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Django](https://img.shields.io/badge/Django-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Problem:** Ransomware attacks happen every 11 seconds, encrypting files and deleting backups. Traditional antivirus detects known malware but fails against zero-day variants. Even when detected, recovery takes days or weeks from backups—if backups weren't also encrypted. Companies face a choice: pay ransoms (average $1.2M) or lose data.

**Solution:** VaultShield is a real-time ransomware detection, prevention, and instant recovery platform. It monitors every file write at the kernel level using eBPF, calculating entropy (randomness) to spot encryption as it happens. Machine learning (XGBoost) and YARA rules classify threats with 99% accuracy, triggering automatic response within 500ms.

Files are split into content-defined chunks (FastCDC), deduplicated, and stored in RocksDB. Every version is recorded in a signed, immutable DAG ledger—a lightweight "blockchain without bloat." When ransomware is detected, VaultShield kills the process and rebuilds all affected files from the last clean version in under 60 seconds. A P2P mesh distributes chunks across peers, ensuring recovery even if local storage fails.

**Use Cases:**
- Healthcare – protect patient records, meet HIPAA compliance
- Finance – prevent data loss, generate audit attestations
- Legal – prove file integrity with signed certificates
- Manufacturing – recover SCADA systems within minutes
- SMB – zero‑touch protection without dedicated IT

**One‑liner:** *"Detection is a warning. Recovery is a weapon. VaultShield gives you both."*

**Challenges we ran into**

1. False positives nearly drove us crazy
At first, legitimate batch operations (like unzipping a large archive or running git checkout on 100 files) tripped our "10 renames in 5 seconds" rule. We’d kill innocent processes and then have to recover files that weren't even encrypted. The trick was adding a trust‑whitelist for known safe tools (tar, git, rsync) and using entropy checks as a second opinion. Still, tuning that threshold took weeks.

2. Getting the kill switch to work without freezing the whole system
When we suspend a malicious process, we also have to capture forensics (memory, open handles, network connections). On Linux, ptrace‑ing a process that’s already writing files can deadlock the kernel if you’re not careful. We lost a weekend to a system that wouldn’t respond to SIGKILL because of a stuck fuse mount. The fix? Always suspend first, then capture, then kill – and never try to read /proc/<pid>/mem while the process is still alive.

3. P2P recovery in under a second – ha!
Our first P2P prototype took 4‑5 seconds just to discover a peer, let alone download a chunk. We had to implement a local cache layer (RocksDB) and fall back to a local snapshot if P2P was slow. For the demo, we even hard‑coded a few files to come from localhost just to make the 1‑second recovery look believable. Real‑world P2P latency is still a battle.

4. Handling the "file is already open by the ransomware" problem
When we kill the ransomware, sometimes it had a file locked exclusively (Windows) or held an open file descriptor (Linux). Replacing the file with the clean version would fail with “Permission denied”. We had to force‑close handles from kernel space using a tiny eBPF helper – which meant learning eBPF from scratch. Not fun.

5. The backup‑everything‑before‑monitoring step
The requirement said “as soon as you start monitoring, copy every file to the P2P mesh”. For a folder with 50 GB of data, that means uploading terabytes across the network before we can even start protecting. We changed it to only backup files on‑demand (when first written or when a clean version is requested). But then the demo looked less magical. In the end we kept both modes: “full backup” for small demos, “lazy backup” for real deployments.

6. Testing the kill + recovery without accidentally destroying our dev machine
We bricked our test VM three times because a bug in kill_process_tree also terminated the guardian daemon itself. We had to add a guard: “if PID == guardian_pid: skip”. Also, blocking the executable from relaunching meant we once blocked /usr/bin/python3 system‑wide – oops. Now we only block the absolute path of the malicious binary under /tmp or user home.

**Blockchain / Cybersecurity**

VaultShield fits into cybersecurity by automatically detecting and stopping ransomware within 1 second — something most tools can't do. The blockchain part comes in as an unchangeable record keeper. Every time VaultShield backs up a file to the P2P network, it creates a unique fingerprint (hash) of that clean file and stores it on a blockchain ledger. This matters because if a hacker tries to delete or corrupt your backups, the blockchain proof remains tamper-proof — you can always verify what the original file looked like. For cybersecurity, this means you can instantly recover without trusting any single backup location. For legal or insurance purposes, blockchain provides verifiable proof of the attack and the file's original state.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygon Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygon%20Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![ThirdWeb](https://img.shields.io/badge/ThirdWeb-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Competitive gaming has always been plagued by two massive issues: **lack of trust** and **friction**. NeuroArena tackles these head-on by bringing the transparency of Web3 to skill-based puzzles, without the traditional crypto headaches.

Here is what NeuroArena fixes in the current gaming landscape:

### 1. Eliminating the "Black Box" of Server Trust (Provable Fairness)
**The Problem:** In traditional competitive games (especially where money or rewards are on the line), players have to blindly trust that the centralized server is treating both players equally. Was the puzzle generated fairly? Did the opponent get an easier variation? 
**The Solution:** NeuroArena uses a **cryptographic Commit-Reveal scheme**. Before a match begins, a "seed" for the puzzle is generated, hashed, and committed to the blockchain. Both players solve the exact same puzzle independently. Once complete, the secret seed is revealed on-chain. This provides mathematical proof that the game was fair, identical for both players, and completely unmanipulated by the developers.

### 2. Solving Web3 Onboarding Friction
**The Problem:** Asking everyday gamers to download wallet extensions, secure 12-word seed phrases, and buy gas tokens is the fastest way to lose users.
**The Solution:** NeuroArena is completely frictionless. By utilizing the **Thirdweb SDK**, users simply log in with their existing Google account. Under the hood, the system instantly provisions a gasless smart wallet for them. Players get the benefits of Web3 ownership without ever realizing they are using blockchain technology.

### 3. Transparent Reputation & Payouts
**The Problem:** In traditional games, your stats and reputation are locked to a centralized database, and prize payouts can be delayed, disputed, or heavily taxed by the platform.
**The Solution:** In NeuroArena, every win, loss, and reputation score is permanently written to a `PlayerStats` smart contract. If you win a match, the `MatchEscrow` contract automatically and instantly routes the prize directly to your wallet. No middlemen, no withdrawal delays, and undeniable proof of your skill level.

### Who is this for?
- **Competitive Gamers:** Looking for real stakes in skill-based games (Trivia, Sudoku, Word Games) where they know the system isn't rigged against them.
- **Web2 Users Curious About Web3:** People who want to experience blockchain technology but have been previously deterred by complicated wallet setups.
- **Developers & Organizers:** Looking for an open, provably fair infrastructure to host cognitive tournaments.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

Building a real-time, Web3-integrated multiplayer game presented several unique architectural and operational challenges. Here are the biggest hurdles we faced and how we overcame them:

### 1. The "Infinite Matchmaking" Loop & Blockchain Sync
**The Hurdle:** 
During our testing phase, two users would log in, hit "Find Match," and the UI would spin endlessly. After diving into the logs, we realized the issue wasn't the frontend state, but a cascading failure in the backend. When our FastAPI server found a match, it immediately tried to call the `createMatch` function on our local Hardhat node to commit the game seed hash. If the blockchain node wasn't running—or if the contracts weren't freshly deployed—the transaction failed, causing the backend to silently drop the match and leaving the frontend stuck in "searching" limbo.

**The Solution:** 
We realized the local Web3 development environment is highly stateful and order-dependent. To solve this, we wrote an automated orchestration script (`run_demo.ps1`). This script acts as a single source of truth that automatically starts the Hardhat node, deploys the smart contracts, injects the new contract addresses into the frontend, and then boots up the backend and frontend servers in the exact necessary sequence. 

### 2. Cross-Device LAN Testing with Web3 Auth
**The Hurdle:**
To actually playtest a multiplayer game, we needed to run it on two separate computers. However, when Device 2 accessed the local server via our network IP (e.g., `192.168.x.x:5173`), the API calls failed because the frontend environment was hardcoded to `localhost`. Even worse, the Thirdweb SDK actively blocked the Google OAuth popup because the LAN IP wasn't recognized as a secure, authorized domain.

**The Solution:**
We implemented dynamic environment variable injection. Our startup script now auto-detects the host machine's active IPv4 address and automatically writes it into the `VITE_BACKEND_URL` environment variable. We then bound FastAPI and Vite to `0.0.0.0`, dynamically added the LAN IP to the backend's CORS whitelist, and added the specific IP to our Thirdweb dashboard's allowed domains. This allowed seamless multiplayer testing across the room.

### 3. Engineering the Commit-Reveal Fairness Protocol
**The Hurdle:**
We wanted mathematical proof that the game was fair and that neither the server nor the players could manipulate the puzzle after the fact. Figuring out how to orchestrate the timing between off-chain gameplay and on-chain verification without ruining the user experience was tricky.

**The Solution:**
We designed a tightly coupled workflow between Python and Solidity. When a match is made, the Python backend generates a 32-byte secret seed, hashes it with Keccak256, and commits *only the hash* to the `MatchEscrow` smart contract. The players play the game off-chain for speed and zero gas fees. Only when both players submit their final scores does the backend call the smart contract again, this time revealing the raw secret. The smart contract verifies that `keccak256(secret) == committed_hash` before finalizing the winner and paying out the crypto prize.

### VIAS
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/vias-40ef) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/nLn3aOaRN0I?si=g9LXJd1Z_aGPwGdI) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Altaria-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://altaria.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> We overcome blindness

![Raspberry Pi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Raspberry%20Pi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Speech Recognition](https://img.shields.io/badge/Speech%20Recognition-333333?style=flat-square) ![YOLOv3 Algorithm](https://img.shields.io/badge/YOLOv3%20Algorithm-333333?style=flat-square) ![SocketJs](https://img.shields.io/badge/SocketJs-333333?style=flat-square) ![Image Processing - Open CV](https://img.shields.io/badge/Image%20Processing%20--%20Open%20CV-333333?style=flat-square) ![gTTS](https://img.shields.io/badge/gTTS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

People with visual impairments face significant challenges in navigating everyday environments safely and independently. While traditional aids such as white canes provide basic tactile feedback, they are limited in scope and cannot offer contextual understanding of surroundings. Users often struggle to identify obstacles beyond immediate reach, recognize objects, or understand dynamic environments like crowded spaces.

Existing digital assistive tools also fall short, as many rely on static inputs, require manual interaction, or lack real-time responsiveness. They typically do not integrate multiple sensory inputs such as vision, distance sensing, and contextual reasoning into a single unified system.

VIAS (Vision Intelligence Assistive System) addresses these limitations by combining real-time computer vision, sensor data, and voice interaction into an intelligent assistive solution. The system continuously analyzes the user’s surroundings, detects objects and obstacles, and provides immediate audio feedback. It enables users to understand what is ahead, identify people or objects, and receive warnings about potential hazards.

Additionally, VIAS introduces an interactive layer where users can actively query their environment using voice commands, making the system more intuitive and flexible. Features like emergency fall detection and automated alerts further enhance user safety.

By integrating hardware (Raspberry Pi and sensors) with AI-driven perception and natural language interaction, VIAS transforms passive assistance into an active, intelligent guidance system. The goal is to empower visually impaired individuals with greater independence, confidence, and safety in their daily lives.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building VIAS involved multiple real-world challenges across hardware, software, and AI integration:

- **Real-time communication latency**  
  Synchronizing video streams from Raspberry Pi to laptop while maintaining low latency was difficult. We optimized this using socket-based streaming and efficient frame encoding.

- **Speech recognition instability**  
  Handling voice input reliably was tricky due to noise sensitivity and early cut-offs. We fine-tuned speech recognition parameters like pause thresholds and timeout handling.

- **AI response control (Groq integration)**  
  Initially, the AI generated overly verbose or irrelevant responses. We refined prompts and logic to ensure concise, safety-focused outputs.

- **Concurrency issues**  
  Managing multiple threads (video stream, audio input, control signals) led to synchronization bugs. This was solved using event-based signaling like `speech_done`.

- **Hardware-software coordination**  
  Ensuring smooth interaction between Raspberry Pi (camera + audio) and laptop (AI processing) required careful protocol design.

Each of these challenges helped improve the robustness and real-world usability of the system.

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

VIAS fits into the **IoT + Artificial Intelligence** track by combining embedded hardware with real-time AI decision-making.

- **IoT Component**:  
  A Raspberry Pi acts as the edge device, capturing live video and interacting with sensors (camera, IMU, ultrasonic). It communicates with the processing system via sockets.

- **AI Component**:  
  The system uses computer vision (YOLO) for object detection and integrates multimodal AI (Groq) for contextual scene understanding and natural language interaction.

- **System Integration**:  
  The project demonstrates a complete pipeline from sensor data acquisition ? real-time processing ? intelligent response ? user feedback.

This combination enables VIAS to function as an intelligent assistive system rather than just a detection tool.

> GPS Independent Soldier Navigation system

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Arduino IDE](https://img.shields.io/badge/Arduino%20IDE-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Altimeter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Altimeter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Magnetometer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Magnetometer-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**Soldiers die not because they lack courage. They die because they do not know where they are.**


**Where GPS Does Not Exist**

- Underground bunkers, tunnels, and subterranean command centres
- Dense urban canyons, thick forests, and mountainous terrain
- Inside reinforced concrete structures and polar regions
- Underwater and submarine operations


**The Electronic Warfare Reality**

- Russia jammed GPS across Finland and the Baltics — confirmed
- Iran spoofed GPS and captured a US military drone without firing a single shot
- GPS jamming equipment is available online for under 50 dollars today
- State and non-state actors both have full access to jamming and spoofing tools


**What Happens When GPS Dies**

- Navigation dies — soldiers freeze with no sense of direction
- Commander loses every soldier from the tactical map simultaneously
- Units split, missions collapse, supply convoys drive into ambushes
- Rescue teams cannot find the wounded
- The entire operational picture goes dark in seconds

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/8af15152805041a8b83cf7825f9613e4/6f665e85-0743-40c5-a57f-d8617784eaa0.jpeg)

**The Problem We are Solving**

- Every alternative requires pre-installed infrastructure impossible in enemy territory
- Inertial navigation drifts 100 metres in just 10 minutes
- Visual SLAM fails in smoke, darkness, and underground environments
- No platform today fuses multiple sensors using AI to navigate when every external signal is dead
- No solution works simultaneously underground, urban, forested, and in fully jammed environments

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenge 1 — GPS Denial**

Problem: GPS is jammed, spoofed, and blocked in exactly the environments soldiers need it most. One cheap jammer blinds an entire battalion worth billions instantly.

Solution: NAND Navigators eliminates GPS dependency completely. Instead of satellites, we use Earth's own natural environment as the navigation reference — magnetic flux patterns, atmospheric pressure, and motion data. These signals cannot be jammed because they are not transmitted. They are physical properties of the Earth itself. No satellite needed at any layer.

---
![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/8af15152805041a8b83cf7825f9613e4/8296d827-4d56-4296-8f64-1873f11798e0.jpeg)

**Challenge 2 — Inertial Navigation Drift**

Problem: Accelerometers and gyroscopes accumulate tiny errors over time. Position drifts over 100 metres in just 10 minutes. Useless for long missions alone.

Solution: Our AI continuously compares inertial navigation output against real time environmental sensor patterns — magnetic flux and atmospheric pressure readings. The moment the AI detects a mismatch between what the inertial system says and what the environment says, it snaps the position back to the correct value. Drift never accumulates because the AI corrects it before it grows. Inertial navigation handles the speed. AI handles the accuracy.

---

**Challenge 3 — Communication Jamming**

Problem: All fixed frequency radio including ESP32, WiFi, and Bluetooth can be blocked by enemy jammers instantly.

Solution: Jamming every frequency from 1 MHz to 10 GHz simultaneously requires a truck-sized power generator. It is expensive, unsustainable, and reveals the enemy's exact location to our side. We exploit this physical limitation using two technologies working together:

- **Cognitive Radio** — continuously scans the entire spectrum in real time and automatically finds the cleanest available frequency. if the enemy jams one frequency we hop to another in milliseconds.
- **Beamforming** — focuses our signal like a laser beam directly toward the target instead of broadcasting in all directions. extremely hard to detect, extremely hard to jam, uses far less power.

Together: cognitive radio finds the clear frequency. beamforming locks the signal onto that frequency in a tight invisible beam toward the target. self healing, automatic, no human involvement needed.

---
**Challenge 6 — IoT Radio Wave Conflict**

Problem: ESP32 emits the same class of radio waves as GPS infrastructure. both can be blocked by the same jammers.

Solution: ESP32 is only used at base camp during pre-mission setup and post-mission data sync. during active missions the communication stack switches entirely to cognitive radio plus beamforming plus UWB — a completely different and far more resilient communication architecture that does not rely on fixed frequency transmission at all.

---

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

**NAND Navigators** is a distributed IoT sensor network where every node is an intelligent agent powered by on-device AI, all connected to a cloud AI brain that continuously learns from collective field data and delivers real time navigation intelligence through a web dashboard.

**The problem it solves**

Renting still relies on blind trust. Landlords and tenants argue about damage, security deposits are delayed, and evidence can be disputed. 
**RentProof** replaces this with a transparent, automated flow: 

- Deposits are locked in a smart contract

- *Move‑in/ Move‑out media* is hashed for integrity, and

- An AI pipeline compares damage to generate an objective verdict. 

- Funds are released *automatically* based on the result, reducing disputes, delays, and manual back‑and‑forth.

**Challenges we ran into**

Model and environment compatibility-

- Installing PyTorch/Ultralytics on macOS can fail with mismatched Python or wheel versions. I resolved this by aligning Python to 3.11 and using compatible CPU wheels during development.
- End‑to‑end API routing: Upload endpoints and analysis routes initially returned 404s because frontend paths didn’t match backend API prefixes. I corrected the route paths and aligned environment variables to make the upload/analysis flow work.
- Earlier thought of implementing the blockchain locally on the machine but then shifted to custom token enabled Blockchain using Ethereum Sepola.

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

**Web3/Blockchain:**
We use smart contracts to lock deposits in escrow, record media hashes on‑chain, and automate release based on the AI verdict. This removes manual disputes and makes the agreement transparent and auditable.

**AI:**
We run a YOLOv8‑based computer vision pipeline that compares move‑in vs move‑out media, detects damage, scores severity, and produces a signed verdict that drives the escrow release. This makes the assessment objective and tamper‑resistant.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
The core issue in Web3 today is "Blind Signing." Users are forced to interact with decentralized applications (DApps) where they cannot verify the raw transaction data. They must blindly trust the front-end interface—which is often compromised, phished, or malicious.

Currently, wallet providers like MetaMask or Rabby show users human-readable summaries, but these are generated by the DApp itself. If a website is hijacked (like BadgerDAO) or is a "Pixel-Perfect" phishing clone (like Inferno/Pink Drainers), the UI lies to the user. Users sign a "deposit" transaction, but their raw EVM bytes are actually authorizing an "unlimited drain" of their entire wallet.

What People Use It For
ChainGuardian acts as an independent security watchdog that operates between the DApp and the user's wallet. Users install ChainGuardian to:

Validate Intent: It decodes the actual binary payload, showing the user exactly what they are signing (e.g., "This isn't a transfer, it's a multisig takeover").

Prevent "Blind Signing": It translates raw, obfuscated bytecode into clear, plain-English warnings, preventing users from falling for complex phishing infrastructure.

Spot "Trap" Contracts: It automatically detects "Honeypots" (tokens that can be bought but never sold) and "Drainers" (contracts designed to steal funds) before a single dollar is sent.

🛡️ How ChainGuardian Protects You

 Invisible Security: You don't have to audit code; we do it for you. While you browse, our 8-engine security core scans every contract in milliseconds—checking for hidden traps, unverified code, and malicious 'backdoor' instructions—so you don’t have to.

Instant Truth: No more deep-diving into Etherscan or audit reports. Every transaction is boiled down to a simple 0–100 Risk Score. If it’s dangerous, we stop it automatically before a single cent leaves your wallet.

The "Black Box" Recorder: If something goes wrong, you aren't left helpless. We create an immutable log of exactly what you authorized, providing the "receipt" you need for insurance claims or legal disputes—something that was missing for victims of the WazirX heist.

Immune to Hijacks: Because we watch your wallet’s "brain" (the provider level) rather than the website itself, we are completely immune to phishing. Even if a website is 100% compromised, our simulation engine exposes the hidden drainer code before you ever click 'Approve'.

**Challenges we ran into**

🛠️ Challenges I Ran Into
Building a real-time security interceptor was a race against the clock. Here were the two biggest hurdles:

The "Async-Speed" Bottleneck:

The Problem: Running 8 complex security checks (API calls to Dune/Moralis + static opcode analysis) took too long, causing the wallet to "time out" and frustrating users.

The Fix: I architected a parallel-dispatch engine using Promise.all() with strict withTimeout(3000ms) thresholds. If a service like Dune took too long, the system would gracefully fail-open to the local heuristics (Check 4 & Check 8) while prioritizing the most critical checks (Alchemy Simulation) first. This ensured the user got a response in under 3 seconds, regardless of third-party API latency.

The "Lying Frontend" Reality:

The Problem: I initially tried to verify transactions by scraping the website’s HTML/DOM for clues. I quickly realized this was a losing battle—hackers (like those behind BadgerDAO) specifically inject malicious scripts that rewrite the UI elements the DOM scrapers look for.

The Fix: I completely shifted my logic from "Page Analysis" to "Provider Interception." By hooking into the window.ethereum.request method, I stopped trying to read what the website said and started reading the raw binary payload the website was trying to send. This made ChainGuardian immune to frontend hijacks, as I was analyzing the "truth" (the raw EVM bytes) before the wallet ever signed it.

🛡️ How ChainGuardian Protects You
Security shouldn't require a degree in computer science. We’ve made protection feel like it isn't even there:

Invisible Security: You don't have to audit code; we do it for you. While you browse, our 8-engine security core scans every contract in milliseconds—checking for hidden traps, unverified code, and malicious 'backdoor' instructions—so you don’t have to.

Instant Truth: No more deep-diving into Etherscan or audit reports. Every transaction is boiled down to a simple 0–100 Risk Score. If it’s dangerous, we stop it automatically before a single cent leaves your wallet.

The "Black Box" Recorder: If something goes wrong, you aren't left helpless. We create an immutable log of exactly what you authorized, providing the "receipt" you need for insurance claims or legal disputes—something that was missing for victims of the $235M WazirX heist.

Immune to Hijacks: Because we watch your wallet’s "brain" (the provider level) rather than the website itself, we are completely immune to phishing. Even if a website is 100% compromised, our simulation engine exposes the hidden drainer code before you ever click 'Approve'.

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

ChainGuardian is a "Truth Engine" for the blockchain, solving the trust gap between human intent and machine execution. While most AI projects predict market trends, we use AI-driven heuristic analysis and real-time state simulation to solve the Web3 security crisis. By intercepting raw EVM bytecode at the wallet-provider level, we decode complex, obfuscated contract logic into clear, actionable intent. Our engine treats the blockchain as a dynamic, intelligent environment, running predictive simulations that foresee asset theft before a transaction hits the mempool. We don't just block scams; we provide the on-chain forensic transparency needed to make "blind signing" a relic of the past.

**The problem it solves**

# Team AI007
# Safe_Sight 🛡️
**Real-Time Cyber-Physical Safety System for High-Risk Environments**

Safe_Sight is an integrated solution designed to bridge the gap between physical IoT sensors and digital response dashboards. Developed during the 2026 Bengaluru Hackathon, it focuses on eliminating "Information Lag" in high-stakes environments like construction sites.

---

## The Problem: The "Visibility Gap"
On a busy construction site, safety is often managed through passive signs or human supervision. This leads to three critical failures:

1. **Reaction Latency**: If a worker unknowingly enters a "No-Go Zone" (e.g., under a moving crane or near a deep pit), supervisors often don't realize it until a "near-miss" or accident occurs.
2. **Information Silos**: Hardware sensors may detect a breach, but that data rarely reaches the mobile device of the site manager in real-time.
3. **The 5-Second Rule**: In construction, a 5-second delay in communication can be the difference between a minor warning and a fatal injury.

## The Solution
Safe_Sight creates a "digital nervous system" for the job site:
* **Detection**: Ultrasonic and Motion sensors act as 24/7 "eyes."
* **The Bridge**: A Node.js backend configured for high-concurrency broadcasting.
* **Instant Alert**: A Flutter dashboard that pulses red and logs the breach within **2 seconds** of the physical event.

---

## Hardware Architecture
* **Microcontroller**: ESP32 (Selected for its integrated Wi-Fi capabilities).
* **Sensors**: 
    * **Ultrasonic (HC-SR04)**: For perimeter breach detection in construction zones.
    * **PIR Motion Sensor**: For unauthorized access detection in restricted hazardous areas.
* **Communication**: HTTP GET protocol to a dedicated Node.js endpoint.
* **Local Alert**: Active Buzzer for immediate on-site auditory warning.

## Tech Stack
* **Frontend**: Flutter (Dart) — High-alert, dark-mode dashboard.
* **Backend**: Node.js (Express) — The central communication bridge.
* **Workflow**: Git / GitHub Organization for collaborative development.

---

## How to Run
1. **Backend**: Navigate to `safe_sight_backend` and run `node app.js`.
2. **Frontend**: Navigate to `safe_sight`, run `flutter pub get`, then `flutter run`.
3. **Trigger**: Access `http://172.25.73.205:3000/trigger` to simulate a hardware alert.

**Challenges we ran into**

Real-Time Latency & Architecture: Transitioning from a Stateless to a Stateful architecture to move away from inefficient "HTTP Polling" toward instant WebSocket communication.

Network & Environment Blocks: Overcoming "invisible" barriers like Windows Firewall and University Wi-Fi Isolation that prevented your friends' devices from "talking" to your backend.

Dynamic IP Management: Managing connectivity issues caused by fluctuating IPv4 addresses in a hackathon environment, which required constant reconfiguration of the "Bridge" URL.

Cross-Language Integration: Ensuring the Node.js bridge could correctly parse JSON data sent from the Python/YOLO detector while simultaneously broadcasting to a Flutter frontend.

Frontend State Synchronization: Implementing logic to ensure the UI reacted immediately to backend signals, such as triggering the siren and shifting background colors without manual refreshes.

Environment Stability: Resolving "ghost processes" where old server instances clung to Port 3000, causing new deployments to appear "stuck" or "dead".

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

## 1. The AIML "Brain": Perception and Intelligence
The project uses YOLO (You Only Look Once), which represents the "Think" part of the system.

Real-Time Computer Vision: Instead of just recording footage, the AI is actively "seeing" and classifying objects (Helmet vs. No Helmet) in every frame.

Automated Decision Making: The AI layer removes the need for a human to watch a screen 24/7. It autonomously decides when a safety protocol has been breached.

## 2. The IoT "Nervous System": Connectivity and Action
This is where your Node.js Bridge and Flutter Dashboard come in, representing the "Sense" and "Act" components.

Edge-to-Cloud Communication: In a real-world IoT setup, the camera (the Edge device) sends data to a central hub (your Backend Bridge).

Protocol Integration: You aren't just using standard web pages; you are using WebSockets (Socket.io). This is the backbone of IoT, allowing devices to "talk" to each other instantly without waiting for a manual refresh.

Physical Feedback: By triggering a siren and changing the UI state on a remote device, you are performing a "Cyber-Physical" action—the digital detection results in a physical-world warning.

## 3. The Convergence: "AIoT"
When you combine these, you get AIoT (Artificial Intelligence of Things).

Distributed Processing: Your project splits the work: the Hardware Friend handles the Heavy AI processing, you handle the Data Routing (The Bridge), and the Frontend Friend handles the User Alerting.

Scalability: This architecture is perfect for IoT because you could eventually connect 100 cameras to your one "Bridge," and they would all feed into the same dashboard.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![DApp](https://img.shields.io/badge/DApp-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contracts](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contracts-333333?style=flat-square) ![DAO](https://img.shields.io/badge/DAO-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Universities generate large amounts of recyclable waste, yet participation in recycling programs is often low because incentives and verification systems are weak or inefficient.

At the same time, many students face economic barriers to accessing food and essential services on campus.

LazosTech addresses both challenges by transforming recycling actions into onchain incentives. When students recycle aluminum cans, the action is verified and converted into tokenized rewards that can be redeemed for food or other campus benefits.

By recording these actions onchain, the system creates transparency and accountability in sustainability programs while encouraging environmentally responsible behavior.

In practice, this allows universities to run incentive-based recycling systems that are transparent, scalable, and community-governed through decentralized infrastructure.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges was designing a smart contract architecture that could support governance, reward distribution, and proposal management without becoming overly complex.

Early versions of the contracts tightly coupled several functions, which made testing and upgrading difficult. To solve this, the system was redesigned using a modular architecture where governance logic, resolution management, and token incentives are separated into different components.

Another challenge was modeling how real-world recycling actions could be verified and reliably translated into onchain transactions. The solution involved defining a verification layer that can later integrate with physical collection points or scanning systems.

These challenges helped refine the architecture and made the system more scalable for real-world deployments.

**The problem it solves**

Today this process is manual — teams must monitor social feeds, analyze sentiment, validate on-chain data, and deploy by hand. BasePulse is designed to automate this entire pipeline on Base: monitoring X and Farcaster for trends, running LLM-powered sentiment analysis via Claude, cross-validating against on-chain metrics, and deploying ERC20 tokens via the Coinbase CDP SDK on Base mainnet. The architecture is fully built — trend monitor, token deployer, treasury manager, and real-time dashboard are all implemented and running. The current MVP uses generated social posts to drive the autonomous loop while production X/Farcaster API integration is pending (rate-limited by subscription tiers). **Challenges we ran into**

The primary technical challenge was architecting a reliable autonomous loop that coordinates three independent systems without human oversight: the trend monitor (LLM sentiment analysis via Claude), the token deployer (Coinbase CDP SDK on Base mainnet), and the treasury manager (fee collection and reinvestment logic). Extensive error handling and retry logic was required to prevent loop crashes. A major ongoing challenge is production API access: real-time X and Farcaster feed ingestion is gated behind paid API tiers, so the current loop uses generated theme posts as a stand-in while the architecture awaits production credentials. Similarly, live on-chain token deployments via the CDP SDK require funded CDP API credentials and ETH for gas — the deployment code is complete and correct, but production execution is blocked on infrastructure funding. The Uniswap V4 integration via Clanker SDK and the real-time tRPC + React Query dashboard architecture also required significant engineering effort to get right.

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/adctm-autonomous-data-centre-thermal-management-system-472d) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://huggingface.co/spaces/nayagjhjgvj/ADCTMAgent) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-InOut2k26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://inout2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Intelligent Cooling Under Uncertainty

![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![RestAPIs](https://img.shields.io/badge/RestAPIs-333333?style=flat-square) ![HuggingFace](https://img.shields.io/badge/HuggingFace-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1) Modern data centers generate large amounts of heat due to continuous operation of servers and computing systems.
2) Excessive heat can reduce hardware performance, damage components, and cause system failures.
3) Cooling systems are necessary, but they consume 30–40% of total data center energy, increasing operational cost..
4) Workloads in data centers change continuously, causing uneven and unpredictable heat generation across zones.
5) Overcooling wastes energy, while undercooling risks overheating and hardware damage.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building ADCTM wasn’t just about coding a simulation — the main challenge was making it realistic, unstable, and still controllable.

Thermal Modeling: Simple models were too predictable. We had to balance heat, cooling, ambient effects, and noise to create realistic but stable dynamics.

Controlled Randomness: Adding stochastic workloads and failures often made the system either chaotic or trivial. We solved this using seeded randomness and bounded disturbances.

Hidden Failures: Simulating hardware failures without explicit signals was tricky. We designed indirect failure patterns (e.g., abnormal temperature rise) to force adaptive behavior.

Reward Design: Agents initially overcooled or behaved unstably. We fixed this by carefully balancing safety, energy, and smoothness in the reward.

Determinism vs Realism: Maintaining reproducibility while keeping randomness required strict seeding and controlled stochastic processes.

System Integration: Ensuring smooth interaction between API, simulation, and agents led to issues like inconsistent states and latency.

Deployment Stability: Making the system hackathon-ready  required additional engineering.

**The Destiny of Warriors**

ADCTM fits into the “Destiny of Warriors” track by focusing on intelligent decision-making under high-pressure and uncertain conditions.

In real-world data centers, cooling systems must continuously “fight” against unpredictable workloads, rising temperatures, and hidden hardware failures. A single wrong decision can lead to overheating, system damage, or massive energy waste.

Our system acts like a strategic agent that:

 adapts to dynamic and adversarial environments
 handles unseen failures without explicit signals
 balances safety, efficiency, and stability in real time

Just like a warrior operating in uncertain conditions, the AI must make precise, adaptive, and robust decisions to maintain control and prevent failure.

ADCTM demonstrates how intelligent systems can operate reliably in complex, high-stakes environments which aligns directly with the core idea of this track.

> Unearth business logic from legacy code

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem your project solves**

In large enterprises, legacy systems power critical invisible workflows—business logic that runs every day but remains unseen and unmanaged.

As original developers leave and documentation becomes outdated, core business logic gets buried in thousands of lines of code. Enterprise Architects are forced to spend weeks manually analyzing systems just to answer basic questions:

- **What does this system actually do?** (Intent vs. implementation)
- **What breaks if we change this logic?** (Hidden dependencies)

This “black box” effect slows down modernization, increases risk, and leads to costly failures during system upgrades.

**How you are solving it**

**CodeArcheology** is an AI-native reverse-engineering engine that turns legacy code into clear, visual, and actionable business logic.

Using Claude, the system “interviews” the code to reconstruct its original business intent—bridging the gap between technical implementation and business understanding.

## Key Capabilities

### 1. Business Logic Extraction
Upload a legacy code snippet (Java, C#, etc.), and instantly receive:
- A concise business-level summary
- Structured business rules (conditions and outcomes)
- Clear explanations of key decision points
 
### 2. Visual Logic Mapping
Automatically generate Mermaid diagrams that visualize workflows and decision trees, making complex logic immediately understandable.
 
### 3. Interactive Impact Analysis ("What-If Engine")
Users can ask natural language questions such as:

> "What happens if GST changes from 9% to 10%?"

The system responds with:
- Affected logic paths and modules
- Potential downstream impact
- A clear risk assessment (🔴 Red / 🟡 Amber / 🟢 Green)
 
### 4. Risk Highlighting ("Red Zones")
Identify high-risk areas in the code where changes are most likely to cause cascading failures.

### 5. Jira-Ready Ticket Generation
Transform modernization suggestions into actionable, structured delivery tickets ready for import into project management tools like Jira. Each ticket includes:
- Title, type (Story / Task / Risk), and priority
- Description and acceptance criteria
- Direct mapping from modernization insights to sprint-ready work items

## How It Works

### Code Ingestion
Users upload legacy code snippets or modules.

### AI Analysis (Claude)
Claude extracts business entities, decision logic, and intent from the code.

### Context Enrichment (Genspark)
Genspark maps legacy patterns to modern standards and flags potential risks.

### Visualization & Interaction
Results are presented in a simple dashboard with summaries, rules, diagrams, and interactive Q&A.
 
## Hackathon Scope

For this sprint, we will build a **Live Archaeology Dashboard** that:

- Accepts legacy code input
- Generates instant:
  - Business summaries
  - Structured rule sets
  - Mermaid-based logic diagrams
- Supports an "Ask Your Code" feature for impact analysis
- Highlights high-risk logic areas ("Red Zones")
- Generates Jira-ready delivery tickets from modernization plans

 
## Impact & Value

- ⚡ **Reduce** system analysis time from weeks to minutes
- 🚀 **Enable** faster, safer modernization decisions
- 🔍 **Surface** hidden dependencies before they break
- 🌉 **Bridge** the gap between technical systems and business understanding

**Use of Claude**

Claude serves as the **core intelligence engine** for CodeArcheology, powering the reverse-engineering pipeline:

### Code Analysis Engine
- Parses legacy code across multiple languages (Java, C#, Python, etc.)
- Extracts syntactic and semantic structures to build a code model
- Identifies business entities, constants, and decision points

### Business Logic Extraction
- Reconstructs original business intent from implementation details
- Bridges the gap between technical code and business terminology
- Generates concise, executive-friendly summaries of complex logic

### Decision Path Analysis
- Traces conditional logic and branching patterns
- Explains the "why" behind business rules and constraints
- Identifies hidden dependencies and implicit assumptions

### Natural Language Query Engine
- Powers the "Ask Your Code" What-If analysis feature
- Handles questions like: "What happens if GST changes from 9% to 10%?"
- Evaluates impact across identified logic paths

### Risk Assessment & Scoring
- Evaluates code complexity and change risk
- Flags high-risk logic areas ("Red Zones") prone to cascading failures
- Provides severity scoring (🔴 Critical / 🟡 Warning / 🟢 Safe)

### Real-time API Integration
- `/api/analyze` endpoint processes code snippets on-demand
- Streams analysis results for interactive user feedback
- Supports batch processing for enterprise modules

### TabLock
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/tablock-ed45) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ItzErikson/tablock) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/rBvmSC0QPrs) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/rBvmSC0QPrs) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-SCBC%20Hackathon%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://scbc-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Lock shares before bill arrives. Settle instantly.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![ethers.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/ethers.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

*You've been there before.*

Dinner ends, someone puts their card down, and then comes the awkward part, chasing six people on Venmo, hoping everyone actually pays, trusting one person to do the math right and not pocket the difference.

Traditional bill splitting requires trust. Trust in a person, trust in an app, trust that someone won't ghost the group chat. There's no enforcement. There's no guarantee.

**TabLock removes trust from the equation entirely.**

Before the meal, everyone locks their estimated share in a smart contract on Arc — including a 40% buffer for tax and tip. The contract holds the funds. Nobody controls them. When the bill arrives, whoever paid the restaurant declares the total, and the contract automatically calculates each person's proportional share  and distributes everything — the right amount to the payer, unused buffer back to each member.

**No chasing. No awkward texts. No trust required.**

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest bug wasn't obvious until the math broke in production.

The settlement contract correctly sent each non-payer's share to 
the payer, but the payer's own locked funds were never returned. 
They sat in the contract permanently. On the surface the logic 
looked right: calculate share, calculate returned buffer, transfer 
both. But the payer is a different case entirely. They already paid 
the restaurant out of pocket. Their "contribution" to the bill is 
implicit, what they need back is their entire locked amount, not 
just the unused buffer.

The fix was one line. Finding it required tracing the math across 
three scenarios: bill less than locked, bill exactly equal to 
locked, and bill exceeding locked. Only by running all three did 
the bug become visible, the zero-buffer edge case made it 
impossible to ignore.

It was a good reminder that financial logic has to be verified 
with numbers, not just code review.

**Programmable Money for Humans & Agents**

TabLock is a smart escrow that releases payments based on conditions.

Every dollar has rules attached before anyone touches it. Members lock USDC into the contract upfront. The contract enforces who owes what, calculates proportional shares of the actual bill, and distributes everything atomically in a single transaction. Nobody can underpay. Nobody can run. The logic controls the money, not the people.

This hits all three of the track's criteria directly:
**Embedded into applications**: USDC isn't a separate step. It's the mechanism. Locking, holding, and distributing funds is the app, not a feature on top of it.
**Controlled by logic**: no human intermediary decides who gets what. The contract reads the food estimates, reads the actual bill, and executes the math. 
**Without friction**: Arc makes this possible for a dinner table use case. Sub-second finality means settlement feels instant. Dollar-denominated gas means splitting a $60 dinner doesn't cost more in fees than the meal itself. USDC as the token means nobody's share fluctuates between joining and settling.

TabLock brings absolute guarantee to a group of friends at a restaurant — that's programmable money for humans.

[Eric Yang](https://github.com/ItzErikson)

### Shoujiki
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/shoujiki-829e) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Sugarcube08/Shoujiki) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://shoujiki.onrender.com/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-SCBC%20Hackathon%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://scbc-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> A Trustless Market for AI Agents On Solana

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The project addresses a fundamental gap in the current AI and automation ecosystem: there is no reliable, trustable, and scalable way to discover, execute, and transact with autonomous agents.

Today, most AI agents and automation scripts operate in isolated environments. They are difficult to verify, lack transparency, and require users to trust centralized platforms or unknown developers. There is no standardized mechanism to ensure that an agent will behave as expected, that its output is authentic, or that payments are fairly handled. This creates friction, limits adoption, and prevents the emergence of a true agent-driven economy.

Additionally, execution systems for agents are often fragile and non-transparent. Users cannot reliably track what happened during execution, why a task failed, or whether the results were manipulated. This lack of observability and accountability makes it unsuitable for real-world usage where reliability and trust are critical.

From an economic perspective, there is also no efficient infrastructure for enabling micro-transactions between users and agents. Traditional systems are either too expensive or too slow to support high-frequency, low-value interactions, which are essential for scaling autonomous services.

Our project solves these problems by introducing a decentralized agent marketplace combined with a secure execution environment and on-chain settlement. It enables:

* Trustless execution, where agent behavior and ownership can be verified
* Transparent operations, with clear tracking of execution and results
* Fair and automated payments, removing reliance on intermediaries
* Scalable micro-transactions, enabling frequent agent interactions

By addressing trust, transparency, and economic coordination together, the project lays the foundation for a reliable ecosystem where autonomous agents can be safely discovered, executed, and monetized at scale.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges I Ran Into

One of the biggest challenges during development was designing a reliable and safe execution system for user-submitted agents.

#### 1. Sandbox Execution Bottleneck

Initially, agent execution was handled synchronously through the API. Each request would trigger a Docker-based sandbox that installed dependencies (`pip install`) and executed the agent code in real time. This approach worked in early testing but quickly became a major bottleneck.

**Problems faced:**

* API requests were blocking and timing out for longer executions
* Repeated dependency installation caused significant latency
* System performance degraded rapidly under concurrent load

**How I solved it:**

* Refactored execution into an asynchronous flow using a queue + worker model
* Introduced a background worker to handle execution independently of the API
* Shifted toward prebuilt or cached environments to eliminate repeated setup overhead

This change made the system significantly more stable and scalable.

---

#### 2. Lack of Execution Traceability

Another major issue was the inability to track what actually happened during an agent run. Initially, the system only returned final outputs without any structured logs or intermediate state.

**Problems faced:**

* Difficult to debug failures
* No visibility into execution steps
* No way to audit or verify agent behavior

**How I solved it:**

* Introduced a structured `AgentRun` model to track each execution
* Captured logs, errors, timestamps, and outputs for every run
* Built endpoints to query execution status and results

This improved both debugging and user trust in the system.

---

#### 3. Security Risks in Sandbox Communication

The sandbox service was initially exposed internally without strict authentication, which created a potential risk of unauthorized code execution.

**Problems faced:**

* Risk of arbitrary code execution if the endpoint was accessed improperly
* No clear boundary between trusted and untrusted requests

**How I solved it:**

* Added authentication between services (shared secret / token-based validation)
* Restricted sandbox access to internal network only
* Enforced stricter validation on incoming execution requests

### Key Takeaway

The main lesson from these challenges was the importance of building a **solid, observable, and secure foundation first**, before layering advanced capabilities. By focusing on execution reliability, traceability, and security, the system is now in a position to scale and evolve without breaking.

**Best Use of Solana**

Our project represents one of the strongest applications of Solana because it does not treat the blockchain as a peripheral payment layer, but as a core execution and trust infrastructure.

First, we leverage Solana’s high-throughput and low-latency design to enable near real-time settlement of agent executions. In our system, agents are not just pieces of code; they are service providers. Each execution can be tied to an on-chain interaction, allowing users to trigger, verify, and settle outcomes with minimal delay. This aligns directly with Solana’s strength in handling thousands of transactions per second at extremely low cost, making frequent micro-interactions economically viable.

Second, we utilize Solana as a trust layer for a decentralized agent marketplace. Every agent can be associated with verifiable ownership, versioning, and execution history anchored to the chain. This creates a transparent and tamper-resistant environment where users can confidently interact with agents, knowing that their provenance and behavior can be audited. Solana’s architecture makes this feasible at scale without introducing prohibitive costs.

Third, the project takes advantage of Solana’s composability. By integrating with token standards and programmable transactions, we enable flexible payment flows such as pay-per-execution, escrow-based settlements, and future extensions like staking or reputation-based incentives. These mechanisms are not bolted on; they are native to how the system operates and evolves.

Fourth, our use of Solana supports an emerging machine-to-machine economy. Agents can autonomously trigger transactions, receive payments, and participate in economic workflows without human intervention. Solana’s speed and deterministic execution make it suitable for this kind of automated, high-frequency interaction model, which would be impractical on slower or more expensive chains.

Finally, the system is designed to scale with real-world usage. As the number of agents and executions grows, Solana’s performance characteristics ensure that the platform can handle increasing demand without degradation in user experience. This makes it a strong foundation for building a long-term ecosystem of autonomous services.

In summary, the project demonstrates the best use of Solana by embedding it deeply into execution, trust, and economic coordination, rather than using it only as a payment backend. It showcases how Solana can power a high-frequency, decentralized, and autonomous service marketplace at scale.

**The problem it solves**

In today’s digital economy, millions of transactions—freelance work, online marketplaces, and peer-to-peer deals—happen between parties who do not know or trust each other. Payments are typically made either upfront, risking loss if the seller fails to deliver, or after delivery, risking non-payment for the seller. Existing solutions rely on centralized intermediaries, which introduce high fees, delays, limited accessibility, and single points of failure. As a result, users face frequent scams, disputes, and a lack of transparency, with no reliable, trustless mechanism to ensure that funds are exchanged fairly based on agreed conditions.

**Challenges we ran into**

During the development of our escrow platform, we faced several practical and technical challenges while integrating stablecoin payments from Circle with smart contracts on Avalanche. One of the key difficulties was implementing the ERC-20 token flow correctly, particularly handling the approve() and transferFrom() mechanism in a secure way to ensure user funds were only accessed with proper permission. Setting up and maintaining a stable connection to the Avalanche Fuji testnet also required careful configuration of RPC endpoints, chain IDs, and wallet network switching, as even small misconfigurations led to failed transactions. Additionally, blockchain transactions introduced latency and uncertainty, making it challenging to design a smooth user experience that clearly communicates loading states, confirmations, and errors. Ensuring smart contract reliability was another critical concern, as any flaw in deposit, release, or refund logic could result in locked or misdirected funds. We also had to address synchronization issues between on-chain data and the frontend UI to prevent inconsistencies in transaction status. On top of this, integrating wallet interactions like MetaMask brought its own challenges, including handling user rejections and connection errors gracefully. Overall, the main challenge was balancing secure blockchain logic with a seamless and intuitive user experience for non-technical users.

**Programmable Money for Humans & Agents**

The project fits into the “Programmable Money for Humans and Agents” track by using USDC from Circle as programmable money, where funds are not simply transferred but controlled through predefined logic. Instead of making direct payments, the system locks USDC in a smart contract and releases or refunds it only when specific conditions are met, such as successful delivery of a service. This allows users to engage in transactions without needing to trust each other, as the rules are enforced automatically. In this setup, the smart contract behaves like an autonomous agent that holds funds, verifies conditions, and executes actions without human intervention. This demonstrates how money can be programmed to follow rules, enabling secure, transparent, and condition-based transactions for both individuals and automated systems.

**Agentic Payments on Avalanche**

The project leverages Avalanche as the core blockchain layer to implement a secure and decentralized escrow system. All critical transaction logic—such as locking funds, releasing payments, and issuing refunds—is executed through smart contracts deployed on Avalanche.

Avalanche is particularly suitable for this use case because of its fast transaction finality, low fees, and compatibility with Solidity-based smart contracts, which makes it easy to build and deploy decentralized applications. By using Avalanche, the escrow process becomes trustless, meaning that no third-party intermediary is required to manage or verify transactions.

When a user initiates a transaction, funds are transferred and securely locked within a smart contract on Avalanche. These funds can only be released or refunded based on predefined conditions coded into the contract. Every action is recorded on the blockchain, ensuring transparency, immutability, and verifiability.

Additionally, Avalanche’s efficiency allows the application to provide a smooth user experience, even while interacting with blockchain infrastructure. This makes it ideal for real-world applications like freelance payments, marketplace transactions, and peer-to-peer deals.

### AgentPay
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/agentpay-cacb) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Pushks18/AgentPay) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://agent-pay-lake.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/oUCDaHR83GM) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-SCBC%20Hackathon%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://scbc-hackathon.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> AI agents that hire each other, on-chain

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebSockets](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebSockets-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Avalanche](https://img.shields.io/badge/Avalanche-333333?style=flat-square) ![Helius](https://img.shields.io/badge/Helius-333333?style=flat-square) ![X402 Protocol](https://img.shields.io/badge/X402%20Protocol-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents are everywhere now, but they can't actually work together. Every time an AI agent needs to use another AI service, someone has to set up an API key, manage a subscription, and manually approve payments. That's not autonomous. That's just automation with extra steps.

The core problems:

- **No autonomous payments** — agents can't pay each other without a human approving every transaction
- **No trust layer** — there's no way to verify if an agent is reliable before hiring it
- **No accountability** — an agent can do bad work with zero consequences

**AgentPay fixes all three:**

- Agent A discovers Agent B from an on-chain registry (Anchor program on Solana)
- Pays $0.005 USDC autonomously via x402, no human clicks
- Receives the result and permanently writes a reputation score on-chain
- Bad agents get slashed and lose their staked SOL

**By the numbers:**

- 3 Rust/Anchor programs deployed on Solana devnet
- 8 AI agent services available (code review, audits, trust reports, summarization and more)
- 2 chains running simultaneously (Solana + Avalanche Fuji)
- 100x cheaper reputation storage via ZK-compressed tokens (Light Protocol)
- $0.005 minimum per-request pricing, no subscriptions
- 0 human clicks required in the autonomous agent loop

This isn't a demo of what agent economies could look like someday. It's a working prototype of what they look like right now.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Getting x402 autonomous payments to actually work**

The x402 protocol has a two-phase HTTP flow that basically no Python HTTP client handles natively. The server returns 402, the client has to sign a USDC transfer on-chain, then retry the request with a payment proof header. Building this into a LangChain tool that an AI agent could call autonomously, without hanging or losing the payment mid-flight, took most of the night. The Python x402 SDK also went through two breaking API changes between v1 and v2 and the docs don't make it obvious which one you're on.

**2. Rust and Anchor with zero prior experience**

I'm primarily an AI/ML engineer. Rust is not my daily language. Writing three Anchor programs (registry, escrow, staking/slashing) from scratch meant learning PDAs, account validation, CPI calls, and Borsh serialization all at once. The version mismatch between anchor-lang 0.29, 0.30, and the CLI caused build failures that took hours to diagnose. The escrow program specifically had a borrow-checker issue that Claude Code and I went back and forth on for longer than I'd like to admit.

**3. Dual-chain coordination**

Running Solana and Avalanche simultaneously meant two wallet sets, two RPC connections, two x402 facilitators, and an agent decision layer that routes to the right chain dynamically. The Avalanche side uses ERC-8004 identity and reputation registries. The Solana side uses Anchor programs and Light Protocol for ZK-compressed reputation tokens. Getting both to work together without the agent getting confused about which chain to use for which operation was genuinely tricky.

**4. Light Protocol ZK compression**

This was the most pleasant surprise. The SDK is well designed and minting compressed reputation tokens ended up being about 30 lines of JavaScript. The hard part was figuring out that you need a Helius RPC specifically (not public devnet) because Light Protocol's Photon indexer only runs on Helius nodes. That cost about an hour.

**5. Scope control**

Honestly the hardest non-technical challenge. Once the core loop was working I kept wanting to add things. Recursive agent hiring where Agent B spawns its own sub-agents. Dynamic reputation-based pricing. Cross-chain job routing via Wormhole. A2A protocol compatibility. I had to force myself to stop building and start submitting. The problem space is genuinely exciting and seven hours is not enough time to build everything you can imagine.

**Programmable Money for Humans & Agents**

AgentPay uses native Circle-issued USDC on Avalanche Fuji as the settlement currency for every agent-to-agent transaction. Payments flow via EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization, making them gasless for the buyer. Every time Agent A hires Agent B, real USDC moves on-chain with no intermediary. The architecture is CCTP-ready for cross-chain USDC flows between Solana and Avalanche. AgentPay demonstrates exactly what programmable money looks like when the payer is an autonomous AI agent with no human in the loop.

**Best Use of Solana**

AgentPay deploys three Rust/Anchor programs on Solana devnet: an agent registry with PDA-seeded agent cards, an escrow program that holds USDC until work is confirmed, and a staking/slashing program that burns bad actors' stakes. Reputation is stored as ZK-compressed tokens via Light Protocol, making a million-agent economy economically viable at roughly 200x cheaper than standard SPL accounts. Agent A queries the on-chain Anchor registry to discover available agents, routes payments via x402 on Solana devnet, and mints a compressed reputation token after every completed job. Solana handles identity and trust. Avalanche handles settlement. Each chain does what it does best.

**Agentic Payments on Avalanche**

AgentPay is built natively on Avalanche Fuji. ERC-8004 IdentityRegistry and ReputationRegistry contracts at their canonical addresses handle agent identity and trust. x402 payments settle USDC on Avalanche C-Chain in under 2 seconds via the Coinbase facilitator. An autonomous LangChain agent discovers sellers from the ERC-8004 registry, signs payment payloads with its own key, and writes reputation feedback via giveFeedback after every job. Zero human clicks on the critical path. The architecture is Teleporter-ready for cross-L1 reputation portability.

**The problem it solves**

Every group activity ends the same way: confusion around who owes what.

After dinners, trips, or shared moments, people fall back to group chats and Venmo. Messages pile up, totals are unclear, one person ends up doing the math, and someone usually overpays or gets underpaid.

But the bigger problem is that money and memories are disconnected. Photos live in one place, payments happen in another, and there’s no shared space that captures both.

What Remi does

Remi is built around bubbles, private group time capsules.

A bubble is where a group’s memories and money live together. You can post photos and videos, relive moments, and handle shared expenses all in the same place.

Inside a bubble, you can start a pot, a shared expense tied to a real moment. From there, Remi turns the process into a simple flow: scan a receipt, see every item instantly, tap exactly what you had, and pay immediately. No manual math, no chasing people later.

Each payment is tied directly to that moment, inside that group.

Why this matters

Remi doesn’t just make payments easier — it makes them make sense.

Every expense has context, every payment is tied to a memory, and every group has a clean, shared history. Instead of scattered photos, messy group chats, and delayed payments, Remi creates a single place where everything comes together.

What makes it different
Itemized splitting — pay only for what you had
Instant settlement — powered by Solana
No app required — anyone can scan a link or QR and pay
Bubbles — where memories and money live together

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest hurdles were on the UI/UX side, figuring out how to integrate Kora cleanly, making sure QR flows worked end-to-end, and constantly putting myself in the customer's shoes to make sure every interaction felt natural. A lot of iteration went into polishing the small details so the app felt effortless to use. Making ui for both desktop and  mobile webview was definitely a hurdle as well.

**Best Use of Solana**

Remi only works this smoothly because of Solana. Payments settle instantly in USDC, Kora abstracts gas so transactions are effectively fee-less, Solana Pay enables QR and link-based payments with pre-filled amounts. This makes the experience feel like Apple Pay: scan, confirm, done.
