### Kompasss
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/kompasss-b14c) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://kompasss.xyz) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/SBoCxXVTc7c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Let AI agents find, trust, and pay each other.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Docker](https://img.shields.io/badge/Docker-333333?style=flat-square) ![GraphQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/GraphQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents today are powerful, but they still cannot really work with each other like businesses do.
There is no standard way for one agent to discover another, understand what it can do, pay it, assign it work, and verify that the job was actually completed. Most agent systems are still siloed, which means agents built on different frameworks cannot easily coordinate or transact.
Kompass solves that by giving agents the missing infrastructure they need to operate in the real world.
With Kompass, an agent can:
create an on-chain identity using Basenames on Base
publish its capabilities, pricing, and endpoint information
discover other agents through a searchable marketplace
pay other agents instantly in USDC
hire agents for larger tasks using escrow
build on-chain reputation as work gets completed
This makes a lot of existing workflows easier.
For example, instead of one agent trying to do everything badly, Kompass lets a task be split across specialized agents. A user can give a simple request like “find the best yield on Base”, and Kompass can automatically route that work across research, data, risk, and execution agents. Each agent handles the part it is best at, another agent can verify the result, and payment happens automatically once the work is done.
It also makes paid capabilities much easier to use. Through x402-based payments, agents can access premium tools like DeFi data, research, swap quotes, token deployment, and portfolio intelligence on a pay-per-call basis. That means no API key setup, no subscriptions, and no manual billing overhead.
In simple terms, Kompass helps turn AI agents from isolated tools into a network of discoverable, transacting, collaborating workers. It makes agent-to-agent coordination easier, safer, and much more practical.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges I ran into was around ENS ownership on Base Sepolia.
When a Basename gets registered through the normal registrar flow, it mints an ERC-721 token that represents name ownership. But the tricky part is that this does not automatically update the ENS L2 Registry’s owner() mapping. Our Kompass contracts relied on that ownership check before allowing an agent to register or update its ENS profile, so agents could successfully register a Basename but still be blocked from actually using it inside Kompass.
That was a frustrating issue because from the outside it looked like registration had worked, but the next steps would fail. I solved it by building a single-call onboarding flow that handles the whole chain for the user — wallet creation, funding, Basename registration, and profile setup. Instead of making users deal with ENS internals, Kompass abstracts the entire process away.
Another major hurdle came from x402 payment integration. The server SDK was returning one version of the payment requirement format, while some of my fallback HTTP 402 responses were using an older version. Because of that mismatch, the client could not properly interpret the payment request. I fixed this by standardizing the response format and adding a fallback path for cases where the facilitator server could not generate requirements cleanly.
I also ran into issues while integrating the Clanker SDK for token deployment. Some of the expected types in practice did not match the examples shown in documentation. I had to dig into the SDK source and inspect the Zod schemas directly to understand the correct payload structure. That was one of those moments where reading the actual implementation was the only way forward.
Another practical challenge was CoinGecko free-tier rate limiting. After a few consecutive quote requests, the USD estimate for swaps would degrade or return zero because the pricing endpoint was being throttled. The actual swap transaction and Uniswap V3 calldata were still correct, so the on-chain execution worked fine, but the user-facing estimate became unreliable under rate limits. I handled this by isolating the estimate issue from the execution flow and treating it as a degraded display state rather than a swap failure.
Overall, the biggest theme was making a complicated stack — ENS, escrow, x402, agent identity, and tool execution — feel simple and reliable for the end user.

**AI**

Kompass treats AI agents as autonomous economic actors, not just tools. Every agent gets an on-chain identity via Basenames,        
  publishes its capabilities as ENS text records, and becomes discoverable through a GraphQL indexer — so any agent can find another  
  by what it does, not who built it.                              

  The commerce layer is where it clicks: agents pay each other directly using x402 (instant HTTP payments in USDC) for API-style
  services, or through ERC-8183 escrow for bigger jobs with milestones and evaluator-based quality checks. No human approval needed —
  agents discover, negotiate, pay, and verify each other autonomously.

  For complex tasks, Kompass routes a natural language intent across four specialist AI roles (research, data, risk, execution) and
  orchestrates them as an on-chain DAG pipeline with dependency resolution and cascade failure handling. We also built an MCP server
  with 40+ tools so any LLM can plug in and start transacting through Kompass immediately.

**Best creative use of ENS**

Kompass turns ENS text records into a full agent capability profile system. Instead of just using ENS for naming, we defined a
  structured namespace (com.kompass.*) where each text record carries a specific piece of agent metadata — type, categories, pricing, 
  MCP/A2A/x402 endpoints, ERC-8004 reputation linkage, and verification keys.

  The creative part: this makes ENS the universal "resume" for AI agents. Any protocol can read an agent's capabilities, trust
  posture, and service endpoints just by resolving their ENS name — no proprietary registry needed. Our indexer watches ENS
  TextChanged events in real-time, so updating an ENS record automatically updates the agent's discoverable profile across the entire
  network.

  We also use ENS ownership as the access control layer — the KompassRegistry contract verifies you own the ENS node before letting
  you register, so agent identities are sybil-resistant by default. ENS went from a naming service to the full identity and discovery
  layer for autonomous agent commerce

**Pool prize**

ENS is the identity backbone of Kompass — without it, nothing works. Every agent registers with a Basename and stores all its
  metadata as namespaced ENS text records under com.kompass.*: agent type, capability categories, pricing model, MCP/A2A/x402         
  endpoints, ERC-8004 reputation linkage, and ENSIP-25 verification keys.

  The KompassRegistry smart contract reads these text records directly from the ENS L2 resolver on Base Sepolia during registration,
  verifying the caller actually owns the ENS node. Our Ponder indexer watches both AgentRegistered events and ENS TextChanged events,
  so whenever an agent updates their ENS records, their discoverable profile updates automatically.

  This means ENS isn't just used for naming — it's the entire agent metadata layer. Agent capabilities, pricing, endpoints, and trust
  signals all live in ENS text records, making every agent profile portable, verifiable, and readable by any protocol without
  depending on a centralized registry.

**AI × Onchain**

Everything in Kompass happens on-chain on Base. Agent identities are Basenames with structured ENS text records. Agent discovery    
  runs through a Ponder indexer watching on-chain events. Payments settle in USDC via two rails — x402 for instant per-call API       
  payments using ERC-3009, and ERC-8183 escrow for milestone-based work with on-chain state machine transitions.

  When an AI agent expresses an intent, Kompass discovers matching agents on-chain, routes the task across specialists, and creates a
  DAG pipeline on Base where each subtask is a funded escrow job. Completion triggers USDC release and writes reputation feedback to
  ERC-8004 through hook contracts. The entire lifecycle — identity, discovery, payment, coordination, reputation — lives on Base, not
  in a database or off-chain service. We also use Coinbase AgentKit for wallet management and the x402 protocol for HTTP-native
  agent-to-agent payments, both core Base ecosystem tools.

**BEST Overall Project**

Kompass solves one of the biggest gaps in the agent ecosystem — there's no open way for AI agents to find each other, build trust,

### Axylosdotxyz
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/axylosdotxyz-9ea1) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/debojyoti10CC/axylosfirstdraft) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://axylos-new-24rq.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/IJzqQsDTQio?si=5CxaQmlMUOZdD5zc) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Automated agent negotiation Protocol

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today, most digital services require manual coordination between users, platforms, and payment systems. Even when two systems want to interact programmatically, they still rely on fixed pricing models, centralized APIs, and manual payment flows. This creates friction for machine-to-machine interactions and prevents autonomous agents from directly purchasing or selling services.

Axylos addresses this by enabling autonomous agents to discover each other, negotiate service prices, and settle payments automatically. Instead of fixed pricing or human involvement, agents dynamically negotiate using strategy-based decision logic and reach agreements in real time.

Once an agreement is reached, the service endpoint enforces payment using the HTTP 402 standard, allowing the buyer agent to automatically settle the payment and receive authorization to access the service. This removes the need for manual payment handling and enables fully automated service transactions between software agents.

By combining decentralized peer discovery, automated negotiation, and programmable payments, Axylos demonstrates how autonomous systems can directly coordinate and transact with each other without relying on centralized platforms.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges during development was implementing the **HTTP 402 payment flow using Elsa x402**. Initially, the client could detect the `402 Payment Required` response, but correctly extracting the `x-402-payment-request` header and retrying the request with the proper **L402 authorization token** required careful handling. The request pipeline had to be modified so the client could automatically intercept the payment challenge, complete the payment, and resend the request with the correct credentials.

Another challenge was coordinating **autonomous negotiation between agents** in a decentralized environment. Since agents communicate over a peer-to-peer mesh network, managing negotiation states (ACTIVE, COUNTER, ACCEPTED, REJECTED) while keeping both nodes synchronized required designing a reliable state machine and message handling logic.

Debugging the interaction between the negotiation layer, the payment challenge, and the final service execution was also tricky. At times the system returned fixed responses instead of triggering the payment flow correctly. This was resolved by restructuring the request handlers and ensuring that the negotiation outcome correctly propagated into the service layer before the payment challenge was issued.

Through iterative testing using multiple terminal instances (buyer and seller nodes), these issues were resolved, resulting in a stable end-to-end workflow where agents can negotiate, trigger the 402 payment challenge, complete the payment, and successfully execute the service.

**Best Use of Elsa x402 and Elsa OpenClaw skills**

Axylos implements an autonomous agent negotiation and settlement protocol that directly integrates **Elsa x402** and **Elsa OpenClaw** capabilities.

Agents in the network discover each other over a decentralized P2P mesh and autonomously negotiate service prices using a strategy-based negotiation engine. Once a price is agreed upon, the service endpoint is protected using the **HTTP 402 payment flow**, where the buyer agent receives an `x-402-payment-request` header and automatically settles the payment using the Elsa x402 protocol.

The payment client retrieves the **L402 token (macaroon + preimage)** and retries the request with authorization, unlocking the service. OpenClaw agents then execute the negotiated action, enabling verifiable on-chain settlement via blockchain transactions.

This demonstrates a full machine-to-machine commerce loop: **agent discovery → autonomous negotiation → x402 payment → L402 authorization → service execution**, showcasing a practical use of Elsa’s programmable payment infrastructure and OpenClaw autonomous agents.

**Projects building with the SDK to solve real-world problems will be eligible**

Axylos uses the **HeyElsa SDK** to enable autonomous machine-to-machine commerce through programmable payments and agent-based execution. The project integrates **Elsa x402** to enforce payment-gated APIs, allowing services to require payment using the HTTP 402 standard before execution.

When a buyer agent requests a service, the seller endpoint returns a `402 Payment Required` response with an `x-402-payment-request`. The Elsa payment client then automatically processes the payment and retrieves the **L402 authorization token**, which is used to retry the request and unlock the service.

The project also integrates **OpenClaw agents** to interpret requests and execute actions such as DeFi transactions once payment is verified. This demonstrates a practical real-world use case for the HeyElsa SDK: enabling autonomous agents to discover services, negotiate terms, pay for access, and execute actions without human intervention.

### ENS-folio
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ensfolio-0b78) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/aneleldho06/ens_portfolio) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/N9ZcBk9nIqY) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Turn your ENS into a Web3 resume.

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem it Solves

In the Web3 ecosystem, a person’s contributions and reputation are fragmented across multiple platforms.

Developers, DAO contributors, and community members leave their digital footprint in many different places such as:

Wallet transactions on block explorers

NFT collections across marketplaces

GitHub repositories

DAO governance participation

Hackathon projects

POAP badges from events

Because this data is scattered, understanding someone’s Web3 identity requires manually checking many different platforms like Etherscan, GitHub, Snapshot, and NFT marketplaces.

This creates several problems:

❌ Difficult for recruiters or collaborators to evaluate Web3 builders

❌ No unified way to showcase on-chain reputation

❌ Web3 contributors lack a simple portfolio or resume

❌ Identity in Web3 is tied to wallets, but wallets don't present meaningful context

As a result, Web3 still lacks a simple, unified identity layer similar to LinkedIn or a personal portfolio in Web2.

How ENS-folio Solves This

ENS-folio transforms ENS names into decentralized Web3 portfolios.

By simply entering an ENS name, the platform automatically aggregates important on-chain and developer data into a single unified profile page.

Each ENS profile can showcase:

🧾 Wallet address and on-chain activity

🖼 NFT collections

🎟 POAP badges from events and hackathons

🏛 DAO participation and governance activity

💻 Projects and developer contributions

🔗 Social links like GitHub and Twitter

This makes it easy for anyone to instantly understand a person’s Web3 reputation and work.

What People Can Use It For

ENS-folio makes several existing tasks much easier and more transparent:

🧑‍💻 For Developers

Create a Web3-native resume

Showcase hackathons, NFTs, and on-chain activity

Share a single ENS-based portfolio link

🏢 For Companies & DAOs

Quickly evaluate developers and contributors

Verify real on-chain reputation

Discover active Web3 builders

🌐 For the Web3 Community

Build credible decentralized identities

Make Web3 contributions more visible

Create shareable ENS-powered personal pages

Why This Matters

ENS-folio helps bridge the gap between wallet-based identity and real reputation in Web3.

Instead of scattered data across platforms, your ENS name becomes your unified Web3 identity and portfolio.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the main challenges we faced was resolving ENS names reliably and linking them to the correct wallet address. ENS resolution requires interacting with Ethereum mainnet, while our smart contract for profile storage was deployed on Base Sepolia. Managing data across multiple networks initially caused inconsistencies in fetching profile and wallet data.

To solve this, we separated the data flow: ENS names are resolved using an Ethereum mainnet RPC provider, while profile data is fetched from our smart contract deployed on Base Sepolia. This clear separation of network responsibilities ensured reliable ENS resolution while still allowing users to store and own their profile data on Base.

Another challenge was aggregating data from multiple APIs such as NFTs, POAP badges, and wallet activity. Each API returned data in different formats, so we had to normalize the responses before displaying them in the UI. By creating a small data processing layer in the frontend, we were able to standardize the data and present it in a clean portfolio interface.

### Pramaan
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/pramaan-9430) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Dev4057/Pramaan.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/aWksmXc-a2k) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-ETHMumbai%202026-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://ethmumbai2026.devfolio.co) ![Likes](https://img.shields.io/badge/Likes-1-FF6B6B?style=flat-square)

> Decentralised identity verification platform

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Gig Economy's "Invisible" Credit Problem
Millions of gig workers (freelancers, Uber drivers, delivery partners) are locked out of traditional financial systems. Because they lack standard corporate salary slips or established credit histories, lenders view them as "high risk."

To prove their creditworthiness today, workers are forced to hand over highly sensitive, raw bank statements and personal IDs. This leads to massive data privacy risks, identity theft vulnerabilities, and heavy human bias in loan approvals.

How Pramaan Solves This
Pramaan is a privacy-first Web3 credit passport. We transform gig workers' off-chain reputations into verifiable, on-chain credit scores without ever exposing their underlying personal data.

What people can use it for:

Gig Workers: Can mint a portable "Gig Score" by cryptographically proving their identity and their income history.

DeFi & TradFi Lenders: Can instantly verify a worker's creditworthiness and disburse loans without doing manual, biased background checks.

How it makes existing tasks easier, safer, and completely trustless:

100% Privacy-Preserving (Zero-Knowledge): Workers prove their identity (via Anon Aadhaar) and income (via Reclaim Protocol) without revealing their actual Aadhaar number, name, or raw bank transaction history.

Eradicating Human Bias: Credit analysis is performed by a Local Autonomous AI Agent (OpenClaw + Llama 3). The AI audits the ZK-proofs deterministically, ensuring loan recommendations are based purely on math and on-chain facts.

Machine-to-Machine API Economy (x402): Lenders don't need expensive monthly Web2 SaaS subscriptions to access credit bureaus. Using the x402 Micropayment Protocol, the Lender's application autonomously pays a 0.05 USDC micro-fee per request. The protocol instantly settles the payment on Base Sepolia and unlocks the AI credit analysis in real-time.

Decentralized Data Portability: Heavy metadata and detailed proof contexts are packed into user-owned dDocs and stored on Fileverse, rather than bloating the EVM, giving workers total sovereign control over their credit data.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building Pramaan was a massive architectural challenge because it required stitching together several cutting-edge Web3 protocols into a single, seamless user experience.
1. Taming Zero-Knowledge Proofs & Gas Limits
Integrating both Anon Aadhaar (for identity) and Reclaim Protocol (for income verification) meant dealing with complex cryptographic payloads. One of our biggest hurdles was managing the sheer size of the ZK-proofs and ensuring they could be verified on-chain without the transactions failing. At one point, our proof submissions triggered a massive 21,000,000 gas limit error! We had to carefully debug our smart contract require statements, manage our nullifiers for replay protection, and refine our gas estimations to get the transactions to flow smoothly on Sepolia.

2. The Multi-Protocol Integration Puzzle
We weren't just building a simple dApp; we were building a multi-layered pipeline. We had to get Fileverse to instantly store our proof metadata as encrypted dDocs, while Base Sepolia handled the core smart contract logic. The absolute biggest roadblock hit when we tried to integrate the OpenClaw AI Agent—the official NPM registry for the core packages was throwing 404 errors. Instead of giving up, we reverse-engineered the x402 protocol and built our own autonomous payment interceptor from scratch using viem, Node.js, and a local Ollama LLM.

3. The Power of the Hacker Community
When you are trying to make disparate Web3 technologies talk to each other at 4:00 AM, documentation only gets you so far. These critical blockers were overcome thanks to the incredible, hands-on support from the sponsor engineers, mentors, and the collaborative energy of the ETH Mumbai community. Whether it was identifying a misconfigured RPC node or figuring out the proper data formatting for a specific protocol, the guidance we received was the exact push we needed to cross the finish line with a fully functional product.

**Privacy**

Pramaan: The Privacy-First ZK Credit Passport for the Gig Economy
The Vision
Millions of gig workers (Uber drivers, freelancers, delivery partners) are systematically locked out of the DeFi and TradFi lending markets. Because they lack corporate salary slips, they are forced to hand over highly sensitive, raw bank statements and government IDs to prove their creditworthiness—exposing them to massive data harvesting, privacy breaches, and human bias.

Pramaan is built to solve this. We are a 100% privacy-preserving Web3 credit protocol that transforms off-chain gig reputation into an immutable, on-chain "GigScore."

Why Pramaan is the Ultimate Privacy Architecture:
We built a completely trustless, multi-layered privacy stack native to the Ethereum ecosystem:

Zero-Knowledge Identity (Anon Aadhaar): Workers prove they are citizens over 18 without ever revealing their actual Aadhaar number, name, or biometric data to the smart contract or the lender.

Zero-Knowledge Income (Reclaim Protocol): Workers generate cryptographic proofs of their gig earnings (e.g., from Uber or SBI) directly from the Web2 source. The smart contract verifies the ZK-proof, completely abstracting away the raw transaction history.

Decentralized Data Sovereignty (Fileverse): Instead of bloating the EVM with metadata or using centralized AWS databases, the heavy proof contexts are encrypted and packed into user-owned dDocs on Fileverse, giving the worker total sovereign control over who views their data.

Local AI Auditing (OpenClaw + Llama 3): To completely eliminate human bias and third-party data leakage, the credit risk analysis is performed by a local Autonomous AI Agent. Zero worker data is ever sent to cloud providers like OpenAI. * Machine-to-Machine API Economy (x402): To access the AI's credit insights, the Lender's application must autonomously execute a micro-payment (0.05 USDC) on Base Sepolia using the x402 protocol. The agent detects the EVM transaction, runs the local LLM analysis on the ZK proofs, and mints the final GigScore on-chain.

The ETH Mumbai Impact
Pramaan represents the true ethos of Ethereum: giving power and privacy back to the user. By combining Zero-Knowledge cryptography, decentralized storage, autonomous machine-to-machine micropayments, and local AI, we have created a completely private financial primitive.

Gig workers finally have a portable, bias-free Web3 credit score, and lenders can deploy capital safely—all without a single piece of raw Personal Identifiable Information (PII) ever touching a public server.

**Build What Big Tech Won't**

How Pramaan Integrates Fileverse for Sovereign Data Portability
Storing rich metadata and heavy Zero-Knowledge proof payloads directly on the EVM is prohibitively expensive and rigid. To solve this, Pramaan utilizes Fileverse as our decentralized, user-owned data availability layer, perfectly executing a "Compute on-chain, Store on Fileverse" architecture.

1. Dynamic dDoc Generation for ZK-Proofs
Whenever a gig worker completes a verification step—whether it's proving their identity via Anon Aadhaar or their income via the Reclaim Protocol—the raw cryptographic proof payloads, metadata, and timestamps are packaged into a JSON object. Our backend seamlessly pushes this object to a Fileverse node, which encrypts and stores the data, returning a unique dDoc ID.

2. The Smart Contract Anchor
Instead of bloating our Base Sepolia smart contract, we only mint the final computed "GigScore" and the lightweight Fileverse dDoc ID on-chain. The blockchain acts as the immutable anchor of truth, while Fileverse acts as the rich, decentralized "Pramaan Passport" that actually holds the worker's data context.

3. Seamless Data Portability & UX
We integrated Fileverse directly into the frontend user experience. Once a worker's Passport is generated, the UI dynamically fetches their specific dDoc IDs. We built sleek "View Identity dDoc" and "View Income dDoc" buttons that bridge users directly to the Fileverse document viewer.

4. Why this matters for the Gig Economy
By using Fileverse, we give workers true data sovereignty. Their sensitive verification proofs aren't sitting in a centralized AWS database; they are stored as user-owned dDocs. The worker can selectively share their specific Fileverse document links with decentralized lenders, proving their creditworthiness without exposing their raw, underlying personal data to the public.

How Pramaan Leverages Base for On-Chain Privacy
Traditional credit systems force gig workers to hand over sensitive, raw data (government IDs, bank statements) to centralized entities. Pramaan flips this model by combining Zero-Knowledge (ZK) cryptography with the Base network to act as our secure, privacy-preserving settlement layer.

1. Zero-Knowledge State Management on Base
Instead of storing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) on a public ledger, Pramaan uses Anon Aadhaar and Reclaim Protocol to generate ZK-proofs for identity and income. The smart contract we deployed on Base never receives raw data. It only receives cryptographic commitments and the final computed "GigScore". Anyone inspecting the Base block explorer will only see hashes and a numerical score, ensuring 100% data privacy for the worker while providing verifiable trust to lenders.

2. Privacy-First AI Micropayments (x402 Protocol)
To analyze this ZK-data without leaking it to centralized cloud AI providers, we built a local, autonomous AI agent. We specifically chose Base to handle the agent's x402 machine-to-machine micropayments (0.05 USDC per risk analysis request). Base's sub-cent gas fees and lightning-fast block times make this micro-transaction economy actually viable. The agent autonomously pays the fee on Base Sepolia, which unlocks a local Llama 3 LLM to generate credit insights completely privately on the host machine.

3. The Ultimate Web3 Credit Passport
By using Base as our immutable truth layer, we achieved a perfect privacy architecture:

Compute: Kept local and private (Ollama).

Identity: Kept anonymous (ZK-Proofs).

Settlement & Scoring: Immutable, fast, and cheap (Base).

Base enabled us to build a high-frequency, machine-to-machine lending protocol where gig workers have total sovereign control over their financial privacy.

**Best Use of Elsa x402 and Elsa OpenClaw skills**

It is 9:17 AM—you are right at the finish line! Here is the exact, hard-hitting description you need to paste into the HeyElsa partner track section on Devfolio.

How Pramaan Integrates HeyElsa & OpenClaw
Pramaan fully embodies the HeyElsa vision of a decentralized, machine-to-machine AI economy. We utilized the OpenClaw architecture to build an autonomous, privacy-first "Credit Auditor Agent" that evaluates a gig worker's Zero-Knowledge proofs without human bias.

1. Engineering the x402 Protocol from Scratch
During the hackathon, we encountered registry 404 errors with the official @openclaw/core NPM packages. Instead of pivoting, we reverse-engineered the OpenClaw specification and built a custom autonomous agent runtime using Node.js and Viem. When our backend requests a credit analysis, the API throws a strict HTTP 402 Payment Required error.

2. Autonomous Machine Micropayments
Our backend agent does not crash when it hits this paywall. It reads the custom headers, accesses its own machine wallet, and autonomously signs a smart contract transaction—paying a 0.05 USDC micro-fee on Base Sepolia. 3. Privacy-Preserving Local AI Intelligence
Once the x402 payment is verified, the agent doesn't send sensitive worker data to OpenAI. Instead, it triggers a local Llama 3 model (via Ollama). The LLM deterministically audits the verified ZK-proofs (Anon Aadhaar identity & Reclaim income) and generates a professional, tamper-proof GigScore and risk insight.

By building this, we successfully demonstrated an end-to-end HeyElsa use case: An autonomous AI agent that possesses its own wallet, encounters a paywall, and spends crypto to unlock the compute power it needs to help a human user.

**The problem it solves**

Crypto investors lack a secure way to automate investment strategies without giving up custody of their funds; we are tyring to  solve that via autostack; AutoStack lets you set up recurring token purchases without depositing funds into a vault or trusting a centralized service. You grant a time-bounded, amount-limited permission to a smart contract, and it executes swaps on your behalf at the frequency you specify.

The key difference from existing DCA solutions: your tokens never leave your wallet until the moment of each swap. No lockups, no custody risk.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Implementing Advanced Wallet Permissions 

Integrating ERC-7715 through the MetaMask Smart Accounts Kit was challenging because the ecosystem is still new.

Issues included:

Limited documentation

Handling session accounts securely

Ensuring permission limits (amount + duration) were enforced correctly

Managing permission expiry

This required careful testing to prevent accidental over-permissioning.

2. Designing a Non-Custodial Automation Model 

Most DCA protocols simply hold funds in a vault.
Building automation while keeping funds in the user’s wallet required a different architecture.

Key difficulties:

Triggering swaps without traditional custody

Managing periodic permissions

Ensuring swaps only execute within allowed limits

3. Integrating Smart Money Signals 

Pulling whale trading signals from Nansen added complexity.

Challenges included:

Designing a reliable trigger system

Filtering meaningful whale activity

Preventing spam signals

Balancing signal thresholds vs execution speed

4. HTTP Micropayments Integration 

Using the x402 Protocol required implementing a new payment flow.

Problems encountered:

Handling HTTP 402 payment responses

Processing small USDC micropayments on Solana

Avoiding repeated payments with caching

5. Real-Time Indexing for the Dashboard 

Keeping the frontend synced with blockchain activity required building a real-time indexer using Envio HyperIndex.

Challenges:

Designing efficient event indexing

Updating strategy execution data instantly

Avoiding slow polling-based updates

6. Managing Cross-Chain Components 

The system interacts with multiple ecosystems:

Smart contracts on Base

Whale data via Nansen

Micropayments on Solana

Coordinating these components introduced latency and reliability challenges.

**Software**

HepatoGuard is a software-based health project because it solves a real problem of spotting early liver cancer risk by using data processing and gene mapping. HepatoGuard takes data from biopsies looks at the important molecular details and creates a molecular progression score with a clear report. It blends programming, bioinformatics data analysis and an easy interface to turn genetic data into useful research results. As members, in our first hackathon we want to show our tech skills, creativity, teamwork and eagerness to learn by building a working prototype that can help future health research and clinical decisions.

**Best Beginner**

We started with the frontend and user experience, then began exploring real liver datasets and building the backend pipeline step by step. Along the way, we’ve had to learn about gene-expression data, dataset challenges, machine learning, explainability, and responsible medical AI.

**Software**

NoticeIQ solves a genuine, universal student problem: information overload from disorganized channels leading to missed deadlines. Our solution combines two complete, working systems: a secure Digital Campus ID with QR-based verification, and an AI pipeline (dual-provider: Groq for text, Gemini for images/PDFs) that converts messy notices into structured tasks with automatically scheduled, multi-stage reminders delivered via real push notifications — confirmed working even with the app fully closed. The entire system is built on production-grade security (Row Level Security on every database table) and deployed as an installable PWA.

**Best Beginner**

This was our first time building a full production-style pipeline: AI extraction, real-time database security (Row Level Security), and — the hardest part — genuine OS-level push notifications that work even when the app is closed, which most beginner (and even experienced) teams don't attempt. We hit real, unglamorous bugs along the way — a silent authentication failure, a date-parsing edge case, a task-deletion bug — and learned to properly diagnose root causes with real evidence (database queries, raw API responses) instead of guessing. We also learned when NOT to build something: we deliberately avoided native mobile app development and a WhatsApp integration once we recognized the live-demo risk outweighed the benefit, choosing a PWA instead.

**Best Girl Team**

Our team built NoticeIQ end-to-end — from architecture decisions to live debugging under time pressure. We made real engineering trade-offs together: pivoting from our original FastAPI + OCR plan to a leaner single-stack architecture once we realized it would be more reliable, and systematically diagnosing genuinely hard bugs (like OneSignal's authentication header format, and a subtle date-parsing bug) rather than giving up or working around them. We divided work across backend, frontend, and pitch/testing roles, and iterated together based on real mentor and judge feedback — reprioritizing our lead feature (Campus ID) mid-hackathon based on direct guidance we received and acted on quickly.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**Hardware**

Our project strongly fits the Hardware Track because the system uses a combination of physical sensors to collect real-world environmental data and feed it into our security and monitoring pipeline. We have integrated **MQ-3, MQ-5, MQ-9, MQ-135, DHT22, and HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensors** to detect parameters such as gas concentration, air quality, temperature, humidity, and distance. These sensors provide continuously changing physical-world inputs, which can be processed as additional entropy and contextual parameters for our encryption model. By combining sensor-generated data with timestamp signatures, hashing, quantization, and human-generated randomness, our system creates a hardware-assisted security architecture rather than relying purely on software. This makes the project applicable to **IoT devices, industrial monitoring, smart systems, and secure edge devices**, where both real-time sensing and secure data transmission are essential.

**Software**

**OpsGenome** fits the **Open Source Software (OSS) Track** because it democratizes advanced SRE and self-healing infrastructure without vendor lock-in, proprietary cloud dependencies, or data privacy compromises:

1. **100% Local-First & Air-Gapped (Zero Vendor Lock-in):** Unlike closed SaaS observability platforms (like Datadog or proprietary AI tools), OpsGenome requires **zero external API keys or cloud subscriptions**. It runs completely on local developer machines using an offline SQLite memory engine (`global.db`), POSIX Unix domain sockets, and local heuristics or air-gapped Ollama models.
2. **Modular & Extensible Plugin Architecture:** It features an open, pluggable parser and specialist registry. Any open-source developer can easily add new technology stacks (e.g. Go, Rust, Helm, Pulumi) by simply inheriting from standard base classes (`BaseSpecialistAgent`, `BaseErrorParser`).
3. **Open Standards & Non-Proprietary Tooling:** It leverages universal open-source standards—transparent Zsh/Bash hooks, standard Unified Diff patches, the official Kubernetes API client, and Kahn’s Algorithm DAGs—rather than black-box proprietary automation.
4. **Community Democratization of Operational Knowledge:** It transforms individual terminal troubleshooting into transparent, reusable, and verifiable open runbooks, enabling open-source teams and solo developers to achieve enterprise-grade incident recovery and prevent recurring outages for free.

**Software**

# Track Submission: Open Innovation / Open Track

### Project Title
**SentinelX — Autonomous Local-First DevSecOps with Dual-Agent Self-Healing Architecture**

---

### Track Fit & Overview
In the **Open Track**, innovation is judged by tackling systemic industry bottlenecks with novel engineering, unconstrained by narrow problem statements. SentinelX re-engineers modern application security by eliminating the trade-off between **privacy, operational cost, and autonomous remediation**. 

Most modern security platforms (like GitHub Copilot Autofix, Snyk, or Veracode) treat code analysis as a cloud-dependent service. This forces companies with proprietary codebases, healthcare data, or defense contracts to leak IP to third-party APIs while paying steep SaaS premiums. Furthermore, existing tools remain passive: they produce raw alerts, inundating developers with false positives, while leaving the remediation burden entirely manual.

SentinelX introduces an entirely autonomous, closed-loop DevSecOps system running **100% locally on commodity consumer hardware**. By pairing a static analysis-driven **AI Red Team** (for discovery and noise filtering) with a verified **AI Blue Team** (for syntax-validated in-place self-healing and Pull Request automation), SentinelX transforms security from a reactive bottleneck into an invisible, self-contained development partner.

---

### Core Innovation & Uniqueness
1. **Zero-Data-Exfiltration DevSecOps:**
   SentinelX executes both discovery and remediation fully air-gapped using local small language models (`qwen2.5-coder:7b` via Ollama) and local CLI static scanners. No line of source code, secret key, or repository metadata ever touches an external server.

2. **Dual-Agent Closed Loop (Red vs. Blue):**
   * **The Red Team:** Gathers scanner signals (Semgrep, Gitleaks, Trivy) and uses contextual AI reasoning to drop false positives (e.g., test tokens or mock database strings). It models modern attack surfaces (SQLi, Command Injection, Insecure Deserialization, XSS, and simulated IDOR/CSRF) into persistent telemetry streams.
   * **The Blue Team:** Takes verified exploits, writes contextual patches, validates structural syntax using local language runtimes (`ast.parse` and `node --check`), writes a safe `.bak` disk backup, and autonomously pushes a branch and GitHub Pull Request with AI-generated developer notes.

3. **Deterministic Safety Architecture:**
   AI agents should never write broken code into production. SentinelX implements a multi-tier fallback mechanism:
   * **Parser Verification:** Hallucinated syntax is blocked at the AST level before writing to disk.
   * **Rule-Based Fail-Safes:** If local hardware encounters memory limits or Ollama timeouts, deterministic rule-based engines (`RULE_BASED_FALLBACK_ENGAGED`) guarantee successful patch delivery.
   * **CLI Portability:** Missing host binaries seamlessly hand off to heuristic regex engines (`HEURISTIC_FALLBACK_ENGAGED`).

---

### Technical Architecture
* **AI & Remediation Engine:** FastAPI (Python 3.11+), Ollama (`qwen2.5-coder:7b`), AST compiler tools, and Server-Sent Events (SSE) telemetry pipelines.
* **Scanning & Detection:** Semgrep rulesets, Gitleaks entropy scanners, Trivy vulnerability databases, and internal heuristic regex fallback engines.
* **Authentication & Integrations:** Node.js / Express microservice handling granular GitHub OAuth token workflows and Octokit PR creation.
* **Frontend & Operations Console:** Next.js / React interactive dashboard visualizing live Red Team attack telemetry, vulnerability triage graphs, real-time code diffing, and automated PR deployment statuses.

---

### Impact & Scalability
* **Cost Disruption:** Zero recurring API token costs. Startups and enterprise teams can run continuous security audits on standard developer laptops or self-hosted CI/CD runners at zero marginal cost.
* **Velocity Multiplier:** Reduces vulnerability triage and patching cycle time from an industry average of **15–20 days to under 30 seconds**.
* **Ecosystem Agnostic:** Expandable across languages (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go, Rust) by simply registering language-specific syntax validation checkers into the Blue Team pipeline.

---

### Future Roadmap
* **CI/CD Action Runner:** Package SentinelX as a self-hosted GitHub Action / GitLab Runner container for air-gapped enterprise pipelines.
* **Multi-File Context Graphing:** Extend the Blue Team's AST analyzer to resolve cross-file import dependencies when patching distributed vulnerabilities.
* **Dynamic Ephemeral Sandboxing:** Spin up isolated Docker containers to dynamically verify exploit payloads before and after Blue Team patch application.

**Software**

HackProof addresses a critical problem in hackathons: how do judges know that a submitted project was actually built by the team during the event? Instead of relying solely on the final repository, HackProof creates an evidence-backed provenance trail by analyzing GPG/SSH commit identities, Git tracking and concealment signals, commit timestamps and chronology, and GitHub activity through webhooks and repository data. These independent signals are correlated into a single integrity report, helping judges identify inconsistencies such as unsigned or unregistered commits, suspicious timestamp patterns, hidden tracking states, or activity that doesn't align with the claimed development timeline.

HackProof doesn't ask judges to blindly trust the code- it gives them evidence to make that judgment.

Here is the exact, high-conviction breakdown of why **ThermalGuard** is the ideal candidate and winning fit for the **Open Track (Open Innovation Track)**:

---

# 🏆 Why the Open Track Best Fits ThermalGuard

The **Open Track** is designed for projects that **defy narrow categories** and tackle massive, open-ended global challenges using creative cross-disciplinary engineering. 

ThermalGuard is the quintessential Open Track project for four distinct reasons:

---

### 1. It Fuses Four Major Tech Domains Into One Unified System
Most track-specific projects stay inside a comfortable silo (e.g., only Web3, only FinTech, or a simple chatbot). ThermalGuard breaks these boundaries by uniting:
* **SpaceTech / Remote Sensing:** Direct orbital ingestion from NASA FIRMS satellites (MODIS & VIIRS).
* **Applied Machine Learning:** Python-based XGBoost pipeline estimating Fire Radiative Power (FRP) and spread probability.
* **Geospatial & Spatial Mathematics:** DBSCAN clustering to aggregate scattered thermal pixels into unified fire perimeters, plus Haversine 25km emergency proximity calculations.
* **Civic Tech & Disaster Management:** Actionable ground-level dispatch targeting Fire (`101`), Police (`112`), and Trauma Hospitals (`108`).

Because it spans Aerospace, AI, Climate Tech, and Public Safety, no single restrictive track can capture its full scope—**it belongs in the Open Track**.

---

### 2. It Rejects "AI Wrapper" Tropes in Favor of Real Systems Engineering
In many open hackathon tracks, judges are overwhelmed by dozens of superficial ChatGPT wrappers with static UIs. 
ThermalGuard stands apart as **deep, practical systems engineering**:
* **Real Automated Testing:** 11/11 automated unit and integration test suites verifying data contracts, API coalescing, and ML model constraints.
* **Production Database Persistence:** Full local SQLite engine running in high-concurrency `WAL` mode to maintain audit trails and watch areas.
* **Optimized DevOps:** Solved Linux C-extension compilation bottlenecks on Render with automated binary wheel deployment.

---

### 3. The "Zero-Hallucination" Standard in Critical Systems
Open innovation awards solutions that are **safe and viable for real-world deployment**.
* In disaster response, hallucinated or simulated data can lead to tragic false dispatches.
* ThermalGuard incorporates strict **data provenance**: if satellite telemetry drops, it never invents synthetic coordinates; it serves authenticated, timestamped cached snapshots with explicit operator alerts.
* This level of operational maturity is rare in hackathon prototypes and immediately resonates with Open Track judges.

---

### 4. Unmatched Humanitarian & Planetary Impact
The Open Track often rewards projects with the **highest ceiling of real-world impact**:
* **Climate Crisis:** Wildfires and agricultural stubble burns emit gigatons of carbon, decimate ecosystems, and trigger severe health and air pollution crises.
* **The Last-Mile Solution:** ThermalGuard does not just visualize the crisis—it provides the missing link between NASA orbiters and local emergency responders on the ground.

---

**Best Beginner**

# 🎯 1. Why Apply for the Beginner Track? (Accurate Reasons)

In hackathons, the **Beginner Track** is not just for trivial "hello world" apps; it is meant for **teams exploring new, complex engineering domains for the first time** and demonstrating an extraordinary learning curve.

Here are the precise, authentic reasons to state:

### A. First Time Building with Remote Sensing & Geospatial Tech
* **The Reality:** Our team had **zero prior background in satellite remote-sensing, GIS (Geographic Information Systems), or orbital data ingestion**.
* **What We Learned From Scratch:**
  * How to query and parse live orbital telemetry from **NASA FIRMS satellites (MODIS & VIIRS)**.
  * How to implement spatial clustering algorithms (**DBSCAN**) to mathematically aggregate scattered heat pixels into cohesive firefronts.
  * How to integrate interactive multi-basemap engines (**Google Maps JS API, OpenStreetMap, Three.js**).

### B. Overcoming Multi-Language & Multi-Tier Architecture Challenges
* Building a beginner project typically means a single-file script or a simple frontend template. Instead, our team stepped outside our comfort zone to connect:
  * **Frontend:** React 19 interactive geospatial dashboard.
  * **Backend & Persistence:** Node.js server with SQLite write-ahead logging (`WAL`) and automated caching.
  * **Machine Learning:** A separate Python pipeline running **XGBoost** for fire radiative power and spread risk estimation.
  * **DevOps & Cloud:** Solving real-world production deployment hurdles on **Render** (resolving Linux C-compilation bottlenecks with binary wheels) and **GitHub Pages**.

### C. Competitive Edge in the Beginner Track
* Beginner track judges look for **ambition, learning speed, and execution**.
* While most beginner projects are mock e-commerce sites or basic chatbot wrappers, **ThermalGuard is an end-to-end, working full-stack system with 11 automated test suites, zero-hallucination data integrity, and live cloud deployment**. This makes it an exceptionally strong contender for top honors in the beginner category.

---

# 🌍 2. Why ThermalGuard is an Impactful Project

Judges and evaluators care deeply about **real-world relevance**. Here is why ThermalGuard carries profound real-world impact:

### A. Solves the Critical "Last-Mile" Emergency Gap
* **The Problem:** Satellites detect fires 24/7, but the data sits in scientific portals that rural fire departments and local police cannot access or interpret.
* **The Impact:** ThermalGuard doesn't just show a dot—it calculates the **nearest Fire Stations (`101`)**, **Police (`112`)**, and **Hospitals (`108`) within 25 km** and auto-generates a one-click **Emergency Dispatch Dossier**. It bridges the gap between orbit and the ground.

### B. Climate & Environmental Protection
* **Wildfires & Stubble Burning:** Uncontrolled fires release gigatons of $CO_2$, destroy biodiversity, and cause catastrophic seasonal air pollution (especially across agricultural belts in North India and global forest regions).
* **Early Intervention:** Extinguishing a fire within the first 30–60 minutes requires a fraction of the water, personnel, and cost compared to fighting an out-of-control crown wildfire. ThermalGuard provides that early-warning window.

### C. Life-Safety Through "Zero-Hallucination" Design
* In emergency tech, bad data costs lives.
* Many modern AI projects blindly generate synthetic data when an API fails. ThermalGuard enforces strict **data provenance**: if NASA APIs experience downtime, it serves authenticated, timestamped cached snapshots with clear warnings, never fabricating false fire coordinates.

> **Why Beginner Track?**  
> *"Our team consists of first-time builders in geospatial engineering and satellite remote-sensing. Entering this hackathon, we had never worked with orbital telemetry or spatial clustering algorithms. Over the course of the event, we pushed through a steep learning curve—integrating NASA FIRMS satellite data, implementing DBSCAN clustering, building a Python XGBoost ML pipeline, and architecting an authenticated Node.js/SQLite backend with full test coverage and live cloud deployment."*
>
> **What is the Impact?**  
> *"ThermalGuard addresses the deadly latency between when a wildfire ignites and when emergency crews respond. By converting raw NASA satellite heat readings into clustered firefronts and instantly mapping the nearest emergency stations (Fire, Police, Trauma) within 25 km with ready-to-use dispatch dossiers, ThermalGuard slashes response times from hours to minutes—protecting lives, ecosystems, and rural communities."*

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Dart](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dart-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vanilla JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vanilla%20JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/React.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**Best Girl Team**

As a team of three women engineers, we deliberately chose to tackle one of India’s most notoriously male-dominated, overlooked, and unsafe sectors: the informal construction and daily-wage labour market.

Here is why our background and perspective make LabourLink uniquely aligned with this track:

1. Designing with Empathy for Vulnerable Female Daily-Wage Workers
The Hidden Reality of Women at Labour Chowks: Women comprise over 30% of India’s informal daily-wage workforce (helpers, brick-carriers, painters, cleaners, and agricultural laborers).
Safety & Harassment on Roadside Curbs: While male workers face physical hardship standing at chowks, women face severe safety hazards, catcalling, and exploitation while waiting on roadside curbs before dawn.
Wage Inequality: Women informal laborers are routinely paid 20% to 35% less than their male counterparts for the exact same hours of heavy manual labor.
Our Impact: By digitizing the chowk through an AI voice assistant accessible from home, female laborers no longer have to endure unsafe street corners or predatory middlemen. The transparent, published daily wage system ensures pay parity and dignity for women workers.
2. Reimagining "Laxmi": An Empathetic, Trust-First Voice Interface
Traditional software systems are built with text-heavy forms, bureaucratic jargon, and cold interfaces.
We intentionally engineered our Conversational Voice AI persona—Laxmi—to speak with patience, warmth, and high emotional resonance in regional languages (Hindi, Bengali, English).
For a marginalized or first-time smartphone user, speaking to a reassuring female voice dispatcher lowers intimidation, establishes trust, and provides an approachable entry point into the digital economy.
3. Women Engineers Tackling Deep Tech & Hardcore Systems
Often, women-led projects are pigeonholed into conventional lifestyle or health domains. We wanted to shatter that stereotype by tackling complex, low-latency deep-tech engineering:
Writing custom low-level in-memory PCM-to-WAV binary header synthesis in Dart to enable real-time streaming audio playback on Android devices.
Architecting a bidirectional bridge uniting modern WebSockets, telephony telecom carriers (Exotel/Twilio), and cloud databases (Supabase/PostgreSQL).
Building production-ready cross-platform experiences on Flutter and Node.js.

> An AI education platform

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square) ![Minimax](https://img.shields.io/badge/Minimax-333333?style=flat-square) ![Deepseek](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deepseek-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gonka Router](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gonka%20Router-333333?style=flat-square)

**Challenges we ran into**

One of our main challenges was connecting the **AI-generated quiz system, backend, and student-facing interface** so that questions could be generated, retrieved, and displayed correctly.

During testing, we encountered issues where changes made by different team members could affect the existing flow, making it important to carefully test the system after integrating each component. We also had to troubleshoot the connection between the deployed frontend and backend and verify that generated questions and student answers were being handled correctly.

We overcame these challenges by working with **separate Git branches**, testing each feature independently, and gradually integrating changes into the main project. We also tested the complete user flow from **lesson generation → quiz generation → student quiz → answer submission → misconception analysis** to ensure the different components worked together as intended.

**The problem it solves**

Teachers often know when students get a question wrong, but it can be difficult to identify **why** they are struggling and which concepts need reinforcement.

**InsightED** uses AI to generate lessons and quizzes based on the teacher’s subject, topic, student level, and language. It then analyses student responses to identify **common misconceptions and learning gaps**, allowing teachers to understand which concepts students are struggling with quickly.

Instead of relying only on quiz scores, InsightED turns student responses into actionable insights that help teachers decide **what to reteach and where intervention is needed most**. This makes the process of identifying learning gaps faster, more targeted, and more personalised for students.

**AI For Society**

InsightED applies AI to **education**, addressing a real-world problem faced by teachers and students: identifying **why students misunderstand concepts**.

Instead of using AI only to generate content, InsightED uses AI to analyse student responses and turn them into **actionable teaching insights**.

**How it contributes to society:**

*  **Supports teachers** by reducing the time needed to identify learning gaps.
*  **Helps students** receive more targeted support based on their actual misconceptions.
*  **Makes personalised learning more accessible** without requiring teachers to manually analyse every student's response.
*  **Improves teaching decisions** by showing class-level understanding instead of only overall quiz scores.

By using **Gonka Router** as the AI inference layer, InsightED demonstrates how AI infrastructure can be applied to a meaningful social need and help improve the quality and accessibility of education.

**The problem it solves**

Build a fact checker base on the LLM. It was different than other tradisional fact checker that just search for the keyword that the user input. And to solve the LLM's hallucination, we build a easy math model to decide the weight for each LLM than combine them to get a final score. And also a mechanism to solve a condition: when the group of LLM divergence to each other, a organizing for each LLM's output will be done to get the final result.

**Challenges we ran into**

The large challanges is the stability of the LLM provider's serve. We found that the request base on the api given very easy to be not responding (especially the kimi k2.6). It cause a large problem when we doing the testing (therefore we build a machanism to do the second requset when the first request for a specifal model is fail).

**AI For Society**

A AI checker based on the LLM model by a specific prompt to ensure to get the better output. It success use the LLM to solve the actual problem that the people usual meet on the social media.

### Puffer
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/test-edc9) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/lapsapthong-16/muba2026) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/txPgGrRqftk) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/txPgGrRqftk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co)

> A wallet that lets AI agents spend autonomously

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI agents can make valid on-chain transactions that are still unsafe.

For example, a trading agent may receive a convincing message to “claim a limited-time airdrop,” then send funds to an unfamiliar address. Nothing needs to hack the wallet or steal a private key—the agent simply misuses the authority it was given.

Puffer makes agent wallet automation safer without forcing a human to approve every routine action.

### What people can use it for

- Let an AI agent check balances and wallet status
- Retrieve live market data
- Dry-run transfers and trades before executing them
- Send SUI transfers
- Trade SUI/DBUSDC through DeepBook
- Review past wallet decisions and understand why an action was allowed, blocked, or escalated

### How it keeps those actions safe

Puffer gives agents a constrained MCP tool interface. They can request a transfer or swap, but they **cannot** submit arbitrary transaction code, change their own safety rules, add recipients, or approve a held transaction.

For each request, Puffer:

1. **Builds and simulates the real Sui transaction** before signing.
2. **Inspects predicted effects**—balance changes, recipients, invoked packages, object transfers, capability transfers, and failures.
3. **Applies hard guardrails** such as transaction limits, weekly spending caps, and recipient/package allowlists.
4. **Runs independent AI risk reviews** that can add caution, but can never bypass a safety rule.
5. **Routes risky actions to a human** for Ledger-backed approval.

### Why it matters

Puffer replaces the false choice between:

| Without Puffer | With Puffer |
| --- | --- |
| Give an agent unrestricted wallet access | Let the agent handle routine, policy-compliant actions |
| Approve every action manually | Escalate only unfamiliar, oversized, suspicious, or disputed actions |
| Trust an agent’s description of a transaction | Evaluate the simulated on-chain effects of the actual transaction |

The result is practical autonomy: agents can handle normal wallet tasks quickly, while the owner keeps hardware-backed control over actions that could put funds at risk.

> Currently built for MCP-compatible AI agents on **Sui testnet**.

**Challenges we ran into**

### Making AI risk checks reliable enough for wallet decisions

We use multiple AI models to review transaction risk, but inference was sometimes slow, timed out, or returned inconsistent responses. That was a problem because a wallet cannot safely treat an unavailable model as an approval.

We solved this by making AI reviews **fail closed**:

- Hard safety rules—such as spending caps, allowlists, and failed transaction simulations—always run independently of AI.
- Two separate low-risk model reviews are needed before an action can proceed automatically.
- If a review fails, times out, disagrees, or flags risk, the transaction is escalated to **Ledger-backed human approval**.

This means model instability reduces automation, not security.

### Enforcing human approval beyond a dashboard button

A major challenge was making sure a “human review required” decision could not be bypassed by the backend. If the server could still sign and submit the transaction on its own, the approval flow would only be a UI promise.

We addressed this using native Sui multisig wallets. Routine actions can use the spending wallet, while escalated actions are rebuilt from a protected wallet that requires both the platform signature and the owner’s Ledger signature. The human approval is therefore enforced directly by the wallet’s on-chain signing rule.

**AI × SUI**

Puffer is an **AI wallet agent safety layer built directly around Sui execution**.

Instead of merely showing blockchain data, Puffer lets MCP-compatible AI agents take real actions: inspect wallet balances, retrieve DeepBook market data, dry-run transfers and swaps, and execute approved transactions on **Sui testnet**.

Sui is integral to the product:

- **Programmable Transaction Blocks** are built server-side from typed agent intents, then simulated before signing.
- **Native Sui multisig** enforces Puffer’s two-level approval model:
  - a spending wallet for routine, policy-compliant actions;
  - a protected wallet for escalated actions that requires a human Ledger signature.
- **On-chain simulation** lets Puffer assess the predicted effects of the *actual transaction*—including balance changes, recipients, invoked packages, and object/capability transfers.
- **DeepBook v3** provides live SUI/DBUSDC market data and swap execution.
- **Sponsored transactions** remove gas-management friction for the agent-wallet workflow.

Puffer addresses a real problem in agentic finance: AI agents need enough authority to be useful, but not so much that one manipulated or mistaken request can move funds unchecked. It makes Sui-based wallet automation practical by allowing routine actions to proceed while routing unfamiliar, oversized, suspicious, or disputed transactions to hardware-backed human approval.

**AI For Society**

Puffer is an AI safety tool for a growing public-interest problem: **how people can safely delegate financial actions to AI agents**.

As agents become able to pay, trade, and execute on-chain actions, users face an unsafe trade-off: either give the agent unrestricted wallet control, or manually approve every transaction and lose the benefits of automation. Puffer creates a safer middle ground.

For every requested transfer or swap, Puffer uses the **Gonka Router** to obtain independent AI risk reviews from multiple model providers. The models assess evidence from the simulated transaction, such as the destination, amount, invoked packages, and asset/object movements.

The AI review system is designed to be cautious and explainable:

- **Two independent low-risk reviews** are required for automatic execution.
- A model timeout, failure, disagreement, or risk flag causes the action to escalate to human review.
- AI can **add caution**, but it can never bypass deterministic protections such as spending caps, allowlists, or failed simulations.
- Puffer records the decision, the agent’s reason, and the rule/evidence behind the outcome for later inspection.

This makes Gonka-powered AI verification useful in a high-stakes setting: not as an opaque “trust the model” decision-maker, but as a multi-model safety layer that helps prevent AI agents from misusing delegated financial authority.

### CTRL_CV
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/ctrlcv-f0db) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/MEISHI13/CTRL_CV) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-MUBA%20Blockchain%20Hackathon-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://muba-hackathon.devfolio.co)

> Turn Trash To Cash

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

SmartWaste: Transforming Waste Management Through Digital Innovation

A Comprehensive Digital Recycling Ecosystem

SmartWaste is a digital platform designed to make recycling more convenient, rewarding, and accessible. It connects users with verified recycling centers through an integrated mapping system while allowing them to track their recycling history, monitor environmental impact, and earn money from recyclable materials.

A key innovation is the Group Pickup feature, which allows users heading to the same recycling center to coordinate and share transportation. This reduces individual transportation costs while minimizing unnecessary trips and associated carbon emissions. By turning recycling into a collaborative activity, SmartWaste makes sustainable waste management more affordable and accessible to communities.

SmartWaste also uses a points-based reward system to encourage consistent recycling habits. Users earn points through recycling activities and can redeem them for rewards from participating brands such as GrabFood, McDonald's, KFC, Tealive, and Starbucks.

Operational Efficiency and Economic Value

SmartWaste provides real-time pricing information for recyclable materials such as aluminum, copper, and electronic waste, helping users understand the potential value of their materials and make informed recycling decisions.

Users can track their earnings, recycling history, and estimated carbon savings through a centralized dashboard. The Group Pickup system also automatically calculates how transportation costs are shared between participants, providing transparency over individual costs and savings.

Safety, Security, and Community Trust

SmartWaste prioritizes user security through secure authentication, password hashing, session management, and transaction records. Notifications provide users with updates on important activities such as completed transactions and payment confirmations.

The platform also promotes community engagement through leaderboards and achievement systems, encouraging positive competition and recognizing users for their environmental contributions.

Creating Measurable Impact

SmartWaste brings recycling-center discovery, shared transportation, material pricing, digital payments, rewards, and environmental tracking together in one platform. By combining convenience with financial and social incentives, SmartWaste transforms recycling from an inconvenient task into a rewarding community experience.

Ultimately, SmartWaste aims to turn waste into value while encouraging sustainable habits and supporting a more efficient circular economy.

**Challenges we ran into**

Development Challenges & Solutions

Map Rendering and Location Services

The Problem

One of the main challenges I encountered was getting the interactive map to render reliably. SmartWaste uses Leaflet.js with OpenStreetMap to display recycling centers and user locations, but the map would sometimes appear as a grey box, with tiles failing to load or markers appearing in incorrect positions.

The main cause was that the map was initialized while its container was hidden inside a page tab. Since the container had no dimensions at the time, Leaflet could not correctly calculate the map's size and positioning. This caused rendering issues when users later opened the Locator page.

The Solution

I solved this using a lazy initialization and forced recalculation approach. Instead of initializing the map immediately, it is created when the Locator tab is first opened, ensuring that the container has proper dimensions. I also trigger a map resize whenever users return to the Locator tab to prevent rendering issues when switching between pages.

I implemented a fallback location system as well. If users deny location permissions or location services are unavailable, the map still loads using default coordinates and displays the available recycling centers instead of failing completely.

The Geolocation Challenge

Another challenge was providing users with clear feedback while their location was being obtained. Geolocation can take several seconds because the browser must request permission and acquire the user's coordinates.

To improve the experience, I implemented status indicators that show different stages such as "Waiting," "Requesting," "Success," and "Error." Once the location is obtained, the user's coordinates and location marker are displayed on the map. This makes the process more transparent and prevents users from assuming the application is unresponsive.

### The Distance Calculation Challenge

I also needed an accurate way to calculate the distance between users and recycling centers. I implemented the haversine formula to calculate distances based on latitude and longitude coordinates.

For usability, distances below one kilometer are displayed in meters, while longer distances are displayed in kilometers. I also implemented dynamic sorting so that recycling centers are automatically arranged from nearest to farthest based on the user's current location.

This required recalculating distances whenever the user's location changed and updating the displayed results without refreshing the page. As a result, users can immediately see the most convenient recycling options based on their location.
