### NexusGuard-AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/nexusguardai-95d6) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Krishna-cell-12/NexusGuard-AI) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/wdyyoF6vgGs) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> Scan. Patch. Reward. Repeat.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygonscan](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygonscan-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Catch Vulnerabilities Before They Catch You.

Open-source powers the modern internet, but it has a critical, unsolved security crisis.

The Broken Reality of AppSec Today

Late Discovery: Zero-days, supply-chain attacks, and memory corruption bugs are found after deployment, when millions of users are already exposed.

Manual Overhead: When a bug is reported, maintainers spend hours reproducing the exploit just to understand it before they can even think about fixing it.

Talent Bottleneck: Open-source maintainers are brilliant developers, but they rarely have dedicated security engineers to interpret complex CVEs and threat reports.

Broken Incentives: Traditional bug bounty programs are agonizingly slow. Researchers submit a report, wait weeks for manual review, and wait even longer to get paid—if they get paid at all.

The result? Critical vulnerabilities sit unpatched for months, silently exposing millions of users worldwide.

What NexusGuard AI Does

NexusGuard AI is a GitHub-native autonomous security engineer that transforms the entire vulnerability lifecycle from a manual, reactive chore into a fully automated workflow. It executes a complete 4-step lifecycle the moment code is pushed:

Detect: Static analysis (Semgrep), secret scanning (TruffleHog), and Docker sandbox dynamic analysis run in parallel on every push or PR.

Explain: AI generates a Proof of Concept—not just a warning, but actual proof of the exploit path and its impact.

Fix: AI writes a secure patch, updates test cases, and automatically opens a Pull Request. The maintainer just hits "Merge."

Reward: A Polygon smart contract instantly releases the bounty to the researcher the moment the patch is approved. No middleman, no delays.

Who It Helps

Open-source maintainers: Get security coverage without needing a dedicated security team.

Security researchers: Submit findings and get paid instantly and transparently via blockchain.

Developers: Ship code confidently knowing every push is scanned and protected in real time.

Organizations: Reduce mean-time-to-remediation from months to minutes.

NexusGuard AI doesn't just find bugs. It fixes them automatically and rewards the community instantly—turning a process that takes months into an automated workflow that takes minutes.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/590406a02eff4513b1aef3340e73fe7e/40bfbed7-bd62-4f37-8df2-1d1da2fe38dc.jpeg)

**Challenges we ran into**

Building NexusGuard AI was as much a systems engineering challenge as it was a security one. Here are the real hurdles we hit:

Orchestrating a Multi-Service Pipeline Without Race Conditions
The hardest architectural challenge was making the scan to AI patch to blockchain bounty pipeline run reliably in sequence. Each service (Node.js backend, Python AI microservice, Solidity smart contract) runs independently, and getting them to hand off state correctly, especially under failure conditions, required building a robust orchestrator with explicit pipeline states (SCANNING to PATCH_RECEIVED to BOUNTY_RELEASED to COMPLETED) and WebSocket broadcasting at every transition.
How we solved it: We designed our orchestrator with a strict state machine pattern and an in-memory run store so every pipeline step is tracked, recoverable, and visible to the frontend in real time.

Docker Sandbox Isolation for Dynamic Analysis
Running untrusted code inside a sandbox without any network access, while still capturing meaningful runtime behavior, was extremely tricky. Too permissive and it becomes a security risk; too restrictive and the analysis produces nothing useful.
How we solved it: We configured Docker containers with no network access and strict resource limits, then analyzed standard output and error output patterns to extract behavioral signals without ever letting the sandbox touch the network.

HMAC Webhook Signature Verification Timing
GitHub's signature verification needs the raw request body, but our Express middleware parsed the body before we could verify it, causing signature mismatches. This silently rejected all real webhook events during early testing.
How we solved it: We used a raw parser specifically on the webhook route to capture the unparsed buffer, then performed HMAC-SHA256 verification before any JSON parsing happened.

Smart Contract Timing with Off-Chain Events
Triggering a Polygon smart contract bounty release based on an off-chain event (PR merge) introduced a classic blockchain oracle problem: how do you trustlessly connect a GitHub event to an on-chain transaction?
How we solved it: We implemented a signed webhook flow where GitHub Actions generates a cryptographically signed payload that the backend verifies before calling the Web3 microservice, creating a trust bridge between off-chain events and on-chain execution.

WSL2 and Windows PATH Conflicts
During development on Windows with WSL2, the system kept resolving to the Windows-native package manager instead of the Linux version, causing path errors that broke the entire install process.
How we solved it: We documented the exact direct invocation path and added it to the setup guide so the team could onboard without losing hours to environment debugging.

**Gemini**

NexusGuard AI utilizes Google's Gemini as the core reasoning engine for its autonomous DevSecOps pipeline. We leveraged Gemini's advanced code comprehension and logical reasoning capabilities to transition from simple vulnerability detection to automated, secure remediation.

Here is exactly how Gemini powers the architecture:

Contextual Exploit Analysis: When our scanners (Semgrep, TruffleHog) flag a vulnerability, the raw, complex error logs are sent to the Gemini API. Gemini interprets these structural threats to generate a clear, human-readable Proof of Concept (PoC) explaining the exact exploit path and impact.

Intelligent Patch Generation: We feed the entire vulnerable file to Gemini. Because of its large context window and deep coding knowledge, Gemini doesn't just suggest a generic fix; it writes the complete, secure code patch while preserving the original architectural logic of the open-source repository.

Strict Structured Output for CI/CD: To make the pipeline fully autonomous, we utilize Gemini's structured JSON output generation. The model returns the exact file paths, line numbers, and code diffs in a strict JSON schema. This allows our Node.js backend orchestrator to parse the response programmatically and automatically push a GitHub Pull Request without human intervention.

By deeply integrating Gemini, we transformed NexusGuard AI from a traditional security scanner into an autonomous AppSec engineer.

**CyberSecurity**

NexusGuard AI tackles the most critical bottleneck in modern Application Security (AppSec): the massive delay between discovering a vulnerability and actually deploying a secure patch.

Here is exactly how our architecture fits the CyberSecurity track:

Proactive Threat Detection (SAST & Secret Scanning): We integrated enterprise-grade security tools—Semgrep for structural static analysis and TruffleHog for hardcoded credential detection—directly into the CI/CD pipeline to catch vulnerabilities the moment code is pushed.

Zero-Trust Dynamic Analysis: To analyze runtime behavior without risking host compromise, we engineered network-isolated Docker sandboxes with strict resource limits, allowing us to safely evaluate untrusted, potentially malicious code.

Automated Remediation & MTTR Reduction: Traditional security tools cause alert fatigue. NexusGuard AI acts as an autonomous DevSecOps engineer. When a threat is detected, it generates a clear Proof of Concept (PoC) and automatically writes a secure code patch, opening a Pull Request to reduce the Mean Time To Remediation (MTTR) from months to minutes.

Next-Gen Bug Bounties: We solved the broken incentive structure of traditional cybersecurity research. By linking merged security patches to a Polygon smart contract, we guarantee instant, trustless escrow payouts to white-hat hackers, completely redefining how open-source security is incentivized.

By transforming vulnerability management from a manual, reactive chore into a fully automated, blockchain-incentivized workflow, NexusGuard AI represents the next evolution of automated cybersecurity.

### KiranaAI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/kiranaai-3a6f) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/AKPranav1/Kirana-orchestrator) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XtE65AkMN7E) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> Your Kirana Store, Now Autonomous

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Natural Language Processing](https://img.shields.io/badge/Natural%20Language%20Processing-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem Kirana AI Solves

Indian Kirana stores, over 12 million of them, still operate primarily on handwritten ledgers, paper order slips, and WhatsApp messages that get lost in daily chaos. A customer sends a voice note ordering two kilos of flour, one litre of oil, and three packets of noodles while asking about their outstanding balance. The shopkeeper, busy with ten other customers, scribbles the order on a scrap of paper. By evening, the paper is lost, the customer disputes the order, and the khata balance becomes a source of conflict. This happens daily in thousands of stores, costing shopkeepers time, money, and customer trust.

The khata system itself is a nightmare of manual tracking. A customer named Ramesh owes two thousand five hundred rupees for forty-five days. The shopkeeper must flip through a dog-eared notebook to find Ramesh's page, then remember to ask him for payment. But Ramesh visits only once a week, and the shopkeeper forgets every time. Meanwhile, other customers accumulate debt silently. The average Kirana store loses fifty thousand rupees or more annually to unrecovered credit simply because there is no systematic way to track and recover debts.

Split bills create another layer of chaos. Four friends walk in together. One wants rice, another wants noodles, a third wants milk, and they all want to split the total equally. The shopkeeper spends ten minutes calculating, writing four separate entries in the khata, and still makes a math error that leads to an argument later. Customers argue over who owes what, and the shopkeeper gets caught in the middle, losing goodwill and wasting precious time that could be spent serving other customers.

Stockouts are equally damaging. A customer asks for a popular brand of noodles. The shopkeeper checks the shelf and finds it empty because he forgot to reorder. The customer walks to the competitor across the street. This happens five to ten times daily. Each lost sale is fifty to two hundred rupees, and each lost customer may never return. Shopkeepers have no way of predicting demand or knowing when to reorder beyond gut feeling and memory, both of which fail under the pressure of a busy store.

Handwritten lists and voice notes are impossible to process at scale. A customer sends a photo of a list scribbled in a mix of Hindi, English, and Kannada script. Another sends a thirty-second voice note rattling off twelve items. The shopkeeper must listen or decipher, then type everything into some system manually, inevitably missing items or misinterpreting quantities. What should take seconds ends up taking minutes, and the shopkeeper falls behind on other tasks.

Kirana AI solves all of these problems by creating an autonomous operating system that never loses an order, never forgets a debt, and never misses a reorder. It automatically transcribes voice notes, extracts text from handwritten photos, and parses messy multilingual messages into structured orders. It maintains a digital khata ledger where every transaction is logged instantly, and when a customer's debt exceeds a threshold, it automatically sends escalating voice reminders directly to their phone. It splits bills among multiple customers without math errors and updates each person's ledger individually. It analyzes sales patterns to predict stockouts days in advance and suggests exactly how much to reorder. The shopkeeper does nothing except approve the occasional purchase order. Everything else runs automatically.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Twilio Credit Ran Out During Testing

While testing the end-to-end order pipeline with a batch of fifty simulated WhatsApp messages, I discovered that Twilio's trial account credit had been completely exhausted. Each test order was sending real WhatsApp receipts and generating actual Vasooli voice notes through ElevenLabs, which consumed both Twilio messaging credits and ElevenLabs character quotas. Had to create multiple accounts and request Twilio for permission.

## Gemini API Quota Exhaustion During Testing
The free tier allows hundred requests per day, but each complex order required two to three Gemini calls due to retries and fallbacks, meaning ten concurrent orders could exceed the quota within seconds. The service would crash with unhandled exceptions, leaving half the orders unprocessed. I solved this by adding a fallback chain to Groq and the heuristic parser ensures that when Gemini is temporarily unavailable, orders still get processed with lower but acceptable accuracy. This made the test suite reliable and the production service resilient to API rate limits.

**Gemini**

Gemini Flash acts as the semantic parsing engine that converts chaotic customer messages into clean, structured order data. The system sends a production-grade system instruction defining operational parameters: multilingual adaptability across 10+ Indian languages, number word normalization (converting "do", "teen", "paanch" to 2, 3, 5), unit mapping ("kilo"->"kg", "doodh"->"litre"), payment intent detection (setting payment_intent to "khata" when phrases like "khate mein daal do" appear), and split grouping (detecting when customers say "Abhi ke saath split karo"). The response schema is strictly typed via Pydantic models - ParsedOrderPayload with payment_intent, request_pdf, raw_splits (each with buyer_name and raw_items), and language. If Gemini fails or returns no items, the system gracefully falls back to Groq's Qwen model, then to a heuristic parser with regex patterns for khata phrases, PDF requests, and item extraction. Gemini enables natural language ordering that works exactly like customers already talk - no forms, no rigid syntax, just "2 kilo aata aur ek doodh ka packet, Rahul ke saath split karo" converted instantly into structured data.

**ElevenLabs**

ElevenLabs transforms the khata debt collection process from a passive reminder into an escalating, emotionally-aware voice intervention. When a customer's outstanding balance exceeds ₹1500, the system automatically triggers a Vasooli (debt recovery) voice note. The send_vasooli_alert function selects a tone based on reminder_count: Level 1 uses calm, friendly settings (stability=0.70, style=0.00) for a polite nudge; Level 2 uses firmer settings (stability=0.50, style=0.40) for a serious reminder; Level 3 uses stern, urgent settings (stability=0.30, style=0.80) for a final warning. Each level has a distinct multilingual script - Hindi, Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, or English - generated dynamically with the customer's name and exact outstanding amount inserted. The system then calls ElevenLabs' text-to-speech API with the selected voice settings, saves the MP3 to audio_files/, and serves it to Twilio for WhatsApp delivery. This isn't a static template; it's generative output that adapts tone, content, and language per customer and escalation stage, dramatically improving collection rates over generic reminders.

**MongoDB**

MongoDB Atlas serves as the persistent storage backbone for the entire Kirana AI system, hosting five core collections. The orders collection stores every processed order with enriched pricing, applied discounts, split shares, and timestamps. The khata collection tracks the double-entry credit ledger where each customer has an outstanding balance, an array of transaction entries (each with order ID, amount, date, and settlement status), and a reminder_count field that drives ElevenLabs voice escalation. The customers collection maintains lifetime spend, order counts, and last purchase dates for loyalty analytics. The products collection holds real-time stock quantities and pricing used for dynamic order enrichment, while purchase_orders and suppliers manage the B2B restocking workflow. Every write operation uses atomic find_one_and_update with $inc for balance changes, ensuring no race conditions when multiple orders arrive simultaneously — critical for a busy Kirana store. MongoDB's document model perfectly matches the nested structure of orders with line items and splits, and the jsonSchema validation in schema.json enforces data integrity at the database level.

**Sarvam.ai**

Kirana AI integrates Sarvam AI's specialized language models to solve two real-world retail problems that traditional software cannot address: voice notes and handwritten lists. When a customer sends a WhatsApp voice order in Hinglish, Kannada, Tamil, or any of the ten supported Indian languages, the system downloads the audio from Twilio and sends it to Sarvam's Saaras STT API, which returns accurate transcribed text even with background noise, Indian accents, and code-switching between languages. Similarly, when a customer sends a photo of a handwritten grocery list in mixed scripts, Sarvam's Vision OCR (optimized specifically for Indian handwriting) extracts the messy text and normalizes it into machine-readable form. Without Sarvam, Kirana AI would either reject voice and image inputs entirely or force customers to type perfect English orders - neither is acceptable for a real Indian Kirana store. By embedding Sarvam's multilingual STT and handwriting-aware OCR as the first step of its ingestion pipeline, the system enables natural multimodal communication that matches how actual customers already interact, then feeds the extracted text into Gemini for structured parsing. This is applied GenAI: using purpose-built Indian language models as critical infrastructure, not superficial wrappers.

**Gen AI&ML**

This Kirana AI project qualifies for the GenAI track because it embeds multiple generative AI models as core business logic components, not superficial wrappers. The system uses Gemini Flash with a production-grade system instruction to parse unstructured, multilingual WhatsApp text (supporting 10+ Indian languages) into structured orders containing items, quantities, split parties, and payment intent - replacing traditional forms with natural language understanding. It integrates Sarvam AI for speech-to-text conversion of customer voice notes and Google Cloud Vision OCR for handwritten order extraction, enabling multimodal inputs that conventional CRUD applications cannot handle. For generative outputs, ElevenLabs dynamically produces escalating debt-collection voice notes (Vasooli) where the tone shifts from polite to stern based on reminder count, not static templates. The semantic SKU matching with multilingual aliases and script variations further demonstrates GenAI's role in handling real-world linguistic ambiguity. This is applied GenAI - using foundation models to solve authentic retail automation problems that rule-based systems cannot address, deployed in a scalable microservices architecture with proper fallback chains (Gemini -> Groq -> heuristics).

### Al AqL
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/al-aql-d845) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Affan-Asif/Offline-Law-Assistant) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/x6qfAXI-6EU?si=vRmSq32RtGuAvkQ2) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> Offline AI Assistant for Lawyers

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![SMTP](https://img.shields.io/badge/SMTP-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Problem It Solves -
Legal professionals handle some of the most sensitive and confidential information in the world. Client statements, case strategies, evidence, contracts, court documents, and internal communications often cannot be safely shared with cloud-based AI systems due to privacy, compliance, and confidentiality concerns.
As a result, lawyers still spend countless hours manually reviewing documents, organizing case information, taking notes during client meetings, preparing arguments, managing schedules, and searching through large amounts of case data.
Al AqL solves this problem by providing a completely offline AI-powered legal assistant that runs locally on the firm's own systems. No internet connection is required, and sensitive client information never leaves the organization's control.

What Can People Use It For?
1. Secure Legal Research and Case Analysis - 
Lawyers can ask questions about case files, contracts, evidence, and legal documents using natural language. The system retrieves relevant information from locally stored documents and provides contextual answers without exposing data to external servers.
2. Client Case Management -
Each client receives a dedicated workspace with separate conversations, memories, documents, and case history. This helps lawyers keep information organized and prevents accidental mixing of case data.
3. Real-Time Meeting and Call Documentation - 
With client consent, lawyers can record consultations and meetings. Al AqL automatically transcribes conversations, extracts important facts, and updates case records, reducing the need for manual note-taking.
4. Contradiction Detection - 
The system identifies inconsistencies across statements, timelines, documents, and evidence. This helps lawyers discover potential issues early and prepare stronger legal strategies.
5. Visual Case Understanding - 
Al AqL automatically builds knowledge graphs that show relationships between clients, witnesses, evidence, events, and legal entities. Lawyers can also manually edit nodes and connections to reflect their professional understanding of the case.
6. Scheduling and Conflict Detection - 
Through calendar integration, the system can detect scheduling conflicts such as overlapping client meetings, court hearings, or important deadlines, helping lawyers avoid costly mistakes.
7. Automated Communication - 
Lawyers can generate case summaries, updates, and professional communications using simple prompts and send them directly through integrated email systems.
8. Firm Performance Monitoring -
The dashboard provides insights into active cases, completed matters, client statistics, success rates, and overall firm productivity, helping legal teams make better operational decisions.
9. How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier and Safer -
* Eliminates the need to upload confidential legal data to cloud AI services.
* Reduces hours spent searching through documents and case files.
* Minimizes manual note-taking during consultations and meetings.
* Helps identify contradictions and inconsistencies before court proceedings.
* Prevents scheduling conflicts and missed appointments.
* Provides a visual understanding of complex cases through editable knowledge graphs.
* Improves collaboration through automated summaries and communications.
* Keeps all sensitive information under the firm's direct control.

Why Al AqL Matters
Al AqL combines artificial intelligence, privacy, and legal workflow automation into a single platform. By operating entirely offline, it allows legal professionals to benefit from modern AI capabilities while maintaining the confidentiality and trust that their clients expect.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/e3f45def95b3406aaca545aa9aaf52c5/fb701701-62c6-4d4a-9b81-8add16b7dc08.jpeg)pabilities while maintaining the confidentiality and trust that their clients expect.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Running a Reliable Legal Assistant on a Small Offline Model - 
Our biggest challenge was that we wanted the entire system to run offline using TinyLlama 1.1B. While lightweight and fast, small models often struggle with accurate reasoning, structured outputs, and consistency.
2. Knowledge Graph Generation -
Automatically generating knowledge graphs from conversations was difficult because small language models often produce inconsistent entities and relationships.
3. Vector Database Stability Issues -
Initially, we planned to use ChromaDB for document retrieval and memory storage. However, we encountered database corruption and compatibility issues during development, which affected retrieval reliability.
4. Privacy-First Design -
Many AI features rely on cloud services, but our goal was complete privacy. Building email, scheduling, retrieval, memory management, and legal assistance without sending client data to external servers required significant architectural redesign.

**Gen AI&ML**

Al AqL combines both **Generative AI (GenAI)** and **Machine Learning (ML)** to provide an intelligent offline legal assistant for law firms. It uses a locally hosted Large Language Model (TinyLlama 1.1B) to understand natural language, answer legal queries, generate summaries, draft emails, and assist lawyers conversationally. At the same time, it applies Machine Learning techniques such as embeddings, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), semantic search, knowledge graph generation, memory retrieval, and contradiction detection to analyze legal documents, recall relevant case information, identify inconsistencies, and organize relationships between clients, witnesses, evidence, and events. By combining GenAI with ML-driven retrieval and reasoning systems, Al AqL delivers secure, context-aware legal assistance while keeping all sensitive client data completely offline and private.

### Campus Flow
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/campus-flow-b1e0) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/vikash1551/CDS.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://cds-gamma.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/3VHqqokJotE?feature=shared) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> Keeping Campus in Motion

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

1. Campus "Last-Mile" Inconvenience: Students waste significant time walking long distances across campus just to buy basic canteen meals, snacks, or daily supplies.

2. Inefficient Peer-to-Peer Lending: When a student urgently needs a short-term item (like a calculator for an exam or a lab coat), they have no secure, reliable way to find a nearby peer willing to lend it.

3. Reliance on Chaotic Networks: Students are forced to rely on disorganized, unverified WhatsApp or Telegram groups to ask for help or coordinate item drop-offs.

4. Untapped Student Time: Students who are already walking across campus have no structured way to monetize their movement and free time.

5. Lack of a Campus Micro-Economy: There is no hyper-local, safe ecosystem that incentivizes students to help each other while allowing them to earn pocket money and rewards.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/280e48c059eb4a818ceb96a477d96e26/f178f69f-9142-435d-9e24-19ec22ea7398.png)

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/280e48c059eb4a818ceb96a477d96e26/714461e1-bd05-4edc-a0d6-8f6af02d0d34.png)

**Challenges we ran into**

1. AI Matching Speed: Balancing accurate AI matching (Gemini/Sarvam) with fast, low-latency API responses to avoid keeping users waiting.

2. Complex State Management: Handling the multi-step lending timeline (Requested → Matched → Accepted → OTP Handover → Returned) without race conditions.

3. Secure Physical Handovers: Implementing a reliable OTP verification system to safely track the physical exchange of items on campus.

4. Dual Database Workflows: Structuring MongoDB to efficiently handle both permanent merchant shop inventories and dynamic, temporary peer-to-peer listings.

**Gemini**

Smart Matching & Routing: Campus Flow uses Gemini to instantly analyze delivery requests and generate intelligent, logical campus routes and courier recommendations.
Dynamic UI Generation: We leverage Gemini's speed to automatically generate relevant emojis and tags for user-uploaded products on the fly, creating a polished, zero-effort user experience.
Automated Analytics: Gemini powers our merchant dashboard by analyzing raw sales and inventory data to generate plain-English, actionable business reports for campus shop owners.

**MongoDB**

1. Geospatial Queries: MongoDB's native geospatial indexing helps us find the nearest courier, lender, or available item on campus using real-time location data.

2. Flexible Schema: CampusFlow supports both merchant products and peer-to-peer lending. MongoDB's document model allows us to store different types of data without rigid table structures.

3. Real-Time Tracking:Courier locations, order updates, and lending activities generate frequent updates. MongoDB efficiently handles these high-velocity write operations.

4. JSON-Based Development:Since our frontend (React) and backend (Flask) communicate using JSON, MongoDB's BSON format provides a seamless data flow, enabling faster development and easier integration.

**Sarvam.ai**

Intelligent Data Processing: CampusFlow uses Sarvam AI to process raw, unstructured campus inventory and sales data into structured, meaningful insights.
Actionable Merchant Reports: It powers our "Inventory Intelligence" feature, automatically generating plain-text, actionable business health reports for campus shop owners.
Optimized Local Context: By utilizing Sarvam, CampusFlow can better understand and generate recommendations that are highly contextualized for local, fast-moving Indian campus environments.

**Open Innovation**

1. Identifies an Unaddressed, Niche Problem Open Innovation is about finding gaps that standard solutions miss. Big delivery apps (like Swiggy or Zomato) stop at the campus gate, and standard e-commerce doesn't handle short-term peer lending. Campus Flow identifies and solves a highly specific problem: the "last-mile" logistics within a closed campus ecosystem.

2. Combines Multiple Domains Creatively Instead of just being one thing, Campus Flow creatively merges three distinct models:

- Quick Commerce (shop-to-student delivery)
- The Sharing Economy (peer-to-peer lending of emergency items)
- AI Optimization (smart matching and route logic) This cross-pollination of ideas is exactly what Open Innovation looks for.

3. Creates a Self-Sustaining Micro-Economy Campus Flow doesn't just provide a service; it creates a community-driven economy. It turns an existing resource (students walking around campus with free time) into a logistical network. It incentivizes students to help each other through gamification, XP, and pocket money, making the ecosystem completely self-sustaining.

4. Highly Scalable to Other Communities Open Innovation projects need to show future potential. While Campus Flow is built for a college campus, the exact same architecture can be scaled horizontally to any closed community—such as massive corporate tech parks, large residential townships, or hospital complexes.

**The problem it solves**

WHAT IS RAKSHA AI

Raksha AI is an AI-powered blood intelligence and care coordination platform built specifically for Thalassemia patients in India. Thalassemia is a genetic blood disorder where patients require frequent, often bi-weekly, blood transfusions to survive — making reliable, fast access to compatible donors a matter of life and death.


WHO CAN USE IT

THALASSEMIA PATIENTS & CAREGIVERS

Find blood donors fast
Instead of frantically calling hospitals or NGOs, patients can get matched with compatible, available donors in real time.

Predict upcoming needs
AI models forecast when the next transfusion will be needed, so the search for blood starts before the crisis hits, not during it.

Receive care reminders
Personalized alerts help patients stay on track with treatment schedules.

Access health education
AI-curated content explains their condition and care options in a personalized way.


VOLUNTARY BLOOD DONORS

Register and be found
Donors can create profiles and get notified when a compatible patient nearby needs blood.

Donate on their own schedule
The platform respects donor availability and lets them respond to requests at their convenience.

A loyalty and rewards system is planned to recognize and incentivize regular donors.


DOCTORS & HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS

Coordinate care securely
Clinicians can interact with patients and caregivers through a secure channel on the platform.

Monitor transfusion history
Smart tracking of a patient's history helps doctors make better-informed decisions.


NGO ADMINS

Central dashboard
A control panel to monitor donor availability, patient requests, and system-wide activity.

Integration with government systems
Works alongside existing infrastructure like e-RaktKosh and Blood Bridge to avoid duplication and extend reach.


HOW AI MAKES IT BETTER AND SAFER

Manually calling donors or hospitals during a crisis
— replaced by — Real-time automated donor matching

Unpredictable donor availability
— replaced by — AI that predicts donor availability in advance

Generic patient education
— replaced by — Personalized, AI-curated guidance per patient

Language barriers
— replaced by — Multilingual chatbot support (planned)

Fragmented records
— replaced by — Smart, unified transfusion history tracking

Stress and delays for families
— replaced by — Proactive outreach before the critical moment arrives


SAFETY & PRIVACY

Patient health data is handled securely. The platform ensures privacy while integrating seamlessly with existing government systems like e-RaktKosh and Blood Warriors' Blood Bridge.


WHAT IS COMING NEXT

AI-enhanced chatbot support in local languages
Smart transfusion history tracking
Integration with hospital management systems
Nationwide donor loyalty and rewards system




Raksha AI transforms a stressful, manual, and time-critical process into a proactive, intelligent, and coordinated support system — giving Thalassemia patients and their families peace of mind.

**Challenges we ran into**

Bugs & Hurdles We Encountered — Raksha AI

Building Raksha AI — a blood intelligence and care coordination platform for Thalassemia patients — came with a unique set of technical challenges. Here is an honest look at what slowed us down and how we pushed through.


1. Hyperparameter Tuning & Grid Search

The problem: Grid search was computationally expensive, and we often could not tell if poor results were due to the model, the parameters, or the data itself.

How we got over it: We narrowed the search space by first running quick experiments with randomized search, then zooming into promising ranges with grid search. We tracked all runs using accuracy logs to avoid repeating failed configurations.


2. Chunking Data in the RAG Pipeline

The problem: Chunks were either too small, losing context, or too large, diluting relevance in the embedding space. Poor chunking led to broken context, missed embeddings, and incoherent retrieved results.

How we got over it: We experimented with overlap-based chunking strategies and tuned chunk sizes based on the nature of the medical content, eventually landing on a chunk size and overlap combination that preserved semantic meaning across boundaries.


3. Multilingual Support

The problem: Embeddings trained on English-heavy corpora performed poorly on regional language inputs, leading to retrieval mismatches and inaccurate responses.

How we got over it: We evaluated multilingual embedding models and tested cross-lingual retrieval quality before settling on a model that handled the primary languages our users needed.


4. Tracking Accuracy & Model Selection

The problem: With multiple models in the mix, keeping track of accuracy scores across experiments was messy. It was easy to lose sight of which version was performing best and why.

How we got over it: We introduced a disciplined logging system, tracking model name, parameters, dataset split, and accuracy per run, which made comparisons much cleaner.


5. Churn in the Pipeline

The problem: Components kept breaking or needing rework as upstream changes propagated downstream through the pipeline.

How we got over it: We modularized the pipeline more deliberately so changes in one layer, such as chunking logic, did not silently break downstream steps like retrieval quality. Better separation of concerns saved us significant debugging time late in the project.


These were real engineering problems. Working through them gave the team a much deeper understanding of production ML systems, RAG architecture, and the nuances of building AI for healthcare in a multilingual context.

**Gen AI&ML**

Raksha AI — How It Fits the Gen AI & ML Track


GENERATIVE AI USAGE

AI-Powered Chatbot
Raksha AI uses a Generative AI chatbot to handle natural language conversations with patients, caregivers, and donors. Users can type requests like "I need blood urgently" or "Register me as a donor" and the AI understands intent and routes them accordingly — no forms, no friction.

Automated FAQ & Education Engine
A Gen AI module generates personalized responses to questions about Thalassemia, treatment options, and blood donation. Instead of static content, patients receive answers tailored to their specific situation and literacy level.

Multilingual Support (Planned)
Gen AI enables the platform to converse in regional Indian languages, making it accessible beyond English-speaking users — a critical factor for rural and semi-urban Thalassemia communities.


 MACHINE LEARNING USAGE

Predictive Donor Availability — LSTM Neural Network
The platform uses an LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) model trained on historical donor behavior to predict when a donor is likely to be available and when a patient will need their next transfusion. This shifts the system from reactive to proactive.

AI-Driven Donor Matching
An ML model evaluates blood type compatibility, donor proximity, and real-time availability to rank and suggest the most suitable donors for each patient request — automatically, within seconds.

Transfusion Need Prediction
Based on a patient's historical transfusion data, the ML model forecasts upcoming blood requirements and triggers early outreach to potential donors before the need becomes critical.

Intent Classification
Natural language understanding classifies every incoming message into actionable categories — request blood, register as donor, check status, ask a question — and routes it to the right workflow without human intervention.


 WHERE GEN AI AND ML WORK TOGETHER

Gen AI handles the conversation layer — understanding what the user wants and responding naturally.
ML handles the intelligence layer — predicting, matching, and ranking behind the scenes.
Together they eliminate the manual effort that currently makes Thalassemia care coordination slow, stressful, and unreliable.


WHY THIS STRONGLY FITS THE GEN AI & ML TRACK

The project is not using AI as a feature. AI is the core infrastructure of Raksha AI. Every critical function — donor matching, transfusion prediction, patient communication, care education — is driven by either a Generative AI model or a trained ML model. The platform would not function without it.

This is a real-world, high-stakes healthcare application of Gen AI and ML solving a problem that affects over one million Thalassemia patients in India.

> The Autonomous Valuation Engine for Private Capita

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

It automates the company valuation process by analyzing financial documents, extracting key data, generating valuation models, and producing investment reports.

Benefits:

Reduces manual document review and data entry
Speeds up valuations from days to hours
Minimizes human errors through automated verification
Helps analysts focus on decision-making instead of repetitive tasks
Generates audit-ready reports with source-backed insights

Use Cases:

Private Equity & Venture Capital valuation
Due diligence automation
Financial modeling
Investment memo generation
Portfolio monitoring

Result: Faster, more accurate, and scalable investment analysis.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges We Ran Into**

- Extracting reliable data from different document formats (PDFs, financial statements, reports) was difficult because every company uses different layouts and structures. We solved this by building a document classification and extraction pipeline that validates information across multiple sources.
- Reducing AI hallucinations in financial analysis was a major challenge. To address this, we implemented confidence scoring, source citations, and verification checks before data is used in valuation models.
- Coordinating multiple AI agents for extraction, verification, modeling, and report generation required careful workflow design. We overcame this by creating a structured agent pipeline where each agent has a specific responsibility and passes validated outputs to the next stage.
- Ensuring transparency and trust in AI-generated valuations was challenging. We solved this by providing an audit trail that shows exactly which documents and data points contributed to each valuation decision.

**Gemini**

utilizes Gemini's multimodal and reasoning capabilities to automate the end-to-end company valuation process. The platform can analyze financial statements, reports, cap tables, and other unstructured documents, extract key insights, generate valuation models, and produce investment-ready reports.

Using a RAG-powered architecture, users can interact with the platform through natural language or voice, asking questions directly against financial documents and structured databases. Gemini enables context-aware reasoning across multiple data sources, allowing investors to receive accurate, explainable answers and valuation insights instantly.

By combining multimodal document understanding, advanced reasoning, autonomous AI agents, and conversational data access, Build with AI transforms complex financial analysis into a fast, intelligent, and scalable workflow.

**Sarvam.ai**

leverages Sarvam.ai's multilingual AI capabilities to make company valuation and financial analysis accessible through natural language and voice interactions. Users can upload financial documents and interact with the platform in multiple Indian languages, enabling broader accessibility for investors, analysts, and businesses.

By combining multilingual AI, document intelligence, voice interfaces, and autonomous agents, our solution demonstrates how advanced Indian AI models can solve complex real-world financial workflows while breaking language barriers in the investment ecosystem.

**Open Innovation**

aligns with the Open Innovation track by applying cutting-edge Agentic AI, RAG, OCR, and real-time voice technologies to solve a major challenge in private capital: company valuation and due diligence.

The platform autonomously analyzes financial documents, extracts and verifies data, generates valuation models, and produces investment-ready reports. By reducing manual effort, improving accuracy, and accelerating decision-making, it transforms a traditionally slow and resource-intensive process into an intelligent, scalable workflow.

Our solution demonstrates how emerging AI technologies can create new ways of working, unlock productivity gains, and drive innovation in the financial industry.

**The problem it solves**

## The Problem It Solves

Students, job seekers, farmers, and entrepreneurs often struggle to find genuine opportunities because information is scattered across multiple websites, eligibility criteria are complex, and fraudulent or misleading links are common. Many people miss scholarships, internships, government schemes, grants, and training programs simply because they do not know where to look or cannot verify the authenticity of the information.

AshaAI is an AI-powered Opportunity Navigator that simplifies this process. Users can interact through text or voice, describe their profile in natural language, and instantly receive personalized opportunities matched to their eligibility.

### Key Features

#### AI-Powered Eligibility Engine

Users enter details such as age, education, income, location, occupation, and interests. AshaAI analyzes their profile and recommends relevant opportunities with eligibility explanations and match scores.

#### AI Voice Assistant

Users can speak naturally instead of filling long forms. The AI assistant understands the user's profile, extracts important information, and helps them discover opportunities through a conversational experience.

#### Verified Original Links Only

AshaAI prioritizes official and authentic application links, helping users avoid misleading, outdated, or fraudulent websites. Users are directed to the original source whenever possible.

#### Personalized Opportunity Recommendations

Different users receive different recommendations based on their profile. A student, unemployed graduate, farmer, and entrepreneur will each see opportunities tailored to their specific needs.

### Who Can Benefit?

* **Students:** Scholarships, internships, fellowships, certification programs.
* **Job Seekers:** Employment opportunities, apprenticeships, training programs, skill development initiatives.
* **Farmers:** Agricultural schemes, subsidies, insurance programs, financial assistance.
* **Entrepreneurs:** Startup grants, MSME support, incubation programs, innovation challenges, funding opportunities.

### How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier

* Eliminates the need to search across multiple portals.
* Provides AI-powered personalized recommendations.
* Supports both voice and text interactions.
* Explains eligibility criteria in simple language.
* Recommends which opportunity to apply for first.
* Directs users to verified official sources.
* Reduces the risk of scams and misinformation.

### Impact

AshaAI acts as a personal AI opportunity advisor, helping people discover genuine opportunities, understand their eligibility, and confidently access scholarships, jobs, government schemes, startup support, and skill-development programs through a single intelligent platform.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges We Ran Into

Building AshaAI involved several technical and integration challenges that required multiple iterations and debugging.

### 1. Integrating AI Services

One of the biggest challenges was integrating Gemini AI into the application for eligibility analysis, opportunity recommendations, and conversational assistance. We initially faced API authentication issues, response format inconsistencies, and challenges parsing structured JSON responses from AI-generated content.

**How we solved it:**

* Updated the integration to use the latest Gemini API request format.
* Added validation and fallback handling for unexpected AI responses.
* Implemented structured JSON extraction and error recovery mechanisms.

### 2. Personalized Opportunity Matching

Different users should receive different recommendations based on factors such as age, income, education, location, and occupation. Creating a reliable matching system while keeping recommendations relevant was challenging.

**How we solved it:**

* Built a profile-based eligibility engine.
* Combined user attributes with AI-powered analysis.
* Added match scores and eligibility explanations for transparency.

### 3. Official Link Verification

Many opportunities are listed across multiple websites, making it difficult to ensure users are directed to authentic sources.

**How we solved it:**

* Designed the platform to prioritize verified and official application links.
* Added validation checks before displaying opportunity URLs.
* Ensured users are directed to original sources whenever possible.

### 4. Authentication and User Personalization

We wanted each user to have a personalized dashboard rather than showing the same information to everyone. Integrating authentication with profile-based recommendations required coordination across frontend and backend systems.

**How we solved it:**

* Integrated Firebase authentication.
* Connected user sessions with MongoDB data storage.
* Enabled personalized opportunity feeds and dashboards.

### 5. Team Collaboration and Merge Conflicts

Since multiple team members worked on different modules simultaneously, we encountered merge conflicts while combining frontend, backend, notification, and authentication features.

**How we solved it:**

* Used Git branches and pull requests for safer collaboration.
* Performed manual conflict resolution where required.
* Created backup branches before major merges to prevent data loss.

### 6. Building a Real-Time User Experience

Our goal was to make the platform feel like a real AI product rather than a static eligibility checker. This required dynamic recommendations, responsive interfaces, and conversational interactions.

**How we solved it:**

* Added AI-powered recommendations and explanations.
* Built an interactive dashboard with personalized results.
* Integrated voice-based interaction capabilities to improve accessibility.

### Key Learning

The project pushed us beyond our comfort zone by requiring us to combine AI, authentication, databases, APIs, frontend development, backend services, and collaborative software engineering into a single working platform. The experience taught us how to design, debug, integrate, and deploy a real-world AI application under hackathon time constraints.

**Gemini**

Google Gemini acts as the brain of AshaAI. Instead of making users fill lengthy forms, Gemini understands natural language and voice inputs, extracts profile information, analyzes eligibility, explains why a user qualifies for an opportunity, and recommends the best opportunities to pursue first. It transforms complex eligibility rules into personalized, human-friendly guidance.

**ElevenLabs**

ElevenLabs gives AshaAI a natural voice. Instead of only displaying text, AshaAI can explain eligibility, application steps, deadlines, and recommendations through realistic speech. This creates a more engaging and accessible experience, especially for users with limited digital literacy or visual impairments.

**MongoDB**

MongoDB serves as the memory and persistence layer of AshaAI. It securely stores user profiles, opportunity data, application status, reminders, deadlines, and personalized recommendations. This allows every user to receive a customized experience rather than seeing generic results.

**Sarvam.ai**

Enables multilingual accessibility by translating opportunity details, eligibility criteria, and application guidance into Indian languages, ensuring that language is never a barrier to accessing opportunities.

**Gen AI&ML**

AshaAI is an AI-powered Opportunity Platform that uses Generative AI to understand user profiles, evaluate eligibility, recommend opportunities, provide conversational guidance, and connect users to verified official resources through personalized text and voice interactions.

### Foresight
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/foresight-66b9) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Niksh-Hiremath/Foresight) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/hBpjjMjooJ8) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> Your plan walks in. Only the truth walks out.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![d3.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/d3.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most strategic decisions a market-entry plan, a pitch deck, a product bet get pressure-tested only *after* they fail. Internal reviews are biased toward agreement, and founders rarely have a CFO, a competitive analyst, a lawyer, and an ops lead in the room at once.

**Foresight stress-tests a decision from the inside, before you commit.** Upload a business plan, pitch deck, or memo and:

- **Five adversarial AI agents**  CFO, Market, Competitor, Legal, and Execution - attack it in parallel from distinct angles, each grounded in *your own document* plus live web evidence (Competitor and Market Agents)
- A **swarm simulation** plays the decision forward across hundreds of
  personality-driven agents to produce bull / base / bear outcome bands.
- You get a **deterministic risk score (0–100)**, a clear verdict
  (DO NOT PROCEED / CAUTION / PROCEED), the 3 questions your team must answer, an India-specific go-to-market strategy, and a remediation roadmap mapping every top finding to a concrete fix.

**Who it's for:** founders validating a pitch before raising, product/strategy teams de-risking a launch, consultants and analysts who need a fast, structure second opinion. It turns a vague gut-check into a defensible, evidence-cited decision review in minutes making high-stakes calls *safer* and faster.

**Challenges we ran into**

**1. Swarm memory quota kept blowing up.** The MiroFish swarm simulation logs every agent interaction as an "episode" in Zep Cloud, and re-running an analysis re-ingested the whole knowledge graph each time we hit the episode quota mid-demo. We fixed it by making the bridge *stateful*: it detects an already-built graph and skips the two graph-construction steps (1-2) on repeat runs, reusing the existing graph instead of rebuilding it. Re-runs now consume zero new episodes.

**2. The swarm returned Chinese.** MiroFish's underlying engine emitted simulation reports in Chinese, which broke our verdict synthesis downstream. We added an auto-translation step in the 7-step async pipeline that translates the swarm output to English *before* it's persisted to MongoDB, so everything downstream stays consistent.

**Gemini**

Our LLM layer is OpenAI-SDK-compatible and fully env-swappable, and we run it on Google's Gemini models to drive all five adversarial agents, the adaptive intake Q&A, GTM generation, and verdict synthesis. Gemini's speed and large context let every agent reason over the full document plus live web evidence in parallel without truncation.

**MongoDB**

MongoDB Atlas is our system of record and our retrieval backbone. We use Atlas (M0) with the async Motor driver to store decision contexts, agent findings, simulation results, knowledge-base docs, and reports, and we use Atlas Vector Search to power the two-layer RAG (a "decision" layer over the uploaded doc and an "internal" layer over the company knowledge base).

**Gen AI&ML**

The core is a multi-agent generative system: five role-specialized adversarial LLM agents running in parallel over SSE, an adaptive intake that generates follow-up questions from gaps in your document, a two-layer RAG pipeline, and a forward-looking agent-swarm simulation. It's GenAI applied to real decision-making, not a chatbot wrapper.

### DecisionX
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/decisionx-ab52) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/aravindpulluri116/DecisionX.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://decisionx-mu.vercel.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/dPdnMjYY9Hk) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> Measure the consequences before you Decide.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenStreetMap](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenStreetMap-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![Framer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Framer-333333?style=flat-square) ![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most high-stakes decisions—whether building a metro line, redeveloping a city block, or launching a public policy—are still driven by first-order thinking. Decision-makers evaluate cost, feasibility, and timelines, but often overlook the cascading second- and third-order consequences: community displacement, fiscal overruns, environmental degradation, stakeholder resistance, and long-term economic trade-offs

**DecisionX** is an AI-powered decision intelligence platform that helps governments, planners, and organizations evaluate critical decisions *before* implementation. Instead of relying on a single AI response, DecisionX orchestrates a dynamic team of specialized AI experts—such as economic, social, environmental, stakeholder, risk, and future-impact analysts—tailored to the decision being evaluated.

The platform enriches every analysis with location intelligence from OpenStreetMap, simulates cross-domain impacts, models downstream consequences, and synthesizes every perspective into a single executive verdict. Rather than providing just a prediction, DecisionX delivers transparent reasoning, evidence-backed assumptions, confidence scores, expert debates, and actionable recommendations—enabling leaders to defend complex decisions with confidence before a single brick is laid.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Multi-agent orchestration without chaos**
Six specialists run in parallel, then the CDO synthesizes prior outputs. We built a strict per-agent JSON schema, shared project context, and event-stream simulation theater so users see each agent’s status in real time.

**Grounding AI in real geography**
Generic “AI analysis” wasn’t acceptable. We added OpenStreetMap enrichment (POIs, density, radius impacts) and required agents to cite location facts in evidence[], separating facts from predictions in assumptions[].

**Trust & explainability**
Users need to know why a score exists. We built an evidence pack: confidence badges, reasoning timeline, trust panel, and per-metric explanations linked to agent outputs and geo sources.

**End-to-end product polish under time pressure**
We shipped a premium marketing site (agents page, dark/light theme), workspace wizard, live simulation UI, and Supabase-backed project persistence — while keeping the core loop: create project → enrich → simulate → report.

**Gemini**

DecisionX uses Gemini as the reasoning core for a seven-agent decision council, where each specialist (economic, social, environmental, stakeholder, risk, future-shock) runs with its own system prompt and returns strict structured JSON — a strong fit for Gemini’s instruction-following and schema-style outputs. Specialists run in parallel, then the Chief Decision Officer reads all prior agent outputs and synthesizes a weighted executive verdict, showcasing Gemini’s multi-step, context-rich reasoning across long, interconnected tasks. Every agent is grounded in real project metadata and OpenStreetMap location intelligence, so Gemini reasons over specific sites, budgets, and communities instead of producing generic analysis. The Future Shock Agent chains second- and third-order consequences, demonstrating Gemini’s strength in causal reasoning and long-horizon impact modeling. End-to-end, DecisionX turns Gemini from a chat tool into a production decision-intelligence system with live simulation UI, evidence trails, and confidence scoring that teams can act on.

**Sustainable Development**

DecisionX helps teams evaluate infrastructure and policy decisions before they are approved, surfacing environmental, social, and economic consequences in one workspace. Its Environmental Agent quantifies emissions, ecological risk, and sustainability trade-offs for real project sites using location intelligence. The Social Agent and Stakeholder Agent map who benefits and who is harmed, supporting equitable, community-aware planning. The Future Shock Agent traces second- and third-order ripple effects that often cause long-term environmental and social damage after implementation. By turning fragmented impact analysis into evidence-backed recommendations, DecisionX supports smarter, more sustainable development aligned with responsible growth and SDG-style decision-making.

### MediTrust AI
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/meditrust-ai-6659) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/sakthidharan1524-lgtm/MediTrust-AI.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://meditrust-ai-135511926714.asia-southeast1.run.app) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://vimeo.com/1201142399?share=copy) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> Zero fake medicines. Verified by AI.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

MediTrust AI makes buying medicine safer and simpler for everyone involved.

For patients, the biggest worry is whether their medicine is real. Our platform removes that guesswork. Before you buy, AI scans your prescription to confirm it's genuine and not AI-generated or forged. During purchase, you see pharmacies ranked by trust score, not just price, so you don't accidentally buy from a risky seller. After delivery, you scan the medicine packaging and our AI checks if it's authentic before you ever open it. If you need a doctor, you can consult one through voice chat in your own language. And if you're recovering from injury, AI rehab tracks your exercise form and corrects you in real time.

For pharmacies, the platform cuts down manual work. Prescriptions are verified automatically, reducing liability from fraudulent sales. Their trust score is built from actual operational data, not fake reviews, so good pharmacies naturally rise to the top. Offline shops can join the verified network, show live stock online, and accept click-and-collect orders with QR code verification at pickup.

For the healthcare system, the impact is structural. Counterfeit medicines that currently slip through at every stage get intercepted before they reach the patient. The 20 to 30 percent fake medicine penetration in India becomes traceable, blockable, and ultimately eliminable. Every verified transaction strengthens the network. Every detected fake triggers investigation. Over time, the system becomes self-reinforcing, driving counterfeit penetration toward zero.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest hurdle we ran into was connecting the frontend to the backend and getting the API layer to work reliably. We built the UI first and it looked great, but when we tried to send prescription images from the React frontend to the FastAPI backend, everything broke. We hit CORS errors constantly because the frontend ran on localhost 3000 and the backend on localhost 8000, and the browser blocked every request. On top of that, the async PostgreSQL connection kept dropping when we tried to save large prescription files, and the multipart file upload for handwritten prescriptions would either timeout or return garbled responses. It was frustrating because the UI was ready but the data simply would not flow.

We got past this by using Google's AI Studio and Firebase Studio to scaffold the backend properly. Instead of writing the FastAPI boilerplate and database connection code manually, we fed the full API contract into Google AI Studio and had it generate the complete async SQLAlchemy setup, the CORS middleware configuration, and the multipart upload handlers. Firebase Studio helped us spin up a working Docker Compose setup with PostgreSQL and Redis in minutes, which eliminated the connection drop issues. The AI also caught that we were missing proper lifespan events in FastAPI for database startup, which was why our async sessions were failing. Once the AI-generated backend skeleton was in place, we only had to tweak the endpoints rather than build them from scratch. That saved us hours and let us focus on the prescription verification logic instead of fighting connection errors.

**Gemini**

We used Gemini at its best by making it do things no basic AI tool can handle.

First, prescription fraud detection. Most apps just read text from a prescription image. We use Gemini to understand the whole document. It looks at the image layout, the text content, and cross-checks everything together. It asks questions like does this doctor's registration number match the medical council database, is the dosage right for the patient's age, and does the handwriting pattern look human or AI-generated. It catches fake prescriptions that other tools miss because they only do text extraction without reasoning.

Second, AI-generated prescription detection. People now use ChatGPT to create fake prescriptions that look real. Gemini spots these by finding patterns that humans cannot see. It checks if the text is too perfect, if the spacing is uniform like a computer made it, and if the medical logic actually makes sense for that doctor's specialty. This is not keyword matching. It is forensic document analysis.

Third, post-delivery medicine verification. After the medicine arrives, the user scans the front, back, and barcode. Gemini analyzes all three images together. It checks if the logo on the front matches the composition text on the back. It flags if the barcode is valid but the packaging colors are wrong. It catches mismatches that only a multimodal AI can see because it reasons across images and text at the same time.

Fourth, the big advantage is context size. Gemini can hold one million tokens in memory. This means we load entire regional doctor registries, drug databases, and known counterfeit patterns into one single analysis. Other models have to break this into pieces and lose connections between data. Gemini sees everything at once and finds hidden relationships.

We did not use Gemini as a chatbot. We used it as a forensic analyst that reads handwriting, detects synthetic fraud, cross-references databases, and reasons across images and text simultaneously. That is using Gemini at its best.

**ElevenLabs**

We used ElevenLabs at its best by building a live AI call assistant trained under full medical guidance.

Instead of making patients wait for doctor appointments or struggle with text-based chat, our AI assistant calls them directly. It speaks in natural regional languages with human-like voice quality, asks about symptoms, explains medicines, and reminds patients about dosages. The conversation feels like talking to a real nurse or doctor, not a robot.

The medical guidance layer is critical. Every response the AI gives is constrained by verified medical protocols. It cannot suggest random treatments or misdiagnose. If a symptom is serious, it immediately escalates to a real doctor. For common issues like fever, cold, or medicine reminders, it handles the conversation fully.

This saves doctor time, helps patients who cannot read or type, and provides 24/7 support when clinics are closed. The voice is warm, clear, and culturally familiar because ElevenLabs clones natural speech patterns rather than sounding synthetic.

That is using it at its best. Not as a text-to-speech tool, but as a medically governed, always-available voice health companion.

**Sarvam.ai**

We used Sarvam AI at its best by solving a problem that breaks every other OCR tool on the market. Indian doctors do not write prescriptions in clean English. They scribble in a mix of English, Latin medical abbreviations, and regional shorthand that looks like random lines to standard AI. Tesseract fails. Google Vision fails. Even basic PaddleOCR chokes on the handwriting.

Saravam AI was built specifically for Indian language chaos. It understands that "OD" means once daily, "BD" means twice daily, and "SOS" means as needed. It recognizes when a doctor writes "Tab. Dolo 650" in half-cursive, half-print, with the dosage squeezed into the margin. It handles Hindi-English code switching where the diagnosis is in Hindi and the medicine name is in English. No generic OCR does this because no generic OCR was trained on ten million Indian medical prescriptions.

Other teams building voice chatbots use Sarvam AI as a basic speech-to-text wrapper. They speak into a microphone and get text back. That is using ten percent of what Sarvam can do. We pushed it to its actual limit.

We feed Sarvam AI raw prescription photographs taken under bad lighting with shaky hands at a medical shop counter. It converts those scribbles into structured digital data. Doctor name. Registration number. Medicine names with exact dosages. Date. Quantity. Everything extracted cleanly so our Gemini layer can verify it against medical council databases.

The real differentiator is the feedback loop. When Sarvam extracts text with low confidence, our system flags it for manual review instead of guessing. Over time, these corrections retrain the extraction model for that specific region's doctor handwriting patterns. The system gets smarter with every prescription uploaded in Tamil Nadu, in Kerala, in Punjab. Each state has different scribble cultures and Sarvam adapts because it was born from Indian data.

Other teams use Sarvam to make talking easier. We use it to read what was never meant to be read by machines. We use it to prevent deaths from misread prescriptions. That is using Sarvam AI at its best potential.

**Sustainable Development**

Our project fits the sustainable development theme because it protects people's health and makes healthcare systems stronger over time.

It targets SDG 3 which is Good Health and Well-being. Right now twenty to thirty percent of medicines in India are fake or substandard. Our platform stops this by verifying prescriptions before purchase, scoring pharmacies by trust, and checking medicine authenticity after delivery. This means fewer people get sick from counterfeit drugs, fewer hospital visits due to wrong medicines, and less money wasted on fake treatments.

It also helps reduce inequality because people in rural areas or small towns can use the app to find verified nearby medical shops instead of depending on unknown online sellers. They get the same safety checks as people in big cities.

The trust score system is sustainable because it runs on AI and real data, not fake reviews. Good pharmacies stay in business and bad ones get filtered out naturally. This creates a healthcare market that rewards honesty and punishes fraud without needing constant manual policing.

By connecting offline medical shops to the digital verification network, we keep local businesses alive while modernizing the system. This supports strong local institutions and responsible consumption of medicines.

In short, we are building a health system that is safer, fairer, and self-improving over time. That is what sustainable development means for healthcare.--
