### BharatLex
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/bharatlex-2f54) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/abdullah-qdev/BharatLex) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://blex-seven.vercel.app/voice-test/mic_test) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W7gxgef1Av0) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> Turn proof into Action!

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![FastAPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastAPI-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Legal awareness and access in India is still fragmented and difficult for most people to navigate. When someone faces a legal issue, the first and most important challenge is not taking action, but understanding what the problem actually means in legal terms. Real-world situations like scams, fraud, threats, or disputes don’t naturally map into clear legal categories for an average person, which creates immediate confusion at the very beginning itself.

Even when legal help exists, it is often not accessible in a way that supports quick early-stage understanding. Consulting a professional can be expensive, and most available resources are not designed to guide users step-by-step from their raw situation to a structured legal interpretation. On top of that, legal language and processes are typically complex, making it harder for non-lawyers to clearly understand their rights or possible next steps.

Because of this gap, many people either delay taking action, misunderstand the seriousness or nature of their situation, or fail to properly structure their information when they eventually seek help. This weakens their ability to respond effectively and can reduce the quality of any legal support they later receive.

Overall, there is a missing first layer of support — a simple, intelligent system that can take a user’s real-world problem and convert it into structured legal understanding in real time, before the need for formal legal intervention.

**Challenges we ran into**

During development, we initially built BharatLex using a RAG-based approach, but after mentor feedback, we were asked to shift towards a multi-agent system. This required us to redesign the architecture so that different agents could handle specific responsibilities like classification, legal reasoning, and response generation. While this improved structure and modularity, it also introduced complexity in coordination between agents.

We also faced frequent token exhaustion issues while using Gemini, especially since our pipeline involves multiple LLM calls per user request. To address this, we integrated Ollama for local model execution, which allowed us to run certain components directly on local machines. This reduced dependency on external APIs, improved speed during development, and made the system more cost-efficient.

Another challenge was that the multi-agent system was taking too long due to extended internal discussions between agents. In some cases, agents were iterating excessively and consuming unnecessary tokens. To solve this, we optimized the system by limiting interactions to a maximum of two reasoning rounds, ensuring faster responses while still maintaining structured output quality.

Overall, these adjustments helped us balance performance, cost, and system complexity, making BharatLex more efficient and practical for real-world use.

**Vultr**

Our backend is deployed on Vultr Cloud Infrastructure, which provides low-latency compute and reliable scalability for our FastAPI-based system. This ensures that every stage — from transcription to classification to legal reasoning — runs efficiently even under load, making the system deployment-ready rather than just a prototype.

**MongoDB**

For data persistence and structured legal memory, we use MongoDB Atlas. It stores user queries, case classifications, analysis outputs, and generated legal insights in a flexible schema. This is essential for handling unstructured legal narratives and also prepares BharatLex for future RAG-based legal retrieval, where past cases and knowledge can be intelligently reused.

**Sarvam.ai**

We use Sarvam AI – Saaras v3 as our core speech-to-text engine. It enables highly accurate transcription of real-world Indian speech, including mixed languages and informal phrasing. This is critical because users don’t “type legal problems”, they speak them. Saaras v3 allows BharatLex to convert raw voice input into structured text, forming the first step of our legal intelligence pipeline.

**Gen AI&ML**

BharatLex uses Generative AI to transform how consumers understand and respond to legal issues in real time. It leverages large language models to analyze user complaints, classify legal categories, generate structured legal insights, and simulate opposing arguments from the other party. By combining speech-to-text, intelligent reasoning, and text-to-speech systems, the platform provides an end-to-end conversational legal assistance experience that simplifies complex legal scenarios into clear, actionable guidance for everyday users.

### Samarth
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/samarth-b1bf) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Aayan-Sayed/samarth-monorepo) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/jPc1M49od3c) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> Glory to Viltrum

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Many citizens, especially elderly people, rural users, and non-English speakers, struggle to navigate government grievance portals. Existing systems require users to identify the correct department, fill lengthy forms, and understand bureaucratic processes.

As a result, civic issues such as potholes, broken streetlights, garbage accumulation, water leakages, and public infrastructure problems often remain unreported or are reported incorrectly.

Samarth simplifies this process by allowing citizens to simply speak their complaint in their preferred language while AI handles classification, location verification, evidence processing, and complaint preparation.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenge 1: Government Portal Complexity

Different departments have different complaint processes and requirements.

Solution: We built a routing layer that categorizes grievances into relevant civic domains and generates structured complaint packages.

Challenge 2: Multilingual Input

Citizens may report complaints in different languages and dialects.

Solution: We integrated speech recognition and translation workflows to normalize complaints into a common format for processing.

Challenge 3: Location Verification

Accurate grievance routing requires precise location information.

Solution: We implemented GPS-based geotagging and address resolution to associate complaints with their relevant jurisdiction.

Challenge 4: Time Constraints

Building a complete grievance ecosystem within hackathon timelines was difficult.

Solution: We focused on delivering a functional end-to-end AI-assisted reporting workflow that demonstrates real-world impact.

**Gen AI&ML**

Samarth fits strongly within the Gen AI track because it uses artificial intelligence to improve accessibility and efficiency in public grievance reporting.

The platform leverages speech processing, language understanding, location intelligence, and automated complaint generation to reduce barriers between citizens and government services.

By simplifying grievance reporting into a voice-first experience, Samarth makes civic participation more accessible and scalable while demonstrating how AI can be used for public good.

**The problem it solves**

### Empowering Millions via Voice-First Public Services

Across India, hundreds of millions of eligible citizens miss out on life-changing government schemes, scholarships, and welfare benefits. The barriers are deep-rooted:
* **Language Barriers:** Most official portals are only available in English or standard Hindi, alienating regional language speakers.
* **Complex Digital Layouts:** Web forms are often cluttered, confusing, and difficult to navigate for semi-literate or elderly populations.
* **Lack of Awareness:** Finding the exact eligibility criteria among thousands of active schemes is like finding a needle in a haystack.

### 🚀 Our Solution: Bharat Voice Agent
**Bharat Voice Agent** acts as India's voice operating system for public services. It allows users to discover, understand, and apply for schemes entirely through natural voice conversations in their native languages.

* **Multilingual AI Assistant:** Supports conversational speech in 9 major Indian languages (Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Gujarati, Bengali, and English).
* **Smart Profile Extraction:** As citizens speak, the system automatically builds and updates their profile (age, occupation, income, caste category, location) in the background.
* **Context-Aware Retrieval (RAG):** Uses a vector database populated with scraped government schemes to instantly recommend only the schemes for which the citizen is fully eligible.
* **Conversational Document Verification (OCR):** Citizens can upload documents (like Aadhaar cards or Income Certificates), which are processed on-the-fly to verify profile fields.
* **End-to-End Automation:** Automatically generates a pre-filled PDF application draft and integrates with n8n/Selenium web automation to fill out the actual government portals under caseworker supervision (Human-in-the-loop).


---

**Challenges we ran into**

### Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. 🎙️ Multi-Browser Audio Recording Sync
**Hurdle:** When capturing voice inputs, different browsers record audio in different formats (Chrome/Firefox default to audio/webm, while Safari on iOS records in audio/mp4). 
**Solution:** We implemented dynamic MIME-type detection in the frontend. The system detects the browser's recording type, formats the payload dynamically with the matching file extension (webm, .mp4, or .ogg), and sends the corresponding content-type headers so the Sarvam AI STT API receives clean, readable files.

### 2. 🎛️ Orb State Latency & Double-Tapping
**Hurdle:** In early testing, a slight delay in the initialization of the `MediaRecorder` created a window where the voice orb remained in the "idle" visual state. If a user quickly double-tapped, it launched multiple recorder instances, crashing the audio stream.
**Solution:** We updated the event loops to transition the UI to the `recording` state *instantaneously* upon the initial click handler. This immediately switches the orb's action to `stopRecording()`, preventing race conditions and ensuring clean user interactions.

### 3. 🌐 Real-Time Translation Scaling
**Hurdle:** Translating matched scheme details dynamically, eligibility grounds, required documents, and draft form stages into multiple regional languages on-the-fly was causing high LLM latency.
**Solution:** We optimized the backend endpoints to run localized translations concurrently and cached frequently requested scheme matrices to ensure responses return in under a second, maintaining a conversational flow.

**The problem it solves**

**Project Description**
**HackCyberIntel AI – Autonomous Web Security Auditor & Threat Intelligence Platform** is an AI-powered, authorized cybersecurity platform that scans web applications, identifies security weaknesses, and explains the risks in simple, actionable language. It combines a **Chrome Extension** for live, real-time website scanning with a **web dashboard** for detailed reports, scan history, remediation tracking, comparisons, and downloadable PDF exports. Along with automated security analysis, it includes a **conversational AI assistant** that helps users understand findings, ask questions about the latest report, prioritize fixes, and interpret security issues more clearly.

**Problem It Solves**
HackCyberIntel AI solves the problem of raw, technical, and difficult-to-read security reports. Traditional scanners often generate long lists of vulnerabilities without enough context, making it hard for developers, founders, or non-technical users to understand what the issue means, how serious it is, and what to fix first. This project transforms those results into structured, color-coded, and human-readable guidance, helping users improve their security posture faster and with more confidence.

**What Makes It Different**
Unlike conventional scanners and dashboards, HackCyberIntel AI combines a **live blue-scanning Chrome Extension**, a **SOC-style web dashboard**, and a **conversational AI layer** into one platform. Users can visually watch the website being scanned in real time, review findings in a professional report, compare scans over time, and ask the assistant follow-up questions about specific vulnerabilities, evidence, and fixes. It also adds advanced features such as **confidence scoring, false-positive reduction, remediation guidance, attack-surface mapping, security drift tracking, and downloadable chart-based PDF reports**, making it more intelligent and practical than a static scanner.

**Sarvam AI Fit**
HackCyberIntel AI fits the Sarvam AI track because it uses conversational AI to make cybersecurity insights interactive, accessible, and useful for both technical and non-technical users. Sarvam powers the assistant that explains scan findings, summarizes risks, generates remediation guidance in natural language, and helps users explore their security reports through a more human-like conversational experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Challenges I ran into**
One of the biggest challenges while building CyberIntel AI was designing a system that feels powerful and real-time, while still staying safe, modular, and non-destructive. The Chrome Extension had to show a live blue scanning effect and stream scan progress smoothly, while the backend handled crawling, analysis, scoring, and report generation in parallel. Coordinating the extension, web app, and FastAPI backend without breaking the existing scan flow required a clean modular architecture and careful message passing between components.

Another major challenge was dealing with modern web apps that are heavily JavaScript-driven, authenticated, and protected by security controls like Cloudflare, Clerk, and rate limiting. A simple request-based scanner was not enough, so I had to use smarter discovery logic and safe validation checks to inspect headers, routes, forms, cookies, redirects, and exposed endpoints without generating too many false positives. To solve this, I designed the scanner around confidence scoring, multi-signal validation, and clear labels such as confirmed, probable, possible, and blocked.

Generating professional PDF reports was also a challenge because the output needed to be readable for both technical and non-technical users. I solved this by separating raw findings from the explanation layer, adding color-coded severity, charts, evidence blocks, and remediation guidance. Overall, the hardest part was balancing realism, usability, and security accuracy while keeping all existing features intact and making the platform feel like a live SOC + pentest intelligence system.

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
Navigating the financial markets is overwhelming for most retail investors. They suffer from information overload, emotional bias, and the sheer complexity of analyzing technical indicators alongside breaking news. Existing tools are fragmented—forcing users to jump between stock screeners, news feeds, and overly simplistic chatbots that lack deep reasoning.

FinPilot AI tackles these problems by acting as an automated, multi-agent advisory board.

What can people use it for?
Instant Portfolio Analysis: Users can ask the floating Gemini assistant to break down their current portfolio risk or fetch real-time data on specific tickers without leaving the dashboard.
Unbiased Stock Verification: Before buying a stock, users run it through our "Boardroom." The system autonomously aggregates technical indicators (RSI, MACD) and news sentiment, then forces a Bull vs. Bear Debate to expose hidden risks before presenting a final verdict.
Regional Market Participation: Users who are not comfortable with English can interact with the assistant and consume complex financial reports natively in Indian regional languages via Sarvam AI text-to-speech and translation.
How does it make existing tasks easier and safer?
Cures Information Overload (Easier): Instead of reading 15 different news articles and trying to interpret a messy candlestick chart, FinPilot digests unstructured data and structured metrics into a single, cohesive, easy-to-read narrative.
Eliminates Emotional Trading (Safer): The LangGraph-powered adversarial debate ensures that users aren't just presented with a one-sided, overly optimistic view (Confirmation Bias). It actively finds reasons not to trade, protecting capital.
Prevents Action Paralysis (Easier & Safer): Instead of leaving the user to figure out the next steps, the system provides Human-In-The-Loop (HITL) verified trade recommendations. Once approved, it handles the execution safely and automatically generates compliant PDF trade statements via email.

**Challenges we ran into**

markdown
 Challenges We Ran Into

Building a multi-agent system from scratch came with its fair share of architectural and technical hurdles. Here are the most significant challenges we faced and how we overcame them:

 1. The React "Blank Screen" Crash (Tool-Calling Serialization)
**The Hurdle:** While building the Gemini Floating Chat Assistant, our entire React frontend would occasionally crash into a blank screen. We discovered that when the new Gemini models utilized tools (like pinging Alpha Vantage or NewsAPI), the LangChain `response.content` wasn't always a string. Sometimes, it returned a multimodal `list of objects`. When this JSON payload hit the frontend, React tried to render an object directly as a React child, which triggered an unhandled runtime exception and instantly killed the UI tree.
**The Fix:** We rewrote the backend `/ask` endpoint to include a robust parsing mechanism. We explicitly intercepted the response, checked if it was a list of dicts, extracted the `"text"` keys from the tool-call objects, and forcefully cast the final payload to a guaranteed string before sending it to the client.

 2. LangGraph State Collisions & Race Conditions
**The Hurdle:** In our "Boardroom", we had multiple agents (Market, News, Technical) scraping data simultaneously before passing it to the Bull vs. Bear debate node. Initially, data was overwriting itself in the global state, leading to the LLM hallucinating market prices based on news data.
**The Fix:** We implemented a strict **State-Machine Architecture** using LangGraph's `MemorySaver`. We created a dedicated `aggregator_node` that waits for all parallel agents to finish their execution, cleanly formatting the data into distinct keys (`market_data`, `news_data`, `technical_data`) within the `AgentState` before passing it down the pipeline.

 3. Async Event Loop Conflicts with Tool Execution
**The Hurdle:** Mixing synchronous tools (like `yfinance` dataframe downloading) with asynchronous tools (like `httpx.AsyncClient` used for Sarvam AI's translation API) inside a unified Gemini agent loop caused `asyncio` thread errors. FastAPIs event loop clashed with LangChain’s internal agent execution.
**The Fix:** We completely transitioned the agent orchestrator to use LangChain's native `ainvoke()`. By decorating our I/O-heavy tools with `@tool async def` and utilizing Python's `asyncio.to_thread` for blocking yfinance tasks, we achieved a non-blocking, fully asynchronous pipeline that handles both heavy data fetching and immediate Sarvam AI API calls flawlessly.
```

**Sarvam.ai**

###  How We Integrated Sarvam AI
To make advanced financial intelligence accessible across India, we deeply integrated **Sarvam AI** into the core workflow of FinPilot. Our platform breaks down the massive language barriers typically found in algorithmic trading and complex financial analytics through two primary implementations:
#### 1. Real-Time Regional Language Translation
Financial terms and stock queries are often difficult to express in English for many retail investors in India. 
- We integrated the `translate_to_english_sarvam` tool directly into our **Gemini-powered Floating Chat Assistant**.
- When a user asks a question in a regional language (e.g., Hindi), the system autonomously triggers Sarvam's API (`hi-IN` to `en-IN`) to accurately translate the query into English *before* running market algorithms, ensuring the underlying AI and data scrapers work perfectly regardless of the user's native tongue.
#### 2. Native Indian Text-to-Speech (TTS)
Reading dense, multi-page financial reports or debate summaries can be exhausting. 
- We implemented Sarvam's high-fidelity `bulbul:v3` Generative Voice model via the `/voice/synthesize` endpoint. 
- Instead of using robotic, generic western text-to-speech, FinPilot reads out the final Boardroom synthesis and market summaries using highly natural, context-aware Indian accents (e.g., the "tanya" voice profile). This makes consuming daily portfolio risk metrics as easy as listening to a local news anchor.

**Gen AI&ML**

###  How We Leverage Gen AI & Machine Learning
FinPilot AI goes far beyond a simple wrapper around an LLM. It showcases an advanced, multi-layered integration of **Generative AI** and **Machine Learning** to handle complex, real-world financial workflows:
#### 1. Multi-Agent Orchestration (LangGraph)
Instead of relying on a single prompt to answer user queries, we implemented an autonomous **State-Machine architecture via LangGraph**. This allows us to orchestrate multiple specialized AI agents (Market, Technical, News) to run in parallel. It completely redefines the workflow by separating data aggregation from reasoning, drastically reducing hallucinations.
#### 2. Specialized LLM Debate Mechanisms
One of our most cutting-edge Gen AI implementations is the **Bull vs. Bear Debate System**. We use high-speed LLMs (Groq Llama-3.3 70B) to pit two distinct personas against each other. This adversarial approach forces the AI to challenge its own assumptions before reaching a conclusion, mimicking a real-world financial advisory board.
#### 3. Agentic Tool Calling (ReAct Patterns)
Our floating Gemini chat assistant doesn’t just generate text—it takes action. By leveraging advanced **Tool Calling / ReAct Patterns**, the Gemini model acts as a reasoning engine capable of deciding *when* and *how* to ping external APIs (like Alpha Vantage and NewsAPI) to fetch live data on the fly.
#### 4. NLP-Powered Sentiment Analysis (FinBERT)
We don't just rely on Generative AI for everything. For highly specific classification tasks, we use **ProsusAI FinBERT**—a specialized, fine-tuned transformer model. This allows us to rapidly classify thousands of real-time financial headlines into positive, negative, or neutral sentiment with extreme accuracy, which is then fed into the Gen AI pipeline as context.
#### 5. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
To process vast amounts of unstructured financial documents, we employ **ChromaDB** alongside sentence transformers. This vector-based semantic search allows our RAG agents to retrieve mathematically similar contextual snippets, enabling the LLM to synthesize precise reports grounded purely in the provided documents.
#### 6. Cross-Lingual Generative Speech (TTS)
We demonstrate true multimodal AI by implementing **Sarvam AI** and **ElevenLabs**. The system isn't just generating text; it is translating massive financial context into Indian regional languages and utilizing state-of-the-art Generative Voice models to read out boardroom summaries naturally.

> ai prescription

![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![JSON](https://img.shields.io/badge/JSON-333333?style=flat-square) ![Streamlit](https://img.shields.io/badge/Streamlit-333333?style=flat-square) ![RAG](https://img.shields.io/badge/RAG-333333?style=flat-square) ![gemini](https://img.shields.io/badge/gemini-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

This project eliminates manual medicine lookup and prescription writing by instantly matching symptoms to conditions, suggesting exact dosages, and generating a downloadable PDF prescription in seconds.

Manual lookup elimination – Doctors no longer need to search reference books or memorize every medicine–symptom pair.

Prescription speed – From symptoms → matched conditions → final PDF prescription in under 30 seconds.

Error reduction – Shows exact dosages from a trusted knowledge base, lowering risk of wrong medicine or dose.

Documentation ease – One‑click generates a printable PDF with patient name, date, medicines, and signature line.

Low‑cost & offline‑ready – Uses free Gemini/OpenRouter tiers; retrieval works without internet, making it accessible for resource‑limited clinics.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Generalized Challenges Faced

- **Ensuring hallucination‑free medical answers** – LLMs tend to invent medicines or dosages not present in the knowledge base. Solved by strict prompt engineering, forcing JSON output, and always grounding responses in retrieved context with no external knowledge.
- **Balancing retrieval precision vs. recall** – Fuzzy matching on condition names missed many symptom descriptions, while full BM25 returned too much irrelevant noise. Hybrid retrieval (BM25 + keyword + symptom‑section matching) was tuned with threshold scoring.
- **Handling rate limits and API failures gracefully** – Free API tiers are unpredictable. Implemented exponential backoff, retries, and fallback to pure retrieval when API is unavailable.
- **Designing an interactive UI that preserves state** – Streamlit’s rerun model made it hard to keep prescription selections across button clicks. Used session state with per‑message keys and forced reruns only when necessary.
- **Processing unstructured medical text into structured prescriptions** – Dosages come in free‑text formats (e.g., “500–650 mg 3–4 times daily”). Parsing and representing them cleanly in JSON/PDF required custom cleaning and Unicode normalization.
- **Making the system provider‑agnostic** – Initially tied to Gemini, then needed to support OpenRouter, OpenAI, and potentially local models. Abstracted the API client and used OpenAI‑compatible interfaces where possible.

**Gemini**

**Gemini acts as the generative reasoning engine** in a RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipeline.

1. **Context retrieval first** – The system queries a local medical JSON tree using BM25 + fuzzy matching to pull relevant condition-specific content (symptoms, medicines, dosages).

2. **Gemini generates structured output** – The retrieved context is fed to Gemini with a strict prompt that forces JSON output. Two modes:
   - **Symptom query** → Gemini returns `{"matched_conditions": [...]}` with condition names, medicine names, and exact dosages.
   - **Informational query** → Gemini returns `{"content": "..."}` with a concise natural language answer.

3. **Enforced JSON schema** – Uses Gemini's `response_mime_type="application/json"` parameter to guarantee parseable output without extra text.

4. **No hallucination** – Gemini is explicitly instructed to base answers **only** on the provided context, never inventing medicines or dosages.

5. **Free‑tier friendly** – Configured for `gemini-2.5-flash` (20 free requests/day) with rate‑limit handling and exponential backoff.

> **Gemini’s role**: Convert retrieved medical text → structured prescription data (JSON) → displayed in an interactive table → exportable PDF.

**Gen AI&ML**

### 1. **Retrieval‑Augmented Generation (RAG)**  
The project implements a complete RAG pipeline:
- **Retrieval**: Hybrid search (BM25 + fuzzy matching + section detection) fetches relevant medical knowledge from a structured JSON tree.
- **Generation**: An LLM (Gemini / OpenRouter) synthesizes answers strictly from retrieved context – no hallucinations.

### 2. **Large Language Model Integration**  
- Uses cutting‑edge LLMs (`gemini-2.5-flash`, `gpt-4o-mini`) for two tasks:
  - Symptom → condition mapping and medicine extraction (structured JSON).
  - Natural language answers for informational queries.
- Demonstrates prompt engineering, response schema enforcement, and JSON mode.

### 3. **Structured Output from Unstructured Input**  
- Converts free‑text symptom descriptions (e.g., *"I have fever and nausea"*) into a structured `matched_conditions` JSON.
- This is a core Gen AI challenge – getting reliable, parseable output from LLMs.

### 4. **Machine Learning Components**  
- **BM25** – classic statistical ranking algorithm for information retrieval.
- **Fuzzy matching (rapidfuzz)** – string similarity to align user queries with condition names.
- **Hybrid retrieval** – combines lexical (BM25) and rule‑based (keyword mapping) methods.

### 5. **End‑to‑End Application**  
- Complete pipeline: user query → retrieval → LLM generation → interactive prescription builder → PDF export.
- Real‑world medical decision support use case – not a toy demo.

### 6. **Model Agnosticism**  
- Supports Gemini, OpenRouter, OpenAI, and can be extended to local models (Ollama, LM Studio). Demonstrates practical LLM deployment flexibility.

### 7. **Evaluation & Safety**  
- Output is grounded in a trusted knowledge base (no external hallucination).  
- Dose recommendations come directly from context – no invented information.

> This project showcases **Gen AI in production**: RAG, structured generation, multi‑model support, and a usable clinical tool – all core themes of the Gen AI / ML track.

**The problem it solves**

# Viral Arena

## The Problem It Solves

Most people validate ideas by asking a single AI, a friend, or an online community.

The problem is that each source provides only one perspective, while real-world success depends on how many different people react to an idea.

An idea may excite investors, attract consumers, raise concerns among skeptics, or reveal opportunities spotted by trend watchers. Gathering all these viewpoints traditionally takes significant time and effort.

**Viral Arena solves this by providing multiple perspectives instantly through AI personas that discuss, challenge, and evaluate an idea together.**

---

## What Can People Use It For?

### Idea Validation
Test startup, product, or business ideas before investing time and resources into building them.

### Finding Strengths and Weaknesses
Discover what people might love, criticize, question, or improve about an idea.

### Opportunity Discovery
Identify hidden use cases, target audiences, and growth opportunities that may otherwise be overlooked.

### Faster Feedback
Receive diverse opinions and discussions in seconds instead of spending days gathering feedback from multiple sources.

---

## How It Makes Existing Tasks Easier

Instead of asking one AI and receiving one answer, users receive a discussion between multiple AI personas with different viewpoints.

This helps users:

- Validate ideas faster
- Spot risks earlier
- Discover opportunities sooner
- Make better decisions before building

---

## Vision

Before spending months building a product, let your idea survive the arena first.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Technical Challenges & Solutions

During the development of the **Viral Arena** debate and simulation platform, we encountered several challenging bugs across state synchronization, subprocess lifecycle management, and web concurrency. Below is an overview of these hurdles and how they were resolved.

---

### 1. WebSocket Concurrency & `KeyError` Server Crashes

#### **The Hurdle**
During rapid page refreshes or quick room transitions, the backend server would occasionally crash with a `KeyError` inside the WebSocket connection manager. 

#### **The Root Cause**
FastAPI yields event loop control during WebSocket connection steps (`await websocket.accept()`). If a client disconnected mid-transition, the synchronous `disconnect()` handler was triggered concurrently. When the connection task resumed, it tried to clean up a room key that had already been deleted from the active connections dict.

#### **The Solution**
We implemented safe dictionary checks inside `ws_manager.py` to ensure room keys and connection indexes exist before removal:
```python
def disconnect(self, room_id: str, websocket: WebSocket, participant_id: str):
    if room_id in self.active_connections:
        # Safely remove connection without raising KeyError
        if websocket in self.active_connections[room_id]:
            self.active_connections[room_id].remove(websocket)
        if not self.active_connections[room_id]:
            del self.active_connections[room_id]
```

---

### 2. Orphaned Debate Subprocesses (Resource Leak)

#### **The Hurdle**
If a user left the debate room or paused the debate, the AI agents' background processes (orchestrating LLM calls) would continue running in the background, consuming CPU and memory.

#### **The Root Cause**
The Python backend spawned simulation scripts in background tasks via `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec`. When the WebSocket closed, the backend did not explicitly stop these running subprocesses, leaving them orphaned.

#### **The Solution**
We created a tracking registry for active processes (`active_debates`) and implemented an explicit termination hook. 
* When a room connection count reaches `0` (or the debate is paused), the backend kills the process and cleans up:
```python
async def kill_debate_subprocess(room_id: str):
    process = active_debates.get(room_id)
    if process:
        try:
            process.kill()  # Force kill the background script
        except Exception:
            pass
```

---

### 3. Double Audio Playback & Re-Request Failures

#### **The Hurdle**
When users toggled the ElevenLabs TTS voice feature on and off, the audio would occasionally double-play or attempt to reload a temporary audio file that had already been deleted, resulting in browser `404` errors in the console.

#### **The Root Cause**
The React component re-rendered elements when WebSocket messages arrived, causing `<audio>` tags to mount again and trigger autoplay.

#### **The Solution**
We introduced a tracking system (`playedAudioIds` state) on the frontend component.
1. When an audio segment finishes playing, its ID is logged.
2. The `<audio>` component is dynamically unmounted from the DOM:
```typescript
{message.audio_url && !playedAudioIds.has(message.id) && (
  <audio
    src={message.audio_url}
    autoPlay
    onEnded={() => {
      setPlayedAudioIds(prev => new Set(prev).add(message.id))
      // Notify backend to clean up file
      sendJsonMessage({ type: "audio_finished", message_id: message.id })
    }}
  />
)}
```

---

### 4. Rigid Localhost and Port Overrides

#### **The Hurdle**
Preparing for deployment was difficult because the API backend was hardcoded to `http://localhost:8000` throughout the frontend code, and npm scripts hardcoded the Vite port to `3000`.

#### **The Solution**
* **Frontend**: Extracted the API URL to a central utility with a fallback:
  ```typescript
  export const API_URL = import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || 'http://localhost:8000'
  ```
* **Vite Config**: Modified `vite.config.ts` to respect dynamic environment ports:
  ```typescript
  server: {
    port: process.env.PORT ? parseInt(process.env.PORT, 10) : 3000
  }
  ```
* **Backend**: Added a post-initialization setting check to dynamically bind to `$PORT` variables supplied by Render.

**MongoDB**

## MongoDB Collections in ViralArena

**MongoDB stores 5 main collections:**

1. **ProductIdea** - User-submitted ideas awaiting debate (title, description, image_url, link, roast_mode flag, timestamps)

2. **ChatRoom** - Debate sessions per idea (links to product_idea, tracks agent_ids, status, created/ended times)

3. **Message** - All debate interactions (sender info, message_type, content, timestamps, room_id reference)

4. **Persona** - AI agent personality profiles (name, stance, personality_traits, system_prompt for behavior)

5. **AgentState** - Real-time agent status in each room (agent_id, room_id, status enum, last_message_index, thinking_data)

**Why this structure:** Ideas flow through ChatRooms as Personas debate via Messages, with AgentState tracking each agent's progress. All records are document-based for flexible schema and async-ready with Motor driver for real-time WebSocket updates.

**Open Innovation**

# ViralArena & Open Innovation

**ViralArena democratizes idea validation by simulating diverse stakeholder feedback through multiple AI personas in real-time.** Instead of seeking opinions sequentially, users instantly get perspectives from investors, marketers, skeptics, and consumers debating ideas together—compressing weeks of external feedback loops into minutes and embodying open innovation principles of leveraging external viewpoints to reduce launch risk.

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem It Solves

Every year, thousands of patients and their families struggle to find compatible blood donors during medical emergencies. Existing solutions are largely passive — they provide donor directories, blood bank listings, or request posting systems, but leave the burden of coordination on patients and hospitals.

The process is often slow, fragmented, and stressful. Patients must manually search for donors, make dozens of calls, verify donor eligibility, coordinate hospital visits, schedule appointments, and manage follow-ups. During emergencies, every minute matters, yet there is no intelligent system that actively manages the entire blood support lifecycle.

SanjeevaniX solves this problem by introducing an AI-powered Blood Intelligence Platform that autonomously coordinates blood support from start to finish.

Using AI voice agents, donor intelligence, memory systems, predictive analytics, and real-time coordination workflows, SanjeevaniX can:

• Search and identify compatible blood donors.
• Verify donor eligibility and availability.
• Automatically contact donors using AI voice agents.
• Schedule appointments through Google Calendar.
• Send SMS reminders and notifications.
• Track donation journeys in real time.
• Maintain long-term donor pools for Thalassemia patients.
• Predict donor availability and future blood shortages.
• Learn from previous donor interactions using AI memory and vector databases.

Instead of merely helping users find donors, SanjeevaniX actively coordinates the entire process until blood support is successfully secured.

The result is faster response times, reduced manual effort, improved donor engagement, better patient outcomes, and potentially life-saving intervention during critical moments.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

Building SanjeevaniX required integrating multiple AI and automation systems into a single autonomous workflow, which introduced several technical challenges.

One major challenge was coordinating communication between AI voice agents, donor databases, appointment scheduling systems, and workflow automation. We needed the system to automatically move from donor discovery to donor verification, appointment scheduling, notifications, and status tracking without human intervention.

Another challenge was handling donor availability intelligently. A donor may not answer calls, may reject requests, or may be temporarily unavailable. We solved this by implementing automated escalation logic that continuously searches backup donors, expands search radiuses, and retries coordination workflows instead of stopping after the first failure.

Google Calendar integration was another hurdle. The system needed to check calendar availability, create donation appointments, synchronize schedules, and notify all stakeholders automatically. This required careful orchestration through n8n workflows and AI-driven appointment coordination.

We also wanted the platform to learn from previous donor interactions. To solve this, we introduced a memory architecture using Pinecone vector databases and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Donor conversations, acceptance history, preferences, and response patterns are stored and retrieved to improve future matching decisions.

The biggest challenge was transforming a traditional blood donation workflow into a fully autonomous AI healthcare coordination system. Through VAPI, n8n, OpenAI, Pinecone, Google Calendar, and Twilio integrations, we successfully built an end-to-end solution that actively manages blood support rather than simply displaying donor information.

**Best Hack Built using n8n**

# Why SanjeevaniX Fits the Best Hack Built Using n8n Track

SanjeevaniX is powered by n8n at its core, using workflow automation to transform a traditionally manual and fragmented blood donation process into an autonomous AI-driven coordination system.

n8n acts as the operational brain of the platform, orchestrating every critical workflow across multiple services and stakeholders. When a blood request is created, n8n automatically triggers donor matching, AI voice outreach, donor verification, appointment scheduling, notifications, memory updates, and dashboard synchronization without requiring human intervention.

Our workflow integrates multiple technologies through n8n, including:

• VAPI AI Voice Agents for donor outreach and patient communication
• OpenAI for transcript analysis, reasoning, and decision making
• Pinecone Vector Database for donor memory and RAG-based retrieval
• Google Sheets for request and donor management
• Google Calendar for appointment scheduling and reminders
• Twilio for automated SMS notifications
• Real-time dashboards for tracking and monitoring operations

Using n8n, we built autonomous workflows that:

• Analyze donor conversations in real time
• Automatically determine donor acceptance or rejection
• Store donor behavior and preferences for future decisions
• Retrieve historical donor data through vector search
• Schedule appointments automatically through Google Calendar
• Send personalized notifications to patients and donors
• Escalate searches from city-level to national-level networks when needed
• Continuously update records and dashboards across the ecosystem

Instead of functioning as a simple automation tool, n8n serves as the orchestration layer that connects AI, communication systems, databases, scheduling platforms, and healthcare workflows into a single intelligent operating system.

SanjeevaniX demonstrates how n8n can be used to build production-grade autonomous systems capable of coordinating life-critical healthcare operations at scale.

**Gemini**

# Why SanjeevaniX Fits the Google Gemini Track

SanjeevaniX uses Google Gemini Flash as a core intelligence component within its AI workflow.

Gemini Flash is used for real-time transcript analysis, conversation understanding, donor response interpretation, and decision-making during blood donation coordination calls.

After every donor interaction, Gemini analyzes the conversation transcript and determines:

• Whether the donor accepted or rejected the request
• Donor intent and confidence level
• Availability indicators
• Preferred communication methods
• Future donor preferences and behavioral insights

This allows SanjeevaniX to move beyond simple keyword matching and instead understand natural human conversations.

Gemini enables the platform to make intelligent decisions, automate donor qualification workflows, improve future donor matching, and maintain contextual memory across interactions.

By leveraging Gemini Flash for real-world healthcare coordination and conversational reasoning, SanjeevaniX demonstrates a practical and impactful application of Google's AI technology.

**ElevenLabs**

# Why SanjeevaniX Fits the ElevenLabs Track

SanjeevaniX uses ElevenLabs voice technology to create natural, human-like communication between the AI system, donors, and patients.

The platform uses the Sarah voice model from ElevenLabs as the voice of Sanjeevani, our AI Blood Intelligence Assistant.

Through ElevenLabs, SanjeevaniX is able to:

• Conduct realistic donor outreach calls
• Communicate with patients during emergencies
• Verify donor availability and eligibility
• Schedule blood donation appointments
• Deliver appointment reminders and updates
• Provide multilingual and emotionally aware interactions

In healthcare emergencies, trust and clarity are critical. The natural conversational quality of ElevenLabs helps create a more comfortable and reassuring experience compared to traditional automated phone systems.

By integrating the Sarah voice model into our autonomous donor coordination workflows, SanjeevaniX demonstrates how advanced voice AI can be used for real-world healthcare operations and life-saving communication.

**Open Innovation**

# Why SanjeevaniX Fits the Open Innovation Track

SanjeevaniX aligns strongly with the Open Innovation track because it reimagines how critical healthcare resources are coordinated using AI, automation, and intelligent decision-making.

Rather than creating another blood donor directory, we built an autonomous coordination system that actively manages the entire process of blood support. The platform combines AI voice agents, workflow automation, predictive intelligence, donor memory, appointment orchestration, and real-time communication into a single operational layer.

The innovation extends beyond blood donation. The architecture can be adapted to solve a wide range of resource-matching and emergency coordination challenges, including organ donor networks, ambulance dispatch systems, hospital bed allocation, medical volunteer coordination, disaster response logistics, and public health outreach programs.

What makes SanjeevaniX unique is its ability to learn from historical interactions. Using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector databases, and donor intelligence, the system continuously improves its decision-making by understanding donor behavior, availability patterns, response rates, and previous outcomes.

The platform also integrates multiple technologies into a unified ecosystem:

• AI Voice Agents for autonomous communication
• Vector Memory for long-term learning
• Predictive Analytics for donor availability forecasting
• Workflow Automation for operational execution
• Calendar and Notification Systems for appointment management
• Real-Time Dashboards for monitoring and coordination

This project demonstrates how emerging AI technologies can be applied to solve complex societal challenges that traditionally rely on manual coordination and fragmented systems.

SanjeevaniX is not just a healthcare application; it is an open, scalable innovation framework capable of transforming how critical resources are discovered, coordinated, and delivered in time-sensitive situations.

**The problem it solves**

# The Problem It Solves

Modern JavaScript development heavily depends on open-source packages from npm. While this speeds up development, it also introduces a serious security risk: developers install dependencies blindly without knowing if they are safe, compromised, or malicious.

Existing tools like `npm audit` only detect **known vulnerabilities**, but they fail to catch:

* Newly compromised packages (supply-chain attacks)
* Malicious install scripts (`postinstall`, `preinstall`)
* Typosquatting or fake packages
* Suspicious runtime behavior in code
* Zero-day or newly injected malware in popular libraries

As a result, attackers can silently inject malicious code into widely used packages and compromise thousands of applications before any official vulnerability report exists.

---

# What Our Tool Does

Safe-Install acts as a **security gateway before package installation**.

Instead of directly running:

```bash
npm install axios
```

developers use:

```bash
safe-install axios
```

Our system then:

* Scans the package across multiple security layers (vulnerabilities, threat intelligence, reputation, scripts, AST analysis, correlation engine)
* Detects suspicious or malicious behavior before installation
* Explains risks in simple, human-readable language using AI
* Suggests fixes and safer alternatives
* Either allows, warns, or blocks installation based on risk severity

---

# How It Makes Development Safer & Easier

### 1. Prevents Supply-Chain Attacks

Blocks malicious or compromised packages before they are installed into the project.

### 2. Saves Developer Time

No need to manually check CVEs, GitHub advisories, or security reports.

### 3. Explains Risks Clearly

Instead of technical logs or scores, developers get:

* Why the package is risky
* What can go wrong (impact)
* How to fix it
* Which version to use instead

### 4. Reduces Human Error

Developers often ignore warnings like `npm audit`. Our tool actively intervenes before installation.

### 5. Works Seamlessly in Existing Workflow

No change in ecosystem—just replace `npm install` with `safe-install`.

---

# In Simple Terms

Safe-Install is like a **security guard for npm** that checks every package before it enters your project, explains the risk like a senior developer, and stops dangerous code from ever reaching your system.

**Challenges we ran into**

# Challenges I Ran Into

## 1. Too many false positives

Early versions incorrectly flagged safe packages (like Axios) due to simple checks like `process.env`.

**Fix:**
Switched to a **layered scoring system** where risks are only serious when multiple suspicious signals combine.

---

## 2. Designing meaningful risk logic

Single signals (CVE, scripts, code patterns) were not enough to judge malicious behavior.

**Fix:**
Built a **correlation engine** that combines multiple weak signals into a final severity score.

---

## 3. Handling npm package analysis safely

Extracting and analyzing packages without installing them was tricky.

**Fix:**
Used npm tarball download + temporary extraction instead of direct install.

---

## 4. Inconsistent AI responses

AI outputs were unstructured and hard to display in CLI.

**Fix:**
Forced a **strict structured response format (why, impact, fix, alternative)**.

---

## 5. Balancing strictness vs usability

Over-strict rules blocked safe packages; loose rules missed risks.

**Fix:**
Introduced **SAFE / WARNING / CRITICAL** levels with optional override flow.

**Gemini**

We use **Gemini AI only for explanation, not detection**.

It takes structured security findings from our backend and converts them into:

* Human-readable risk explanations
* Real-world impact (e.g., credential theft, RCE risk)
* Recommended fixes and safer alternatives
* Developer-friendly guidance

### Example

Instead of:

> “postinstall + process.env + network request detected”

Gemini outputs:

> “This package may leak AWS credentials and environment variables to external servers during installation.”

---

## Why this matters

* Makes security understandable for developers
* Turns technical findings into actionable insights
* Improves adoption by reducing complexity

**MongoDB**

Our project uses **MongoDB as the threat intelligence and scan history database**.

We store:

* Known vulnerable packages (CVE data)
* Previously detected malicious packages
* Scan results for each dependency check
* Risk scores and metadata history
* Repeated attack patterns (e.g., compromised versions like supply-chain incidents)

### Why this matters

MongoDB enables:

* Fast lookup of vulnerabilities during scans
* Continuous learning from past detections
* Building a growing internal security intelligence layer

 **MongoDB acts as the memory of our security engine.**

**CyberSecurity**

# Why This Project Fits in the Cybersecurity Track

This project directly addresses **software supply-chain security**, which is one of the fastest-growing areas in cybersecurity today.



## 1. Protects against Supply-Chain Attacks

Modern attacks often happen through open-source dependencies (npm packages), where attackers inject malicious code into trusted libraries.

Our tool prevents this by analyzing packages **before installation**, stopping threats before they enter the system.



## 2. Detects Real-World Attack Vectors

It analyzes common exploitation techniques such as:

* Malicious install scripts (`postinstall`, `preinstall`)
* Credential theft via `process.env`
* Remote code execution patterns
* Compromised package versions and CVEs

These are the exact techniques used in real npm supply-chain attacks.



## 3. Prevents Zero-Day Dependency Threats

Unlike traditional tools that rely only on known CVEs, our system also flags suspicious behavior in **new or unreported malicious packages**, making it relevant for emerging threats.



## 4. Shifts Security Left (Pre-Install Protection)

Instead of detecting issues after installation or during runtime, our tool enforces security **before the package is installed**, aligning with modern “shift-left security” practices.



## 5. Improves Developer Security Awareness

It not only blocks threats but also explains:

* Why a package is risky
* What damage it can cause
* How to fix or replace it

This helps developers make informed security decisions.

---

## Finally

This project fits the cybersecurity track because it actively prevents, detects, and explains **real-world software supply-chain attacks** before they reach the developer’s environment, making open-source usage safer and more transparent.

### Kinetix
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/kinetix-6430) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/I-iUsha/KINETIX) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/_8Je6L2kcVw?si=tuiE2x108OhzNjog) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> validates before output

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SciPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/SciPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AI-generated 3D scenes often contain unrealistic placements such as floating objects, blocked pathways, overlapping furniture, or unstable structures. KINETIX acts as a validation and repair layer between AI agents and 3D engines, automatically detecting physical and accessibility issues, explaining why they occur, and generating fixes. This enables safer, more realistic, and production-ready virtual environments.

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/1c5aa580150a4e00b141c1c5056bcfc1/bdd78ce8-74ac-4ec3-990a-13595d51e78a.jpeg)

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was ensuring reliable stability validation. Early versions relied on physics drop simulations, which produced inconsistent results across different assets and environments. We replaced this with a deterministic center-of-mass-over-support-polygon stability margin, making validation faster, reproducible, and easier to explain. We also faced coordinate-system mismatches between 3D formats, solved through a single canonical world-space adapter.

**Gemini**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/1c5aa580150a4e00b141c1c5056bcfc1/5cb4c157-6487-4858-9e6f-912dc5ace800.jpeg)

KINETIX uses Gemini as its semantic intelligence layer. Gemini analyzes uploaded 3D assets and natural-language scene instructions to identify object classes, materials, and affordances. This understanding is combined with KINETIX's physics-validation cortex, which checks stability, collisions, accessibility, and constraints. Together, they enable AI-generated 3D worlds that are both context-aware and physically valid.

**Open Innovation**

KINETIX addresses a cross-industry challenge: AI-generated 3D environments often ignore physical reality, creating unstable, inaccessible, or unusable scenes. Our platform acts as a universal validation layer between AI agents and 3D engines, making virtual worlds physically grounded and trustworthy. Its applications span gaming, robotics, simulation, architecture, digital twins, accessibility auditing, and AI-powered content creation, making it a strong Open Innovation solution.

> AI Powered WEB3 Governance Simulator

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Three.JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Three.JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

![image](https://assets.devfolio.co/content/06f177561dbe4fefad3d60503c283052/d3d299fb-56d5-4de7-9daa-ede1dcaebbc8.jpeg)

Parallel Earth DAO solves the problem of understanding and testing decentralized governance systems before they affect real communities, economies, or organizations. Today, most DAO and governance platforms only allow voting and treasury management, but they do not help people visualize the long-term societal consequences of those decisions.

Our platform creates a live AI-powered governance simulation where users can experiment with proposals, economic policies, treasury allocation, crisis management, and governance structures inside a dynamic digital civilization. Instead of relying only on charts or spreadsheets, users can actually see how governance decisions impact participation, inequality, infrastructure growth, economic stability, and societal health in real time.

The platform also makes decentralized governance more transparent and accessible through AI-powered policy explanations, blockchain-backed proposal verification, and wallet-based participation using MetaMask. By combining AI, Web3, and procedural simulation, Parallel Earth DAO helps researchers, DAO communities, students, and future digital governments better understand how decentralized societies may evolve and how governance decisions can shape entire ecosystems over time.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges we faced was integrating multiple advanced systems, AI governance agents, procedural 3D rendering, MetaMask/Web3 functionality, and real-time simulation, into a single stable platform. The 3D civilization system was the biggest headache, especially while importing and optimizing large evolving city assets and handling real-time rendering performance. We used Draco Loader compression techniques to optimize heavy 3D models and improve loading efficiency inside the browser.

During deployment, we also encountered hydration mismatches and strict Content Security Policy issues that caused parts of the UI and blockchain integrations to break in production. We solved this by restructuring unstable client-side components, optimizing rendering behavior, and carefully adjusting deployment security policies to support modern Web3 and AI systems safely.

Another challenge was making the governance simulation feel meaningful rather than cosmetic, so we connected proposal outcomes directly to treasury behavior, participation levels, inequality metrics, and even the evolution or collapse of the procedural civilization itself.

**BlockChain & Web3**

Parallel Earth DAO fits into both Blockchain and Web3 because it models a decentralized governance ecosystem where users interact through wallet-based participation, transparent proposal systems, DAO economics, and blockchain-backed verification instead of centralized control. MetaMask integration and cryptographic proposal anchoring ensure governance actions are verifiable and tamper-proof using Ethereum-compatible Web3 infrastructure.

At the same time, the platform pushes Web3 beyond simple transactions by combining AI governance councils, real-time treasury and participation analytics, and an evolving procedural civilization that visually reacts to governance outcomes — creating a simulation of how future AI-assisted decentralized digital societies could operate.

### ExoCompute
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/exocompute-4ac2) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/yasser-XD/exocompute.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://exocompute.vercel.app/) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/jJpxx8Vom9c?si=OsLdqWhU3Sr4OoSO) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> The Zero-Friction,Browser-Based P2P Edge Inference

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ExoCompute bridges the gap between expensive AI demand and wasted consumer supply by eliminating the friction of entry.

By running AI inference models natively inside a standard web browser (using WebGPU and WebAssembly), ExoCompute allows any user to monetize their idle laptop instantly just by opening a web link. It provides developers with a hyper-local, low-cost decentralized inference network, and gives everyday consumers a frictionless path to passive income.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The SharedArrayBuffer Crash

Hurdle: Multi-threaded WebAssembly (WASM) execution silently failed because modern browsers block SharedArrayBuffer by default to prevent side-channel attacks.

Fix: We configured our Node.js server to globally inject strict cross-origin isolation headers (COOP/COEP), allowing the WebGPU and WASM pipelines to fire up securely.

2. "Thundering Herd" Task Duplication

Hurdle: Because our Orchestrator broadcasts tasks to all nodes simultaneously for speed, multiple laptops were computing the same task, causing wallets to double-count earnings.

Fix: We built a "First-Response-Wins" architecture. The server maps incoming webhooks to unique UUIDs in an active Set. The first node to return the calculation gets paid, and subsequent redundant results are silently dropped.

3. Network Bandwidth Choking

Hurdle: Our 20MB edge AI model kept re-downloading every time a worker browser tab refreshed, which would have killed our local network on the demo floor.

Fix: We explicitly forced env.useBrowserCache = true in Transformers.js. This utilized the browser's native Cache API to store the quantized model locally, dropping subsequent load times to milliseconds with zero network payload.

4. Wiring Pre-Built UI to a Vibe-Coded Backend

Hurdle: Merging our manually crafted static UI screens with the rapidly generated backend engine caused WebSocket routing and asset conflicts.

Fix: We avoided heavy bundlers like Vite or Webpack entirely. By mapping Express to serve the static folder directly and exclusively using vanilla JS ES Modules via CDN, we kept the architecture completely flat and conflict-free.

**Vultr**

To make ExoCompute a truly viable product, our central orchestration engine required an ultra-reliable, low-latency environment. While the actual AI inference happens on decentralized edge browsers, the backbone routing those tasks must never go down. We deployed our Node.js and Socket.io Master Orchestrator directly onto a Vultr Cloud Compute instance.

Here is exactly how Vultr powered our architecture:

High-Frequency WebSocket Hub: The core of ExoCompute relies on maintaining hundreds of simultaneous WebSocket connections with consumer browsers while instantly broadcasting AI task matrices. Vultr’s high-performance compute environment provided the CPU stability and ultra-low latency network required to handle the "Thundering Herd" of micro-telemetry data without dropping a single node connection.

Production Webhook Gateway: Relying on temporary local tunnels (like ngrok) is a massive point of failure for Twilio WhatsApp webhooks. We utilized our Vultr instance to establish a permanent, secure, and dedicated ingress gateway (via an Nginx reverse proxy). This guaranteed that when a judge sends a WhatsApp prompt, the webhook is ingested, parsed, and distributed by Vultr in milliseconds.

Proximity to the Database: By deploying our Vultr instance strategically, we minimized the network hop latency between our WebSocket orchestrator and our MongoDB Atlas cluster, ensuring that our real-time reputation scoring and routing algorithms could execute flawlessly on the fly.

Vultr provided the exact high-speed, reliable cloud backbone necessary to orchestrate our decentralized mesh network.

**MongoDB**

MongoDB Atlas serves as the strategic orchestrator and absolute source of truth for ExoCompute’s decentralized peer-to-peer network. While the raw AI inference happens via WebGPU inside the edge browsers, MongoDB is the "brain" responsible for keeping the chaotic mesh network secure, efficient, and reliable.

Here is exactly how we utilized MongoDB's architecture for this track:

Reputation-Based Task Routing: To prevent bad actors and slow machines from bottlenecking the system, we store the historical confidence and reputation scores of every connected consumer PC in MongoDB. We utilize Aggregation Pipelines to instantly query the active node pool, sorting them by latency and reputation, to intelligently route complex AI tasks to the most reliable machines.

Flexible Document Model for Edge Hardware: Our network's hardware is completely unpredictable—ranging from M2 MacBooks to standard Windows desktops. MongoDB’s schema-less document model allows us to seamlessly ingest these highly disparate hardware profiles, connection states, and dynamically changing node capabilities without being locked into rigid SQL constraints.

High-Velocity Telemetry & Payouts: Every time a node finishes a matrix calculation, it fires back telemetry (execution duration, tokens-per-second, and micro-transaction earnings). MongoDB handles these high-throughput write operations flawlessly, allowing us to dynamically adjust a node's reputation score in real-time based on its actual, verifiable performance history.

**Open Innovation**

ExoCompute embodies the spirit of Open Innovation by fundamentally rethinking how global computational infrastructure is sourced, distributed, and monetized. We aren't just solving a specific industry problem; we are proposing a radical new paradigm for decentralized edge computing.

Here is why ExoCompute belongs in the Open Innovation track:

Democratizing AI Infrastructure: We are challenging the monopoly of centralized cloud giants. By creating a peer-to-peer marketplace, we enable indie developers and startups to access hyper-local, low-cost AI inference, while everyday consumers can finally monetize the 70-80% of their laptop's computational power that currently goes to waste.

The "Zero-Friction" Breakthrough: Previous attempts at decentralized compute networks failed to reach the masses because they required complex Docker containers, CLI knowledge, and specialized mining hardware. Our true innovation is our frictionless architecture: by executing complex AI models natively inside a standard web browser using WebGPU and WebAssembly, we reduced the barrier to entry to a single URL click.

Universal Applicability: ExoCompute is an industry-agnostic infrastructure layer. While our MVP demonstrates AI inference triggered seamlessly via WhatsApp, the underlying browser-based mesh network can be adapted to process anything from medical image rendering to climate data parsing.

By turning any consumer device with a web browser into a secure, sandboxed inference node, ExoCompute represents an open-ended, scalable shift in the future of global computing.

**Gen AI&ML**

Here is exactly how ExoCompute pushes the boundaries of the AI/ML track:

Decentralized Edge Inference: We shifted the heavy lifting of machine learning away from expensive, centralized GPU data centers directly to the edge. By crowdsourcing idle consumer laptops, we proved that distributed ad-hoc networks can handle low-latency AI inference tasks seamlessly.

Web-Native ML Execution: We successfully engineered a pipeline that downloads, caches, and executes quantized machine learning models (such as DistilBERT) natively inside standard web browsers. By leveraging Transformers.js and the WebGPU API, our worker nodes execute complex tensor math using their local graphics hardware, requiring zero external server compute.

Democratizing AI Deployment: Currently, deploying ML features at scale requires massive venture funding just to cover AWS or Azure compute costs. ExoCompute slashes the cost of AI inference by up to 50% by tapping into the 70% of consumer hardware that sits idle daily. We lower the financial barrier to entry, allowing indie developers to integrate AI seamlessly.

Privacy-First Pipeline Potential: Because the ML inference happens completely within an isolated browser sandbox on the edge, ExoCompute lays the groundwork for highly secure, privacy-preserving AI applications where sensitive data never has to be transmitted to a centralized server for processing.

ExoCompute isn't just an AI application; it is the decentralized engine that will power the next generation of affordable, scalable machine learning.

### SafeStay
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/safestay-98a8) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Sreekarji/safestay.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/n0AY-OxcJU8?si=Iv4d6vQ85pgpGQcU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-HackPrix%20Season%203-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hackprix-2026.devfolio.co)

> Your Safety. Their Accountability.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![JWT](https://img.shields.io/badge/JWT-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB Atlas](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB%20Atlas-333333?style=flat-square) ![Nodemailer](https://img.shields.io/badge/Nodemailer-333333?style=flat-square) ![mongoose](https://img.shields.io/badge/mongoose-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every year, thousands of Indian students relocate to new cities for college and choose PGs or hostels based on fake reviews, broker promises, and misleading listings. There is no reliable, verified system to assess accommodation safety. Students end up facing food poisoning, water contamination, security threats, poor sanitation, and structural hazards — with no way to warn others.
SafeStay fixes this by letting only verified college students report real safety issues. Every report is verified by 3 AI models before it affects any score. A dynamic SafeStay Safety Index (SSI) is computed per accommodation and displayed on an interactive map — giving students honest, AI-verified safety intelligence before they commit to a place.

**Challenges we ran into**

Our biggest challenge was building a reliable AI verification pipeline under time pressure. We initially used 2 models (Mistral + Groq) but one would occasionally fail under free-tier rate limits, killing the entire pipeline. We switched to Promise.allSettled with a 2-of-3 consensus system across Mistral Pixtral 12B, Groq Llama 3.3 70B, and Gemini Flash — so even if one model fails, the verdict still goes through.
The second challenge was team environment setup. MongoDB Atlas was only connecting successfully on one team member's machine — others were getting connection refused errors due to IP whitelist restrictions on the Atlas cluster. We fixed this by whitelisting 0.0.0.0/0 for development and sharing a single Atlas URI across the team.
Cloudinary API keys were also causing silent failures — image uploads were returning 401s without clear error messages. We traced it to mismatched environment variable names across team members' .env files and standardised them with a shared .env.example.
Permission issues on shared routes and middleware were blocking team members from testing their own features — admin and owner middleware was rejecting valid tokens due to role field mismatches in the JWT payload. We fixed this by aligning the token signing payload across all auth routes and documenting the exact shape expected by each middleware.

**Gemini**

Gemini Flash is the third model in our AI verification pipeline. It runs in parallel with Mistral and Groq via Promise.allSettled. A 2-of-3 consensus is required for a VERIFIED verdict. Gemini acts as the tiebreaker when Mistral and Groq disagree, making the pipeline more robust and reducing false positives.

**MongoDB**

MongoDB Atlas stores all users, reports, accommodations, OTPs, and verification results. The SSI computation uses aggregation pipelines across reports with time decay, severity weights, and resolution status. The CounterReport schema enables owner dispute tracking. TTL indexes auto-expire OTPs. GeoJSON location data powers the map markers endpoint.

**Sarvam.ai**

Sarvam AI powers real-time translation for safety report summaries and SSI explanations into Telugu and Hindi, making the platform accessible to students who are more comfortable in their regional language. The language toggle is persistent across sessions.

**Sustainable Development**

SafeStay creates measurable social impact by giving India's 35+ million college students access to community-verified, AI-moderated safety data about their accommodation options. The platform incentivises owners to fix issues through a public trust score, creating a feedback loop that improves living conditions over time. It is built to scale beyond student housing to any rental market in India. This directly addresses SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities), SDG 3 (Good Health and Wellbeing) and SDG 9 Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure: SafeStay introduces a novel multi-model AI verification pipeline (Mistral Pixtral 12B + Groq Llama 3.3 70B + Gemini Flash).
