### Namma Marga
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/namma-marga-130c) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Altaria-hackathon-teams/iot-triplepaneerroll) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Altaria-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://altaria.devfolio.co)

> Trading30seconds of a civilian time for savinglife

![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![OpenCV](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCV-333333?style=flat-square) ![Android SDK](https://img.shields.io/badge/Android%20SDK-333333?style=flat-square) ![Vanilla JS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Vanilla%20JS-333333?style=flat-square) ![RTDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/RTDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS3​](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS3​-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML5​](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML5​-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Primary Problem**: The Lost "Golden Hour"
In major metropolitan cities, the difference between life and death is often decided by a single red light. Ambulances regularly lose their critical "golden hour" trapped in urban gridlock. Current solutions are insufficient.
Sirens rely on human reaction times in densely packed spaces where cars physically have nowhere to move.
Hardware pre-emption systems (like RFID sensors) require ripping up roads and executing expensive, city-wide hardware overhauls.

**How Namma Marga Solves It**
Namma Marga acts as an invisible, digital traffic cop that parts the sea of traffic before the ambulance even arrives—using zero new road hardware.
We solve this by turning the ambulance driver's smartphone into a high-frequency IoT beacon. Our cloud-based Logic Engine constantly calculates the Haversine distance between the moving ambulance and registered "smart intersections." When the ambulance breaches a 500-meter radius, the system autonomously secures the intersection, giving the emergency vehicle a clear green light without requiring the driver to interact with the system.

**The Secondary Problem: Post-Emergency Gridlock**
Traditional pre-emption systems solve the emergency problem but create a massive secondary problem: horrific traffic jams for civilian commuters who were forced to wait.
Namma Marga solves this through a closed-loop Computer Vision pipeline. The moment the ambulance clears the intersection, our AI cameras calculate a live "congestion index" based on the backlog of waiting cars. The system then autonomously holds the green light for those specific civilian lanes just long enough to flush the displaced traffic, instantly restoring normal urban mobility.

**Challenges we ran into**

Android Background Kills: Android 14's strict battery limits kept killing our live GPS tracking when the phone screen turned off.

Solution: We built a robust LocationForegroundService with explicit OS-level permissions to keep the app alive and safely pinging coordinates every second.

Map Routing Crashes: Fetching complex route data from our routing API caused the Android app to freeze and silently fail.

Solution: We moved all heavy network calls to background threads, cleanly bridging the data back to the main screen only when it was ready to draw.

Cloud Data Desync: Getting the Android app, web simulator, and Node.js engine to speak the exact same language in Firebase was a nightmare. A single missing variable broke the system.

Solution: We created and enforced a strict, universal 9-field JSON "data contract" across the entire stack to guarantee flawless synchronization.

Database Overload: Scaling our math to track multiple intersections at once threatened to exhaust our Firebase database write limits.

Solution: We optimized our Logic Engine so it only writes to the database at the exact moment the ambulance crosses the 500-meter trigger boundary, drastically reducing server load.

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

**The IoT Component**: The emergency vehicle acts as a high-frequency IoT beacon. Using a native Android app, it streams live GPS telemetry (latitude, longitude, speed) to our Firebase cloud infrastructure every second. Our Node.js Logic Engine continuously calculates the Haversine distance between this moving IoT node and registered "smart intersections" to autonomously trigger traffic light pre-emption.

**The AI Component**: To prevent the pre-emption from causing civilian gridlock, we deployed a Computer Vision pipeline. Using OpenCV and a custom Roboflow model, our system analyzes live camera feeds at the intersection to calculate a real-time "congestion index." The AI dynamically adjusts the subsequent green-light duration to flush the displaced traffic, creating a closed-loop, intelligent traffic management system.

### Cognify Grid
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/cognify-grid-7cc6) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Altaria-hackathon-teams/iot-cognify-grid.git) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/SDcInodKRzY) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Altaria-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://altaria.devfolio.co)

> SEE THE GRID THINK!

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![pandas](https://img.shields.io/badge/pandas-333333?style=flat-square) ![MQTT](https://img.shields.io/badge/MQTT-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Commercial buildings waste up to 30% of their energy because equipment faults and gradual degradation often go unnoticed until a breakdown occurs. NeuralGrid addresses this by detecting issues in HVAC systems, compressors, and pumps early, giving teams time to act before failures happen. It helps reduce energy waste by identifying equipment that is consuming more power than normal in real time. The system replaces manual inspections by operating 24/7 and monitoring all equipment simultaneously. It also makes maintenance more actionable by providing a complete AI-based diagnosis, including the root cause, confidence level, recommended fix, urgency, and estimated cost impact in rupees per day. Additionally, it ensures instant communication by sending Telegram alerts within seconds, even during late hours, along with a downloadable PDF report.

**Challenges we ran into**

1) False positive storm
Isolation Forest flagged too many anomalies during small occupancy spikes
Solution: Added ARIMA as a second check
Alert triggers only when both models agree
Result: False positives almost eliminated

2) ARIMA crashing on short data
Errors occurred for short, constant, or invalid time series
Solution:
Wrapped code in try/except
Added minimum 30 readings requirement

3)Telegram asyncio conflict
python-telegram-bot v21 is async but monitoring loop is sync
Using asyncio.run() caused RuntimeError
Solution: Created a new event loop for each alert

4) Cross-process buffer sharing issue
Streamlit and FastAPI run as separate processes
Cannot share in-memory data
Solution:
Dashboard runs its own MQTT subscriber
Used alerts_log.json and reports folder for shared data

5) Groq returning malformed JSON
LLaMA3 sometimes returned responses with markdown formatting
Caused parsing issues
Solution:
Removed backticks and json labels before parsing
Added fallback error logging to prevent crashes

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

Here it is rewritten in **simple points (no bullets, only numbers and clean text):**

---

1 NeuralGrid combines AI/ML and IoT tightly
NeuralGrid is not just AI using sensor data and not just IoT running a model
Both parts depend on each other and cannot work separately

2 IoT layer provides real-time data
Six sensors send data every 2 seconds using MQTT
Sensors include power meter, HVAC, lighting, compressor, and two pumps
Each reading has value, baseline, unit, and timestamp
This continuous data is the only input for the ML system

3 AI layer makes data useful
Raw sensor values alone are not meaningful
Example: compressor using 29 kW means nothing without context

4 Isolation Forest detects anomalies
Compares current data with normal behavior
Gives an anomaly score to identify unusual patterns

5 ARIMA predicts future trends
Uses last 60 readings to forecast future behavior
Helps identify if the issue is growing or just normal variation

6 Dual-gate system improves accuracy
ThreatConfirmer triggers alerts only if both models agree
Reduces false alerts and makes system reliable

7 AI + IoT work together for deep analysis
When alert triggers, LLaMA3 receives data from all sensors
Does not analyze one sensor alone
Compares multiple sensor readings together

8 Context-based fault detection
Example:
Compressor high + power meter high + HVAC rising → likely motor issue
Compressor high alone → different problem
This level of reasoning is not possible with basic IoT rules

9 Final outcome
IoT acts as the data source (eyes)
AI acts as the decision maker (brain)
System converts raw sensor data into clear maintenance actions quickly

**The problem it solves**

The Problem It Solves
In modern enterprise cybersecurity environments, critical assets (Crown Jewels) such as databases and sensitive servers are the primary targets for attackers. However, security analysts often struggle to clearly understand how an attacker can move through the network from an initial entry point to these high-value systems.

Today’s enterprise networks are:
Large and highly distributed
Complex and deeply interconnected
Segmented but misconfigured
Filled with hidden privilege relationships
Because of this, organisations fail to fully identify:
Complete attack paths
Lateral movement routes
Privilege escalation chains
Real risk to Crown Jewel assets
This lack of visibility leads to reactive security, where threats are addressed only after damage is done—resulting in financial loss, data breaches, and regulatory impact.

💡 What This System Enables
Our platform transforms this process into a proactive, intelligent, and automated defence system.
1. End-to-End Attack Discovery
Instead of isolated alerts, the system models the entire enterprise as a graph-based network, capturing:
Assets (servers, applications, databases)
Identities and privileges
Vulnerabilities (CVEs, misconfigurations)
Relationships between all components
This allows analysts to see complete multi-hop attack paths, not just individual weaknesses.

2. Realistic Attack Simulation (Red Team Automation)
The system integrates real-world attack simulation using multiple payloads such as:
SQL Injection
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
Brute Force attacks
Directory fuzzing
Parser-based attacks (DSL / HTTP parsing)
It actively identifies exposed servers linked to the system and attempts exploitation, mimicking real attacker behaviour.

3. Intelligent Path Analysis
Using graph algorithms like:
K Shortest Paths → finds realistic attack routes
Min S-T Cut → identifies critical choke points
The system highlights:
The easiest paths attackers will take
The minimum set of defenses needed to block all attacks

4. Risk-Based Prioritisation
Each attack path is ranked using:
Exploitability
Asset criticality
Path complexity
This ensures teams focus only on high-impact vulnerabilities, reducing noise and effort.

5. AI-Driven Reasoning & Mitigation
The platform uses an LLM-based reasoning engine to:
Understand relationships between vulnerabilities and assets
Generate realistic attack chains
Recommend targeted, cost-effective mitigations
Instead of generic fixes, it suggests:
Which CVEs to patch first
Which privileges to revoke
Which nodes to secure for maximum impact

6. What-If Simulation (Decision Support)
A built-in simulation engine allows teams to:
Patch vulnerabilities virtually
Modify configurations
Instantly see how attack paths change
This enables safe testing of security decisions before deployment.

🎯Real-World Impact
This system helps:
SOC Teams detect attack paths faster
Red/Blue Teams simulate real attack scenarios
Security Architects design stronger networks

It:
Reduces time to detect threats
Cuts remediation costs
Improves compliance and audit readiness

**Challenges we ran into**

Getting a real dataset that is as close to a enterprise network was the biggest hurdle we faced when we were starting this project.
We got over it by first trying to use whatever academic data we got to build upon it to make a larger dataset and then we switched to system logs and network logs to make sure it was real time data.

Another hurdle was finding websites were we can test our attack detection model since most of the websites would directly flag our model we then figured we will have to test it for a protected environment like a docker or juice shop.

**Cybersecurity + Artificial Intelligence**

Since its clearly a tool for cyber analysts for attack and defence its under the Cyber Security part
For the AI part our mitigation and LLM for detecting attack is done by a model

README.md:# FairChain — AI Governance Platform

![FairChain Dashboard](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stellar/stellar-logo/master/stellar-logo.png) <!-- Replace with actual banner if available -->

**FairChain** is a production-ready, blockchain-anchored AI Governance Platform built to ensure fairness, transparency, and accountability in automated hiring and decision-making systems.

By combining **Multi-Agent AI Debate**, **Deterministic Rule Engines**, and **Stellar Blockchain Cryptographic Audits**, FairChain transforms the "black box" of AI into a transparent, legally defensible, and auditable process.

---

## 🌟 Key Features

### 1. Multi-Agent Courtroom Debate
Instead of relying on a single, potentially biased LLM, FairChain uses an adversarial multi-agent system:
*   **The Advocate (Pro Agent):** Evaluates candidates purely on merit (skills, experience, certifications).
*   **The Inquisitor:** Actively searches for bias signals, proxy variables, and fairness violations.
*   **The Judge:** Weighs both arguments and delivers a final, balanced verdict.

### 2. Disparate Impact Ratio (DIR) Monitoring
FairChain actively calculates the **Disparate Impact Ratio (DIR)** for protected classes (gender, race, age) in real-time. If the DIR falls below the EEOC-standard **0.80 threshold**, the system detects a fairness violation and triggers visual alerts (glitch effects) and potential rule overrides.

### 3. Cryptographic Blockchain Audit (Stellar Testnet)
To ensure legally defensible decisions:
*   Every decision generates a cryptographic receipt using a **Merkle Tree**.
*   The **Merkle Root** is anchored to the **Stellar Testnet**.
*   **Soroban Smart Contracts** validate the DIR score on-chain.
*   Fairness **Soulbound Tokens (SBTs)** can be minted to prove a candidate was treated fairly.

### 4. Interactive 3D Command Center
The frontend is a "Command Center" built with **Next.js** and **Tailwind CSS**, featuring a pitch-black, dark-glass aesthetic.
*   **React Three Fiber (R3F):** Powers a live 3D courtroom where holographic agents debate decisions in real-time.
*   **MerkleChain3D:** An interactive 3D visualization of the cryptographic audit ledger.

### 5. Automated Telegram Bot & Email Receipts
*   **Telegram Integration:** Recruiters can upload resumes (PDF/TXT) directly via Telegram for instant processing.
*   **Automated Email Receipts:** Candidates receive a personalized cryptographic audit receipt detailing their evaluation, fairness score, and a link to the Stellar Testnet transaction proving the integrity of their assessment.

### 6. Red-Teaming "Saboteur" Agent
An integrated adversarial testing feature that generates highly qualified but structurally biased candidate profiles to stress-test the platform's bias detectors and Inquisitor agent.

---

## 🏗️ Architecture Stack

### Backend (FastAPI / Python)
*   **Framework:** FastAPI for high-performance





The "Black Box" of AI Hiring
As companies rush to adopt AI for screening resumes, they face a critical problem: AI models act as opaque black boxes. Single-model LLMs silently reject candidates based on hidden biases (proxy variables like zip codes or employment gaps), leaving companies vulnerable to massive legal risks under frameworks like the EU AI Act. Meanwhile, candidates are frustrated by unexplained ghosting. Furthermore, centralized HR databases can be easily manipulated by corrupt managers to cover up discriminatory practices.

The FairChain Solution
FairChain transforms AI recruitment from a legal liability into a transparent, mathematically verified, and fully auditable process.

For HR Teams (Risk Mitigation): Instead of blindly trusting a single AI, FairChain acts as a "Digital Courtroom." Three distinct AI agents (Advocate, Inquisitor, and Judge) actively debate the candidate to hunt for bias. It calculates a strict Disparate Impact Ratio (DIR), automatically blocking decisions that violate fairness thresholds.

For Legal Auditors (Tamper-Proof Proof): We use the Stellar Blockchain to ensure records can never be secretly edited. The system hashes the AI debate into a Merkle Root and anchors it to the Stellar Testnet, providing cryptographic proof of a fair audit.

For Candidates (Total Transparency): Candidates automatically receive a Cryptographic Audit Receipt via Email. If approved, the system mints a Soulbound Token (SBT) to their Freighter wallet, giving them a permanent, verifiable "Proof of Fairness" badge.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a platform that bridges advanced multi-agent AI with Web3 cryptographic verification presented several intense engineering hurdles:

1. Multi-Agent Orchestration (LangGraph)
Getting three distinct AI agents (Advocate, Inquisitor, Judge) to debate dynamically without hallucinating or falling into infinite loops was difficult.

How we got over it: We utilized LangGraph to enforce a strict state-machine architecture. We isolated the agents' system prompts and forced the Judge agent to act as a strict deterministic router, cutting off the debate once sufficient bias-checking conditions were met.

2. Deterministic Cryptography for AI Transcripts
To anchor the decision to the Stellar blockchain, we needed to generate a Merkle Root from the AI debate. However, AI outputs can contain slight whitespace or formatting variations, which completely breaks cryptographic hashing.

How we got over it: We built a normalization pipeline in FastAPI that strips and sanitizes the JSON payload of the debate transcript before passing it to our SHA-256 hashing functions. This ensured 100% deterministic Merkle Roots every time.

3. Seamless Web3 UI Integration
We wanted a dominating, immersive 3D Web2 aesthetic (using React Three Fiber and Glassmorphism) while running heavy Web3 wallet interactions in the background. Initially, triggering the Freighter Wallet API caused frame drops in our 3D particle background.

How we got over it: We decoupled the wallet authentication state from the 3D rendering canvas using custom asynchronous React hooks, allowing the 3D nodes to continue pulsing smoothly while awaiting Stellar network consensus.

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

FairChain sits perfectly at the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Web3 by using blockchain to solve AI's biggest flaw: the "black box" trust problem.

Here is exactly how the two technologies work together in our platform:

The Artificial Intelligence Layer: We built a complex multi-agent system (using LangGraph and Python) acting as a digital courtroom. Instead of one opaque algorithm, three distinct AI agents—an Advocate, an Inquisitor, and a Judge—actively debate candidate resumes to hunt for hidden biases and calculate strict Disparate Impact Ratio (DIR) scores.

The Web3 / Blockchain Layer: Because AI logs can be secretly altered by humans on private servers, we use the Stellar Blockchain as an immutable vault for AI governance.

The Synergy: We mathematically hash the AI's final debate transcript into a Merkle Root and anchor it directly to the Stellar Testnet. Furthermore, we wrote Soroban Smart Contracts to act as automated referees that physically block biased AI decisions on-chain, and we use the network to mint Soulbound Tokens (SBTs) to candidates as a cryptographic "Proof of Fairness."

FairChain uses AI to do the heavy lifting of evaluation, and Web3 to provide the mathematical, untamperable trust that AI inherently lacks.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![NumPy](https://img.shields.io/badge/NumPy-333333?style=flat-square) ![C++](https://img.shields.io/badge/C++-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Our project addresses the critical issue of ineffective and delayed monitoring of industrial wastewater discharge, which poses serious risks to ecosystems and human health. Traditional methods rely on periodic manual testing and fixed threshold-based systems, making them slow, reactive, and often unable to detect complex pollution patterns in time. To overcome this, we propose an intelligent IoT-based solution integrated with machine learning that enables continuous, real-time monitoring of key water quality parameters. The system not only detects anomalies early but also predicts potential contamination trends, allowing for timely alerts and faster corrective actions.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the key challenges we faced was the lack of visible variation in sensor data due to the use of stagnant water during testing. Since the water conditions remained almost constant, the readings (such as pH, turbidity, etc.) showed little to no fluctuation, which made the dashboard graphs appear flat and uninformative. This became a hurdle while demonstrating the effectiveness of our real-time monitoring and anomaly detection system.

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

Our project falls under the Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) tracks, as it combines real-time data collection with intelligent analysis to address industrial wastewater monitoring. The IoT component enables continuous monitoring of water quality through sensors that capture parameters like pH, turbidity, and temperature, ensuring a steady flow of real-time data.
On the other hand, the AI aspect enhances the system’s capability by analyzing this data using machine learning algorithms to detect anomalies and predict potential contamination. This allows the system to move beyond basic threshold-based monitoring and provide smarter, more adaptive insights, enabling early detection and timely response to harmful wastewater discharge.

**The problem it solves**

🚨 The Problem It Solves

Industrial machines often fail without warning, leading to:

⚠️ Unexpected downtime
💸 High repair and replacement costs
🛑 Safety risks for workers
📉 Production losses

Most existing maintenance systems rely on:

Expensive sensors (vibration, thermal cameras)
Complex setups
Or reactive maintenance (fix after failure)
💡 Our Solution

ELECTRA provides a low-cost, real-time predictive maintenance system using electrical signals.

Instead of waiting for failure, it:

Monitors current consumption in real time
Detects deviation from normal behavior
Flags early warning signs before breakdown
Classifies machine health into:
🟢 Normal
🟡 Warning
🔴 Failure
🏭 Where It Can Be Used

ELECTRA can be deployed in:

Manufacturing plants
Assembly lines
HVAC systems
Motors, fans, and pumps
Small workshops and factories
⚡ Why This Matters
✅ Works with cheap hardware
✅ Requires minimal setup
✅ Provides instant insights
✅ Improves safety and reliability
✅ Enables preventive maintenance instead of reactive fixes
🎯 Key Impact

“We shift maintenance from after failure → to before failure, using real-time electrical intelligence.”

**Challenges we ran into**

⚠️ Challenges I Ran Into

Building ELECTRA involved several real-world challenges across hardware, data processing, and frontend integration.

🔌 1. Incorrect Sensor Readings (Hardware Issue)

Initially, the INA219 sensor was showing extremely low current values (~0.1 mA), even when the fan was running.

Problem:
The sensor was not placed correctly in the circuit, so it wasn’t measuring the actual load current.

Solution:
I corrected the wiring by placing the INA219 in series with the load, ensuring all current passed through the sensor. This immediately fixed the readings.

📡 2. Serial Data Conflicts

At one point, the Python script was receiving only one data packet or inconsistent values.

Problem:
The Arduino Serial Monitor and Python script were both trying to access the same serial port.

Solution:
I ensured only the Python script accessed the serial port and closed the Arduino Serial Monitor completely.

🧠 3. Data Parsing Errors

The system initially failed to process incoming data correctly.

Problem:
Mixed data formats (CSV from ESP32 and JSON from other sources) caused parsing errors like:

could not convert string to float

Solution:
I implemented strict filtering logic to only process valid CSV lines starting with the machine ID.

⚡ 4. “Zero Current” Detection Was Inaccurate

Even when the fan was turned off, the sensor did not output exactly 0.

Problem:
Sensor noise caused small non-zero readings, preventing accurate failure detection.

Solution:
I introduced a threshold-based deadband, treating values below a certain range as zero.

🎨 5. UI Color Mapping Didn’t Update Correctly

Even after backend logic was correct, the frontend dashboard did not reflect the correct machine status.

Problem:
The UI was not properly bound to the status field from the API.

Solution:
I debugged the data flow, verified API responses, and implemented fallback methods to ensure correct visual updates.

🔄 6. Real-Time Synchronization

Ensuring all components updated in real time was tricky.

Problem:
Data delays or stale values caused the dashboard to appear static.

Solution:
I implemented consistent polling, verified MQTT flow, and ensured the latest data was always stored and served by Node-RED.

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

🌐 IoT + Artificial Intelligence

ELECTRA sits at the intersection of IoT sensing and AI-driven decision making.

🔌 IoT Component

The system uses an ESP32 + INA219 sensor to continuously monitor real-world electrical parameters (current, voltage, power) from a physical machine.

Real-time data acquisition from hardware
Continuous streaming of sensor data
Communication via MQTT protocol
Integration with Node-RED for live API generation

👉 This enables live monitoring of physical systems through connected devices, which is the core of IoT.

🧠 AI Component

On top of raw sensor data, ELECTRA applies intelligent analysis:

A machine learning model predicts anomalies based on current behavior
Deviation-based logic identifies early signs of failure
Health and risk scores are computed dynamically
The system classifies machine states (Normal / Warning / Failure)

👉 This transforms raw electrical signals into actionable insights, which is the role of AI.

⚡ Combined Impact

By combining IoT and AI, ELECTRA:

Detects anomalies before physical failure occurs
Provides real-time predictive maintenance insights
Reduces downtime and maintenance costs
Enables smart industrial monitoring without expensive sensors
🎯 Summary

ELECTRA uses IoT to capture real-world machine data and AI to interpret it, creating a real-time predictive maintenance system that bridges physical hardware and intelligent decision-making

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The Problem AgentGuard v2 Solves
The Core Issue
AI agents are no longer just chatbots — they're being handed real crypto wallets and told to operate autonomously. They swap tokens, interact with DeFi protocols, and execute irreversible on-chain transactions with zero human involvement. Two catastrophic failure modes exist here that nobody has fully addressed:

Problem 1: Unaudited Smart Contracts Are Everywhere
90% of small DeFi projects deploy smart contracts with no security audit. Professional audits cost $50,000–$200,000 completely inaccessible to indie developers and small teams. The result:

Vulnerable contracts go live daily
Attackers find and exploit them
$3 billion+ lost annually to smart contract exploits
No certificate, no public record, no warning for users interacting with them

AgentGuard fixes this with PhantomAudit  free, automated, and done in under 60 seconds, with an immutable on-chain certificate for contracts that pass.

Problem 2: AI Agents Have Zero Semantic Safety
Every existing safety tool Forta Network, OpenZeppelin Defender, kill switches  monitors how much money moved. None of them ask why the agent moved it or whether that action matches what the agent was supposed to be doing.
An agent given the goal "maximize holdings" could:

Interact with a malicious contract
Execute an exploit sequence,
Drain a wallet into an unknown protocol and as long as the dollar amount looks normal, every existing system waves it through. By the time anyone notices, the transaction is confirmed and irreversible.

AgentGuard fixes this with a three-layer middleware that checks semantic intent  not just dollar thresholds  before a single transaction reaches the chain.

Why Irreversibility Makes This Urgent
On a database, a bad action can be rolled back. On a blockchain, it cannot. The combination of AI unpredictability and blockchain finality creates a uniquely dangerous environment where the window to intervene is before execution, not after. AgentGuard is built entirely around that principle intercept first, execute only when safe.

**Challenges we ran into**

Slither  Dependency Hell
Both tools have deep system dependencies and conflicting Python requirements. Solved by containerizing the entire analysis pipeline and carefully isolating package environments so both could run side by side without breaking each other.
Turning Raw Scan Output into Readable Exploit Stories
Slither return dense technical JSON that means nothing to most users. We solved this by engineering precise LLM prompts that take the raw findings and produce grounded, human-readable exploit narratives with realistic attack steps and estimated financial impact without hallucinating details.
On-Chain Certification Edge Cases
Gas estimation failures, RPC timeouts, and async transaction states made the Sepolia certification flow brittle early on. We solved this by building explicit fallback states throughout the UI and making the app fully functional even when the blockchain layer was offline.
Middleware Intercepting Transactions in Real Time
Getting the middleware to evaluate agent transactions against the constitution before execution with low enough latency to not break the agent's flow required multiple architectural rethinks around how we hooked into the agent's execution loop.
Frontend Data Model Kept Shifting
As the backend evolved, our shared app context kept going out of sync across pages. We solved this by refactoring the context layer early and establishing a strict data contract between frontend and backend so new fields wouldn't silently break downstream pages.
Caching Duplicate Contract Scans
Re-scanning the same contract wasted time and gas. We added a contract hash lookup on the backend so repeat uploads instantly return the existing audit record and on-chain certificate instead of triggering a full re-scan.

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

AI agents are increasingly being given autonomous control over crypto wallets and DeFi protocols — making irreversible on-chain transactions without human involvement. The risk here isn't purely an AI problem or purely a blockchain problem; it's the collision of AI's unpredictability with blockchain's immutability. A bad AI decision on-chain can't be rolled back.
AgentGuard addresses this in two ways that are native to both domains. PhantomAudit uses AI (LLM-generated exploit narratives on top of deterministic static analysis) to democratize smart contract security — something that's historically been gated behind $50-200K professional audits. The runtime middleware uses a hybrid of deterministic rules and LLM intent classification to intercept agent actions before they hit the chain, and uses a Solidity time-lock contract to create an immutable, on-chain audit trail of every flagged decision.
The core innovation is semantic safety: existing blockchain monitoring tools only watch financial thresholds, while AgentGuard is the first system that checks whether an AI agent's intended action actually matches its declared purpose — and enforces that check at the middleware layer, outside the agent's own reasoning where it can't be prompt-injected or hallucinated away.

> A cross bank fraud vaccine!!

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hyperledger](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hyperledger-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![stellar](https://img.shields.io/badge/stellar-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Sentinel Mesh addresses a critical gap in the financial ecosystem: fraud detection across institutions without compromising user privacy.

Today, banks operate in silos — even if the same fraudster targets multiple banks, there is no secure way to share intelligence without exposing sensitive customer data or violating regulations.

What people can use it for:

Detect cross-bank fraud patterns in real time
Share fraud signals without revealing raw data
Reduce financial losses from repeated or coordinated attacks
Improve risk scoring using network-wide intelligence
Enable safer collaboration between banks, fintechs, and regulators

How it makes things easier/safer:

Uses hashed transaction identifiers, so no personal data is shared
Simulates zero-knowledge proofs, ensuring trust without exposure
Provides a real-time fraud alert system across a shared network
Reduces dependency on slow, manual fraud reporting processes
Improves decision-making with aggregated, privacy-safe insights

In short, Sentinel Mesh transforms fraud detection from an isolated effort into a secure, collaborative intelligence network.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges was ensuring consistent hashing across simulated institutions.

Since fraud matching relies on comparing hashed transaction data, even a small difference in input formatting (like spacing, order, or casing) would generate completely different hashes, breaking cross-network detection.

How I solved it:

Standardized the hashing input format:
(sender + receiver + amount) in a fixed structure
Applied preprocessing:
Trimmed whitespace
Converted strings to lowercase
Ensured consistent data types
Centralized the hashing logic in a single utility function

Another challenge was simulating a privacy-preserving system (like zero-knowledge proofs) without implementing full cryptography, which is complex and time-consuming.

Solution:

Designed a mock proof system where:
Only verification results are shared
No raw data is exposed
Focused on concept demonstration, not full cryptographic implementation

A third hurdle was real-time synchronization of fraud alerts across the app.

Solution:

Integrated Socket.io for live updates
Ensured frontend state updates immediately when new fraud events are triggere

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

Sentinel Mesh is a privacy-preserving fraud intelligence platform that enables financial institutions to detect and share fraud signals without exposing sensitive user data. By combining hashed identifiers, simulated zero-knowledge proofs, and real-time analytics, the system bridges the gap between collaboration and confidentiality, helping organizations identify cross-platform fraud patterns efficiently and securely.

### ShieldChain
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/shieldchain-26b5) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://shieldchain-roan.vercel.app/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Altaria-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://altaria.devfolio.co)

> Secure smarter. Trust on-chain.

![IPFS](https://img.shields.io/badge/IPFS-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Monaco Editor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Monaco%20Editor-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ShieldChain is designed as a six-layer pipeline that guides a smart contract from input to verifiable audit transparency. It begins with developers pasting their Solidity or Soroban (Rust) code into a Monaco-based web editor, ensuring a familiar and efficient coding experience. The contract is then analyzed by a large language model via the Groq API running Llama 3.3 70B, which interprets the code with contextual understanding similar to a human security expert. This AI identifies vulnerabilities, explains their risks, assigns severity levels, and suggests precise fixes. To strengthen reliability, the system runs a parallel static analysis using Slither, cross-validating findings to reduce false positives and produce a more trustworthy assessment.

Following analysis, ShieldChain generates a structured PDF audit report that includes vulnerability details, annotated code, a risk score, and recommended fixes. The integrity of this report is secured by anchoring its SHA-256 hash, along with the contract hash, score, and timestamp, onto a Stellar/Soroban-based AuditRegistry smart contract, creating an immutable on-chain record. Finally, a public verification portal allows anyone to check whether a contract has been audited, view its risk score, and track re-audits, ensuring transparency and accountability. Together, these layers create a comprehensive, AI-enhanced smart contract auditing system that combines deep analysis with permanent, verifiable trust.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the key challenges in building ShieldChain was integrating dynamic analysis alongside AI-driven evaluation. While the LLM provides deep semantic understanding of smart contract logic, dynamic analysis requires simulating real execution environments, handling state changes, and capturing runtime behaviors like reentrancy or gas-related issues. Bridging these two approaches is non-trivial because dynamic tools often produce low-level execution traces, whereas AI models reason in a more abstract, human-like way. Aligning their outputs into a unified format for meaningful cross-validation—and doing so efficiently without slowing down the pipeline—required careful design and orchestration.

Another major hurdle was coordinating AI agents to behave consistently and reliably within the system. LLMs can sometimes produce non-deterministic or overly verbose outputs, which makes it difficult to standardize vulnerability reporting and severity scoring. Ensuring that the AI’s findings align with deterministic tools like Slither, while also maintaining accuracy and minimizing false positives, demanded prompt engineering, output structuring, and validation layers. Balancing flexibility (AI reasoning) with precision (static/dynamic analysis) was essential to make the system both intelligent and trustworthy.

**Web3 / Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence**

ShieldChain fits the Web3 + Blockchain + Artificial Intelligence track by combining advanced AI reasoning with decentralized infrastructure to solve a critical problem in smart contract security. It uses a large language model to perform deep semantic analysis of Solidity and Soroban contracts, identifying vulnerabilities with context-aware explanations, severity scoring, and suggested fixes—something traditional rule-based tools cannot achieve. This AI layer is further strengthened by integrating static analysis (Slither) and planned dynamic analysis, creating a hybrid security pipeline that improves accuracy and reduces false positives.
On the blockchain side, ShieldChain ensures transparency and trust by anchoring audit results on the Stellar/Soroban network through an immutable AuditRegistry smart contract. Each audit is permanently recorded using cryptographic hashes, enabling public verification of contract safety, audit history, and risk scores. This fusion of AI-powered auditing with on-chain verification creates a novel, end-to-end security and trust layer for Web3 applications, directly aligning with the goals of the track.

### Heapify
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/heapify-5c6b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Altaria-hackathon-teams/blockchain-heapify) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/3q8a6jGEhRU) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Altaria-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://altaria.devfolio.co)

> Heapifying Cross Border Transactions .

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum TestRPC](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum%20TestRPC-333333?style=flat-square) ![Defi](https://img.shields.io/badge/Defi-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygon Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygon%20Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The "Glass Bank" Enterprise Dilemma
Right now, public blockchains are fundamentally incompatible with Fortune 500 corporate treasuries. Why? Because Web3 operates like a bank made entirely of clear glass. If a massive enterprise tries to use USDC for cross-border settlements, their competitors can look at the public ledger and immediately reverse-engineer their supply chain, transaction volumes, and vendor identities. 

Furthermore, traditional Web2 compliance is a post-execution nightmare. Today, when a company sends $50k across borders, the receiving crypto exchange freezes the funds and triggers a multi-day, manual "sneakernet" process of emailing PDF invoices back and forth just to prove the "intent" of the transfer. 

We built the enterprise antidote: A Zero-Trust, Zero-Knowledge Corporate Treasury OS.

 What It Actually Does
We eliminate the manual compliance duct-tape and the privacy leaks of public ledgers by layering advanced cryptography over an AI risk engine:

Total On-Chain Privacy (ZK + FHE): We use Zero-Knowledge (ZK) proofs to cryptographically attest to the "intent" of a payment off-chain, verifying it without ever exposing the underlying corporate invoices. Concurrently, we utilize Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) to execute internal corporate rules (like multi-sig thresholds and daily velocity limits) on entirely encrypted balances. We do the math blindly. 
Automated Cryptographic Reconciliation: We replace 3-day manual compliance reviews with 300-millisecond API handshakes, delivering machine-readable intent data directly to destination exchanges. 
Proactive AI Risk Intelligence:Before a transaction ever hits the mempool, our locally-hosted LLM (ensuring zero data-sovereignty leakage) cross-references the user's intent against a live Neo4j graph database of the destination wallet's history, instantly blocking sybil attacks or interactions with tainted entities. 

We deliver the speed of a public ledger with the absolute privacy of a dark pool.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building an enterprise-grade cryptographic pipeline in a hackathon timeframe is like trying to change the tires on a car while driving 100 mph. Here is where the architecture fought back the hardest:

1. The FHE Ciphertext Nightmare
We wanted the smart contract to enforce a CFO's daily velocity limit (e.g., "reject transfers > $100k"). But because we were using Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) to hide the amounts, standard Solidity logic completely broke down. You can't just write `if (amount > limit)` when both variables are encrypted gibberish. Learning how to properly evaluate Boolean greater-than/less-than logic on ciphertext—and actually updating the state without decrypting the data on-chain—was a massive 3 AM hurdle.

2. The Data Sovereignty vs. Latency Tradeoff
To ensure strict enterprise data privacy, we couldn't just pass transaction metadata to OpenAI's public API. We had to run our Risk Intelligence Agent entirely locally using Ollama. Orchestrating the backend so that our local LLM could ingest raw Neo4j graph database outputs, calculate a deterministic Risk Score (0-100), and hand that JSON back to the strict Policy Engine—all under 15 seconds so the user didn't think the app crashed—required heavy asynchronous pipeline optimization. 3. The "Vibe Coding" Reality Check
I leaned heavily on rapid AI-assisted development to construct the frontend React dashboards and standard backend API routes. However, when it came to the bleeding-edge cryptography (FHE and ZK-rollups), the AI models started hallucinating non-existent library methods. It forced a hard pivot from moving fast with AI to sitting down, aggressively reading the raw documentation for tools like Zama and EAS, and manually wiring the cryptographic handshakes myself. It was brutal, but it forced me to truly understand the math beneath the abstraction.

**The problem it solves**

Modern AI systems, especially in sensitive domains like healthcare and finance, can be compromised through hidden backdoors known as neural trojans. These attacks do not visibly break the system—the model behaves normally until a specific trigger appears, after which it can silently execute malicious actions like leaking sensitive data. Since traditional security methods only monitor inputs and outputs, this internal malicious behavior often goes completely undetected

Our system introduces a real-time defense layer that monitors the internal behavior of AI models using entropy-based analysis. By observing how the model distributes attention during inference, we detect abnormal shifts that indicate a transition from normal reasoning to malicious execution. If such a deviation is detected, the system immediately halts generation, preventing any harmful output or data leakage before it occurs.

Unlike rule-based or output-based detection systems, our approach is dynamic and model-agnostic. It does not rely on known attack patterns or trigger keywords, making it effective even against unknown or zero-day threats. The system operates in real time, provides early detection before damage occurs, and can be integrated into existing AI pipelines without retraining the model.

The solution can be offered as a security layer for AI deployments through a SaaS model or enterprise integration. Organizations using AI in high-risk environments—such as hospitals, financial institutions, and legal platforms—can integrate this system as a monitoring and protection module. Revenue can be generated through subscription-based access, API usage, and enterprise licensing for on-premise deployments.

This project strengthens trust in AI systems by addressing one of the most critical emerging risks—model-level attacks. It helps protect sensitive data, prevents silent breaches, and enables safer deployment of AI in real-world applications. By shifting security focus from external inputs to internal model behavior, it lays the foundation for a new class of AI-native cybersecurity solutions.

**Challenges we ran into**

==>Creating a Realistic Threat Model (without harming anyone)

We needed a convincing way to demonstrate a backdoor without actually weaponizing a model. The challenge was to design a safe, synthetic scenario (e.g., special tokens or tagged samples) that mimics a trigger while ensuring no real data or endpoints are affected. This meant carefully scoping the demo so it’s representative but contained.

==>Keeping Normal Behavior Intact

A believable demo requires the model to behave normally on standard inputs while showing a clear, detectable shift on “triggered” inputs. Balancing these two modes is tricky—even in a simulation—because any obvious degradation makes the demo unrealistic. We had to iterate to keep clean behavior stable while still producing a distinct internal signal for detection.

==>Avoiding False Alarms

Not every drop in entropy is malicious—sometimes the model just becomes confident in a correct answer. The challenge was to avoid overreacting and blocking valid outputs. We had to design our detection around relative changes and patterns rather than relying on a single fixed threshold.

==>Making It Work in Real Time

Running entropy checks for every generated token adds computational overhead, especially with a quantized model. The challenge was to keep the system responsive while still analyzing enough information to detect attacks early. Balancing speed and accuracy was one of the toughest engineering trade-offs.

> A Maternal Assistant

![TensorFlow](https://img.shields.io/badge/TensorFlow-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flutter](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flutter-333333?style=flat-square) ![IR Sensor](https://img.shields.io/badge/IR%20Sensor-333333?style=flat-square) ![Image Processing](https://img.shields.io/badge/Image%20Processing-333333?style=flat-square) ![Sensors](https://img.shields.io/badge/Sensors-333333?style=flat-square) ![Piezoelectric sensor](https://img.shields.io/badge/Piezoelectric%20sensor-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Every year, hundreds of thousands of pregnant women — especially in underserved and rural communities — lose their lives or their babies to preventable complications. Not because medicine doesn't have the answers, but because access to timely, continuous care is a privilege many simply don't have.

These women cannot afford frequent hospital visits. They often live far from specialists. Their fetal health goes unmonitored for weeks at a time. A dangerous fetal position or an irregular heartbeat goes undetected — until it's too late.

Chiguru exists to change that.

We are building an end-to-end platform that puts clinical-grade fetal and maternal monitoring into the hands of every pregnant woman — regardless of geography, income, or access. By combining a Flutter mobile application, Firebase cloud infrastructure, custom-built IoT hardware, and an on-device ML model, we create a continuous thread of care between patient and provider — anywhere in the world.

**Challenges we ran into**

The primary challenge addressed by the Chiguru system lies in the absence of a continuous, reliable, and low-cost maternal–fetal monitoring infrastructure in resource-constrained environments. Conventional fetal monitoring relies heavily on intermittent clinical measurements such as ultrasound imaging and cardiotocography, which require hospital-grade equipment, trained personnel, and physical presence. This creates a temporal gap in observation, during which critical physiological anomalies—such as fetal bradycardia, tachycardia, or abnormal positioning—can develop undetected. From a systems perspective, this is a sampling problem with insufficient temporal resolution, where sparse data acquisition leads to loss of clinically relevant signal patterns.

On the hardware side, acquiring accurate biosignals in a non-clinical environment introduces significant technical constraints. The ECG-based fetal heart rate estimation using the AD8232 analog front end suffers from low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) due to interference from maternal cardiac signals, muscle artifacts (EMG), motion artifacts, and environmental electromagnetic noise. The fetal ECG component is inherently weak (in the order of microvolts), making its extraction a non-trivial blind source separation problem. Analog filtering alone is insufficient; it requires robust digital signal processing techniques such as adaptive filtering, bandpass optimization, and peak detection algorithms to reliably compute beats per minute (BPM). Additionally, electrode placement variability and skin impedance fluctuations introduce non-stationarity in the signal, further complicating consistent acquisition.

**IoT + Artificial Intelligence**

The Chiguru system is fundamentally an AI-enabled IoT (AIoT) architecture, where sensing, communication, and intelligence are tightly integrated into a unified pipeline for real-time maternal–fetal monitoring. At the lowest layer, the IoT subsystem—comprising the ESP32 microcontroller interfaced with analog front-end circuits such as the AD8232 ECG module and the developing ultrasonic Doppler unit—acts as a distributed edge sensing network. These devices perform continuous acquisition of physiological signals (bioelectric cardiac activity and Doppler-shifted ultrasonic reflections) and convert them into digital time-series data via on-chip ADCs. Given the constraints of low-power operation and limited bandwidth (BLE), part of the signal processing pipeline is executed at the edge itself, including filtering, peak detection, and preliminary feature extraction (e.g., RR intervals, instantaneous BPM). This edge computation reduces transmission overhead and latency, effectively transforming raw biosignals into semantically meaningful feature streams before communication to the mobile layer.

On top of this IoT data layer, the AI subsystem introduces contextual interpretation and predictive intelligence. The system leverages both algorithmic signal processing and machine learning models to analyze incoming data. For instance, time-series analysis techniques—potentially augmented with adaptive filtering or lightweight ML—are used to isolate fetal cardiac signatures from composite maternal signals, addressing a classic signal separation and pattern recognition problem under noisy conditions. Additionally, the TensorFlow Lite model deployed on-device performs fetal position classification, converting imaging or sensor-derived inputs into discrete clinical categories. This represents an embedded inference pipeline where model optimization techniques such as quantization and graph pruning are necessary to meet real-time constraints on limited hardware resources (CPU, memory, and power). The AI layer thus transforms continuous sensor data into higher-level abstractions such as anomaly flags, positional diagnostics, and trend-based risk indicators.

## 1. What This Project Does

The OS Process Isolation Validator is a fully containerised, real-time monitoring system that continuously verifies whether OS-level processes running simultaneously on a machine are genuinely isolated from each other.

**The core question this answers:** Is Process A behaving as if it cannot see, touch, or interfere with Process B — right now, based on live kernel telemetry?

This is fundamentally different from what Task Manager, `top`, or `htop` provide. Those tools answer: "Is this process using too many resources?" This system answers: "Is this process doing something it should never be doing relative to its own learned normal behaviour, in a way that suggests it is interacting with another process it should not be touching?"

The system detects isolation failures automatically and in real time using a three-layer detection architecture: hard rules for unambiguous violations, statistical Z-score thresholds for single-metric deviations, and an IsolationForest ML model for multivariate behavioural anomalies that no single threshold can catch.

---

## 2. Why This Exists — The Real-World Problem

Process isolation failures have caused some of the most significant security breaches in computing history:

**Spectre and Meltdown (2018):** Two processes running on the same CPU core could read each other's memory through CPU cache timing side channels. A malicious process read kernel memory, passwords, and encryption keys from a completely separate process — without any direct access, purely by measuring how long memory reads took. Affected virtually every Intel, AMD, and ARM processor made in the last 20 years. Patching cost billions globally.

**Dirty COW (2016):** A race condition in Linux kernel memory management allowed an unprivileged process to write to read-only memory mappings belonging to other processes. Present in the Linux kernel for 9 years before discovery. The anomalous `mmap` and memory write syscall pattern from an unprivileged process is exactly what our feature monitoring detects.

**Rowhammer (2015+):** By repeatedly reading specific memory locations at high frequency, a process could flip bits in adjacent memory rows belonging to other processes. The abnormally high memory read frequency — far above any process's normal baseline — is a direct signal our IsolationForest would flag.

**Adobe Reader Sandbox Escape (2013):** Attackers exploited inter-process communication channels between a sandboxed process and a privileged broker process to escape the sandbox entirely. The anomalous IPC socket and file descriptor activity between the two processes is detectable as unusual cross-process communication.

**The gap these breaches share:** No monitoring tool at the time was watching for *behavioural deviation* of a process relative to its own normal profile across multiple signals simultaneously. That is the gap this system fills.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![WebAssembly](https://img.shields.io/badge/WebAssembly-333333?style=flat-square) ![Mediapipe](https://img.shields.io/badge/Mediapipe-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

DeepShield addresses the critical security gap created by the rise of sophisticated, real-time deepfakes in digital communication. As an engineering student focused on AI safety and cybersecurity, we have developed this to solve the problem of trust in an era where pixels and decibels can be easily forged.

**The Problem DeepShield Solves**

- Identity Spoofing: It prevents attackers from using AI-generated avatars or voice clones to impersonate executives, colleagues, or family members during live video calls.

- Social Engineering: By providing real-time liveness detection, it neutralizes "Man-in-the-Middle" injection attacks where a hacker feeds a pre-recorded or synthetic stream into a meeting to authorize fraudulent transactions or steal sensitive data.

- Privacy-First Security: Traditional detection often requires sending data to a cloud server; DeepShield solves the privacy concern by running all biometric and spectral analysis locally on the user's machine.

**How People Can Use It**

- High-Stakes Business Meetings: Users can activate the extension during board meetings or financial discussions to verify that the person on the other end is a living human and not a high-quality digital puppet.

- Remote Interviews & Onboarding: Recruitment teams can use the Challenge-Response mechanism to ensure that candidates are physically present and responding in real-time, rather than using a loop-video or AI overlay to cheat technical assessments.

- Secure Remote Banking: When customers perform identity verification over video calls, DeepShield's rPPG (Bio-Sense) engine adds a layer of "liveness" proof by detecting micro-fluctuations in blood flow that synthetic videos cannot replicate.

**Making Tasks Easier and Safer**

- Automated Vigilance: Instead of a human trying to spot "uncanny valley" glitches (which are becoming harder to see), the Audio Engine scans for "dead zones" in frequency—hidden artifacts in AI speech—making the task of detection objective rather than subjective.

- Instant Verification: The extension integrates directly into existing workflows like Google Meet and Zoom, providing an immediate "Trust Score" without requiring the user to switch apps or stop the conversation.

- Active Defense: The Challenge-Response system makes the "task" of proving identity safer by randomly prompting movements (like "Look Left"), which disrupts pre-recorded loops and forces a fake AI to fail the logic test.

**Challenges we ran into**

**Hurdle 1:** One of the biggest challenges was navigating Chrome’s Manifest V3 security protocols. Specifically, the Content Security Policy (CSP) strictly prohibits executing remotely hosted code (like loading TensorFlow.js or MediaPipe from a CDN). My initial builds failed because the browser blocked the "brains" of the AI to prevent potential code injection.
I had to pivot to a Zero-External-Dependency architecture. I manually downloaded the massive library files (like face_mesh.js), bundled them directly into the extension's lib/ folder, and updated the manifest to allow wasm-unsafe-eval. This ensured the AI could run high-performance WebAssembly calculations locally without violating security rules.

**Hurdle2:** Getting a reliable rPPG (remote heart rate) signal was incredibly difficult.

& more..

These hurdles weren't just bugs; they were lessons to us. By overcoming them, we ensured that DeepShield isn't just a "cool AI project," but a hardened security tool that respects privacy and performs under pressure.

### ZERO_PROOF
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/zeroproof-a-hardwareenforced-authorization-layer-for-ai-agents-5c3b) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Altaria-hackathon-teams/cybersecurity-cipher-minds.git) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/0kpBNA6XAsE) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Altaria-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://altaria.devfolio.co)

> stop AI agent from going Rouge - in code,not trust

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

ZeroProof is a hardware-anchored authorization layer for AI agents that solves the security gap no one has closed yet — the missing cryptographic link between what a user actually authorized and what an AI agent does. Every existing permission system, from ChatGPT to Copilot, stores its checks on a server that can be compromised. ZeroProof moves the trust anchor to the user's device: the user signs a fine-grained capability grant with Touch ID, and every agent action is checked against that grant in deterministic server-side code — no LLM involved, no way to social-engineer past it. We tested hidden prompt injection against 7 major models and 5 out of 7 were fully hijacked, calling an unauthorized API to exfiltrate real data. In every case, ZeroProof blocked it. The system runs four layers — prompt integrity verification, hardware-signed capability enforcement, replay attack prevention, and semantic drift detection.

**Challenges we ran into**

• Bridging the WebAuthn gap — Making the capability grant feel hardware-enforced without full Secure Enclave signing of arbitrary payloads, which the Web Crypto API doesn't directly expose. We solved this by combining WebAuthn device attestation with HMAC-signed grant tokens, cryptographically tying the grant to device identity.

• WASM cold starts on Vercel — The MiniLM embedding model used for drift detection is large enough to cause serverless cold-start timeouts. We worked around this with lazy loading on first drift-check call and a lightweight keep-warm strategy so Layer 3 stays responsive.

• Making an invisible attack visibly real  — A log message saying "blocked" doesn't convince anyone. We had to build both sides of the attack a realistic attacker page with hidden prompt injection and a live exfiltration sink accepting real HTTP POST requests ,so judges could watch actual bytes move to an attacker server, not just read about it.

• Stateless nonce coordination — Vercel serverless instances don't share memory, so replay protection via in-memory nonce storage breaks across instances. We scoped the demo to single-instance usage and flagged distributed nonce storage (Redis) as the production requirement.

• Threshold tuning for drift detection — Cosine similarity drift detection required balancing false positives on legitimate multi-step agent workflows against catching genuine behavioral manipulation, with no labelled dataset to validate against under hackathon time constraints.

**Cybersecurity + Artificial Intelligence**

ZeroProof sits at the exact intersection where AI and cybersecurity collide, the moment an AI agent stops being a chatbot and starts taking real actions in the world.

The AI side of the problem

Modern AI agents don't just answer questions , they read emails, write code, call APIs, and manage files. The attack surface moves with the capability. Prompt injection, the core attack ZeroProof defends against, is fundamentally an AI problem: the model is too trusting, reads attacker-controlled content, and decides to act on it. No amount of firewall or network security stops this because the threat enters through the model's input, not the network.

The cybersecurity side of the problem

Traditional cybersecurity solved authorization with server-side checks — OAuth scopes, RBAC, ACLs. These work when the entity requesting access is a human or a deterministic program. They break when the entity is an LLM that can be manipulated through its input to request things it was never meant to request. The entire permission model assumes the requester is trustworthy. AI agents are not, they can be hijacked mid-session.

Where ZeroProof fits

ZeroProof applies a classical cybersecurity principle hardware-rooted trust, cryptographic authorization, zero-trust architecture to the AI agent layer specifically. It treats the AI the same way a zero-trust network treats an unverified endpoint: don't trust what it says it's allowed to do, verify it against a signed credential that the AI cannot forge or influence. The capability grant is essentially an AI-native access token, signed by hardware the attacker can't reach, checked by code the model can't touch.

This maps directly onto three active areas in the cybersecurity + AI space — AI red teaming (the injection tests), AI governance and compliance (the audit trail capability grants produce), and agentic security
(enforcing least-privilege for autonomous AI systems)  which are among the fastest-growing concerns in enterprise security right now.

> Detect. Correlate. Destroy.

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Express.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Express.js-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

AegixChain AI is an autonomous, multi-layered security ecosystem designed to act as a self-healing digital immune system. It integrates an Aegix Brain (AI Agent) with real-time system sensors (EDR/IPS) to provide 360-degree visibility. The platform doesn't just notify; it intervenes. It utilizes a hierarchical defense strategy—from sub-second deep learning anomaly detection at the packet level to high-reasoning agentic analysis for complex incident response—ensuring that threats are neutralized at the earliest stage of the kill-chain.

How the Idea Uses AI and Cybersecurity
The project leverages a unique "Tri-Model" AI architecture integrated with core Cybersecurity primitives:
   Agentic AI (Gemini & LangGraph): A high-reasoning "Analyst Agent" that correlates disparate logs, maps them to the MITRE ATT&CK framework, and explains complex attack paths to human operators.
   Reinforcement Learning (PPO): An autonomous decision engine that learns optimal defense policies over time, deciding when to block an IP, isolate a host, or deploy a Deception Layer (Honeypots/Honey-credentials).
   Deep Learning (MLP & Isolation Forest): Used for real-time pattern recognition in system processes and network flows to detect statistical anomalies without pre-defined signatures.
   Automated EDR: Implements absolute quarantine (permission stripping) and autonomous vulnerability patching using system audit data.

 The Expected Impact & Real-World Use Case
AegixChain AI revolutionizes enterprise security by reducing the Mean Time to Respond (MTTR) from hours to milliseconds. Its real-world application is critical for protecting high-stakes infrastructure (Financial Services, Cloud Providers, or Smart Cities) where an "Isolation-First" autonomous response can prevent catastrophic data exfiltration. By automating 90% of routine triage and remediation, it allows human experts to focus on strategic threat hunting rather than manual blocklists.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenge:
Handling real-time data synchronization caused database locks and UI timeouts. High-frequency API polling for system logs, network traffic, and IPS threat intel overwhelmed the Express backend and caused our Firebase Auth interceptors to hang.
How I Overcame It:
I optimized the architecture by removing blocking Firebase token requests from the API interceptor, relying strictly on cached JWTs. I also implemented staggered UI polling intervals and asynchronous Gemini AI processing to ensure the dashboard remained highly responsive while ingesting live telemetry.

**Cybersecurity + Artificial Intelligence**

Aegix CyberSOC is an AI-driven security platform that transforms traditional reactive SOCs into autonomous defense systems. It integrates EDR, IPS, threat hunting, and Zero Trust to monitor, analyze, and actively stop threats in real time. Using machine learning for anomaly detection, NLP for explanations, and multi-agent collaboration, it reduces alert fatigue. The system correlates data, predicts attacks, and autonomously responds—shifting cybersecurity from manual detection to intelligent prevention and decision-making.
