> Disputes to Trust — Decentralizing Land Ownership.

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Smart Contract](https://img.shields.io/badge/Smart%20Contract-333333?style=flat-square) ![Hardhat](https://img.shields.io/badge/Hardhat-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

🚨 The Problem It Solves

Land ownership systems are often fragmented, paper-based, and prone to fraud, manipulation, and disputes. Verifying ownership requires manual checks across multiple offices, making the process slow, unreliable, and inefficient.

✅ How This Solution Helps
🔐 Fraud Prevention
Stores land ownership records on blockchain, making them tamper-proof and immutable.
⚡ Instant Verification
Anyone can verify ownership in seconds without relying on manual paperwork.
🧾 Trusted Digital Records
Integrates KYC (DigiLocker) and verified documents to ensure only legitimate owners are registered.
👨‍⚖️ Reduced Disputes
Transparent ownership history reduces conflicts and legal complications.
🌐 Easy Access for All
Citizens, buyers, and authorities can access records anytime from anywhere.
📉 Eliminates Middlemen
Removes dependency on brokers and manual approvals, reducing corruption and delays.
🎯 Real-World Impact

This system transforms land registry into a secure, transparent, and efficient digital infrastructure, making property transactions safer, faster, and more trustworthy for everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

⚠️ Challenges I Ran Into
🔗 1. Blockchain Connectivity Issues

While integrating ethers.js, I faced ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED errors because the app was trying to connect to a local node (localhost:8545) that wasn’t running.
👉 Solution: Switched to Infura (Sepolia testnet) and configured the correct RPC URL in environment variables.

🔐 2. Verifying Real Ownership (Biggest Challenge)

Ensuring that the user claiming land ownership is the actual owner was complex. Blockchain alone cannot verify real-world identity.
👉 Solution: Designed a hybrid approach using DigiLocker-based KYC, document validation, and authority approval before storing data on-chain.

📄 3. Handling Sensitive Data Securely

Storing Aadhaar or legal documents directly on-chain is unsafe and impractical.
👉 Solution: Used hashing (keccak256) for Aadhaar and stored documents on IPFS, keeping only hashes on blockchain.

⚡ 4. Event Filtering & Data Retrieval

Fetching specific land records using events was tricky, especially filtering by hashed Aadhaar.
👉 Solution: Corrected ethers.js filter usage and optimized query logic to efficiently fetch and match on-chain data.

🧠 5. System Design Complexity

Balancing decentralization with real-world validation (government systems, KYC, approvals) was challenging.
👉 Solution: Adopted a hybrid architecture — off-chain verification + on-chain storage — ensuring both trust and practicality.

💡 Key Learning

Blockchain is powerful, but real-world problems require combining it with trusted off-chain systems.

### CredVault
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/credvault-44db) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/monojitgoswami69/hackstorm) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hack%20Storm%202.26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hack-storm.devfolio.co)

> Own your data, share at your will

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Web3](https://img.shields.io/badge/Web3-333333?style=flat-square) ![Polygon](https://img.shields.io/badge/Polygon-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Today's credential verification system is fundamentally broken:

- *Fraud is rampant* - Fake degrees, forged certificates, and fabricated employment records cost businesses billions annually and erode trust in legitimate credentials
- *Verification is slow and expensive* - Background checks take weeks, require manual phone calls, and cost $50-200 per verification
- *Users have zero control* - Your university, employer, or government owns your credentials and decides who can access your personal data
- *Privacy doesn't exist* - To prove you graduated, you must expose your GPA, date of birth, and other sensitive information you may not want to share


**Who suffers?**

- *Job seekers* wait weeks for background checks while opportunities slip away
- *Employers* waste resources on manual verification and still get deceived by fake credentials
- *Universities* field thousands of verification calls instead of focusing on education
- *Individuals* have no way to prove qualifications without surrendering their privacy


**How CredVault Solves This**

CredVault is a decentralized identity verification system that puts users in control:

- **Blockchain-anchored credentials** - Merkle roots are stored on Polygon, making forgery mathematically impossible while keeping data off-chain for privacy
- **Instant verification** - Verifiers get cryptographic proof in seconds, not weeks
- **Selective disclosure** - Share only what's needed. Prove you have a degree *without* revealing your GPA. Prove you're over 21 *without* showing your birthdate
- **User-owned identity** - Your credentials live in your wallet. You decide who sees what, when, and for how long

**Challenges we ran into**

**Smart Contract Gas Optimization**

Our initial smart contract was too expensive to deploy on testnet - the gas fees exceeded free faucet limits. We had to completely rearchitect the contract, removing issuer management and revocation logic to MongoDB, keeping only merkle root anchoring on-chain. This reduced deployment cost by *over 90%* while maintaining cryptographic integrity.

**Wallet Address Case Sensitivity**

Ethereum addresses are case-insensitive but string comparisons are not. We spent hours debugging why credentials weren't appearing for users before realizing MongoDB queries were doing exact string matches. *Solution:* Implemented case-insensitive regex matching for all wallet address lookups.

**Selective Disclosure Logic**

Building the ZKP-style selective disclosure was tricky - we needed to let users hide specific credential fields while still allowing verifiers to validate the credential's authenticity. We solved this by separating the merkle proof verification from the data disclosure, so verifiers can confirm *a valid credential exists* without seeing hidden fields.

**Session Management Across Roles**

With three distinct user roles hitting different API endpoints, keeping authentication consistent was challenging. We built a unified session system that determines role from wallet address at login and enforces role-based access at the layout level.

**IPFS Pinning Reliability**

Early tests showed credentials occasionally failing to load because IPFS content wasn't pinned properly. We switched to Pinata's pinning service and added retry logic with fallback gateways to ensure credential data remains accessible.

**The problem it solves**

## What People Can Use This For

* **Transparent Donations**
  Donors can contribute using their wallets and **track exactly where their money goes**, eliminating doubts about misuse.

* **Trustworthy Fundraising for NGOs**
  NGOs can create verified campaigns, making it easier to **build credibility and attract more donors**.

* **Milestone-Based Funding**
  Funds can be released in stages, ensuring money is used **only when progress is proven**.

* **Global Accessibility**
  Anyone with a wallet can donate—no banking barriers, no geographic limitations.

---

## How It Makes Things Easier

* **No Middlemen**
  Direct wallet-to-wallet transfers reduce delays and extra fees.

* **Real-Time Tracking**
  Every transaction is recorded on **Solana**, allowing instant verification.

* **Simple Campaign Management**
  NGOs can easily create and manage campaigns using structured data stored in **MongoDB**.

* **Fast & Low-Cost Transactions**
  Micro-donations become practical due to minimal fees.

---

## How It Makes Things Safer

* **Immutable Records**
  Transactions cannot be altered, ensuring **complete transparency**.

* **Reduced Fraud Risk**
  Donors don’t have to blindly trust organisations—everything is verifiable.

* **Secure Wallet-Based Payments**
  No need to share sensitive banking details.

* **Audit-Friendly System**
  NGOs and regulators can easily review fund flow and usage.

---

## Bottom Line

This platform transforms donations from **“trust-based” → “proof-based”**, making charity more **transparent, efficient, and accountable** for everyone involved.

**Challenges we ran into**

## Challenges I Ran Into

### 1. Solana Devnet & Transaction Visibility Issues

One major hurdle was that transactions were not appearing on the explorer, often showing *“account does not exist.”*
This was caused by:

* Using inconsistent RPC endpoints
* Wallet connected to a different network than the backend

**Fix:**
I standardised everything to **Solana Devnet**, switched to a reliable RPC provider, and ensured both frontend and wallet were aligned to the same cluster.

---

### 2. Faucet Balance Not Reflecting

Even after requesting airdrops, the balance wasn’t updating.

**Fix:**

* Forced a fresh airdrop request
* Confirmed wallet network settings
* Used CLI checks to verify balance independently

This helped isolate UI vs network issues.

---

### 3. Wallet Integration & Transaction Handling

Handling wallet-based transactions in a React/Next.js environment introduced issues like:

* Failed or unconfirmed transactions
* UI not updating after payment

**Fix:**

* Added proper transaction confirmation (`confirmTransaction`)
* Implemented state refresh after successful transfers
* Improved error handling for failed signatures

---

### 4. Schema Consistency Between Frontend & Backend

Mismatch between frontend forms and backend validation schemas caused failed campaign/NGO creation.

**Fix:**

* Centralised validation using shared Zod schemas
* Ensured strict alignment between form inputs and database structure in **MongoDB**

---

### 5. UI Stability (Card Layout Breaking)

Dynamic content caused inconsistent card sizes and overflow issues.

**Fix:**

* Used fixed height with flexbox layout
* Applied text clamping and overflow control
* Stabilised components for consistent rendering

---

## Key Takeaway

Most challenges came from **network inconsistencies, async blockchain behaviour, and schema mismatches**. Solving them required aligning environments, improving validation, and handling blockchain confirmations more reliably.

**Best Use of MongoDB**

This project utilises **MongoDB** to efficiently manage NGOs, campaigns, and user interactions with a flexible schema. Its document-based structure enables rapid development, seamless scaling, and real-time updates, supporting dynamic campaign data and integrations while ensuring reliable storage alongside blockchain transactions for a robust hybrid architecture.

**Best Use of Gemini API**

This project uses **Gemini API** to verify the NGOs by validating their background, their deatails, their uploaded documents and all about the NGO's.

**Best Build on Solana**

This project leverages **Solana** for fast, low-cost, and transparent donations, enabling real-time tracking of funds on-chain. By integrating wallet-based transactions, milestone-based disbursements, and verifiable records, it showcases an efficient, scalable, and trustless charity system—aligning perfectly with Solana’s strengths in high throughput and minimal transaction fees.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Flask](https://img.shields.io/badge/Flask-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

FreshDrop solves the problem of food wastage in local grocery and fresh produce markets. Vendors often struggle to sell perishable items before they expire, leading to heavy losses and environmental waste.

At the same time, consumers miss out on affordable fresh food because pricing is static and does not reflect real-time demand or shelf life.

FreshDrop bridges this gap by introducing a smart pricing engine that dynamically adjusts product prices based on freshness, demand, and time remaining. This ensures vendors maximize sales while customers get better deals.

Additionally, blockchain-based verification ensures transparency and trust in pricing and product quality.

**Algorand**

**How Algorand is Used:**
FreshDrop logs every price optimization as a real 0-ALGO transaction on Algorand Testnet. The transaction note contains product pricing data — old price, new price, margin, expiry score — creating a tamper-proof audit trail. Each update returns a real TxID verifiable on Lora AlgoKit Explorer.

**Why Algorand:**
Retail pricing is prone to manipulation. Algorand's immutability ensures no one can alter historical price records — making pricing transparent and compliance-ready for quick commerce platforms. 🚀

### Decentralised Carbon Footprint Optimisation Engine
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/decentralised-carbon-footprint-optimisation-engine-ba1f) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/Hacknovate-7-0/CFOE-blockchainV2) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/Hpbz9f33kWw) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Hacknovate--7.0-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://hacknovate07.devfolio.co)

> Bankrupting Carbon, Not the Planet.

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![Gunicorn](https://img.shields.io/badge/Gunicorn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Blockchain](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blockchain-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![ReportLabs](https://img.shields.io/badge/ReportLabs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

70% of corporate carbon emissions are hidden inside supplier operations, yet most enterprises audit their suppliers only once per quarter. That 90-day blind spot is where violations fester, fines accumulate, and ESG commitments quietly collapse.
CfoE solves this for procurement teams, compliance officers, and sustainability leads who are tired of flying blind between audits. A supplier receives an EPA fine in March. Your quarterly audit runs in June. Three months of non-compliant parts enter your production line. The resulting recall costs $50M. CfoE detects it in under an hour.
Manual ESG scoring is inconsistent, slow, and impossible to audit. CfoE's deterministic scoring engine guarantees that identical inputs always produce identical risk scores — no human error, no variance. No CTO will deploy AI that can suspend a sole-source supplier without human sign-off, so CfoE's mandatory Human-in-the-Loop gate pauses the entire workflow at score ≥ 0.80 and waits for explicit human approval before any action is taken.
Every audit result, every HITL decision, and every report hash is anchored to the Algorand blockchain — immutable, timestamped, and verifiable by any regulator or investor without calling your compliance team. And because compliance shouldn't just be a penalty game, the Carbon Credit Gamification System rewards suppliers who consistently reduce emissions with credits, badges, and leaderboard rankings — turning sustainability into a performance competition.
Procurement officers get real-time supplier risk flags before contracts are signed. ESG analysts reclaim 97% of audit time — from 8 hours to 15 minutes. CFOs avoid $250K+ average regulatory fines per violation. Sustainability leads track supplier emissions continuously against 2030 targets. And regulators can verify any audit result independently via Algorand — no trust required.

**Challenges we ran into**

The hardest architectural decision was realising that LLMs cannot be trusted for compliance-critical calculations. Early builds used the LLM to compute ESG scores and got different answers for the same input on different runs. For a system that can suspend a supplier, non-determinism is a dealbreaker. We scrapped LLM scoring entirely and built a DeterministicCalculationAgent that bypasses the LLM reasoning loop completely, calling a fixed algorithm directly. Identical inputs now always produce identical scores across 100 runs — verified by our 22-test suite.
Implementing a workflow that genuinely pauses mid-execution and waits for human input without losing session state was technically brutal. Early attempts either timed out, lost context, or resumed from the wrong point in the pipeline. We used ADK's LongRunningFunctionTool with request_confirmation() and ResumabilityConfig to persist full session state between pause and resume. The workflow now freezes exactly at the PolicyAgent and resumes precisely where it left off after human approval.
AlgoKit's LocalNet requires Docker, which our development environment didn't have. This blocked account creation, LocalNet startup, and the VibeKit MCP tools. We switched to Algorand Testnet via Algonode's public endpoints — no Docker, no local node. Accounts were generated directly via py-algorand-sdk, funded via the Testnet faucet, and all audit anchoring goes directly to Testnet. For VibeKit MCP, we switched from the official Docker-dependent MCP to GoPlausible Remote MCP which requires no local container at all.
Our agents needed realistic supplier data but we had no live ERP or IoT feed. Static dummy data made demos unconvincing and made it impossible to test spike detection or dynamic HITL triggering. We built a real-time carbon emitter simulator that models a steel manufacturing factory with 5 emitting processes, shift-based multipliers, Gaussian noise, random violation injection, and manual spike triggers — all streaming via WebSocket to a live dashboard and posting directly to CfoE's audit endpoint.
Finally, py-algorand-sdk was installed but Python kept throwing ModuleNotFoundError. The SDK was installed in the old project's venv but we were running Python from the new project's venv. Activating the correct environment and reinstalling resolved it. Always confirm pip show shows the right Location path.

**Algorand**

We built CfoE on Algorand because enterprise compliance has one unsolvable problem, nobody trusts the records. Audit scores get altered, HITL approvals get backdated, and compliance reports get quietly edited after the fact. A regulator or investor has no way to verify what actually happened and when.
Algorand fixes this. Every time our pipeline completes an audit, we anchor three things permanently on-chain, the ESG risk score, the SHA-256 hash of the emissions input data, and the SHA-256 hash of the final report. If anyone tampers with the record after the fact, the hash won't match. The proof is on-chain and anyone can verify it without calling our compliance team.
We chose Algorand specifically because it is carbon-negative, which matters deeply for a project built around carbon accountability. We couldn't anchor ESG audit results on an energy-intensive chain — that would be embarrassing. Algorand's 4-second finality and near-zero transaction fees (~0.001 ALGO per audit) also make it viable at enterprise scale across thousands of suppliers without the cost becoming prohibitive.
For development, we used AlgoKit as our primary toolkit and integrated VibeKit with the GoPlausible Remote MCP server, which let our AI coding agent interact directly with the Algorand blockchain ,compiling, deploying, and querying without leaving the development conversation. We ran into a Docker dependency issue with AlgoKit's LocalNet and the official VibeKit MCP, so we switched to Algorand Testnet via Algonode's public endpoints, which required zero infrastructure and worked immediately.
The foundation we've laid also sets up our next phase, minting carbon credits as Algorand Standard Assets (ASAs) for suppliers who consistently score below the 0.40 ESG threshold, making those credits tradeable on-chain and giving the gamification system real economic weight.

**The problem it solves**

India’s voter data is fragmented across states, causing major issues for millions of people who move for work, education, marriage, or housing. Migrants often lose their voting rights because updating or transferring a voter ID is slow, manual, and error-prone. Duplicate, outdated, or fake voter entries also weaken trust in the electoral system. Citizens cannot easily check their voter status, track updates, or verify their identity in real time. Election officers (BLO/ERO/DEO) struggle with manual verification, paper-based processes, and lack of centralized, trustworthy data. This creates delays, confusion, and large-scale inefficiencies during elections.

With the Unified Electoral Roll & Voter Mobility System, every citizen gets a single verified voter identity that stays with them no matter where they move in India. They can easily register, update details, or request constituency changes from the app, without visiting offices. Aadhaar-based OTP eKYC ensures fast and secure verification. QR scanning and digital records reduce mistakes and eliminate fake or duplicate entries.

Election officers get digital dashboards, automated verification tools, and real-time updates, making their work faster, cleaner, and more transparent. By storing critical voter logs on a secure Algorand-backed system, the platform ensures tamper-proof records, stronger data integrity, and a more trusted electoral process.

In short, the system makes voting easier for citizens, verification easier for officers, and democracy safer and more transparent for everyone.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges I ran into, Sir, was building a unified voter identity system that works seamlessly across states while preventing duplicate and fake entries. Integrating Aadhaar-based OTP eKYC, QR scanning, and real-time verification required strong security and careful data handling. A major hurdle was implementing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process digitally. Traditionally, SIR involves BLOs conducting door-to-door verification, updating rolls, removing duplicates, and validating shifted voters. Converting this manual, paper-heavy workflow into a fully digital, real-time system—while keeping it compliant with electoral rules—was complex. Designing digital SIR forms, officer verifications, and automated discrepancy detection took several iterations.

Another challenge was managing role-based access for BLOs, EROs, DEOs, and State Admins because each officer performs a different part of the verification cycle. Sir, I also struggled with UI/UX for features like scanning, face matching, and migration status tracking. To overcome these issues, I broke each module into smaller tasks, tested them repeatedly, refined the data model, added strict validations, and used Algorand’s secure logging for transparent, tamper-proof audit trails. These step-by-step improvements helped me build a more reliable, scalable, and compliant system.

**Algorand**

Our project fits perfectly into Algorand’s Governance, Identity, and Social Impact tracks because it uses Algorand’s secure, transparent, and high-performance blockchain to build a unified national voter identity system. By anchoring voter registration, migration requests, verification logs, and audit trails on Algorand, the system ensures tamper-proof data integrity and eliminates duplicate or fake voter entries. Algorand’s low-cost, low-latency transactions enable real-time, seamless voter mobility across states, allowing every citizen—students, workers, migrants, and families—to carry a single verified voter identity wherever they go. This transforms India’s electoral infrastructure into a trustworthy, transparent, and citizen-centric ecosystem. By combining decentralized identity, strong cryptographic security, and social impact, our solution demonstrates how Algorand can power the next generation of digital democracy.

**The problem it solves**

AutoPilotX acts as a 24/7 digital employee specifically engineered to solve the operational bottlenecks faced by Indian MSMEs:

Eliminates Manual Data Entry: Automatically extracts structured data (GSTIN, line items, totals) from messy PDFs, JPEGs, and physical invoices using multimodal AI.

24/7 Customer Support: Replaces missed after-hours calls with a conversational Voice Agent that can answer complex product and pricing queries by instantly searching internal business documents.

Automates the Back-Office: The Email Manager agent automatically categorizes incoming emails, filters out spam, drafts context-aware replies, and compiles daily financial/GST summaries for the business owner.

Unifies Fragmented Data: Transforms scattered physical bills, catalogs, and ledgers into a searchable, centralized RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) knowledge base.

**Challenges we ran into**

Building a real-time, bi-directional AI voice architecture presented several tough technical hurdles:

Audio "Chipmunking" & Sample Rates: The browser natively captures audio at 44.1kHz or 48kHz, but the Gemini Voice API strictly requires 16kHz. Sending raw audio caused the AI to hear everything "sped up."

How I fixed it: I implemented a hard 16000Hz internal resample loop directly off the user's mic using AudioContext before packetizing the data.

Network Jitter & Audio Cracking: Because WebSocket chunks arrive unpredictably, playing them instantly caused the synthesized voice to constantly pause and crackle.

How I fixed it: I engineered a custom 100ms Jitter Buffer. By intentionally delaying the playback of the first audio chunk by 100 milliseconds, the subsequent chunks could queue up smoothly, resulting in gapless audio playback.

Prompt Injections & Data Security: I needed to ensure the Voice Agent couldn't be tricked into giving 100% discounts or leaking data to malicious callers.

How I fixed it: I built a strict, unambiguous system prompt with "few-shot" examples of how to politely decline off-topic requests, and implemented strict character limits on queries to prevent text-bomb injections.

Blind Phishing Replies: Allowing an AI to automatically draft emails is dangerous if a phishing email asks for bank details.

How I fixed it: I created a pre-processing categorization pipeline using gemini-2.5-flash that classifies the intent of every email first. If an email is flagged as "High Risk," the system halts the RAG pipeline entirely and alerts the owner.

For your Devfolio submission, you can use these polished paragraphs to describe your project. They are designed to sound professional, technically grounded, and high-impact.

## Project Description: KrishiShakti
The Problem
Traditional agriculture, particularly in arid regions like India, Israel, and the UAE, remains a high-stakes gamble against an increasingly unpredictable climate. Farmers are currently trapped in a cycle of "Resource Blindness," where over-irrigation wastes up to 40% of precious groundwater, and "Micro-Droughts" stress crops long before visible wilting occurs, cutting millet yields by nearly 20%. Furthermore, the crisis doesn't end at the harvest; without precise environmental monitoring, nearly one-third of stored millets are lost to fungal Aflatoxins caused by undetected humidity spikes in storage silos.

The Solution
KrishiShakti is a comprehensive IoT-driven Agri-Tech ecosystem designed to transform millet farming from a manual struggle into a data-backed science. At its core, the system utilizes a NodeMCU-based sensor array to automate precision irrigation, ensuring the soil moisture stays within the "Goldilocks Zone" for specific millet varieties across their 60–120 day growth cycles. To combat total water scarcity, the project integrates an Atmospheric Water Generation (AWG) system using a Peltier-Desiccant hybrid model, which "mines" liquid water from air humidity as a sustainable backup source. All critical data—from temperature and gas leaks to water levels—is fetched via a Python-based REST API and logged into a JSON digital twin, providing farmers with a historical ledger for predictive crop management.

The Innovation
What sets KrishiShakti apart is its circular approach to energy and resources. The system doesn't just treat "Latent Heat" from the water condensation process as waste; it redirects this thermal energy to dry harvested seeds or warm nurseries during cold winter nights. By combining real-time Blynk cloud control with an automated "Safety-First" logic, the project solves the conflict between human oversight and machine precision. It effectively bridges the gap between traditional harvesting and high-tech sustainable farming, offering a low-cost, scalable solution that directly addresses global food security and water conservation challenges.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. The "Ghost Switch" Pin Conflict
The Challenge: Early in the build, the Water Pump would trigger automatically whenever the water tank was full, even if I manually turned it "OFF" in the Blynk app. After hours of debugging, I discovered a GPIO Pin Conflict. I had assigned both the Pump Relay and the Green Status LED to pin D4.

The Fix: The Ultrasonic sensor logic was sending a HIGH signal to D4 to light the LED, which the Relay board interpreted as a command to start the pump. I performed a "Pin Migration," moving the LED to an independent pin (D8) and the Gas Sensor to D2. This physically isolated the high-current relay logic from the status indicators, restoring 100% manual control via the Blynk cloud.

## 🌡️ 2. Latent Heat & Peltier Thermal Runaway
The Challenge: When testing the Atmospheric Water Generator (AWG), the cold side of the Peltier module would stay cold for only 5 minutes before the entire unit began to overheat. I realized that the Latent Heat released during condensation, combined with the module's own heat, was causing "Thermal Runaway."

The Fix: I redesigned the cooling stack using a high-CFM brushless fan and a dual-heat-pipe aluminum sink. I also implemented a Software Interlock in the code that monitors the ambient temperature via the DHT11. If the temperature exceeds a safety threshold, the system automatically toggles the Peltier relay to prevent hardware burnout, while the LCD alerts the user to "Cooling Mode."

## 📡 3. The REST API "Data Throttling"
The Challenge: While fetching real-time data into my JSON ledger using Python, the script would frequently crash or return "Error 429" (Too Many Requests). My initial script was pinging the Blynk Cloud too fast, hitting the server's rate limits.

The Fix: I implemented Request Pacing and Error Handling in the Python script. I added a time.sleep(2) delay between fetches and wrapped the API calls in a try-except block. This ensures that even if one sensor read fails, the script continues to log the rest of the data, maintaining a consistent and reliable historical record for the crop's digital twin.

**Main Track: The Deepforge Arena**

KrishiShakti "forges" three distinct engineering fields into one:Electronics: Managing high-current DC loads for the Peltier and Pump relays while maintaining signal integrity for sensitive $I^2C$ and DHT sensors.Thermodynamics: Managing Latent Heat and Dew Point calculations. You aren't just cooling a surface; you are manipulating phase changes (Vapor to Liquid) to create a new water source.Fluid Dynamics: Using Ultrasonic sensors to manage reservoir levels and calculating soil saturation to prevent nutrient leaching.## ⚙️ 2. This "Circular Economy" approach is exactly what high-level engineering judges look for—optimizing every Joule of energy in the system.

# ClearFund: The Problem It Solves

## **Transparency Crisis in Public Fund Management**
Government infrastructure and public projects often lack real-time visibility. Citizens, auditors, and stakeholders struggle to track:
- Where public funds are being allocated
- How much has actually been spent or released
- Project progress and milestone completion
- Whether contractors are delivering on commitments

## **Core Problems Addressed**

### 1. **Accountability Vacuum**
Public funds disappear into bureaucratic black boxes. ClearFund brings every transaction on-chain, creating an immutable audit trail that cannot be falsified or hidden.

### 2. **Contractor Trust & Performance**
- Governments struggle to vet and monitor contractors fairly
- Contractors face barriers to entry due to lack of reputation systems
- Bidding processes are opaque and favor incumbents

**Solution:** Blockchain-verified contractor profiles, competitive bidding dashboards, and milestone-based fund release ensure trust without intermediaries.

### 3. **Delayed Fund Disbursement**
Traditional escrow and fund release takes weeks. Projects stall while waiting for approvals.

**Solution:** Smart contract escrows automatically release funds when milestones are verified and accepted by government approvers—no delays, no paperwork.

### 4. **No Real-Time Visibility for Citizens**
Citizens have no way to know if their tax money is being spent wisely or if projects are progressing.

**Solution:** Public Projects Ledger shows real-time tracking of all projects, budgets, funds released, and completion status—fully transparent and blockchain-verified.

### 5. **Fragmented Proof & Evidence Management**
Milestone proofs (photos, documents, receipts) are scattered across emails and drives. Hard to verify authenticity.

**Solution:** IPFS-pinned evidence logs with on-chain hashing mean every proof is immutable, timestamped, and directly linked to milestones.

---

## **Who Benefits**

| Stakeholder | Benefit |
|---|---|
| **Citizens & Taxpayers** | See exactly where public funds go; verify project progress in real-time |
| **Government Agencies** | Reduce fraud, speed up fund release, gain audit-ready compliance automatically |
| **Contractors** | Fair bidding process, reputation building, faster payment (no manual escrow delays) |
| **Auditors** | Complete immutable audit trail; no data manipulation possible |
| **Project Managers** | Streamlined milestone approval workflow; AI-powered context for faster decisions |

---

## **Key Use Cases**

- **Infrastructure Projects** — Roads, bridges, water systems: track spend vs. actual construction

-  **Social Programs** — Healthcare clinics, schools: verify fund utilization and service delivery

-  **Disaster Relief** — Rapid, transparent allocation and distribution of emergency funds

-  **Land Development** — Track plot allocation, surveys, and construction phases with proof at each step

- **Government Procurement** — Competitive bidding with reputation scores and performance tracking


---

## **Why It Matters**

In markets where **trust is broken**, ClearFund rebuilds it through **technology, not institutions**. Every rupee, every milestone, every decision is verifiable on-chain—making corruption economically irrational and transparency the default.

**Challenges we ran into**

# ClearFund: Challenges & Solutions

## 1. MetaMask Connection & Reconnection

### Challenge
We started with unreliable wallet state: users who reconnected or switched accounts/networks experienced stale UI and failed transactions.

### Detailed Behavior
- accountsChanged and chainChanged were not consistently handled in all components.
- A user might sign in, switch network in MetaMask, then try a tx on the wrong chain.
- Disconnect and reconnect flows were fragmented, so a page refresh sometimes left the app in “ghost” connected state.

### Solution
- Global wallet context with listeners for accountsChanged, chainChanged, disconnect.
- Exponential backoff + retry for reconnection; fallback to explicit "Reconnect" prompt.
- On-mount validation with window.ethereum.request({ method: 'eth_accounts' }).
- Network detection before every write operation; error message when mismatch.

### Result
Predictable connection state, immediate UI update after account/network change, and fewer failed TX attempts.

---

## 2. Duplicate Fund Release Logging

### Challenge
Financial flow required strict correctness, but we saw duplicated backend entries for one release action due to repeated events.

### root causes
- Unthrottled frontend button caused rapid repeated calls on poor connectivity.
- Ethers.js event listeners emitted same transaction more than once due to multiple block confirmations.
- No database guard, so backend persisted all events.

### Solution
- Frontend: button lockout (1s cooldown) + spinner until confirmation.
- Backend: in-memory dedupe cache keyed by transaction_hash + event_type + milestone_id with short TTL.
- DB: unique constraint on transaction_hash + event_type + milestone_id (final source-of-truth safeguard).
- Pre-write contract state check: do not process if milestone already released.

### Result
One real release becomes one persisted record, no over-counted funds or milestone statuses.

---

## 3. Approval/Rejection Idempotency

### Challenge
Similar concurrency issue in approval flow: repeated clicks / retry logic could produce both approve and reject records for same milestone.

### Root causes
- No state lock during processing.
- Race conditions between transaction and event synchronization.
- Absence of idempotent keys at DB layer.

### Solution
- DB unique key for transaction_hash + milestone_id + approval_type.
- Milestone state machine validated before changing state:
  - Reject not allowed if marked completed.
  - Approve not allowed if already rejected (or requires reset cycle).
- Action lock and UI blocking while pending.
- Store `approval_timestamp` and `approver_address` for audit.

### Result
Consistent final state; duplicate actions are ignored and logged safely.

---

## Key Lessons
1. Idempotency must be implemented at UI, backend, and database layers.
2. Blockchain apps require user-feedback for transient states (pending, retries, and network mismatch).
3. Unique constraints are the ultimate defense in financial workflows.
4. Testing edge cases (rapid clicks, refresh mid-TX, wallet disconnect) is essential.

---

## Impact
After the fixes, ClearFund works as a production-grade system with resilient wallet connectivity, dev-grade transaction accuracy, and strong audit credibility.

**Ethereum Track**

# ClearFund: Ethereum Track Submission

## Project Fit for the Ethereum Track

ClearFund is designed as an Ethereum-first platform that uses smart contracts and decentralized assets to bring transparency and trust to public fund management.

### Ethereum in Action

- Solidity contracts manage project-specific escrows and milestone-based fund release.
- Factory contract deploys per-project escrow instances, enabling modular governance and tracking.
- All key actions are logged as on-chain events: project creation, bid submission, approvals, rejections, and fund release.
- On-chain state is continuously synchronized with frontend via ethers.js and Alchemy.

### Why Ethereum

- Immutable audit trail for public funds (critical for corruption-resistant governance).
- Conditional execution on milestone completion with no manual override possible.
- Publicly verifiable project history that anyone can confirm on-chain.
- Interoperability with ERC-20 token flows (future extension for stablecoin governance).

### Decentralized Data and Evidence

- Proof documents and milestone evidence are stored on IPFS.
- Transaction hashes tie off-chain proofs to blockchain events.
- Ensures proof immutability even when application data is audited later.

### Governance + Security

- Wallet-driven approval workflow via MetaMask.
- Idempotency and event de-duplication logic implemented to prevent duplicate actions.
- Reputational tracking of contractors and completion performance embedded in smart contract events.

## Conclusion

ClearFund is a production-ready ETH-based solution where state transitions and fund flows are secured by Ethereum, designed to make public project finance transparent, accountable, and proven in real time.

**Blockchain & Decentralized Applications**

# ClearFund: Blockchain & Decentralized Applications Track

## How ClearFund Fits Into Blockchain & Decentralized Applications

ClearFund is fundamentally a blockchain-native application that removes intermediaries from public fund management through decentralized infrastructure and smart contracts.

---

## Core Blockchain Components

### 1. Smart Contract Escrow System
ClearFund deploys Solidity-based smart contracts on Ethereum:
- **ProjectEscrow.sol**: Manages fund holding, milestone verification, and conditional fund release
- **Factory.sol**: Deploys individual escrow instances for each project

These contracts encode the fund release logic immutably, ensuring that milestones cannot be skipped, funds cannot be embezzled, and release happens automatically when conditions are met—without any central gatekeeper.

### 2. On-Chain Audit Trail
Every transaction is recorded on Ethereum:
- Fund allocations
- Milestone completions
- Approvals and rejections
- Fund releases

This creates an immutable, publicly verifiable ledger that cannot be altered retroactively. Corruption becomes transparent, auditable, and economically irrational.

### 3. Decentralized Identity & Reputation
Contractor profiles, bidding history, and performance ratings are stored on-chain:
- No central authority can blacklist a contractor unfairly
- Reputation is portable and verifiable
- Bidders compete based on merit, not relationships

### 4. IPFS for Proof & Evidence Management
Milestone proofs (photos, documents, receipts) are stored on IPFS:
- Decentralized storage—no single point of failure
- Content-addressed (hash-based), ensuring immutability
- Proofs are pinned and timestamped on-chain via transaction hashes
- Cannot be deleted, altered, or censored once submitted

---

## Key Blockchain Features

**Removing Intermediaries**
- Traditional public fund management relies on government bureaucrats, officers, and approval chains
- ClearFund replaces this with smart contracts: code executes transparently without human intervention
- Reduces corruption vector, delays, and costs

**Transparency Without Trust**
- Citizens don't need to trust government officials
- They can directly verify transactions on Ethereum
- Every rupee is traceable in real-time

**Conditional Execution**
- Smart contracts enforce "if-then" logic: Milestone proven → funds released automatically
- Not conditional on a person's decision, but on objective verification
- Removes discretionary power from officials

**Immutable Records**
- Blockchain creates tamper-proof records of all fund movements
- Auditors can't be told "the records were lost"
- Every state change is timestamped and irrevocable

---

## Ethereum Integration

ClearFund interacts with Ethereum via ethers.js and Alchemy:
- Fund transfers via smart contracts (ERC-20 compatible USDC/stablecoin paths in future phases)
- Event listeners track contract state changes in real-time
- Gas-optimized contract design for cost efficiency
- Testnet deployment available for staging

---

## Decentralized Architecture

**No Single Point of Failure**
- Frontend: Decentralized storage ready (IPFS/Arweave integration path)
- Backend: Stateless API (can scale horizontally)
- Database: Currently Supabase (centralized for MVP, can migrate to decentralized proofs)
- Blockchain: Ethereum mainnet (owned by no entity)

**User Sovereignty**
- Users control wallets—no KYC gatekeeping
- Government agencies use MetaMask for signing transactions
- Contractors hold their own private keys
- No platform can freeze accounts or revoke access

---

## Why Blockchain Matters Here

Traditional systems already exist for public fund management (bank accounts, approval workflows, audits). Blockchain becomes essential because:

1. **Trust Deficit**: Government institutions in many regions lack public trust. Immutable records rebuild confidence.

2. **Speed**: Smart contracts release funds automatically, reducing approval time from weeks to seconds.

3. **Permanence**: Physical documents can burn. Digital records can be "lost." Blockchain records are forever.

4. **Openness**: Citizens globally can audit projects in real-time. Full transparency for public funds.

5. **Contractor Fairness**: Small contractors can compete fairly without needing bank relationships or political connections.

---

## Blockchain Challenges We Solved

- Handling high transaction costs through batching and event-driven updates
- Ensuring idempotency of smart contract calls (no duplicate fund releases)
- Bridging on-chain and off-chain data (blockchain stores facts, database stores context)
- User experience with wallet connectivity and MetaMask integration

## Conclusion
ClearFund is not blockchain for blockchain's sake. It uses decentralized infrastructure because the problem it solves—rebuilding trust in public fund management—fundamentally requires immutability, transparency, and removal of central intermediaries. Blockchain is the technology that makes this possible

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/yieldrouter-ebec) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/ephemeral78/yieldRouter) [![Video](https://img.shields.io/badge/Video-Watch-FF0000?style=flat-square&logo=youtube&logoColor=white)](https://youtu.be/1H8vqKA0p-M) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-DevsHouse%20'26-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://devshouse26.devfolio.co)

> Cross-Chain Risk-Optimized Yield

![Solidity](https://img.shields.io/badge/Solidity-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![AAVE](https://img.shields.io/badge/AAVE-333333?style=flat-square) ![Ethereum](https://img.shields.io/badge/Ethereum-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![0x](https://img.shields.io/badge/0x-333333?style=flat-square) ![Optimism](https://img.shields.io/badge/Optimism-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

DeFi users seeking stablecoin yield face a fragmented market where lending
opportunities are scattered across multiple protocols and blockchains. Each protocol
offers different APYs and risk profiles that change constantly , making it difficult to
identify and capture the best opportunities.
Manually comparing protocols, evaluating smart contract risk, and bridging funds
across chains is time-consuming, expensive, and technically challenging. Most
users either settle for suboptimal yields in a single protocol or chase high APYs
without proper risk assessment and diversification.
Currently, there is no simple, automated solution that allows users to earn
optimized, risk-adjusted yield across multiple chains and protocols from a single
deposit. While tools exist to view yield data and standards exist for vault interfaces, no
product combines real-time discovery, risk-aware allocation, and cross-chain
execution into one seamless user experience.

**Challenges we ran into**

🌉 1. Cross-Chain Coordination is Asynchronous by Nature

“One of the biggest challenges was dealing with the asynchronous nature of cross-chain systems.

When the Parent Vault sends instructions to Child Vaults via LayerZero, execution doesn’t happen instantly or atomically. Messages can arrive later, in different order, or even fail.

This made it difficult to:

Maintain consistent global state
Track in-flight operations
Design reliable withdraw and rebalance flows

To handle this, I had to design callback-based accounting and introduce mechanisms like pending withdrawals and balance reports.”

🔄 2. Rebalancing Without Breaking Positions

“Rebalancing sounds simple in theory — just move funds — but in practice it’s complex.

The hardest part was:

Handling existing deployed capital
Avoiding unnecessary withdraw/redeposit cycles
Minimizing gas and slippage

Right now, the system prioritizes reallocating idle or new capital, while full forced migration of positions is still being refined.

Designing a clean strategy for:
‘old allocation → new allocation’ across chains
was one of the most challenging parts.”

🧠 3. Designing a Reliable Risk Model (RAYS)

“Another challenge was building RAYS — the risk-adjusted yield scoring system.

Raw APY isn’t enough, so I had to think about:

How to normalize APY across protocols
Incorporating risk signals like TVL and historical stability
Structuring the output in a way smart contracts can consume

Also, since this runs via Chainlink Functions:

The response had to be encoded, parsed, and validated onchain
Which introduced constraints on format and gas usage”
🔗 4. Offchain ↔ Onchain Integration Complexity

“Integrating Chainlink Functions wasn’t just plug-and-play.

Challenges included:

Handling async request lifecycle
Preventing overlapping or duplicate requests
Parsing string responses safely into structured allocations

I had to build safeguards to ensure:

Only valid responses update allocations
The system doesn’t rebalance based on stale or partial data”
⚙️ 5. Automation with Guardrails (Gelato)

“Automation introduces its own risks.

If you rebalance too often:

You waste gas
You overreact to noise

If you rebalance too slowly:

You lose yield

So I had to carefully design:

Drift thresholds
Cooldowns
Hysteresis buffers

Getting this balance right took multiple iterations.”

💸 6. Withdrawal UX vs Capital Efficiency Tradeoff

“A major design challenge was balancing:

Fast withdrawals
vs
Maximizing deployed capital

Keeping too much idle liquidity hurts yield, but deploying everything slows withdrawals.

The solution was a hybrid model:

Fast withdrawals via local reserve
Async withdrawals via cross-chain unwind

But coordinating this cleanly required careful accounting logic.”

🔁 7. State Synchronization Across Chains

“Each chain has its own local state, but the system needs a global view.

This required:

Periodic balance reporting from Child Vaults
Aggregating data in the Parent Vault
Handling stale or delayed reports

Ensuring the Parent always has a reasonably accurate snapshot was non-trivial.”

🧪 8. Testing Cross-Chain Logic Locally

“Testing was surprisingly difficult.

Since real cross-chain messaging is slow and external, I had to:

Build mock LayerZero endpoints
Simulate message passing synchronously
Create integration tests that mimic real-world flows

Even then, there are edge cases that only show up in real environments.”

🖥️ 9. Simulation vs Real Execution Gap

“The frontend includes a simulation engine, but bridging that with real contracts was tricky.

Challenges included:

Representing cross-chain intent without actual bridging
Keeping simulation state consistent with contract logic
Making it useful for demos without being misleading

So the simulation is representative, not exact, which required careful design decisions.”

🔐 10. Security & Failure Handling

“In a system like this, many things can go wrong:

Cross-chain message failure
Oracle issues
Protocol-level risks

So I had to think about:

Fallback paths
Access control (owner, future multisig)
Minimizing trust assumptions

Designing for safety while keeping the system flexible was a constant tradeoff.”

🎯 How to Present This (Tip)

In your video, don’t list all 10.

Pick 3–5 strongest ones, like:

Cross-chain async complexity
Rebalancing difficulty
RAYS design
Withdrawal tradeoffs

That’s enough to show depth without overwhelming.

**Blockchain & Decentralized Applications**

Blockchain is a decentralized digital ledger that records transactions across a distributed network of computers, ensuring transparency, immutability, and trust without relying on a central authority. Data is stored in blocks that are cryptographically linked, making it secure and tamper-resistant. One of its most powerful applications is in the “Blockchain and its Applications” track, which focuses on building real-world solutions such as decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms for lending and yield optimization, supply chain systems for transparent tracking of goods, digital identity management, healthcare record sharing, and smart contracts that automate agreements without intermediaries. This track combines core blockchain principles with practical development skills, enabling the creation of scalable, trustless applications across industries.

**The problem it solves**

AI Alchemist is a no-code backend builder that allows users to visually create APIs by connecting workflow blocks like HTTP requests, database queries, and logic processors. It eliminates the need for manual backend setup by automatically generating API endpoints from the designed flow. The platform focuses on simplicity, flexibility, and rapid development of real-world backend systems such as e-commerce APIs.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Workflow Scalability (UI Complexity)

Designing a drag-and-drop system that remains clean for large workflows was difficult. As nodes increase, managing readability and connections becomes challenging.

⸻

2. Data Flow Between Nodes

Ensuring consistent data passing between blocks (HTTP → DB → Transform → Response) required careful handling of context and variable mapping.

⸻

3. Dynamic Execution Engine

Building a backend engine that can interpret and execute user-defined workflows dynamically (instead of static code) was complex.

⸻

4. Database Abstraction

Abstracting database operations so users don’t need to manually define schemas while still maintaining flexibility was a key challenge.

⸻

5. API Generation

Automatically converting a visual workflow into a working API endpoint with proper request/response handling required careful backend design.

⸻

6. Balancing Simplicity vs Flexibility

Making the platform easy for non-technical users while still supporting advanced logic (code blocks, transforms) was difficult.

⸻

7. Real-Time Debugging & Feedback

Providing meaningful feedback (errors, outputs) for each node during execution was challenging but critical for usability.

**Web3**

Our project, AI Alchemist, fits this track by enabling users to build backend APIs using AI-assisted workflow design. It simplifies backend development by allowing users to visually compose logic instead of writing code. This approach aligns with modern decentralized and AI-driven development trends, where automation, abstraction, and rapid prototyping are key. By integrating AI into backend creation, we make development more accessible, scalable, and efficient.

### FinPilot
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/finpilot-c861) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/David-2610/Finpilot.git) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Stellaris-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://stellaris.devfolio.co)

> Your personal Finance Buddy and Mentor

![HTML](https://img.shields.io/badge/HTML-333333?style=flat-square) ![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square) ![MongoDB](https://img.shields.io/badge/MongoDB-333333?style=flat-square) ![MERN stack](https://img.shields.io/badge/MERN%20stack-333333?style=flat-square) ![axios](https://img.shields.io/badge/axios-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Most Indians know money is tight. They just don't know why — or what to do about it.
FinPilot fixes that. Upload your bank statement and it instantly shows you where your money is actually going. Then it does something no finance app has ever done — it talks to you. In plain language. Using your real numbers. No jargon, no assumptions, no financial degree required.
By the end of the conversation, you have a plan built around your life — not a generic template. And next month, FinPilot checks if you kept your promises to yourself.
Your money, finally making sense.

**Challenges we ran into**

The biggest challenge wasn't the code — it was making the AI behave like a financial mentor, not a chatbot.
Early versions of our conversational layer kept giving generic advice despite having the user's complete financial data in context. The model would say things like "consider reducing discretionary spending" when it had Rahul's exact ₹8,200 food bill sitting right there. Getting the prompt architecture right — so every response was grounded in the user's actual numbers and explained in plain language — took significant iteration.
For TTS/STT integration, syncing speech input with the conversational state without breaking the chat flow was trickier than expected. We solved it by treating voice as an input layer sitting above the chat logic rather than embedded inside it.

Integrating voice into a financially sensitive conversation turned out to be the hardest engineering problem we hit.
The challenge wasn't speech recognition itself — it was handling interruptions, partial inputs, and accented Hindi-English speech accurately enough that a financially illiterate user wouldn't get frustrated and drop off. We went through three different approaches before landing on something stable.
The prompt engineering for the conversational mentor was its own battle — early versions ignored the user's financial context and defaulted to generic advice. We rebuilt the system prompt architecture around explicit grounding rules: every claim the chatbot makes must trace back to a number in the user's bank data.

**AI/ML**

FinPilot is an agentic AI system not a model wrapper. It combines a rule-based transaction classifier, a financial memory store built from the user's actual bank data, and a conversational LLM layer that reasons exclusively over that personal financial context. The AI doesn't generate generic financial advice  it grounds every response in the user's real rupee numbers. Future implementation includes a RAG pipeline using ChromaDB and Google text-embedding-004 for retrieval over regulatory documents and insurance policies  eliminating hallucination on compliance-critical financial information.

### ScrowX
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/scrowx-62de) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/MrLajawab19/Escrow) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Stellaris-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://stellaris.devfolio.co)

> AI that automates trust in every deal

![JavaScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/JavaScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In today’s digital economy, online transactions between buyers and sellers often lack trust and security. Buyers risk losing money if a seller fails to deliver, while sellers face the possibility of completing work without getting paid. This trust gap creates friction, limits collaboration, and exposes users to fraud.

Traditional payment systems do not provide a structured mechanism to ensure that both parties fulfill their commitments. There is also a lack of transparency in transaction processes and no reliable way to handle disputes when things go wrong.

ScrowX solves these challenges by introducing a secure escrow-based system where funds are held safely until all agreed conditions are met. This ensures that buyers only release payment after satisfactory delivery, while sellers are guaranteed that funds are secured before they begin work.

By acting as a neutral intermediary, ScrowX builds trust, reduces fraud, and creates a transparent and reliable transaction environment for both parties.

**Challenges we ran into**

One of the biggest challenges I faced while building ScrowX was managing synchronization between the frontend and backend, especially during the escrow workflow. Ensuring that order states (created, funded, delivered, completed) remained consistent across both buyer and seller dashboards required careful API design and state management.

Another major challenge was handling database configuration and environment setup. While integrating Sequelize with PostgreSQL, I encountered issues related to environment variables and configuration mismatches, which caused runtime errors during development. Debugging and structuring the configuration properly took significant effort.

I also faced difficulties with Git version control while managing different project states. Handling merge conflicts and dealing with diverged branches required a deeper understanding of Git workflows, especially when reverting commits and syncing with the remote repository.

Additionally, implementing a smooth and intuitive UI while maintaining responsiveness across devices required multiple iterations and refinements. Balancing functionality with user experience was a constant challenge.

Despite these challenges, each problem helped me improve my debugging skills, understand system design better, and build a more robust and scalable application.

![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![scikit-learn](https://img.shields.io/badge/scikit--learn-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![XGBoost](https://img.shields.io/badge/XGBoost-333333?style=flat-square) ![Setu](https://img.shields.io/badge/Setu-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square) ![Nodejs](https://img.shields.io/badge/Nodejs-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

**The Problem**
Legacy credit bureaus lock out millions of financially responsible, "credit invisible" people simply because they lack a history of debt.

**What It Does**
Consumers link their bank statements to instantly generate a cash-flow-based Equis Financial Resilience Score.

**Why It’s Better**
Banks use our deterministic, fair-lending-compliant ML pipeline to safely underwrite these untraditional borrowers. By analyzing real-time income, rent stability, and spending metric, Equis replaces stale credit scores with instant, mathematically rigorous risk assessments, unlocking growth.

**Challenges we ran into**

Our biggest hurdle was localized data ingestion. We initially integrated Plaid, but its US/Europe-centric model struggled with the nuances of Indian bank transaction formats.


We overcame this by pivoting to Setu, an India-centric API. This successfully pulled the localized statements needed to seamlessly feed our custom NLP cleaning pipeline.

**AI/ML**

Equis fits the FinTech track by applying machine learning to real-time bank data, creating an alternative credit scoring model that safely unlocks direct financial access for millions of untraditional borrowers.

> #GraphSpeaks #MakeVisualsSpeak #DecodingVisuals

![Deep Learning](https://img.shields.io/badge/Deep%20Learning-333333?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-333333?style=flat-square) ![AI/ML](https://img.shields.io/badge/AI/ML-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

The primary objective of our solution is to make graphical representation
accessible to visually impaired people by providing explanation in audio
form for each chart during online STEM study . To achieve this objective we
want to design and train a computer vision pipeline capable classifying
various chart topologies and extracting data from them using deep
learning architecture.

**Challenges we ran into**

Challenges We Ran Into

1. Heavy OCR Slowing Down the App
EasyOCR made the app slow and resource-heavy due to Pytorch.
Tried to use lightweight version for Pytorch.

2. Mapping Text to Graph Structure
Text alone wasn’t enough without position context.
Solution: Used OCR bounding boxes + YOLO to map text to graph elements.

3. Converting Pixels to Values
Detected objects didn’t directly give numerical values.
Solution: Built a scaling logic using axis numbers to map pixels → real values.

4. Developing the app from via flutter for Android Devices

### aurva-in
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/aurvain-a4cb) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/cherry-bisht/aurva) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Stellaris-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://stellaris.devfolio.co)

> DpDp compliance tool

![Go](https://img.shields.io/badge/Go-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Modern companies store massive amounts of user data across cloud services like AWS (S3, databases, logs). This data often contains Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as emails, phone numbers, PAN numbers, and more.

The problem is:

❌ No visibility into where sensitive data actually exists
❌ Manual audits are slow and incomplete
❌ Misconfigured storage can expose critical data
❌ New regulations (like India’s DPDP Act, 2023) require strict compliance
❌ Existing tools (e.g., AWS Macie) are expensive and complex
💡 What People Can Use It For

Aurva helps teams:

🔍 Automatically discover sensitive data in their cloud (e.g., S3 buckets)
🧠 Identify types of PII (emails, phone numbers, IDs, etc.)
⚠️ Detect risky storage locations (public buckets, unprotected files)
📊 Understand compliance status with DPDP Act
📄 Generate actionable reports for audits and internal reviews
⚡ How It Makes Things Easier & Safer
Before Aurva:
Engineers manually inspect data (or don’t at all)
Compliance is reactive and stressful
High risk of unnoticed data exposure
With Aurva:
✅ 1-click scan of cloud data
✅ Centralized dashboard showing all sensitive data locations
✅ Clear risk insights instead of raw logs
✅ Faster compliance readiness
✅ Reduced chances of data leaks

**Challenges we ran into**

Understanding IAM Roles & ARN

Handling AWS IAM roles and ARNs was confusing at first, especially for cross-account access.

Challenges:

Structuring the correct Role ARN
Setting up trust relationships
Ensuring least-privilege access while still making the scanner functional

How I solved it:

Broke down ARN structure and IAM role flow
Created a minimal read-only role (AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess)
Focused on getting a working AssumeRole flow before adding complexity
 Moving from Prototype to Real Product

The project was built quickly (~8 hours), which made it easy to create a working UI but harder to ensure real functionality.

Challenges:

UI looked complete, but backend lacked real-world reliability
Risk of overfocusing on frontend instead of core functionality

How I solved it:

Shifted focus from UI → backend integration

Defined a clear milestone:

Different AWS accounts must produce different real scan results

Prioritized real data scanning over visual polish
 Handling Large Data & Performance

While testing with large datasets (~100MB), performance and scanning efficiency became noticeable concerns.

Challenges:

Efficiently scanning large files for PII
Avoiding slow or blocking operations

How I solved it:

Used Go for concurrency and performance
Built initial benchmarking scripts (bench_pii.go) to measure limits
Planned optimization for streaming and chunk-based scanning

[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/kisan-ai-6699) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub-Source%20Code-181717?style=flat-square&logo=github&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/deepraj-07/Kisan-AI) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1uCSGigGDmpj82d8tBrc8yScAFVWUCdYC?usp=sharing) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Stellaris-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://stellaris.devfolio.co)

> Kisan AI   - Har khet ka  Digital Agronomist

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Firebase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Firebase-333333?style=flat-square) ![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![Google Cloud Vision API](https://img.shields.io/badge/Google%20Cloud%20Vision%20API-333333?style=flat-square) ![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind%20CSS-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

In India, farmers still rely on fragmented and unreliable sources of information — weather from one app, market prices from another, and disease diagnosis mostly based on guesswork.

This leads to major challenges:

Poor crop selection → financial losses

Late pest/disease detection → reduced yield

Unpredictable weather → wrong irrigation & spraying decisions

Lack of market awareness → selling at lower prices

Kisan AI solves this by bringing everything into one intelligent platform.

It helps farmers to:

Make data-driven farming decisions

Detect crop diseases early using AI vision

Plan irrigation and spraying using real-time weather insights

Track farm activities and expenses

Access market prices and government schemes easily

 In short:
Kisan AI transforms traditional farming into a smart, AI-powered decision system.

**Challenges we ran into**

1. Gemini API Rate Limits (429 errors)

During development, the free API tier frequently hit rate limits, causing failed responses.

Solution:

Implemented fallback handling

Optimized prompts for efficiency

Used multiple API keys during testing

2. Real-time Location Accuracy

Browser GPS sometimes failed or returned incorrect locations.

Solution:

Integrated OpenStreetMap (Nominatim) for reverse geocoding

Added fallback default locations per state

Implemented manual refresh logic

3. Making Weather Data Useful

Raw weather API data was not directly helpful for farmers.

Solution:

Calculated derived metrics like evapotranspiration (ET₀)

Built an AI advisory layer for irrigation and spraying decisions

4. Image-based Disease Detection Issues

Different lighting and image quality caused inconsistent AI outputs.

Solution:

Improved prompt engineering

Structured the response format

Added severity classification logic

5. Full-stack Integration Complexity

Integrating AI, Firebase, APIs, and frontend created complexity.

Solution:

Designed a modular architecture

Separated API routes cleanly

Used reusable hooks and structured data flow

**AI/ML**

Kisan AI — AI/ML Track Submission

Kisan AI directly addresses this track by deploying multiple AI/ML technologies to solve a critical real-world problem: the lack of accessible agricultural intelligence for 140 million Indian farmers.

AI/ML Technologies Used:

Computer Vision — Gemini Vision API analyzes crop photos to identify diseases and pests, returning disease name, severity level, and treatment protocol with confidence scoring and web-search fallback for low-confidence predictions.

Natural Language Processing — Multilingual conversational AI supports 6 Indian languages (Hindi, Punjabi, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil, English) with real-time context injection of live weather, soil moisture, and mandi prices into every response.

Predictive Analytics — FAO Penman-Monteith evapotranspiration model combined with Open-Meteo soil moisture data generates AI irrigation alerts and spray window predictions based on actual farm conditions.

Recommendation Systems — Crop advisor engine analyzes soil type, season, water source, and previous crop to recommend optimal crops with ROI breakdown — investment, revenue, profit per acre, and risk assessment.

Meaningful Impact — India has 140 million farmers, 70% of whom lack access to agronomic expertise. Kisan AI puts an AI agronomist in every farmer's pocket, in their own language, with real-time local data — bridging the gap between enterprise agricultural intelligence and ground-level farming decisions.

Technical Depth — End-to-end integration of Gemini Vision, real-time APIs, Firebase, multilingual NLP, and confidence-based web search grounding demonstrates production-grade AI system design.

**The problem it solves**

**TryVia — Virtual Try-On Platform**

**TryVia** is a virtual try-on platform that lets users visualize clothes and accessories on their own photos before buying — removing guesswork from online shopping.

**What can you use it for?**

 1. Smarter Shopping
→ See how outfits actually look on you before purchasing

 2. Style Experimentation
→ Try different outfits, colors, and combinations instantly

 3. Social Shopping
→ Test outfits on friends’ photos & take opinions

 4. In-Store Experience (QR Feature)
→ Scan product QR in stores → instantly visualize on yourself

 5. All-in-One Try-On
→ Works across multiple e-commerce platforms

**How it makes life easier**

✔️ Faster decisions (no more “will it suit me?”)
✔️ Saves time (no trial rooms, no multiple orders)
✔️ Reduces returns (better visualization = better choices)

 **How it’s safer**

✔️ Contactless shopping
✔️ No shared trial rooms
✔️ Less physical handling of products

**Impact**

→ Boosts confidence while shopping
→ Improves user experience
→ Helps businesses increase conversions

**Challenges we ran into**

##  **Challenge & Solution**

While building Tryvia, we wanted users to paste any product link and simply add our domain before it to access virtual try-on directly, similar to price comparison tools. Initially, we used web scraping to fetch product data from platforms like Amazon and Flipkart, but most e-commerce sites blocked our bots, making the feature unreliable. We realized the proper solution is to use official APIs, which require joining affiliate programs and approval. Since API access isn’t immediate, we decided to postpone this feature and implement it in the future once we get proper access.

### EquiFund
[![Devfolio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Devfolio-View%20Project-4B32C3?style=flat-square&logo=devfolio&logoColor=white)](https://devfolio.co/projects/equifund-d14d) [![Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Demo-Live-00C853?style=flat-square&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://jethin10-abes-hackathon-web.onrender.com/) [![Built at](https://img.shields.io/badge/Built%20at-Stellaris-0052CC?style=flat-square)](https://stellaris.devfolio.co)

> Fund the future without the fees

![React](https://img.shields.io/badge/React-333333?style=flat-square) ![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Node.js-333333?style=flat-square) ![SQLite](https://img.shields.io/badge/SQLite-333333?style=flat-square) ![PostgreSQL](https://img.shields.io/badge/PostgreSQL-333333?style=flat-square) ![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-333333?style=flat-square)

**The problem it solves**

Crowdfunding platforms help people raise money, but they do not ensure accountability after funding. Backers usually lose control once they pay, and founders who are genuinely building have no structured way to prove progress.

Equifund solves this by tying funds to milestones. Capital is locked, founders submit proof, backers vote, and money is released only when progress is approved. This makes fundraising more transparent, safer, and more trust-driven for both founders and backers.

**Challenges we ran into**

One major challenge was balancing real-world compliance with Web3-style transparency. We solved that by designing two separate rails: a fiat-first flow for India and a crypto-native flow for global users, both sharing the same milestone and governance engine.

Another challenge was deployment reliability. We ran into production issues around auth, campaign publishing, and demo flows, and fixed them by hardening the backend, improving Render deployment setup, and making the judge demo paths more resilient.

**Web3**

Equifund fits the Web3 track because it brings programmable escrow, milestone-based fund release, and governance into crowdfunding. For global users, campaigns can follow a crypto-native USDC rail with smart-contract-style escrow logic.

Even when using a compliance-aware fiat rail for India, the core trust layer is still built around Web3 ideas like transparent release conditions, wallet-ready architecture, and decentralized-style voting and arbitration.
